title: Fact Check: Video of colleagues fighting over Hindi during Zoom call is SCRIPTED - not real
content:
This is a scripted video made for entertainment. It does not show a real incident.
Amid New Year celebrations, a video of a group of people allegedly quarrelling about NYE plans over an office Zoom call was widely shared. In it, one person can be seen interrupting his colleague, urging him to speak in English as he was unable to understand Hindi. This ultimately fuels a heated argument.
Posts containing the video were shared  with claims like: " Kalesh b/w Colleagues over one Guy was speaking Hindi during Team Zoom meeting."
India Today Fact Check found that this video was staged. Its creator confirmed that it was made for entertainment only.
It's noteworthy that several news outlets reported on the video, including Aaj Tak, India Times , News Nine , and Money Control . Aaj Tak has since retracted the story.Â
Upon reverse searching keyframes from the viral video, we found that it was shared on Instagram on December 22, 2023  by a person named Rahul Salim. The caption of this post carried a disclaimer stating that the video was made for fun and was a light-hearted reel depicting corporate life.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by MC GUDDU (@rahul_salim)
A post shared by MC GUDDU (@rahul_salim)
On this account, we found multiple such videos  of colleagues similarly quarrelling during office Zoom calls . Additionally, some attendees remained the same in all of these videos, suggesting that the videos were staged.
We then reached out to Rahul Salim, the person running this account. Salim told India Today that this video was scripted and was made purely for fun. He added that he has been a content creator for almost a decade now, and now works as a manager at VerSe Innovation. The people in the video are his teammates.
Salim explained to India Today, "The sole purpose behind the video was obviously to make a viral and entertaining video. As I have mentioned in the description, we respect all the languages and it was only for fun."
It is thus clear that a scripted video made for entertainment was shared on social media as a real incident. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jan 2, 2024 15:49 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show British oil tanker attacked by Houthi missile!
content:
This video is from Oman's territorial waters and has nothing to do with the Houthis or a British oil tanker.
Amid the Israel-Hamas war, Houthi militants from Yemen have launched more than 100 attacks against commercial vessels in the Red Sea, affecting traffic there. A video now going viral shows a vessel burning in the middle of a sea. Allegedly, a British oil tanker was attacked by the Yemeni rebel forces.
"Breaking: British oil tanker ablaze off the coast of Hodeidah, Yemen, following a missile strike! The situation is rapidly developing in the maritime region," read one post on X.
On Facebook, one such post read: "Houthis attack a British oil tanker near Hodeidah." The archived version of a similar post can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that the video does not show a British oil carrier and has nothing to do with Houthis.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a news report from the Times Of Oman  published on December 23, 2023. This report contained a screenshot from the viral video.
Per the report, a ship caught fire in the Sultanate of Oman's territorial waters when it was en route to the Republic of Somalia with 11 Indian citizens on board. Subsequent searches yielded another similar news report published by the Arabian Daily  the next day. Video: 11 Indian rescued from burning ship off Oman coast #Oman #rop pic.twitter.com/LKRbYU0rHq — Arabian Daily (@arabiandailys) December 23, 2023 Both reports confirm that the vessel, with 11 Indian nationals on board, caught fire in Oman's territorial waters. The crew, however, was promptly rescued. Notably, neither report mentioned Houthis, any kind of terrorist attack, or the involvement of a British oil tanker. Both reports quoted the Oman police. Through a keyword search, we came across the original video shared by the official X account of the Oman Police. احتراق لنش في المياه الإقليمية لسلطنة عمان قبالة سواحل نيابة حاسك بمحافظة ظفار، محمل بمجموعة من البضائع متّجهًا إلى جمهورية الصومال، وتم إجلاء طاقمه المكون من ١١ شخصاً من الجنسية الهندية عن طريق المواطنين وجميعهم بصحة جيدة مع إصابة أحدهم بإصابة بسيطة ونُقل لتلقي العلاج اللازم. pic.twitter.com/BZGHdHMsS9 — شرطة عُمان السلطانية (@RoyalOmanPolice) December 23, 2023 The Arabic statement roughly translates to: "A boat burned in the territorial waters of the Sultanate of Oman off the coast of the Hasik Niyabat in the Dhofar Governorate, loaded with a group of goods heading to the Republic of Somalia. Its crew, consisting of 11 people of Indian nationality, was evacuated by citizens, all of whom were in good health, with one of them sustaining a minor injury and being transported to receive the necessary treatment." Therefore, it is clear that an unrelated video of a fire accident on a ship in the territorial waters of Oman was falsely shared as a purported Houthi aggression.  - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 2, 2024 15:51 IST

title: Fact Check: These videos have NOTHING to do with the recent earthquakes in Japan
content:
None of these clips are from Japan. One is from Turkey, the other from the US, and the third one is from Indonesia.
Japan was hit by a series of earthquakes  on January 1, the strongest of which measured a staggering 7.4 on the Richter scale. Soon after, the authorities issued Tsunami warnings, which were lifted later on.
Amid this disaster that has led to the loss of at least 48 lives, numerous old and unrelated videos surfaced on social media. Let us talk about three such viral videos.
Claim 1: This video allegedly shows  hospital staff rescuing children during the recent earthquake in Japan.
Fact: This video dates back to February 2023. It shows the staff of Topcuoglu Hospital rescuing children in Turkey's Gaziantep province during the deadly earthquakes that hit the country at the time. Turkish media outlet TRT World uploaded the video on its YouTube channel on February 13, 2023. The Turkish Health Minister Dr Fahrettin Koca had also shared it on X. Daha ilk anda deprem illerine koÅŸmaya baÅŸlayan insanlarımız da aynı ÅŸeyi yaptı. pic.twitter.com/4R7vsAH2y7 — Dr. Fahrettin Koca (@drfahrettinkoca) February 12, 2023

Daha ilk anda deprem illerine koÅŸmaya baÅŸlayan insanlarımız da aynı ÅŸeyi yaptı. pic.twitter.com/4R7vsAH2y7 — Dr. Fahrettin Koca (@drfahrettinkoca) February 12, 2023
As per reports , the Turkey-Syria earthquakes led to the deaths of more than 50,000 people in February 2023.Â
Claim 2: This video report  allegedly shows massive waves hitting the shore during the recent tsunami in Japan.
Fact: This video is not from Japan but from California in the US. It is part of an ABC News report dated December 29, 2023. Per the report, massive waves flooded the streets in California. Many were injured and at least eight people had to be hospitalised.
Per the Los Angeles Times report  dated December 28, 2023, high surf and flood advisories were issued for California's coastal regions.Â
Claim 3: This clip shows people trying to take selfies when tsunami waves recently hit Japan. They were swept away when waves hit the shore.
Fact: This video is from Indonesia and shows a natural phenomenon called the Bono wave, not a tsunami. Using a keyword search, we found its longer version posted on a Facebook page called "Bono local surfer" on December 10, 2021 .
As per Tribune News , the woman seen in the video is Rina Bono, a content creator based in the Riau province of Indonesia. Rina strategically did this act of facing the tidal waves with fellow content creators to promote the tidal bore of the Kampar River, known as Bono .
A Bono wave  is a sporadic phenomenon that happens when tidal currents meet river currents, forming giant waves in the estuary of the river. - Ends Published By: Poulami Kundu Published On: Jan 3, 2024 13:31 IST

title: Fact Check: This video does not show US attacking Houthi boats! It's from 2017
content:
This video is from 2017 and shows trials being conducted by the US Navy in the Pacific Ocean.
On December 31, 2023, the US claimed  to have sunk three Houthi boats and killed 10 crew members after a clash in the Red Sea. Houthi gunmen on said boats were allegedly trying to attack a container ship . Now, a video allegedly showing this has gone viral on social media. The video seems to show some shots being fired at a distant boat. Â
An X user  shared the video and wrote, "The US Navy has destroyed Houthi boats whose crew attempted to board a container ship in the Red Sea." Its archive can be seen here . Times Now also used this clip in a report about the US sinking three Houthi boats.Â
India Today found that the video in question is around seven years old and shows a trial conducted by the US Navy. Our Probe
Many people reacting to the viral video claimed that it dates back to 2017 . Using this information, we ran a keyword search and found its longer version on the YouTube channel "Gung Ho Vids" which claims to post videos produced by the US armed forces. The viral clip can be seen here at around the 40-second mark in this video.Â
As per the video's description, the US Navy staff was conducting a test called the Combat Systems Ship Qualifications Trials, during which, a Mark 38 machine gun was used to hit small boat targets on February 2, 2017.
The channel attributed the video to "Joshua Samoluk". Based on this information, we looked further, which led us to the website of the Defence Visual Information Distribution Service . This is a platform , the US Department of Defence's "direct line of communication for news and information to US forces deployed worldwide, on land, sea and air". Here, the video was credited to Petty Officer 3rd Class Joshua Samoluk.
As per the website , the video was recorded on February 2, 2017, somewhere in the Pacific Ocean. It showed sailors aboard the USS America (LHA 6) loading ammunition into a close-in weapons system, for operational testing. As per a press release by the US Navy , the final phase of the Combat Systems Ship Qualifications Trials and follow-on operation testing of the ship's weapons systems was completed on February 2, 2017.
Thus, it is clear that this video has nothing to do with the US combatting Houthi militants in the Red Sea. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Jan 3, 2024 16:07 IST

title: Fact Check: This video is not from Ayodhya Ram Mandir, shows arrangements at Varanasi temple
content:
This video shows makeshift toilets at Varanasi's Swarved Temple, not the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya.
As Ayodhya prepares for the upcoming grand consecration ceremony of the Ram Mandir, a video that's circulating on social media purports to show the state of sanitation arrangements in the temple complex.
In the viral video, hundreds of toilets- predominantly "Indian-style", and some "Western" commodes can be seen. A Facebook user while sharing the viral video wrote, "Oh my God, is it the Unity in Diversity mode of toilets? Toilet setup for the Ayodhya Ram temple inauguration day in Uttar Pradesh?" The archived version of the viral post can be seen here. Â
Indian Air Force veteran Rajiv Tyagi shared the video and wrote: "Arrangements for visitors to Ayodhya - two rows of open Indian toilets, directly splashing their contents into an open deep trench latrine." Arrangements for visitors to Ayodhya - two rows of open Indian toilets, directly splashing their contents into an open deep trench latrine... 😎 pic.twitter.com/Ry8Fyt3eMI — Rajiv Tyagi (@rajivtango) January 3, 2024
Arrangements for visitors to Ayodhya - two rows of open Indian toilets, directly splashing their contents into an open deep trench latrine... 😎 pic.twitter.com/Ry8Fyt3eMI — Rajiv Tyagi (@rajivtango) January 3, 2024
India Today found that the viral video does not show preparations for the Ayodhya Ram Temple inauguration but rather makeshift or under-constructed toilets at the recently-inaugurated Swarved Temple in Varanasi.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led to several YouTube uploads featuring similar visuals. These videos claimed that the location of the video was Varanasi . Further searches took us to a YouTube video stating that it was from the Swarved Temple in Varanasi.
Taking these cues, we performed keyword searches that led us to a YouTube blog  about the Swarved Mahamandir Dham in Varanasi, where the vlogger detailed arrangements for visitors, including accommodation and sanitation.
Another YouTube vlog on Swarved Mahamandir Dham in Varanasi also featured similar visuals.
These vlogs were shot and uploaded before Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the meditation centre  on December 18, 2023. While we couldn't ascertain if the viral video showed under-constructed or makeshift toilets, it is nonetheless clear that the video is not from the Ayodhya Ram Mandir but from the Swarved Temple in Varanasi. - Ends Published By: Shweta Kumari Published On: Jan 4, 2024 14:57 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Ireland expel its Israeli ambassador? No! Read to know
content:
The Ambassador of Israel to Ireland has not been expelled. That motion was defeated. The woman seen in the video is the president of Ireland's main opposition party.
South Africa has moved to the International Court of Justice against Israel , accusing it of crimes of genocide against Palestinians in Gaza. Several countries, including Malaysia and Turkey, have thrown their weight behind South Africa's case  and issued statements of solidarity.
Now, a video of a woman criticising Israel's destruction of Gaza  is being shared on social media platforms. The claims suggest that Ireland has officially decided to expel its Israeli ambassador and take Israel to the International Criminal Court.Â
One Facebook user sharing the viral video wrote , "It's official, Ireland decides to immediately expel the Israeli ambassador from Dublin and accuses the International Criminal Court of genocide and war crimes. So wonderful to see many countries waking up and standing up for the Palestinian children." An archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today found that motions in the Irish Parliament calling for the expulsion of the Israeli ambassador and taking Israel to the ICC were defeated.Â
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to several reports about the video. A report by Politico dated November 15 , 2023, contained a grab from the viral video and identified the woman seen in it as Mary Lou McDonald, president of Ireland's main opposition party, Sinn Fein. The report noted that at Sinn Fein's annual conference, McDonald in her keynote speech called for the expulsion of Israel's ambassador to Ireland, Dana Erlich.Â
We also found the extended version of the viral video  uploaded on the official channel of Sinn Fein, titled, "Mary Lou McDonald Sinn Féin Ard Fheis Presidential Address 2023." The clipped portions of the viral video can be seen at the 12:45  and the 13:29 timestamps .
Turkish state media agency Anadolu  also carried excerpts from her speech at the conference. Similar reports about McDonald coming down heavily on Israel in her speech at her party's annual conference can be seen here  and here .
Further, we found that motions in the Irish parliament  calling for the expulsion of the Israeli ambassador and referring Israel to the International Criminal Court, moved by Social Democrats and Sinn Fein respectively, were defeated .
Thus, it's clear that a video of an Irish opposition leader calling for the expulsion of the Israeli ambassador to Israel and taking Israel to the ICC is being shared with false claims. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Jan 8, 2024 19:55 IST

title: Fact Check: No, this cobra doesn't aim to become LIC agent. It visited a hospital
content:
This video is from 2022 and shows a rescuer holding a snake at a hospital in Bilaspur.
A video making the rounds on social media  featured a woman holding a huge snake and a group of people recording videos  of it on their smartphones.
Allegedly, this snake was caught in the offices  of the Life Insurance Corporation of India in Mumbai. One such Facebook post read : "Mumbai: LIC corporate office record room.  A king cobra paid a surprise visit to inspect how well the old record was kept there. The brave firewoman got its custody. Salute to the officer."
India Today Fact Check found that this video is neither recent nor from Mumbai. It shows a 2022 incident at a hospital in Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh. Our Probe
A keyword search led us to a post by the official X account of LIC India  from November 8, 2022. The post read: "It has come to our notice that a video is in circulation showing a snake caught in the record room of the Corporate Office of LIC Of India, Mumbai. We confirm that no such incident has happened and the video is fake." It has come to our notice that a video is in circulation showing a snake caught in the record room of Corporate Office of LIC Of India, Mumbai. We confirm that no such incident has happened and the video is fake.
— LIC India Forever (@LICIndiaForever) November 8, 2022
It has come to our notice that a video is in circulation showing a snake caught in the record room of Corporate Office of LIC Of India, Mumbai. We confirm that no such incident has happened and the video is fake.
— LIC India Forever (@LICIndiaForever) November 8, 2022
Further searches led us to an extended version of the viral video , shared on the YouTube channel "Kamal Choudhary Snake Rescue Team Bilaspur". The channel is run by Kamal Choudhary, a snake rescuer based in Bilaspur, who has shared several such videos featuring the same woman  seen in the viral clip .
The video contained two clips: the viral video and another clip shot from a different angle. The woman can be seen handing over the stick holding the snake to one of the men present there.Â
In the second clip, we noticed a blue board on top of a door that read "Dr Rashmi Budhia". With the help of a Google search, we found out that Rashmi Budhia is an Obstetrician and Gynaecologist  at Budhia Hospital — a hospital located in Bilaspur , Chhattisgarh.
Around November 2022, several people shared this video on social media , stating that a snake was caught at the Budhia Hospital of Bilaspur .
It is thus clear that a 2022 video from Bilaspur was falsely shared as a recent incident in Mumbai's LIC office. - Ends Published By: Ashmita Saha Published On: Jan 8, 2024 21:20 IST

title: Fact Check: To hit back at Male, celebs flaunt amazing Lakshadweep pics. Turns out, they're from Maldives
content:
Two of these pictures are from Maldives while the third one is from French Polynesia.
On January 7 and 8, you couldn't scroll X without seeing Indian celebrities, cricketers, and politicians sharing scenic photos of sparkling blue waters and white sandy beaches. All this was in service of promoting India's hidden gem — Lakshadweep — to the world.Â
What sparked this was Prime Minister Narendra Modi posting pictures of the union territory , calling it a "stunning beauty", which was seen by some Maldivian politicians as an attempt to hurt its tourism business, which led to a war of words and a bit of a diplomatic tussle.
But while the photos of the beachy paradise being shared online were all beautiful, some — to everyone's chagrin — were not from Lakshadweep at all and in fact from Maldives (and at least one from French Polynesia)!Â
Many X users including Union Minister Kiren Rijiju and Bollywood actor Ranveer Singh shared pictures of what they called Lakshadweep. Unfortunately, neither of the three photos they shared were from India. They've since deleted their posts.Â
So, let's take a look at these photos and where they came from: The First PhotoÂ
Minister of Earth Sciences Kiren Rijiju shared two alleged photos of Lakshadweep multiple times on X while responding to other celebrities' posts about the Indian islands. One of these featured two people kayaking. We found that this photo is from the Dhaalu Atoll (island) in Maldives.Â
Upon reverse-searching it, we found that many websites and Facebook posts claimed it was from Maldives. We also found a similar picture on the popular website Maldives.com .Â
We eventually found the picture on the image-sharing website Flickr which also contained its original metadata. Per this, the image is from the Angsana Velavaru resort located at Dhaalu Atoll in Maldives.Â
According to the EXIF data, the image dates back to November 14, 2011, and was captured by photographer Felix Hug. We found the Instagram and Facebook accounts of Felix Hug, a Swiss photographer based in Singapore, known for photographing Maldivian resorts .Â
India Today also reached out to Felix Hug on Instagram, who confirmed that the picture shows the Angsana Velavaru resort in Maldives. The Second Photo
The second image shared by Rijiju shows a man swimming near an island. As per the stock image website Alamy, the picture is from Bora Bora, an island in French Polynesia. It was captured on July 10, 2012.Â
We also found a similar photograph on Getty Images' platform iStock that was credited to Alexander Shalamov , a photographer based in Finland.  Shalamov also shared a similar picture on his Instagram page and mentioned the location as Ninamu Resort in French Polynesia. The Third Photo This picture was shared by Ranveer Singh who wrote alongside: "Chalo Bharat Dekhe" or "Let's explore India". We found that the image is from the Maldives and was listed as such on Shutterstock , the stock image website. Upon digging further, we found that the picture was also shared on the Canva-owned stock website Pexels. Here it was uploaded by an account called "Asad Photo Maldives". Asad is a Maldives-based photographer who shared the same picture on his X and Instagram handles . The location here mentioned is Baa Atoll. With the help of this, we also geolocated the place seen in the photo. advertisement So, it's clear that while Lakshadweep is home to beautiful pristine beaches, the three photos mentioned above don't show those at all. Update: India Today received a response from the photographer who captured the first photo after the story was published. This response has been added to the story. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 8, 2024 21:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Yet another Delhi road rage video? Nope, this is from Mexico
content:
This video is from December 2022, and shows a road rage incident in Toluca, a city in Mexico.
Delhi is no stranger to incidents of road rage. Now, a video of one such alleged incident from India's capital is making the rounds on social media. In the video, a car rams into a man multiple times.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the incident was not from Delhi. It's not even from India. It's a 2022 indecent from the Mexican city of Toluca. Our Probe
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a Reddit post, featuring the video in question. In its comment section, we found a news report about the incident .
According to this Spanish report, a fight occurred between men driving in Avenida Tecnológico in Mexico, on December 3, 2022. The conflict led to a man driving over the other man twice with his car. The culprit was later arrested by the police.
We then found several social media posts  and news reports about this incident . According to them, this road rage incident occurred in front of a McDonald's outlet  at the Avenida Tecnológico, Toluca.Â
Another report about the incident contained photos of the damaged vehicle and the men involved in the road rage incident. The Secretary of Security of the State of Mexico also tweeted about the incident on December 4, 2022, stating that the police had detained the culprit. La #SSEdoméx informa que en relación al video difundido en redes sociales sobre un accidente de tránsito ocurrido en #Toluca , donde al parecer varias personas se encuentran involucradas. (1/2)
— Secretaría de Seguridad del Estado de México (@SS_Edomex) December 4, 2022
La #SSEdoméx informa que en relación al video difundido en redes sociales sobre un accidente de tránsito ocurrido en #Toluca , donde al parecer varias personas se encuentran involucradas. (1/2)
— Secretaría de Seguridad del Estado de México (@SS_Edomex) December 4, 2022
We looked for a McDonald's outlet near the mentioned location of the incident and found one at 'Av Tecnológico 1342' . The street view of the road opposite this outlet matched the location of the viral video.
It is hence, clear, that a road rage video from Mexico's Toluca was falsely shared as a Delhi incident. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jan 9, 2024 19:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Did cops brutalise pro-Palestine protestor in LA? This video is from 2022
content:
This video is from an abortion rights protester in Los Angeles in 2022.
A video allegedly showing police brutality at a pro-Palestine protest in Los Angeles in the US has been widely shared. In the video, a policeman can be seen tackling a woman with a megaphone, assaulting her, and finally handcuffing her.
An X user  wrote, "This is Los Angeles. Police brutality attacks a pro-Palestine demonstrator." Archives of this and other similar posts can be seen here  and here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video shows an abortion rights protester in Los Angeles in 2022. It has nothing to do with the ongoing crisis in Palestine. Our Probe
When we reverse-searched keyframes from the viral video, it led us to multiple news reports from June 2022. Reportedly, a female protester in Los Angeles was tackled by Secret Service officers after she walked out onto the street and approached President Joe Biden's motorcade. The Los Angeles Police Department assisted with her arrest.
Biden was in LA for the ninth "Summit of the Americas" in June 2022. The protester, who resisted officers during her arrest, appeared to be advocating for abortion rights. She could be heard shouting, "An abortion ban will not stop abortions — only safe ones." On YouTube, we found this clip on the official account of FOX 11 Los Angeles, shared on June 09, 2022. As per the video report, this incident did not impact Biden's motorcade. In it, the protester said she was protesting for women's rights, making it more than clear that it has nothing to do with Palestine. Thus, it's evident that a video from 2022 was falsely shared as a recent pro-Palestine protest. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Jan 10, 2024 01:09 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOESN'T show NCP leader attacked by mob for comments on Lord Rama
content:
This video is more than eight years old and has nothing to do with Jitendra Awhad's recent comments on Lord Rama.
National Congress Party leader and MLA Jitendra Awhad on January 3 courted controversy after he claimed that Lord Rama was non-vegetarian. Awhad reportedly said: "Lord Ram is ours. He belongs to the Bahujans. The Ram who hunts and eats is ours, we belong to the Bahujans. We follow the ideals of Ram and today we eat mutton."
Multiple cases have been registered against him and Maha Vikas Aghadi leaders have advised him to refrain from making such controversial statements. Awhad has expressed his regret for hurting religious sentiments.
Now, a video allegedly showing the NCP leader being assaulted by a mob is making the rounds online. A Facebook user wrote, "Sharad Pawar's Party MLA Jitendra Awhad beaten for his derogatory comments on Prabhu Ram. Karyakarta of Shiv Pratishthan Sangli gave royal treatment for hurting sentiments of Hindus." The archive of a similar post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is more than eight years old and has nothing to do with Jitendra Awhad's comments on Lord Rama.Â
We found this video's screengrabs in several news reports published in July 2015 . According to them, the incident took place in Sangli, Maharashtra, when a fight broke out between two groups at Awhad's program.
During the event, the leader allegedly made derogatory remarks about veteran Indian writer and historian Babasaheb Purandare and demanded his prestigious Maharashtra Bhushan award be revoked. Irked by these comments, some members of Shivpratishthan Sangathan came to the stage to beat up Jitendra Awhad. A fight subsequently ensued between them and Awhad's party workers.
Taking a clue from this, we searched about this incident on YouTube and found the video of the stage fight uploaded to India Today's channel on July 21, 2015. This video report also mentioned the same details.Â
We also noticed that the viral video contained another clip of Awhad walking out accompanied by a group of people that was not part of the 2015 video. When we reverse-searched screengrabs from that part, we found it shared on Awhad's own YouTube account on November 27, 2023. This too predates his recent controversial statement.
We also found no news reports of the NCP leader being assaulted following his controversial comments. Thus, it is more than clear that the viral video was shared with a false claim. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jan 10, 2024 16:47 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of taxi driver threatening female tourists is not from Maldives
content:
This incident is from Bali, Indonesia.
As the India-Maldives row continues, a video of a taxi driver threatening two women passengers is being widely shared on social media. Allegedly, this incident was in an archipelagic nation.Â
The video shows two women screaming for help and requesting the driver to let them out. One of the women even threatens the driver of calling the US Embassy and the cops. She even bangs the window of the car. The driver insists that they pay 50 dollars. After the women exited the car, one of them said, "That taxi driver threatened us with a knife."Â
An X user shared the video and wrote,"Maldives is too unsafe for women for obvious reasons. Many girls have reported rape, molestation, extortion etc in the Maldives. Girls should avoid going there," along with "Boycott Maldives" hashtags. Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the video is from Bali, Indonesia — not the Maldives.
We noticed many people responding to the video pointed out that it was from Bali in Indonesia.
Around the 1 minute 58 seconds mark in the video, we noticed the registration plate of the car which begins with "DK". As per worldlicenseplates.com  and platesmania.com , vehicle registration numbers in Bali start with "DK". We then ran a keyword search, which led us to a report in The Independent  from January 9, 2024, that said that the tourists in the video were Americans who were travelling through Kuta, a popular beach resort in the south of Bali. Reportedly, they offered the driver 50,000 Indonesian rupiah for the cab fare but the driver kept asking them for $50. As per Yahoo News , the driver was later identified as Yanuarius Toebkae. The incident  was widely covered  by the Indonesian News outlets. As per the Bali Post , the weapon that the taxi driver used to threaten the women was not a knife but a folding fan. The report also said that the argument erupted because the cab driver asked the tourists for $50 (approximately Rs 4,150), whereas they assumed that he meant 50,000 Indonesian Rupiah (which is around Rs 260). Thus, it is clear that a video from Bali was falsely attributed to the Maldives. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Jan 11, 2024 00:46 IST

title: Fact Check: Sex doll at Thailand beach becomes murder victim in Maldives
content:
This image shows a silicone sex doll that was found at a beach in Thailand in 2022.
News of a tourist being raped and murdered in the Maldives is being widely shared on social media as the India-Maldives row continues.
A blurry photo of what appears to be a human body at a beach is being shared with claims like, "A girl who went on a trip to the Maldives was found dead naked near the seashore. She was gang-raped and tortured before being killed!" The archive of one such post can be seen here .Â
India Today found that this image shows a sex doll that was found near the Bang Saen beach of Thailand's Chon Buri province in 2022. OUR PROBE
We noticed that many people reacting to the viral photo said that this photo was from an old incident when a sex doll was found near a beach in Thailand. A subsequent keyword search led us to a Mirror report .
According to the report, on August 18, 2022, a silicone sex doll was found lying near the Bang Saen beach in Chon Buri, Thailand. Incidentally, beachgoers initially assumed it was a corpse and informed the police. However, when the police arrived, they discovered that it was a sex doll with a missing head.Â
News outlets like the New York Post and Pattaya Today had also reported this incident at the time.Â
We also found no credible report of any such grisly incident taking place in the Maldives recently.Â
It's noteworthy that amid the ongoing India-Maldives row, there have been other similar instances of misinformation. For instance, earlier, a video of female tourists being threatened by a taxi driver in Bali was falsely shared as an incident from the Maldives. Read our fact-check of that here . - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Jan 11, 2024 16:57 IST

title: Fact Check: Make AI-merica Great Again? This Trump pic is fake
content:
The viral picture is AI-generated.
A photo now making the rounds on social media  shows former US President Donald Trump sitting with a group of young black men. Per those sharing the photo , Trump stopped his motorcade to take pictures with the young men who waved at him. An archived version of the viral post can be seen here. Â
India Today found that the viral photo is not real but AI-generated. Our Probe
We performed a keyword search and a reverse image search. Neither yielded any results except for the social media accounts that posted it alongside the aforementioned claim.
Upon closer examination, we identified several unusual flaws in the viral picture. Firstly, the man sitting on the right side of Trump has two thumbs, with one having a long nail — a common deformity in AI-generated images.
Secondly, Trump has three fingers in each of his hands. Thirdly, the man on Trump's left is wearing a gumboot on one leg but not on the other. Lastly, the skin and hair of the subjects, including Trump, appear over-smooth.Â
These are all telltale signs that the image is AI-generated.
Further, we also noticed a watermark of @Trump_history45 on the viral photo. We searched for the account on X  and found the viral image uploaded there .
We observed that this shared many AI-generated images of Trump in unusual places and attires.
Thus, it's clear that an AI-generated image of Trump is being shared with misleading claims. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Jan 11, 2024 20:43 IST

title: Fact Check: In Lakshadweep-Male row, Kerala boat accident becomes vessel for fake news
content:
This video is from Kerala where two boats collided during a boat race back in December 2023.
As Lakshadweep basked in newfound attention, making its way to the bucket list of many, including celebrities, a video of a dramatic collision  of two boats began making the rounds on social media. People rowing the boat could be seen toppling down one after another into the water following the collision. Those sharing the clip claimed that this incident unfolded in Lakshadweep.Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from Kerala, where two boats collided with each other during a race. OUR PROBE
Upon reverse searching keyframes from the viral video, we found that the same video was shared on YouTube on December 4, 2023. Its title in Malayalam stated that this accident took place during a boat race held at Pandanad, a village in the Alappuzha district of Kerala. We then found several videos of this incident shot from different angles  on YouTube .
In one of these better-quality videos , we found words on the boat written in Malayalam. Using Google Lens, we found out that it read "Pallathuruthy Boat".Â
A quick search revealed that Pallathuruthy Boat Club or PBC is based in Alappuzha. The club shared a video of this accident on its Instagram page  back in December 2023.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Jeff Holubeshen (@paddler_life) We also found several media reports about the video in question. According to a report by Manorama  dated December 3, 2023, this video is from the Pandanad Champions Boat League. Following their victory in the boat race, PBC club members started rowing their boat back to the pavilion and got hit by another boat in the way. One rover, a native of Thrissur, was hurt in the accident and was admitted to a hospital. It is thus, clear that a boat accident from Kerala was falsely linked to Lakshadweep. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 11, 2024 21:25 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video falsely links US warship fire to recent Houthi attack in Red Sea
content:
The video shows the USS Bonhomme Richard on fire in San Diego, California, in July 2020. It's unrelated to the recent Houthi attacks.
On January 10, the US and UK's naval forces shot down 21 drones and missiles  fired by Yemen's Houthi rebels, one of the largest attack  in the Red Sea shipping zone.Â
Now, a video of a warship up in flames is going viral on social media. Allegedly, it shows the USS Bonhomme Richard on fire after an attack by the Houthis in the Red Sea. The warship in the video can be seen engulfed in fire with thick smoke billowing from it.Â
One X user claimed , "Footage: American warship that was targeted in the Red Sea yesterday." An archived version of the post can be seen here. Footage: American warship that was targeted in the Red Sea yesterday….😳 #GazaGenocide #Gaza #Yemen #Houthis #USA #Israel pic.twitter.com/O0l4O6U0Ci — Nawab Naeem Sial (@NawabNaeem8058) January 10, 2024
Footage: American warship that was targeted in the Red Sea yesterday….😳 #GazaGenocide #Gaza #Yemen #Houthis #USA #Israel pic.twitter.com/O0l4O6U0Ci — Nawab Naeem Sial (@NawabNaeem8058) January 10, 2024
India Today found that the viral video shows the American battleship USS Bonhomme Richard on fire in San Diego, California, in July 2020.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the video led us to several media reports from July 2020. An Iranian news portal  carrying the viral video in its report, noted that the American Navy warship USS Bonhomme Richard engulfed in flames off the coast of San Diego in the US.Â
With this clue, we performed keyword searches and came across several news  and video reports  from July 2020. A video report by The Global News on YouTube  uploaded on Jul 13, 2023, highlighted that a US warship docked at Naval base in San Diego erupted in fire and left 21 people injured. The San Diego Fire-Rescue Department reported an explosion in conjunction with the blaze. Arson charges were filed against one sailor who was accused of starting the fire out of animosity toward commanders. However, he was found not guilty on all counts during a trial by a Navy judge. Similar reports about the fire that destroyed the USS Bonhomme Richard in San Diego can be seen here  and here . USS Bonhomme Richard was decommissioned following the fire that left it damaged beyond "affordable repair". The video of its decommissioning ceremony can be seen below. We looked for reports if any US or UK ship was damaged in the recent Houthis attack. However, the reports suggested the contrary . Thus, it's clear that the video circulating on social media falsely links an old incident off the California coast to the recent Houthi attack in the Red Sea. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 12, 2024 18:30 IST

title: Fact Check: The place where Moses split the Red Sea? Nope, this video is from China!
content:
This video shows the fishbone-shaped sandbank in China's Dongshan Island.
A breathtaking video of a narrow stretch of sandy land surrounded by sparkling water is making the rounds on social media. Allegedly, this was the same place where the Jewish prophet Moses, as the myth goes, split the Red Sea to help his people escape the Egyptian army.Â
According to religious scriptures , Moses guided the Hebrews out of Egypt where they were being ill-treated as slaves. It is believed that as they reached the Red Sea, Moses stretched out his hand, and the waters split, allowing them safe passage.
An X user  shared this video and wrote, "This is the place in the Red Sea, where Hazrat Musa created a passage for his people to escape from the army of Pharaoh, Ramses II. The passage appears twice a year and then disappears." The archive of one such post can be seen here .
India Today found that the video in question has nothing to do with the Red Sea. Instead, it shows the fishbone-shaped sandbank in China's Dongshan Island.Â
We noticed some people reacting to the viral video  pointed out that this was Dongshan Island in China. A quick reverse search of the keyframes of this video led us to a Pinterest post that also said the video shows the fishbone sandbar of Dongshan Island, located in the Fujian Province of China.Â
The video here was credited to a Douyin user with ID "@207697002". Douyin is a video-sharing app similar to TikTok that's also owned by the latter's parent company, ByteDance.Â
We then found the person with the Douyin ID number "@207697002" shared  this video on October 30, 2021. Its caption in Chinese language said: "Maldives? No, this is the fishbone sandbar of Dongshan Island, Fujian. Bring them to Dongshan Island."Â
The user's bio stated that they shared content related to landscape photography. And on this account, we found many similar videos.
Using keyword search, we found that "China Plus Culture", a news outlet that covers China's culture and tourism, also shared this video on November 5, 2021, with the caption, "Yugu Shazhou, which translates to 'fishbone-shaped sandbank', in Fujian's Dongshan Island, has been attracting hordes of tourists with its natural beauty and catchy name. Local fishermen say the moniker relates to a natural 'miracle' whereby this uniquely-shaped sandbank appears as if by magic whenever the tide goes out."
China's state-controlled media People's Daily China also shared a video from this location in 2020, which looks quite similar to the viral video.Â
According to the Global Times , the fishbone-shaped sandbank is located in the Qixia Village of Dongshan County, in southeast China's Fujian Province. WHAT DO THE EXPERTS SAY
We sent the viral post to the former chancellor  of Maulana Azad National Urdu University, Firoz Bakht Ahmed , who is also the grand nephew of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
He told India Today that the "parting of the sea" event is generally believed to have happened in the Red Sea and not near China. "There could be some differences in the opinion of experts about the exact place where this happened, however, it certainly took place in the sea area near Egypt in the Middle East Region," he added. - Ends Published By: Poulami Kundu Published On: Jan 15, 2024 15:05 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral plane video from Chicago storms internet- but it's 4 years old!
content:
This video is from 2019 when an aeroplane skidded off the Chicago O'Hare Airport's runway.
On January 12, a major winter storm unleashed icy winds and heavy snowfall across large parts of the United States , disrupting travel and leaving thousands without power. Over 2,000 flights were reportedly cancelled nationwide , while a ground stop was issued at the Chicago O'Hare International Airport. Â
Amid this, a video  of an aeroplane making a bumpy landing on a snowy runway started making the rounds on social media. Allegedly, this video showed an American Airlines plane skidding off the runway at the Chicago O'Hare Airport amid the massive snowstorm.
One such post  read: "Alert: Chicago O'Hare grounds all flights amid a snowstorm. Chicago's O'Hare Airport cancelled all flights after an American Airlines plane skidded off the runway during a massive snowstorm. Over 650 flights have been cancelled at O'Hare so far. Source: ABC News".
India Today Fact Check found that this is from 2019. Our Probe
We searched for reports about an American Airlines flight skidding off the runway at the Chicago airport amid the winter storm, but could not find any such recent report. We then reverse searched keyframes of the viral clip, which led us to a USA Today report  dated November 11, 2019.Â
According to it, this video showed an American Airlines flight skidding off the runway at the Chicago O'Hare International Airport back in 2019. All 38 passengers and three crew members were safely deplaned from the aircraft added the report.Â
We then found several media reports from 2019 about this incident . Per CNBC, Flight 4125, an Embraer E-145 regional jet, was arriving in Chicago from Piedmont Triad International Airport in North Carolina, when it skidded off the runway. Joseph Lian, one of the passengers onboard the flight, shot the video in question .
At the time as well, a winter weather advisory was in effect for Chicago and more than 1,000 flights were reportedly cancelled between the city's two airports.
It is thus clear, that a 2019 video of a plane skidding off the runway at a Chicago airport was falsely shared as recent. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Jan 15, 2024 15:36 IST

title: Fact Check: This is a 2023 'Kalash Yatra', NOT a procession from Nepal to Ayodhya Ram Mandir
content:
This video shows a July 2023 procession taken out by followers of Dhirendra Shastri or Bageshwar Dham Sarkar in Greater Noida.
A video of a procession of saffron-clad men and women chanting "Jai Shree Ram" is making the rounds on social media. Women in the video could be seen holding something on top of their heads. Those sharing the clip claimed that people from Nepal were marching to Ayodhya for the Ram Mandir's consecration ceremony.Â
Sharing the video on Facebook, one person wrote , "Procession from Nepal, mother's house of Goddess Sita Devi, carrying gifts and offers for the Kumbabhishekam ceremony of Sri Rama Sita temple in Ayodhya. So not only India but Nepal is also in full 'josh' for the Ram Temple." Janakpur, a city in Nepal, is considered to be the birthplace of Lord Ram's wife Sita .
India Today Fact Check found that this video shows a "Kalash Yatra" held in Greater Noida back in July 2023. OUR PROBE
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook Reel dated July 12, 2023 . The video contained the hashtag "Bageshwar Dham Sarkar" and the geotag "Greater Noida". Using these clues, we found a YouTube video of a procession taken out by the followers of self-styled godman Dhirendra Shastri , also known as Bageshwar Dham Sarkar, ahead of his "Bhagwat Katha" event in Greater Noida.
Further, we found media reports that said a three-kilometer-long procession was taken out in Greater Noida on July 9, 2023 , ahead of Shastri's "Bhagwat Katha" scheduled to be held between July 10 to 16 in 2023 at the Jaitpur village.Â
Women participated in huge numbers, carrying a "Kalash", a metal vessel, and coconut on their heads. News 18 reported the same , adding that around 2,000 CCTV cameras were installed and 1,200 police personnel were deployed in the area ahead of the event . A video of this procession was also shared on the official YouTube channel of Bageshwar Dham Sarkar  on July 9, 2023. Some portions of the viral video can be seen after the 1:05 minute mark in the video . It is worth noting that over 3,000 gifts , including silver shoes, ornaments and clothes, reached Ayodhya from Nepal's Janakpur on January 6. Per reports, the presents were brought by a convoy of three dozen vehicles and more than 500 devotees . - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jan 15, 2024 16:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Tale of a different tragedy - video of sobbing girl is from Syria, NOT Gaza
content:
This video was shot in a displacement camp in northern Syria. It has nothing to do with Israel or Palestine.
As the Israeli offensive into Gaza continues, a video allegedly showing a young Palestinian girl sobbing was widely shared. According to the subtitles of the video , she spoke about her horrific living conditions in Gaza saying, "Death is better than all these things that have happened."Â
Sharing this video on Facebook , one person wrote, "Children should not feel this way," along with hashtags like "Genocide in Gaza" and "Israeli Terrorists".
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from Syria. It has no connection with the ongoing situation in Israel and Palestine. Â Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook post containing the video in question , dated January 9. The caption is Arabic, loosely translated to English, read: "Sham. A displaced Syrian girl talks about her wishes and harsh living conditions in a tent in one of the camps in the Idlib countryside." On the top-right corner of this video, we saw the logo of Al Jazeera.Â
Using this clue, we found an extended version of this video on the YouTube channel of Al Jazeera Mubasher , shared on January 8. According to Al Jazeera, this was a Syrian girl called Sham, narrating the ordeal of her displaced family after their tent burned down in northern Syria. According to the text inside the video, the clip was shot on January 1, 2024, at a displacement camp in northern Syria. title: Fact Check: Not an Anti-Hero! This isn't Taylor Swift with convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein
content:
The person sitting next to Taylor Swift is Republic Records CEO Monte Lipman.
Recently unsealed court documents from the Jeffrey Epstein case  have unveiled a list of rich and powerful celebrities among his associates, including Hollywood stars like Leonardo DiCaprio, Cameron Diaz, Cate Blanchett, and Kevin Spacey. Now, a photo of American pop singer Taylor Swift with her arm around a man is going viral on social media. Allegedly, the photo shows the pop star with the financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein .Â
An X user shared the post and wrote , "BREAKING: Taylor Swift and Jeffery Epstein photograph surface after judge orders Epstein files to be revealed." The archive of o ne such post can be seen here . So Taylor Swift was a close friend of Epstein 🤔 pic.twitter.com/bJeYFLkp3F — Edd 🪶✡️ (@Eerikvb) January 5, 2024
So Taylor Swift was a close friend of Epstein 🤔 pic.twitter.com/bJeYFLkp3F — Edd 🪶✡️ (@Eerikvb) January 5, 2024
  India Today, however, found that the person in the photo is not Jeffrey Epstein, but Monte Lipman, the CEO of Republic Records. OUR PROBE
A reverse image search led us to several social media posts from December 2021 . The image had not appeared on the internet before December 2021 when it was initially shared. A Taylor Swift fan, while sharing the photograph on Instagram , identified the man as Monte Lipman, CEO of Republic Records.

Taylor Swift Switzerland  and Taylor Swift Style , two websites run by Swift fans, also identified the man in the picture as Lipman. A close comparison of photos of Lipman available online with Epstein would reveal that the man in the viral picture is indeed Lipman.Â
However, we were not able to find the source of the viral photo.
The court documents from the Jeffrey Epstein case did reveal associations with well-known personalities, but Taylor Swift was not among them. Swift's name also did not surface in the preceding court documents related to the Epstein case. Nor have we found any media reports associating her with Epstein.
The complete list of people named in the documents with links to Epstein can be seen here . Taylor Swift is currently signed to Republic Records , co-owned by Lipman. Several other pictures of Swift with Lipman are available on the internet.
Thus, it's clear that the person sitting next to Taylor Swift in the viral photograph is not the convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jan 15, 2024 18:10 IST

title: Fact Check: This is China's rocket launch, NOT North Korea attacking US tanker in Taiwan
content:
The video shows a Chinese rocket launch from a marine platform in the Yellow Sea.
On January 14, North Korea conducted a test of its new ballistic missile , equipped with a hypersonic manoeuvrable warhead amidst growing tensions with the US and South Korea. Now, a video going viral purports to show North Korea targeting a US oil and gas tanker in Taiwanese waters.
An X user while sharing the viral video, wrote on Facebook , "North Korea bombs USA Oil and gas tanker with missiles in the waters of Taiwan." Its archive can be seen here . ⚡🇰🇵 Breaking: North Korea bombs USA Oil & gas tanker with missiles in the waters of Taiwan 🇹🇼 #GazaMassacare #Hamas #IsraelPalestineWar #Iran #Hezbollah #Houthis #Iraq #Yemen #Taiwan #TheTraitors pic.twitter.com/URhyY9RrEh — GeoPolitics (@GeoPolitics52) January 13, 2024

India Today, however, found that the video shows a Chinese rocket launch in the Yellow Sea. OUR PROBE
Conducting a reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to several media reports .
Chinese state-owned media CGTN reported on January 11 about China's successful launch of the world's most powerful solid propellant rocket. The Gravity-1 (YL-1), developed by the private Chinese aerospace company Orienspace, successfully deployed three Yunyao-1 meteorological satellites into orbit in its maiden flight off the coast of Haiyang City, Shandong Province. We also came across a video report of the launch on YouTube . The South China Morning Post highlighted the rocket's capabilities , including a thrust of 600 tonnes and the ability to lift 6.5 tonnes of cargo into near-Earth orbit. The cargo compartment, measuring 4.2 meters in diameter and 9 meters tall, can accommodate decently weighing cargo for China's space station if necessary.

The cargo compartment, measuring 4.2 meters in diameter and 9 meters tall, can accommodate decently weighing cargo for China's space station if necessary.
Similar reports featuring the viral video and details about the Gravity-1 launch can be found here  and here .
There have been no media reports of North Korea attacking a US tanker. Notably, China remains North Korea's primary ally . The development surprisingly coincided with Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party securing a historic third consecutive presidential victory . While China regards Taiwan as a breakaway province , the self-ruled nation, with tacit US support, asserts its distinct sovereign identity.Â
Despite these concurrent events in East Asia's geopolitical landscape, the North Korea missile test and Taiwan's election results are not perceived to be directly related.Â

title: Fact Check: Is this how the Indian Navy trains? Nope, this video is from the US
content:
This video shows underwater training by a US-based group called Deep End Fitness.
A video making rounds on the internet shows a group of men training underwater with their hands and legs tied up. Allegedly, this is an Indian Navy training session.Â

India Today Fact Check found that this video does not show the Indian Navy's training but training conducted by a US-based fitness organisation, Deep End Fitness. OUR PROBEÂ
A simple reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post carrying the same video . title: Fact Check: Gaza aid being dumped? Nope, this video is from 2016
content:
This video is from 2016 and shows Saudi Arabian authorities dumping packs of expired chicken. It has nothing to do with the ongoing conflict in Gaza.
A video making the rounds online purports to show relief aid meant for Gazans being dumped. The clip that shows thousands of packaged boxes being thrown out of trucks in the middle of a desert was allegedly shot in Egypt.Â
Sharing this video, a Facebook user wrote , "The aid allocated to Gaza has expired in Rafah, Egypt, and is in a landfill. While people are dying of hunger in Gaza and the Arabs are unable to bring in aid until it has expired. What a shame." The archive of such a post can be seen  here.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from 2016 and shows Saudi Arabian authorities dumping several packs of expired chicken. Our Probe
We noticed that many people responding to the viral video pointed out that it wasn't from Egypt but from Saudi Arabia, and that it showed expired chicken being dumped.Â
We then searched online using relevant keywords and found several media reports from November 2016, which contained screengrabs of this video.Â
Al Arabiya reported that these boxes containing expired chicken were confiscated from 25 refrigerated trucks before distribution. Around 80,000 packs of expired chicken not fit for human consumption were destroyed as part of an official operation under the supervision of the Secretariat of Saudi Arabia's al-Qassim region.Â
When we reverse-searched screengrabs from the viral video, we found that a longer version of this clip was uploaded to YouTube on November 17, 2016.Â
Thus, it's clear that an old Saudi Arabian video from 2016 was falsely shared as Gaza aid being dumped in Egypt. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jan 16, 2024 22:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Jinping didn't endorse Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra, viral screenshot is fake
content:
The viral screenshot is fake and digitally created. Xi Jinping has made no such comment.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra entered Nagaland on January 15 after spending two days in violence-gripped Manipur. The Congress rally, spanning 6,200 km across 14 states from east to west, is now being dubbed by some as a "Chinese franchise".
