Sharing this screenshot, one person wrote on X: "What did I told you on day one when this yatra first route was published, Arunachal was left out. Congress means Chinese franchise." The archive of one such post can be seen here . India Today, however, found that the viral screenshot was forged. Xi Jinping made no such comment and the Global Times did not report this. Our Probe We checked all social media accounts of Global Times  to look for posts even remotely related to Gandhi or Congress's the Bharat Nyay Jodo Yatra. A perusal of their website also yielded no such report. Further keyword searches on the internet failed to produce any media reports about Xi Jinping's alleged statement. If such a statement had been made, it would have been widely covered by both Chinese and Indian news outlets.
India Today, however, found that the viral screenshot was forged. Xi Jinping made no such comment and the Global Times did not report this.Â
We checked all social media accounts of Global Times  to look for posts even remotely related to Gandhi or Congress's the Bharat Nyay Jodo Yatra. A perusal of their website also yielded no such report.
Further keyword searches on the internet failed to produce any media reports about Xi Jinping's alleged statement. If such a statement had been made, it would have been widely covered by both Chinese and Indian news outlets.
Upon close observation of the viral screenshot, we noted irregularities, including a shredded bottom, uneven borders, stray cutouts of a face, and random objects in Jinping's photo.
Thus, it is evident that a screenshot of a fabricated tweet by a Chinese media portal is being circulated to undermine Gandhi's yatra. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jan 17, 2024 17:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Palestinian girl crying as her home is demolished is over three years old
content:
This video is not from the ongoing conflict. It is from August 2020, when four Palestinian families were forced to destroy their own homes by decree of the Israeli municipality of Jerusalem.
A video  that's been widely shared online purports to show a young Palestinian girl crying because the Israeli army was demolishing her home. Young Palestinian girl cry's as she watches the Israeli army demolish her home… There are over 15,000 demolition orders in Jerusalem alone, in some cases they give the family the choice to demolish their own home, or pay for the demolition…🇵🇸💔 pic.twitter.com/GC2fzXWuCR — Pelham (@Resist_05) January 16, 2024
Young Palestinian girl cry's as she watches the Israeli army demolish her home… There are over 15,000 demolition orders in Jerusalem alone, in some cases they give the family the choice to demolish their own home, or pay for the demolition…🇵🇸💔 pic.twitter.com/GC2fzXWuCR — Pelham (@Resist_05) January 16, 2024
Sharing the video  on X user wrote, "A Palestinian girl cries as Israel demolishes her home in Jerusalem, leaving her and her family homeless. Someone tell me what Israel is 'defending itself'?" The archive of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is more than three years old and unrelated to the ongoing war between Israel and Hamas. Our Probe
A reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip uploaded to several Facebook pages  in August 2020 with similar claims.
While these posts didn't provide any additional details, it is clear that the video had nothing to do with the ongoing conflict that began after a Hamas attack on October 7, 2023.
An advanced search with relevant keywords led us to the same video uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Turkish public broadcaster TRT Arabic  on August 11, 2020. The description of the video stated that a Palestinian cried as she watched her family's home, South of occupied Jerusalem, being destroyed by Israeli occupation forces under the pretext of not having a permit.
On the same day, another version of this video was uploaded to YouTube that stated the house belonged to Ibrahim Saiba.Â
Further searches led to a report from the Middle East Eye  published on August 17, 2020, which stated that the Israeli municipality of Jerusalem had issued new demolition orders against four Palestinian families. Subsequently, families were forced to raze their own homes to avoid costly fines.Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral video is old and unrelated to the ongoing conflict. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Jan 17, 2024 23:35 IST

title: Fact Check: This is NOT Srinagar's Lal Chowk, Lord Ram's photo on clocktower is from Dehradun
content:
This video is from Uttarakhand's Dehradun, not Srinagar.
Ahead of the consecration ceremony in Ayodhya's Ram Mandir, a video allegedly from Jammu and Kashmir'e Srinargar is being widely shared. In the video, a photo of Lord Ram can be seen being projected onto a clock tower. According to those sharing the video, it was shot in Srinagar's Lal Chowk.Â
An X user wrote while sharing the video , "Lal Chowk Srinagar. Beyond fathomable. The Power of your vote to the right Party. Jai Shree Ram." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that this video is from Uttarakhand's Dehradun, not Jammu and Kashmir. Our Probe
Responding to the viral tweet, many people pointed out that this video showed Ghantaghar in Dehradun, Uttarakhand. Subsequently, a search with relevant keywords led us to the Facebook page of Punjab Kesari Uttarakhand, which shared a snippet of the video on January 19, calling the tower Dehradun's Ghantaghar.Â
We also found that Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami also shared a similar video on X on January 14, saying: "Residents listening to Ram Bhajan at Ghantaghar, Dehradun. From today, cultural programs, special puja, kirtan and cleanliness campaigns in temples have started with public participation in the entire state." राममय देवभूमि! घंटाघर, देहरादून में राम भजन सुनते नगरवासी। आज से पूरे प्रदेश में जन सहभागिता से सांस्कृतिक कार्यक्रम, विशेष पूजा, कीर्तन एवं मंदिरों में स्वच्छता अभियान शुरू हो चुका है। pic.twitter.com/0RlQPI6LxC — Pushkar Singh Dhami (@pushkardhami) January 14, 2024 We then compared the images of Dehradun's Ghantaghar  and Lal Chowk, Srinagar with the viral video. This proved without a doubt that the video was shot in Dehradun. We also found several news outlets  reported about how Lord Ram's photo was projected onto the clocktower in Dehradun. It is noteworthy that on January 18, a clock tower in Srinagar's Lal Chowk was illuminated with tricolour lighting ahead of India's Republic Day. The news agency ANI shared a video of this. Journalist Ashraf Wani of Aaj Tak's Srinagar bureau also confirmed that this video was not from the city. He added that photos of Lord Ram had not been projected onto towers there. Thus, it's clear that this video is not from Jammu and Kashmir's Srinagar. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jan 19, 2024 18:48 IST

title: Fact Check: No helicopter crash in Mathura, old photo from Arunachal Pradesh incident viral
content:
This photo is from a 2021 incident in Arunachal Pradesh. No helicopter crash has been reported from Mathura.
A photo of what appears to be a crashed helicopter has been shared by many online. Those sharing it claimed it was an Indian Air Force chopper. Per such posts, Air Marshal Pankaj Mohan Sinha, who allegedly was in the helicopter, died in the crash that happened in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh. BREAKIBG: An Mi-17V5 of the #Indian Air Force carrying the Commander of Western Air Command of IAF, Air Marshal Pankaj Mohan Sinha has crashed near Mathura. His condition remains unknown, and internet services in the area have been suspended. #Iran #Pakistan #ISPR pic.twitter.com/dV0robzGHu — عمران خان (@lmrankhanISP1) January 17, 2024
BREAKIBG: An Mi-17V5 of the #Indian Air Force carrying the Commander of Western Air Command of IAF, Air Marshal Pankaj Mohan Sinha has crashed near Mathura. His condition remains unknown, and internet services in the area have been suspended. #Iran #Pakistan #ISPR pic.twitter.com/dV0robzGHu — عمران خان (@lmrankhanISP1) January 17, 2024
A Facebook user wrote , "BREAKING: An Mi-17V5 of the Indian Air Force carrying the Commander of Western Air Command of IAF, Air Marshal Pankaj Mohan Sinha has crashed near Mathura. His condition remains unknown, and internet services in the area have been suspended," wrote an X user who shared the image." The archive of one such post can be seen here .
India Today found that the picture is from a 2021 crash in Arunachal Pradesh, and no recent crash has been reported in Mathura. OUR PROBE
Upon reverse searching the keyframes of the viral video, we found it in several media reports from November 2021 . A Mi-17 helicopter of the Indian Air Force crash-landed at Rochham helipad in Arunachal Pradesh due to a technical snag, resulting in minor injuries to the pilots and crew members.
Several media reports  confirmed that the helicopter, on a sortie from Hayuliang to Rochham in Anjaw district, experienced rotor damage during the crash landing. All officers and crew members were reported safe. #WATCH video of the Indian Air Force Mi-17 helicopter that crash-landed near a helipad in Eastern Arunachal Pradesh today with two pilots and three crew members. All of them are safe with minor injuries. (Source: a local person) pic.twitter.com/cTUbzZRT3J — ANI (@ANI) November 18, 2021
#WATCH video of the Indian Air Force Mi-17 helicopter that crash-landed near a helipad in Eastern Arunachal Pradesh today with two pilots and three crew members. All of them are safe with minor injuries. (Source: a local person) pic.twitter.com/cTUbzZRT3J — ANI (@ANI) November 18, 2021
A search on the internet for recent helicopter crashes in Mathura yielded no results. Additionally, we scrutinised social media accounts associated with the Air Force and the Ministry of Defence but couldn't find any news about a helicopter crash or internet outage in Mathura. We also found no news reports about the death of Air Marshal Pankaj Mohan Sinha, who assumed the position of Commander-in-Chief of the Indian Air Force's Western Air Command on January 1, 2023.
Thus, it's clear that the viral claim is patently false. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Jan 22, 2024 13:36 IST

title: Fact Check: Not Ram Mandir! Sea of devotees from 2023 Rath Yatra in Odisha
content:
This image dates back to June 2023 and shows the Rath Yatra in Odisha's Puri
Following the consecration ceremony of the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, a photo of a street allegedly jampacked with devotees in the holy city went viral on social media. Tamil Nadu's Bharatiya Janata Party state general secretary Raama Sreenivasan shared the photo on Facebook claiming it was shot at 6 pm on January 22.Â
India Today found that the viral image dates back to June 2023 and shows the Rath Yatra in Odisha's Puri.   OUR PROBE
A quick reverse search of the viral image led us to a Facebook post by Odisha Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik on June 20, 2023. This post contained several photos. These photos, per the CM, were from the 2023 Rath Yatra in Badadanda in Odisha's Puri district. Badadanda is an area close to the famous Jagannath Temple in the state. One of these photos was the viral one.Â
NDTV also used the viral photo in a visual story about the 2023 Jagannath Puri Rath Yatra. Â
India Today's Odisha correspondent Ajay Nath also confirmed that this image was from Odisha's 2023 Rath Yatra, adding, "This place falls in the route of Jagannath Puri Rath Yatra."
Thus, it's clear that this photo is not from Uttar Pradesh's Ayodhya at all. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Jan 24, 2024 16:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Old Hyderabad video of cops arresting people FALSELY linked to Mira Road violence
content:
This 2022 video is from Hyderabad and shows police arresting people protesting against T Raja Singh.
Amid escalating communal tensions in Thane's Mira Road, a video allegedly showing police action in the locality has been widely shared. In the video, a group of policemen in protective gear arresting and assaulting several young men. As per several posts , the young men in the clip allegedly attacked a Hindu rally on January 22. The archive of one such post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this is a Hyderabad video from 2022. It has nothing to do with the recent incidents in Mira Road. OUR PROBE
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook post dated August 26, 2022 , which contained this video. According to the post, the police on the night of August 24, 2022, barged into several homes and dragged out Muslim youth in and around the Shalibanda area in Hyderabad after protests against suspended Bharatiya Janata Party MLA T Raja Singh swelled following derogatory remarks on Prophet Muhammad.Â
In August 2022, Singh was suspended by the BJP and arrested by the state police for allegedly delivering derogatory remarks against Prophet Muhammad in a video posted on social media. This came two months after the BJP suspended its national spokesperson Nupur Sharma and expelled its Delhi leader Naveen Kumar Jindal for their remarks on the Prophet. Then, in October 2023, the BJP revoked his suspension .Â
According to a report by The Siasat Daily , Singh's immediate release on bail on August 23, 2022, enraged many and despite several warnings by the Hyderabad police to stay indoors, angry Muslim youth took to the streets to protest. This led to the arrests.Â
In the viral video, a police vehicle with a license plate beginning with "TS 09" could be seen parked on the road. Motor vehicles registered in Telangana start with "TS", and "TS 09"  is the RTO code of Hyderabad.Â
Thus, it is more than clear to say that this video has nothing to do with the recent communal violence in Thane's Mira Road. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 25, 2024 22:40 IST

title: Fact Check: Staged photo of a person stuck under debris FALSELY linked to Gaza violence
content:
This is a staged photograph that's more than a decade old. It has no links to the current situation in Gaza.
The International Court of Justice on January 26 ordered Israel to do all it could to prevent acts of genocide in Gaza, while not ordering an end to the military offensive. "The court is acutely aware of the extent of the human tragedy that is unfolding in the region and is deeply concerned about the continuing loss of life and human suffering," court President Joan Donoghue said  as the death toll in Gaza surpassed 26,000.Â
Amid this, a photo of a hand sticking out of the rubble was shared by many on social media. Those sharing it linked the visual to the Gaza Strip with hashtags  such as "Gaza stained with blood".Â
India Today Fact Check found that it was a staged photograph with no links to the ongoing situation in Gaza. OUR PROBE
With the help of a reverse search, we found the viral picture on several stock image websites like Dreamstime  and Shutterstock . According to the description, this was a staged photo showing a dead man's hand sticking out of demolished concrete rubble debris after a catastrophic earthquake.Â
Apart from the viral picture, we found other similar photos  taken from different angles  of the same hand on these stock image websites, reiterating that the photo was staged. These photos were credited to Olivier Le Queinec, a stock photographer based in Maine in the US.
We then found the viral photo shared on the website of Olivier , uploaded in the category of "Earthquake photographs". The site noted that this was a staged photograph. It is noteworthy that the photo was shared on the website back on April 27, 2012. Other than that, a similar black-and-white photograph of the hand was also available for sale .Â
Thus, it is clear that a staged photograph was falsely linked to Gaza. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Jan 29, 2024 13:45 IST

title: Fact Check: These students were suspended for Islamophobic slogans, not for 'Jai Shri Ram' chants
content:
Administrative action at PSIT came after students of the college allegedly chanted Islamophobic slogans.
Tensions flared across the country after the consecration ceremony of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, leading to communal clashes in several cities. Amid these sporadic incidents, a video  of a man allegedly rebuking a student for chanting "Jai Shri Ram" and celebrating the Ram Mandir consecration in a college was widely shared. A ram bhakt student threatened to be expelled from PSIT kanpur by chief DRUNKEN SMITH [Rice Bag] & manpreet dhillon for just raising jai shri ram slogans in the college. They were celebrating pran pratishtha of bhagwaan Ram Lalla. Please look into this matter @myogiadityanath … pic.twitter.com/lr7Ad3sB9O — Kapil (@kapz30) January 25, 2024
A ram bhakt student threatened to be expelled from PSIT kanpur by chief DRUNKEN SMITH [Rice Bag] & manpreet dhillon for just raising jai shri ram slogans in the college. They were celebrating pran pratishtha of bhagwaan Ram Lalla. Please look into this matter @myogiadityanath … pic.twitter.com/lr7Ad3sB9O — Kapil (@kapz30) January 25, 2024
Social media users claimed that the incident occurred at Pranveer Singh Institute of Technology (PSIT), a private engineering college in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh. A Facebook user sharing the viral video wrote, "A Ram bhakt student threatened to be expelled from PSIT Kanpur by Chief DRUNKEN SMITH [Rice Bag] & Manpreet Dhillon for just raising Jai Shri Ram slogans in the college. They were celebrating Pran Pratishtha of Bhagwaan Ram Lalla." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today found that while students chanted "Jai Shri Ram", they also shouted derogatory slogans against Muslims, a video of which has also been widely shared on social media. The police have registered a case against the students involved.
A keyword search on social media led us to several posts  from January 22, the day of the Ram Mandir consecration. These posts contained a video , seemingly from a hostel, where a popular Hindutva pop song "Bharat ka Bachha Bachcha" was being played loudly, accompanied by Islamophobic chants made by students in the background. #Kanpur : Students at PSIT( Pranveer Singh Institute of Technology) Kanpur alleged involved in hutling abuses at Allah while chanting Jai Sri Ram slogans in boys hostel. Muslim students expressed discomfort as no action against the miscreants was taken following the incidence. pic.twitter.com/bn3CqhWMlm — Saba Khan (@ItsKhan_Saba) January 22, 2024
#Kanpur : Students at PSIT( Pranveer Singh Institute of Technology) Kanpur alleged involved in hutling abuses at Allah while chanting Jai Sri Ram slogans in boys hostel. Muslim students expressed discomfort as no action against the miscreants was taken following the incidence. pic.twitter.com/bn3CqhWMlm — Saba Khan (@ItsKhan_Saba) January 22, 2024
Reports from January 22 confirmed that the police took cognisance of the video , and subsequently, a case was filed against unknown individuals. The college administration also suspended some students.Â
The hostel warden's reprimand, as seen in a viral video , was also mentioned in the reports. ETV Bharat quoted the police stating that culprits were being identified after a case was registered against unknown individuals for making objectionable slogans against a particular religion.
To verify if it was indeed PSIT college, we compared the viral video of the warden reprimanding students and the one featuring students chanting slogans with videos of the boys' hostel at PSIT available on YouTube . Upon comparison, it became evident that both videos were from the same college.Â
Thus, it is evident that the students faced repercussions not for shouting "Jai Shri Ram" but for making objectionable slogans against Muslims. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Jan 29, 2024 15:13 IST

title: Fact Check: Convoy heading towards Texas for border control? No, this video is from 2022
content:
This video is from March 2022 and shows a protest called "People's Convoy", whose participants were demanding the withdrawal of Covid-19 restrictions.
Tensions at the US-Mexico border escalated following a Supreme Court ruling favouring the Joe Biden administration's decision to cut razor wire to control migrant movement. A standoff emerged as Texas Governor Greg Abbott insisted on adding more wires, leading to a confrontation between federal authorities and the Texas National Guard.
Amid this, a video of a convoy of trucks on a freeway accompanied by people waving American flags began making rounds on social media. Allegedly, the video showed Americans heading towards the Texas border to stop illegal immigration. Wow Americans have had enough!!!!! Patriots, farmers, truckers & more, are all heading to the Southern border to assist the #Texas Armed Guard against the continued Invasion of America. #texasbordercrisis #TexasNationalGuard #TexasBorder pic.twitter.com/nvbGaCZCtD — WorldNews (@RichKidsClips) January 27, 2024
Wow Americans have had enough!!!!! Patriots, farmers, truckers & more, are all heading to the Southern border to assist the #Texas Armed Guard against the continued Invasion of America. #texasbordercrisis #TexasNationalGuard #TexasBorder pic.twitter.com/nvbGaCZCtD — WorldNews (@RichKidsClips) January 27, 2024
"Wow, Well done, Americans have had enough unity against the illegal immigrants! Patriots, farmers, truckers and more, are all heading to the Southern border to assist the Texas Armed Guard against the continued Invasion of America. They have finally realised the Biden administration is actively working against the country," proclaimed such posts  shared on X and Facebook. The archive of such a post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video is nearly two years old and unrelated to the proceedings in Texas by any means. Our ProbeÂ
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a report from Business Insider published on March 21, 2022. The article that featured screenshots from the video in question was about a cyclist who impeded a truck convoy in Washington DC, causing it to move at a snail's pace. Reportedly, the convoy drove from Adelanto, California, to Washington DC, to protest against pandemic restrictions. Taking a clue from that, an advanced search with relevant keywords led us to news reports from The Guardian and India Today . Published in March 2022, these reports mentioned that the "People's Convoy" was organised in the US capital with thousands of trucks and recreational vehicles with a demand to end all the Covid-19 restrictions.Â
Taking a clue from that, an advanced search with relevant keywords led us to news reports from The Guardian and India Today . Published in March 2022, these reports mentioned that the "People's Convoy" was organised in the US capital with thousands of trucks and recreational vehicles with a demand to end all the Covid-19 restrictions.Â
We also found the extended version of the video uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Insider News on March 4, 2022, making it evident that the video is unrelated to the recent developments along the Texas border. Â
The description of the video reads, "A convoy of truck drivers is making its way from Adelanto, California all the way to the US capitol to express outrage over Covid restrictions. Huge crowds of supporters are cheering them on along the way."Â
Therefore, it is clear that a nearly two-year-old video was falsely shared as a recent protest by Americans against the migrant movement at the US-Mexico border. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Jan 29, 2024 15:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral Video falsely links old incident to recent Houthi missile attack on ship
content:
The video is unrelated to the Houthi attack. It's a 2019 video of a ship on fire off the coast of Sharjah in the UAE.
On January 26, Yemeni Houthi militants reportedly struck Bermuda-owned M/V Marlin Luanda with an anti-ship ballistic missile in the Gulf of Aden. According to an Indian Navy spokesperson, the INS Visakhapatnam, a guided missile destroyer, responded to a distress call from the vessel that had 22 Indian and one Bangladeshi crew onboard.Â
Now, a video going viral on social media claims to show the visuals of the strike. The post claimed: "First Visual of the British oil tanker hit by a missile launched by Yemen's Houthis Terrorist." An archive of the post can be seen here . Update🚨 UK🇬🇧 Yemen🇾🇪 First Visual of the British oil tanker hit by a missile launched by Yemen's Houthis Terrorist . pic.twitter.com/9FmXNTRTsg — Izlamic Terrorist (@raviagrawal3) January 26, 2024
Update🚨 UK🇬🇧 Yemen🇾🇪 First Visual of the British oil tanker hit by a missile launched by Yemen's Houthis Terrorist . pic.twitter.com/9FmXNTRTsg — Izlamic Terrorist (@raviagrawal3) January 26, 2024
India Today found that the viral video is four years old and shows a vessel on fire off Al Khan beach in Sharjah. Our Probe
While conducting a reverse search on the keyframes of the viral video, we came across a report from Gulf Today dated September 4 , 2019, which featured grabs from the same video. Per the report, a fire broke out in a vessel in the sea off Al Khan beach in Sharjah, UAE, destroying 104 vehicles onboard.Â
Another report added that the Sharjah Civil Defense Department extinguished the fire and that no one was injured. You can read other reports about the incident here  and here .
According to the US Central Command, M/V Marlin Luanda, the ship that was struck, was Marshall Islands -flagged and Bermuda-owned, and it was transporting for commercial use a cargo of Naphtha, a highly flammable liquid hydrogen mixture.
Thus, it's clear that the viral clip doesn't show a recent Houthi attack. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jan 29, 2024 17:04 IST

title: Fact Check: French farmers use tractors against police? Nope, this video is from 2015
content:
This video is more than eight years old and from Belgium.
As French farmers continue to protest, seeking better remuneration for their produce and protection against cheap imports, a video of tractors pushing a law enforcement vehicle and tractors dispersing straw into the air is being widely shared.
An X user wrote , "Farmers continue to resist, French Farmers Tractor pushes armoured vehicle out of the way then they spray fertiliser on Macron's thugs. Support your farmers." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video is more than eight years old from Brussels in Belgium, not France. Our Probe
A reverse search on the viral video's screengrab led us to the official YouTube channel of elDiarios, an online newspaper based in Spain. The longer version of this video was uploaded to the channel on September 7, 2015. The video's title suggested that this was a protest in Brussels, Belgium.
We then reverse-searched the other part of the viral video, where a tractor can be seen dispersing straw at the police. We found that the video was published on September 7, 2015, by the official YouTube handle of the Associated Press. As per the video report, protesting farmers used a tractor to "spray straw at police during confrontations at a demonstration in Brussels to demand EU action to counter slumping prices." We then found multiple media reports about the 2015 farmers' clash with police in Brussels during protests against falling dairy prices. As per Al Jazeera's report, thousands of farmers protested, demanding the European Union to counter slumping prices of milk and pork. Thus, it's clear that an eight-year-old video from Belgium was falsely shared as the ongoing French farmers' protest. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Jan 29, 2024 19:23 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Mira Road, video of man vandalising Lord Ram statue is from Ayodhya
content:
This incident happened in Uttar Pradesh's Ayodhya.
A video of a man climbing atop a giant statue of Lord Ram and attempting to vandalise it is going viral on social media. Allegedly, this incident happened in Thane's Mira Road , where communal tensions escalated in the aftermath of the consecration ceremony at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh.Â
Some tagged Mumbai Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and the Mumbai Police on X , inquiring if any action had been taken. The archives of two such posts can be seen here  and here . Â
India Today found that this incident took place in Uttar Pradesh's Ayodhya. Our Probe
We found that several people had also shared the video on social media claiming this happened in Ayodhya, with some also alleging that it was during the Amrit Mahotsav event. A keyword search with relevant keywords led us to a video shared by Hindu spiritual leader Jagadguru Rambhadracharya on his official Facebook page. The idol of Lord Ram in this video was the same as the one in the viral video.Â
We also found a Navbharat Times photo story related to the Amrit Mahotsav published on January 18. This story too featured the same idol. The Amrit Mahotsav was held in Ayodhya  from January 14 to 22 celebrating Jagadguru Rambhadracharya's 75th birthday. The viral video's idol was part of a theme park inspired by the "Ramcharitamanas" at the Mahotsav venue.Â
The Amrit Mahotsav was held in Ayodhya  from January 14 to 22 celebrating Jagadguru Rambhadracharya's 75th birthday. The viral video's idol was part of a theme park inspired by the "Ramcharitamanas" at the Mahotsav venue.Â
This proved that the incident was not from Mira Road in Thane. Eyewitness account
We came across a video shared on Instagram  which showed the vandalism incident, shot from a different angle. It was attributed to the Instagram account "vloggershiva". This account is run by Vaibhav Srivastava based in Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh. Srivastava shared a vlog about the Amrit Mahotsav on his YouTube on January 25. The vlog ends with a longer version of the incident, in which, the miscreant could be seen being thrashed by the attendees.Â
In this video, we also observed several with "UP Police" written on their uniforms. A board with "Ayodhya" written on it was also visible. Â
India Today reached out to Srivastava, who said that this incident happened in his presence and he had captured it on camera. He shared a screenshot of the video's metadata, which confirmed that it was filmed on January 20 in Ayodhya at 9.25 pm. Srivastava shared with India Today another video of this incident in which the man can be seen climbing the idol from behind. Who was the man? Rahul Srivastava, Uttar Pradesh Police's social media cell in-charge, told India Today that the man vandalising the idol in the viral video was Mukhtar Ali Mondal.    He said that on January 20, during the Amrit Mahotsav event, Mukhtar Ali climbed Lord Ram's idol in a drunken state, adding that on January 24, when a person named Nirmal Kumar Pandey tried to explain to him that he shouldn't have done such a thing, Mukhtar Ali said that "he did it knowingly, as he wanted to seek revenge for the destruction of the Babri Masjid." Rahul Srivastava further said that Mukhtar Ali then attacked Pandey with a knife, following which, he was arrested and sent to jail. Thus, it is clear that this incident did not happen in Thane's Mira Road but in Ayodhya.  - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Jan 29, 2024 22:03 IST

title: Fact Check: This is NOT Rajasthan Deputy CM Diya Kumari displaying her sword skills!
content:
The woman in this video is not Diya Kumari but Nikitabaa Rathod, a Gujarat resident.
In a video  that's being shared widely online, Rajasthan's Deputy Chief Minister Diya Kumari is purportedly displaying her skills with the sword.Â
An X user shared the video and wrote, "Diya Kumari - Deputy CM of Rajasthan. She truly represents Bhartiya Naari." The video was also picked up by news outlets like the Navbharat Times , which also identified the woman as Diya Kumari. Â
India Today found that the woman in the video is Nikitabaa Rathod of Gujarat — not the Rajasthan Deputy Chief Minister. Our Probe
Several people reacting to the viral video claimed that  the woman displaying her sword skills was Nikitabaa Rathod. A subsequent keyword search led us to her social media accounts, where she had shared  the viral video on January 22.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Nikitabaa Rathod (@nikitabaa_rathod)
A post shared by Nikitabaa Rathod (@nikitabaa_rathod)
Rathod also shared a similar video on her Facebook account on January 25, where she can be seen wearing the same pink saree. India Today contacted Rathod, who confirmed that she is the woman in the viral video.Â
"This video was recorded by my associates during an event organised in Ahmedabad's Naroda on January 22. Eleven thousand lamps were lit during this event to celebrate the inauguration of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya," she explained. Rathod also sent us a video of her clarification on the viral video, which can be seen below. Hence, it is clear that the woman seen in the video is not Rajasthan's Deputy CM Diya Kumari but Niikitabaa Rathod from Gujarat.  - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 30, 2024 19:40 IST

title: Fact Check: Yemeni Navy targeting US ship? Nope, this is 2020 video from America
content:
This video shows the US Navy warship USS Bonhomme Richard that caught fire in July 2020 off the coast of San Diego.
On January 26, Yemen's Houthi rebels launched a missile at a US warship patrolling the Gulf of Aden. The American ship, USS Carney, reportedly shot down the projectile, which struck a British vessel. Now a video of smoke billowing out of a ship was shared by many on social media. In it, helicopters could be seen flying over the ship, attempting to extinguish flames.Â
An X user wrote while sharing the clip: "Breaking: Video surfaces showing Yemeni Naval Forces targeting US Battleship in Bab Al-Mandab. British media releases footage of the confrontation. The incident marks a significant escalation in Yemen-US tensions." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that this video shows a July 2020 incident off the coast of San Diego in the US. Â OUR PROBE
We noticed that several people reacting to the viral post pointed out that the ship in the video was USS Bonhomme Richard, which caught fire off the coast of San Diego in 2020. A subsequent keyword search led us to the official YouTube channel of the US Navy. The viral video was shared on July 14, 2020, titled "USS Bonhomme Richard (LHD 6) Firefighting Efforts, July 13th Part Three". The US Navy video was much better quality, and the viral clip appeared to be its laterally inverted version.Â
According to the video's description, it showed the Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron (HSC) 3 attempting to extinguish a fire aboard the amphibious assault ship USS Bonhomme Richard (LHD 6). The US Navy stated that on the morning of July 12, 2020, a fire was called in aboard the ship while it was moored pier side at Naval Base San Diego in the US.Â
According to the New York Times , at least 57 people were injured after a fire and explosion broke out on the vessel. Federal investigators reportedly questioned a sailor for suspected arson . However, he was later found not guilty .Â
Notably, this isn't the first time a video of USS Bonhomme Richard was shared in the context of the ongoing Houthi crisis in the Red Sea. You can read India Today's previous fact-check here .Â
It's also worth noting that the Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah, are an armed group that controls most parts of Yemen . This included the capital, Sanaa, some of the western and northern areas close to Saudi Arabia, and the Red Sea coastline. According to the BBC , a significant part of the Yemeni population resides in these areas, and the Houthis run a de facto government that collects taxes and prints money. The internationally-recognised government of Yemen is based in the southern port of Aden. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 30, 2024 19:51 IST

title: Fact Check: Video from political clash in Karachi FALSELY shared as militant attack on Pak forces
content:
This video from a political clash in Karachi has been falsely shared as the Baloch Liberation Army's attack on the Pakistani forces.
On January 29 and 30, the militant group Balochistan Liberation Army targeted Pakistani military and security installations with guns and rockets in the city of Mach, near Balochistan's capital, Quetta.
Reportedly, four security forces and two civilians were killed in the attack and 15 members of the Pakistani security forces were wounded. Interim Balochistan Information Minister Jan Achakzai claimed that seven militants were also killed .Â
Now, a video making rounds on social media shows multiple motor vehicles on fire. An X user wrote , "Local sources claim that multiple Pakistani forces have been killed and wounded in the ongoing major attack in Mach, Bolan. Balochistan." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video does not show Baloch separatists' recent assault on Pakistani forces, but a violent clash between the two political parties in Karachi.Â
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an X post dated January 29, 2024. This video, along with two others, was shared by a Pakistani journalist named Samar Abbas . According to the post, this was a "clash between MQM and PPP workers near Karachi, Nazimabad Inquiry Office" and "one person Faraz, son of Ghafoor, was killed, two injured, and two vehicles were set on fire by angry people". کراچی ناظم آباد انکوائری آفس Ú©Û' قریب ایم کیو ایم اور پیپلز پارٹی Ú©Û' کارکنوں Ú©Û' درمیان تصادم ایک شخص فراز ولد غفور جاں بحق دو زخمی مشتعل افراد Ù†Û' دو گاڑیوں Ú©Ùˆ Ø¢Ú¯ لگا دی #Karachi #Election2024 pic.twitter.com/HVhiYabvkJ — Samar Abbas (@Samarjournalist) January 29, 2024 Subsequent searches with relevant keywords led us to multiple news reports that contain screengrabs from the viral video. As per The Express Tribune , a worker of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) died while a Pakistan People's Party (PPP) worker sustained injuries during a violent clash between members of the two parties on the night of January 28 in Karachi's Nazimabad area. According to locals, the clash occurred when a PPP rally was passing by the area and some attempted to hoist the party flag in front of the MQM-P office. This escalated to physical violence, during which, unidentified individuals set fire to two vehicles. As per the police, the deceased was 44-year-old Faraz Ahmed Qureshi. Thus, it's clear that a video from a political clash in Karachi was falsely shared as the Baloch Liberation Army's attack on the Pakistani forces near Quetta. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jan 31, 2024 15:44 IST

title: Fact Check: 8-year-old video viral as the recent Israeli raid on West Bank hospital
content:
This video dates back to 2015 when Israeli forces raided a hospital in Hebron to capture a Palestinian man accused of stabbing an Israeli person.
Israeli special forces on January 30, dressed as civilians and medical staff, entered Ibn Sina Hospital in the occupied West Bank city of Jenin and killed three Palestinian men. While Israel has claimed the targets were members of Hamas and Islamic Jihad, experts say this raid is a violation of international humanitarian law.
Meanwhile, CCTV footage allegedly showing this raid has gone viral on social media. In the video, a group of people, some armed, can be seen walking through the corridor of a building. Towards the end of the video, we see bloodstains on the floor and curtains.  Â
An X user wrote, "Another video from the action early in the morning in a joint operation by the Shin Bet and the IDF in Ibn Sina Hospital in Jenin that resulted in the elimination of three Hamas terrorists." The archives of two such posts can be seen here and here.   Â
India Today found that the video dates back to 2015 and shows a different undercover operation carried out by Israeli forces.Â
Many people reacting to the viral video claimed that this footage showed a 2015 incident at the Al-Ahli hospital in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron. A keyword search in Arabic led us to the viral video uploaded to the official YouTube channel of EuroNews Arabic on November 13, 2015. As per its description, the video showed Israeli forces killing one man and arresting his cousin for allegedly stabbing an Israeli person on October 25, 2015. This incident happened in a hospital in Hebron. Business Insider published a detailed report about this incident on November 13, 2015.Â
As per its description, the video showed Israeli forces killing one man and arresting his cousin for allegedly stabbing an Israeli person on October 25, 2015. This incident happened in a hospital in Hebron. Business Insider published a detailed report about this incident on November 13, 2015.Â
According to it, Israeli undercover officers dressed as Palestinian civilians raided the Al-Ahli Hospital in Hebron on November 12, 2015. They arrested Azzam Shalaldeh, a Palestinian man accused of stabbing and severely wounding an Israeli man. A man was killed during this raid who was later identified by the hospital staff as Shalaldeh's cousin.Â
Multiple news outlets like The Guardian and CBS News reported this incident and included the viral video in their reports.Â
The actual footage of Israel's recent raid on the Ibn Sina Hospital in Jenin can be seen below.  - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jan 31, 2024 18:06 IST

title: Fact Check: Virat Kohli's mother not sick, Pak accounts spread hoax
content:
Virat Kohli's mother is not unwell. His brother Vikas Kohli debunked the rumours.
The Indian cricket team on January 28 faced a 28-run defeat  against England at the Rajiv Gandhi stadium in Hyderabad. Following the match, several former players and cricket enthusiasts claimed  that the outcome might have been different had Virat Kohli, who withdrew from the first two tests matches in ongoing series citing personal reasons, led India instead of Rohit Sharma.
Despite the absence of a clear reason for Kohli's break, a viral social media post attributed it to his mother's illness. A Facebook user wrote , "Heard Virat's mother is suffering from liver issues and is serious. My strong prayers for his mother's good health. Parents getting ill is the worst pain you will ever feel. Really tough times for Kohli. Prayers with his mother." The post also included a photo of Kohli with his mother. Its archive can be seen here .
India Today, however, found that the viral claim was false. Virat Kohli's brother refuted it. OUR PROBE
We came across several news reports  from January 31 that noted the former Indian captain's brother had addressed rumours about their mother being ill .
Vikas Kohli wrote on his official Instagram account , "Hello everyone I have noticed that there is this fake news about our mom's health been circulating around. Let me clear that our mom is absolutely fit and fine. Also, I would request everyone and also the media, not to spread such news without proper information. Thanks everyone for your concern."     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Vikas Kohli (@vk0681) SOURCE OF RUMOURS
A post shared by Vikas Kohli (@vk0681)
We found that many of the misleading posts appeared to have originated from Pakistan, such as a Facebook page called " Babar Azam Army " that lists its location as Multan, and an X account that claims to be a Pakistani sports journalist . One such post was shared by another Babar Azam fan page called " The Babarians Army ". India Today has previously exposed misinformation campaigns from Pakistan about the Indian cricket team and players, with similar patterns in their dissemination. For instance, we debunked an incorrect statement  attributed to Pakistani cricketers Wasim Akram and Waqar Younis. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jan 31, 2024 23:55 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT TikTok's founder, this amputee is a Chinese motivational speaker
content:
This video does not show the founder of TikTok, but disabled Chinese motivational speaker Chen Zhou.
Is the founder of TikTok, the globally popular video-sharing app, an amputee with no legs? A series of videos making the rounds on social media seem to claim so. The videos feature a man without legs riding a scooter and using what looks like wooden blocks to walk up the stage.
One person shared the video on Facebook writing, "Tiktok Chairman is just like the founder of 99 Speedmart. Both also OKU but so successful. Despite his handicap he still made it to become Chairman of Tiktok. Lessons learnt are 'never to say die when one is not dead'! With determination and sheer grit, We are glad he made it to his pinnacle of success!"Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video does not show the founder of TikTok, but a Chinese motivational speaker Chen Zhou. Our Probe
In one of the keyframes of the video, we noticed text in Mandarin, which loosely translates to: "Inspirational Master Young Singer" and "Famous Chinese Speaker". Using this clue, we performed a keyword search on Google and found an article by China Daily about a disabled motivational speaker, Chen Zhou. The article featured some photos of Zhou, climbing a mountain and doing pushups using his special wooden "shoes". This was the same person seen in the viral video.Â
We then found several media reports about Zhou, a Chinese motivational speaker who uses two wooden boxes as his legs. The 41-year-old was born to a poor family in a village in Shandong province. He lost both of his legs at age 13  when he sneaked onto a train carriage hoping to get to a large city but jumped off after finding it was going the wrong way and was hit by another train.Â
Zhou is now a well-known speaker and gives speeches at stadiums, schools, and hospitals in China. He also appeared as a speaker on TED Talks.
Zhang Yiming founded ByteDance, the company that developed TikTok. He, however, stepped down as the chairman of TikTok owner  and was replaced by Liang Rubo in 2021. Yiming as can be seen in a number of videos of him, is not an amputee. Given below is a comparison between him and the man in the viral video.
It is, thus, clear that an amputee motivational speaker was misidentified as TikTok's founder. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Feb 1, 2024 17:54 IST

title: Fact Check: Nepali cycling contest FALSELY viral as India postmaster exam
content:
This video is not from India at all. It shows the Cycle Plank Balance competition held in Nepal.
Many have shared a video of a man riding a bicycle on a very narrow bridge on a waterbody, claiming that this is how postmasters are selected in India. In the video, people could be seen spectating the event, with a few even inside the water on either side of the track.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video is not from India. It shows the Cycle Plank Balance competition held in Nepal. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to similar videos of the activity shared on multiple YouTube channels . According to the descriptions of these videos , they showed the Cycle Plank Balance competition held in Kapilvastu, a district in the Lumbini province of southern Nepal. Additionally, the national flag of Nepal could be seen on one of the boards in the viral video.
We then found the video in question shared on YouTube in December 2023. This video, per its title and description, showed the second edition of the Cycle Plank Balance competition, organised by the Lions Club of Kapilvastu , a social welfare organisation, at Rajapani, a town in Khotang District of Nepal.Â
Manik Shrestha reportedly won the competition by crossing the 52-meter track in 56 and one-tenth seconds. He was followed by Anis Tamang, Subham Bhattai, and Arun Aryal, who secured second, third, and fourth positions.
 We then found a Vlog  made by one of the people present at the competition. In this, we saw two adjacent banners in the middle of the water body that could also be seen in the viral video, confirming that it is indeed from this competition. A comparison between the two can be seen below.
We then found Nepali media reports  about this competition , which stated that 11-yea-old Manik Shrestha from Butwal, a city in Nepal, won the second edition of the Cycle Plan Balance competition held at Rajapani on the occasion of Vijayadashami.Â
The selection process for India Post Office Recruitment  usually involves a written examination, followed by a personal interview or document verification. The eligibility criteria for all the posts  involve an age limit between 18 and 40 years, a secondary school examination certificate, knowledge of computers, and cycling, among other things.
Thus, it is clear that a competition held in Nepal was falsely shared as an examination for the selection of a postmaster. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Feb 1, 2024 21:59 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Ram Mandir! Viral video of large cash donation is from Rajasthan temple
content:
This video is not from Ayodhya at all. It shows a donation made to the Shri Sanwalia Mandir situated in Chittorgarh, Rajasthan.
A video of a woman donating bundles of cash, allegedly at Ayodhya's Ram Mandir , is making the rounds on social media. The video featured a photo of the Ram Lalla idol placed in the sanctum sanctorum of the temple.
Some claimed that the woman donated Rs 3 lakh to the Ayodhya Ram Mandir. Many replied to one such post , sharing their views about the alleged donation .
India Today Fact Check found that this video is not from Ayodhya at all. It is from Rajasthan's Shri Sanwalia Mandir.
Reverse searching keyframes of the viral video led us to several September 2023 social media posts  featuring the video in question . According to these posts, the video was from Rajasthan's Shri Sanwalia Mandir, where a woman allegedly donated Rs 10 lakh in cash.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by sanwaliya_____seth🚩 (@sethji_kadiwana)
A post shared by sanwaliya_____seth🚩 (@sethji_kadiwana)
We then found a media report about this video, dated September 11, 2023 . According to it, the video was shot at the Shri Sanwalia Seth Prakatya Mandir in the Chittorgarh district of Rajasthan. The woman in the video reportedly donated Rs 10 lakh on Janmashtami, which was celebrated on September 7 that year.Â
We found the video in question shared with the same information on various YouTube channels.  We then compared a better-quality version of the clip with another video from the temple  focussing on the design of the donation box. Their similarities confirmed the viral video's location. The comparison can be seen below. We also contacted Prahlad Soni, the chief executive officer of the Shri Sanwalia Mandir. He confirmed to India Today that the video was from the temple in Mandpiya, Chittorgarh. Soni, however, added that contrary to social media posts and news reports, the woman's donation did not amount to Rs 10 lakh. He said, without revealing the amount, that it was a smaller figure. It is noteworthy that Ayodhya's Ram Mandir reportedly received donations worth a whopping Rs 11 crore in the eleven days following the consecration ceremony. What is clear, however, is that the viral clip isn't from Ayodhya at all. - Ends Published By: Shweta Kumari Published On: Feb 5, 2024 14:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Old Croatian video falsely shared as celebrations in El Salvador after Bukele win
content:
This 2020 video shows the 70th anniversary celebration of Torcida Split, the supporters' group of Croatian football club Hajduk Split.
El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele on February 4 secured a thumping victory in the country's elections. It was speculated that he is going to win a second term after his administration suspended civil liberties to conduct a brutal crackdown on criminal gangs in the South American country which resulted in a fall in the murder rate, once the highest in the world.
On February 4, supporters of Bukele celebrated as fireworks went off in the sky in front of the National Palace after the presidential election in San Salvador. "All together the opposition was pulverized," Bukele told his supporters.
Now, a video of spectacular fireworks, allegedly set off to celebrate Bukele's victory, is being shared online. Sharing the video, an X user wrote, "El Salvador, Fireworks erupt in the streets as President Nayib Bukele is re-elected in a historic landslide." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video shows the anniversary celebrations of Torcida, a fan group of the Croatian football club Hajduk Split.
A reverse image search of screengrabs from the viral video led us to the same clip uploaded to YouTube on October 29, 2020. The video was titled, "Hajduk split 70 years." This means that the actual video predates El Salvador's Presidential elections by more than three years.Â
HNK Hajduk Split is a Croatian professional football club based in the city of Split. We searched about this incident on YouTube and found a video that resembles the viral clip  uploaded to a channel named "KN Torcida Split '' on October 28, 2020. The video's title translates to, "70 years of Torcida/Because of one love."Â
We searched for media reports that covered this incident and found a video report by Yahoo Finance  published in November 2020, which featured photos of similar-looking fireworks. As per the report, Torcida, a famous supporters' group of the Croatian football club Hajduk Split, celebrated its 70th birthday at the stroke of midnight by lighting up the city of Split with flares and fireworks. Thus, it is more than clear that an old video from Croatia was falsely shared as reelection celebrations for El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar.) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Feb 5, 2024 18:51 IST

title: Fact Check: Does this video show Himachal factory fire? No, this clip has been around since 2015
content:
This video has been on the internet since as early as 2015 and reportedly shows a chemical factory fire in China.
A massive fire broke out at NR Aroma, a perfume manufacturing factory in Himachal Pradesh's Baddi on February 2. As per police, of the 85 people present at the factory at the time of the incident, five died. Chander Shekhar, the manager of the company, has been arrested, and the police have dispatched a team to Madhya Pradesh to search for the factory's owner Nilesh Patel.
Now, a video of a massive explosion is being widely shared online with many claiming it's from Himachal Pradesh.Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video is old. It has been on the internet since 2015 and has nothing to do with the recent factory fire in the mountain state. Our Probe
In the comments section of the Instagram post, many pointed out that this video does not show the massive fire that broke out at NR Aroma's manufacturing plant in Baddi.Â
A reverse image search of screengrabs from the viral video led us to the longer version of the same clip uploaded to YouTube on November 19, 2015. The video's title read: "Chinese chemical plant explosion". This proves that the actual video predates the recent factory fire by more than eight years.
Using relevant keywords, we searched for media reports that covered this incident and found the same video clip posted in November 2015 to the website "Military.com", which published news and information about the United States military, veterans, and foreign policy. The article stated that this video showed a chemical plant explosion that took place on November 17, 2015, in the Zhejiang province of China.
A search with both English and Mandarin keywords did not lead us to any credible articles about such an explosion in November 2015. However, we did find several Chinese and international news reports about a chemical factory explosion in the province in September of that year. According to Reuters, there was a blast at a chemical plant in Lishui City shortly before midnight on September 6, 2015.
The Baddi fire incident has been covered by multiple media channels and there exist many videos of the fire captured from different camera angles. We compared the viral video with one of the videos of this incident and found no similarities between them.
So, while India Today could not independently verify the actual location of the viral video, it's more than clear that it has nothing to do with the perfume factory fire in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Feb 6, 2024 18:50 IST

title: Fact Check: This photo of French farmers' protest at the Eiffel Tower is AI-generated
content:
While French farmers' unions are now in the process of halting protests involving tractor blockades a photo showing a Parisian protest scene with tractors and hay heaps near the Eiffel Tower has gone viral on social media.Â
A Facebook user who shared the viral photo wrote, "French farmers by Eiffel Tower yesterday." An archived version of the post can be seen here.
French farmers have been protesting against green rules, taxes, rising costs, and unfair competition from abroad.
India Today found that the viral photo was generated using Artificial Intelligence.
A reverse image search led us to the Instagram user "thetrillionairelife", which shared the photo on February 2 crediting another account, "Ifonly.ai", for creating it using Midjourney, a generative-AI tool.
"Ifonly.ai", a Paris-based Instagram account, explicitly states in its bio that its posts are AI-generated images. In its bio, "Ifonly.ai" credits Midjourney as the tool used to create images. Further, the account posted a story acknowledging how one of its photos went viral with misleading claims. It also shared fact-checks by Forbes and Channel 4 about it. India Today reached out to the account. The person who runs the account said, "Yes, I am the artist who AI-generated the viral picture of farmers/Eiffel Tower. I was inspired by the context in Paris. But I wrote an important disclaimer which wasn't respected." We checked the account and found that the viral post contained the disclaimer: "This series was generated by Al on Midjourney. To prevent any fake news related to the above photos, please specify when sharing that these are not real but Al-generated images." Thus, it's clear that an AI-generated image of the Eiffel Tower is being shared with misleading claims. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Feb 7, 2024 18:57 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of ballot theft from 2022 Karachi by-elections FALSELY shared as recent
content:
This video is from 2022 by-elections in Karachi. It has nothing to do with Pakistan's 2024 general elections.
As Pakistanis cast their votes in the country's general elections on February 8, a video of a person allegedly stealing ballots was widely shared. An X user wrote while sharing the clip, "Breaking News, early in the morning in Karachi, election staff are handing out ballot papers to people of PPP from the windows. Will the Election Commission notice? In Port Pakistan, the election staff is mixed with thieves. PTI keep a special eye on them". Its archive can be seen here.
Former Prime Ministers Shehbaz and Nawaz Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) and Bilawal Bhutto-led Pakistan People's Party (PPP) are the two major parties in this election. Reportedly, members of ex-PM Imran Khan's party Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf have been forced to participate independently after the party was prohibited from using their "cricket bat" election symbol.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video isn't from the 2024 Pakistani general elections. It's two years old. Our Probe
A reverse image search of screengrabs from the viral video led us to the same clip uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Samaa TV, a leading Pakistani news channel, on June 16, 2022. As per the video report, during by-elections for the National Assembly seat of Karachi's NA-240 constituency, a presiding officer was caught stealing ballot papers.
We searched for media reports about this incident and found a video report by Geo News , published in June 2022, which featured the same viral clip. The report said that the incident happened during Karachi's NA-240 constituency elections that were taking place after the seat fell vacant following the death of National Assembly member Muhammad Ali Khan of the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan on April 19, 2022.Â

title: Fact Check: No, Imran Khan DIDN'T vote like this in 2024 Pak polls, this is from his good old days!
content:
The photo is from Pakistan's 2018 by-elections, not the 2024 general elections. Imran Khan voted via postal ballot from Adiala Jail.
As votes were being counted in Pakistan following the general elections, a photo of former Prime Minister Imran Khan casting his ballot was widely shared. Allegedly, this photo of Khan was shot inside the Adiala Jail in Islamabad, where he has been languishing since August 2023. "Imran Khan has cast his vote from Adiala Jail, Constituency NA 47 Islamabad," the caption of such a post.Â
India Today fact check found that the viral photo is from 2018 and shows Khan voting in Islamabad during by-elections in Pakistan. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching the viral photo led us to a 2018 Facebook post on the official page of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf , Khan's party, dated October 14, 2018. It was captioned: "I just cast my vote, we need your support to continue in our mission for Naya Pakistan ... have you cast your vote?"
Using this information, we found a report in the Pakistani daily Dawn , dated October 14, 2018. The report, titled, "In pictures: Pakistan votes in by-elections on 35 constituencies," highlighted that 370 candidates contested in by-elections held in 35 constituencies. The report also featured the viral photo alongside the caption, "Prime Minister Imran Khan casts his vote in Islamabad's NA-53
We also found the same photo in several other news reports from October 2018 , thus, confirming that it's not from the recently held general elections in Pakistan.
Imran Khan and other prominent incarcerated political figures, according to a February 8 Dawn report , cast their votes through a postal ballot from Adiala Jail. Other political leaders who voted by mail reportedly included former foreign minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi, former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Parvez Elahi, Awami Muslim League chief Sheikh Rashid, and former information minister Fawad Chaudhry. Khan's wife Bushra Bibi, however, was unable to vote. According to Dawn, she was convicted and arrested after the completion of the postal voting process. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Feb 9, 2024 23:11 IST

title: Fact Check: Is this Vande Bharat launch schedule real? No, says Indian Railways
content:
This information is misleading. Some of these routes are in the works but there's no news of a February 18 launch as of yet.
Many people on social media shared a list of train routes  and claimed that a series of new Vande Bharat trains will be inaugurated on February 18. These routes include Kolhapur-Mumbai, Patna-Lucknow via Varanasi, Dehradun-Lucknow, Howrah-Varanasi, Indore-Jaipur, and Pune-Secunderabad.
Some websites also shared a picture of a detailed route chart between Howrah and Varanasi.
India Today Fact Check found that this schedule is faulty. The Indian Railways has not announced any Vande Bharat Express which is scheduled to be inaugurated on February 18. OUR PROBE
Howrah Railway station comes under the Howrah Division, which is the oldest Division of the Eastern Railway. We checked the social media accounts of the Eastern Railway to find if there was any truth to the viral claims. On the official X account, we found a February 9 post that declared the route chart for the alleged Howrah-Varanasi Vande Bharat Express fake. Currently, there are a total of four Vande Bharat trains running from or to West Bengal . Fake news pic.twitter.com/76M2t1vhGg — Eastern Railway (@EasternRailway) February 9, 2024
Fake news pic.twitter.com/76M2t1vhGg — Eastern Railway (@EasternRailway) February 9, 2024
 In January 2024, Maharashtra State Railways Minister Raosaheb Danve stated that a Vande Bharat Express service will start soon from Kolhapur to Mumbai but did not mention any specific date. Also, there is a proposal to start Vande Bharat between Patna to Lucknow. However, it is yet to be finalised.Â
Currently, there is only a single Vande Bharat running from Uttarakhand's Dehradun  that goes to the Delhi Anand Vihar station. A Dehradun-Lucknow Vande Bharat is in the works right now.Â
Upon checking the rest of the routes of Indore to Jaipur and Pune to Secunderabad, we found no current Vande Bharat routes between these respective cities. As per reports , however, these projects are also underway.Â
Thus, it is more than clear that the viral claim is misleading. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Feb 10, 2024 16:31 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of policemen giving a befitting reply to mob is NOT from Haldwani
content:
This video shows an incident that happened in Madhya Pradesh's Damoh.
Six people were killed and over 100 injured  in the violence that broke out in Uttrakhand's Haldwani on February 8 over an anti-encroachment drive. As the situation escalated, the authorities imposed a curfew and deployed paramilitary forces to bring the situation under control.Â
Meanwhile, a video allegedly showing a policeman being heckled by a mob has gone viral on social media. In the video, the cop can be seen confronting people standing around him.
An X user shared the video and wrote , "Shoot at site order against peaceful pigs in Haldwani, Uttarakhand. Haldwani Uttarakhand SHO Anand Singh Thakur says 'I came alone. I am standing alone. Touch me.'"
India Today found that this video in question shows an incident which happened in Madhya Pradesh's Damoh district. Our Probe
We noticed that there was text in the viral video that read: "Muslim Mob surrounded police station in Damoh Madhya Pradesh. They threatened to behead four youths in front of the Police. SHO Anand Singh Thakur confronted the mob alone and announced, 'I have come alone. I'm standing alone. Put a hand on me.'"Â
Getting a clue from this, we ran a keyword search and found that the viral video was shared on the official YouTube channel of MP Tak on February 5, 2024. In this version, the cop can be heard saying, "I am standing alone. If you have guts, try to put your hand on me."
As per the MP Tak report, the policeman in the viral video was Anand Singh Thakur, the town inspector of Damoh's Kotwali police station. Navbharat Times published a detailed report about the incident .
According to it, there was a scuffle between a tailor and some people. Following this, hundreds gathered at Damoh's Kotwali police station, created a ruckus, and threatened to chop off the hands of people from the other side. After this, Thakur confronted them and warned them not to use provocative language.Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral video has nothing to do with the violence in Haldwani. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Feb 10, 2024 17:20 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video of Bareilly clashes misidentified as Haldwani violence
content:
The footage shows communal tension in Bareilly after the chief of Ittehad-e-Millat Council, Tauqeer Raza Khan, was detained by the police.
Following the violence in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, where five were killed and over 300 were injured , a video of Muslim men running amidst chaos was widely shared on social media . Allegedly, the footage showed Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi migrants attacking police officers in Haldwani.
India Today found that the video shows agitated followers of Tauqir Raza Khan, the chief of Ittehad-e-Millat Council, in Bareilly. It's not from Haldwani. OUR PROBE
Upon closely observing the viral video, we noted a signboard bearing the name "Sahu Gopinath" in Hindi, which led us to identify the location as Gangapur, Bareilly, using Google Maps . Street View on Google Maps matched the visuals of the viral video. A comparison of the two can be seen below.
With this clue, we conducted further search and came across several news reports  of communal tension and stone-pelting in Bareilly on February 9 following a protest call by Tauqeer Raza Khan. His detention by the police for advocating a protest over the Gyanvapi case led to demonstrations by his followers , resulting in minor clashes and stray incidents of stone-pelting.
On February 8, Khan, the founder of the Ittehad-e-Millat Council, a political party based in Uttar Pradesh, called for a protest against  Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's statements regarding mosques in Varanasi and Mathura.
So, it's clear that while tensions persist in both Haldwani and Bareilly, the viral video circulating does not show Haldwani violence. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Feb 11, 2024 14:56 IST

title: Fact Check: Change in timing owing to clashing Board Exams in Karnataka given FALSE communal spin

The SSLC exam to be held on Friday, March 1, is scheduled in the afternoon instead of 10.15 am like the other exams as the PUC exam will be held in the morning shift that day.
A timetable for the upcoming Class 10 Secondary School Leaving Certificate (SSLC) exams in Karnataka is making the rounds on social media platforms.
Those sharing it, claimed that all exams were scheduled for the morning except the one falling on a Friday to "suit the timings of namaz", accusing the state government of minority appeasement .
One person posted the schedule on X , writing: "Below is the Karnataka State Preparatory Exam timetable of 10th class. Check the Science exam timings. The Science exam falls on Friday. So the timings have changed from the usual 10.15 AM-1.30 PM to 2.00 PM-5.15 PM to suit the namaz timings of the muzzies. Next five years of Karnataka."
India Today Fact Check found that both Class 10 and 12 students have their board exams on March 1, the Friday in question. This is why exams for one group are in the morning and the other is in the afternoon.Â
According to media reports , the Karnataka School Examination and Assessment Board (KSEAB) released the timetable of the Karnataka Secondary School Leaving Certificate Preparatory Exam 2024 on February 2. According to it, exams are set to be conducted from February 26 to March 2 in both morning and evening shifts. The morning shift will be conducted from 10.15 am to 1.15 pm, while the evening shift will be conducted from 2 pm to 5.15 pm.
We then looked for the exam schedule on the official website of KSEAB. At the bottom of the schedule, we found a note that read: "As 2nd PUC Examination-1 will be held on 01.03.2024, some of the Composite PU Colleges & Karnataka Public Schools are examination centers for the PUC examination. Hence Science subject Preparatory Examination of SSI.C is scheduled on 01.03.2024 afternoon session."
We then looked for the schedule of Karnataka's second Pre University (PUC) Exams 2024, which was reportedly issued by the KSEAB on January 17. According to it, the second PUC exams are set to be conducted from March 1 to March 22.Â
It is worth noting, that all of these exams will be held in the morning shift, from 10.15 am to 1.15 pm, three of which will fall on Fridays, dated March 1, March 15, and March 22.Â
The official Twitter account of the Karnataka Congress also wrote about this issue in a post on X on February 5. title: Fact Check: Video of Haldwani girl crying is NOT from recent violence, it's from 2023
content:
This video dates back to January 2023, when residents of Haldwani's Banbhoolpura were protesting an eviction order. The reporter who recorded the video confirmed this to India Today.
Amid the unrest in Uttarakhand's Haldwani, where five people were killed , a video of a young girl crying and requesting Prime Minister Narendra Modi not to demolish her home was widely shared on social media. Allegedly, she made this request following the February 8 violence in the district.
In the video, the girl says in Hindi , "I want to request the prime minister that our houses should not be razed, we have our schools here, how will we study?"     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by MUMBAI TV (@mumbai_tv)
A post shared by MUMBAI TV (@mumbai_tv)
India Today found that while the video is from Haldwani, it dates back to January 2023, thus making it unrelated to the recent violence. The reporter who interviewed the girl confirmed that to India Today. Our Probe
A reverse image search led us to the full video which was posted on Instagram on January 4 , 2023, by Clarion India, a news portal. The viral clip of the girl crying was part of a larger ground report from Uttarakhand's Haldwani by journalist Ghazala Ahmed.
Ahmed too shared the video report, which featured several other people, and the reporter herself, on her Instagram account on the same day . This proves that the viral video predates the recent spate of violence in Haldwani.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Ghazala Ahmad | غزالہ احمد (@ghazalaahmad_) To get more details about the clip, India Today reached out to Ahmed. The Delhi-based reporter said, "I had gone to report from Haldwani on January 2, 2023, where the residents were peacefully protesting against a court order. I was in Banbhoolpura talking to locals when I saw this young girl crying." She said she approached the girl, who then made her request to the PM, as seen in the video.Â

To get more details about the clip, India Today reached out to Ahmed.
