title: Fact Check: Turkey Chalo? This video is not from Delhi farmers' march, it's not even from India
content:
This video has nothing to do with farmers protesting in Delhi. it is from Turkey.
Chaos emerged at the Punjab-Haryana (Shambhu) border on February 13, as police fired rounds of tear gas  at farmers' "Delhi Chalo" march. Farmers have reportedly been attempting to cross multi-layer barricades of concrete blocks, iron nails, and walls of containers at the city's border points using tractors.Â
Now, a video  of a tractor modified with metal grills around it is being widely shared  as one of the tractors being used by the protesting farmers. Zee News also reported that the viral video showed a tractor belonging to farmers protesting in New Delhi.Â
One person shared the video on Facebook , writing: "The so-called farmers making unrealistic demands from the GoI seem fully prepared as if gearing up for a war against the state. These purportedly poor farmers can afford to modify their tractors but also demand pensions and other stuff from the GoI. It's evident that this protest against the Modi government is politically motivated."
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from Turkey. It has nothing to do with the ongoing farmers' protest.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to an Instagram post  from February 1 containing the video in question. The video was shared by the Turkish media outlet  "Ortaköy Haberim".     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Ortaköy Haberim (@ortakoy_haberim)
A post shared by Ortaköy Haberim (@ortakoy_haberim)
Further, we saw the text "HATTAT 260G" written on the body of the tractor. Using this, we found photos of the non-modified version of the same tractor model on the website of Hattat Traktor , a company based in Cerkezkoy, Turkey  that manufactures multi-purpose tractors . We also found multiple YouTubers based in Turkey sharing videos of the same model of tractor. We then found a better-quality version of the same video shared on January 31  by a Turkish person called Emirhan Cengiz on Instagram. The caption in Turkish read: "Original video and owner is mine #agriculture." We found that this account contained multiple videos of this modified tractor model as well as those of other tractors . Further, a Tiktok account with the same username also shared the viral video . We have reached out to this account on Instagram, and the story will be updated as and when they respond.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by @cengizler_tarim_55 In this video, we saw a yellow board at the back of the tractor. The text written on it read: "Celik Aku". This is a battery company also based in Turkey. It's worth noting that there have been several news reports about farmers using modified tractors at the protest. "Tractors have been fitted with hydraulic tools to remove barricades, fire-resistant hard-shell trailers being readied to fight tear gas shells. They have also performed drills with these modified vehicles," the news agency ANI quoted a Central intelligence agency official as saying. advertisement However, it's more than clear that this viral clip does not show the tractors in question. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Feb 13, 2024 18:20 IST

title: Fact Check: This old lady DID NOT scream at protesting farmers, viral video unrelated to Delhi Chalo march
content:
India Today fact check found that the viral video dates back to November 2022 and is unrelated to the farmers' protest. The sit-in was called by petrol pump owners in Patran, Patiala.
Several protesting farmers were detained at the Punjab-Haryana border while attempting to head towards the national capital. Their march embarked from Fatehgarh Sahib after negotiations over legal guarantees for MSP for crops, loan waivers, and other concessions, failed.
Amid public concerns over traffic disruptions, a video  of an elderly woman screaming at protestors in Punjabi has gone viral. An X user shared the video and wrote , "Punjab Public is fed-up with daily blockades. An elderly lady from Punjab breaks down, slams andolanjeevi farmers: 'Your Demand never ends, You want everything for free, The Centre is giving you so much for free'," alongside hashtags related to the "Delhi Chalo" march.
Vishwa Hindu Parishad leader Sadhvi Prachi also shared the viral video with a similar claim.Â
India Today fact check found that the viral video dates back to November 2022 and is unrelated to the farmers' protest. The sit-in was called by petrol pump owners in Patran, Patiala, following a financial dispute and non-clearance of dues.
The woman in the video expressed her discontent with the protestors and questioned the necessity of daily blockades when many of their demands had supposedly been met. She also expressed anger at the inconvenience caused to commuters by such frequent disruptions.
A keyword search led us to Facebook posts from November 2022  which also attributed the woman's outburst to blockades caused by farmers. This proved that the video was not related to the ongoing protests.
In the video, we noticed a bus with a signage reading "Jagdambey". A search of travel companies by this name operating out of Punjab led us to the Facebook account of "Jagdambay Bus Service" . The signage design of the buses listed on this page matched with the bus in the viral video.Â
Subsequently, India Today reached out to Keshav Kinker Singla, the operator of the bus service. He said that the footage showed a protest called by petrol pump owners on November 3, 2022, adding that it was not a farmers' protest.Â
Singla explained that the protest was organised outside a petrol pump that he owns in Patiala. He said he was present during the protest and confirmed that the woman in the video was a passerby who was frustrated by the blockade. He added, however, that a few farmer union leaders who were passing by also sat in solidarity with them.
Further, he shared a video news report , containing statements of the police and agitators, that corroborated the protest's cause — a financial dispute between petrol pump owners and a liquor shop proprietor.
The first stir of the farmers' protest lasted from November 2020 to September 2021, predating the viral incident by almost a year. The second wave of the protest began on February 12, 2014. Thus, it's clear that the viral video has nothing to do with either. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Feb 13, 2024 22:36 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of feud between Hamid Ansari and Mayawati has nothing to do with namaz
content:
While Mayawati called out Ansari in 2012, her comments had no mention of namaz whatsoever.
A video that has been widely shared online purports to show Bahujan Samaj Party supremo Mayawati calling out former Vice President and former Rajya Sabha Chairman Hamid Ansari for repeated adjournments of Parliamentary proceedings every day to offer namaz. In the clip, Mayawati could indeed be seen chiding Ansari for not managing the proceedings and maintaining order in the House post-noon.
Sharing the video on Facebook , one person wrote: "Shocking Revelation. Congress made Hamid Ansari the Vice-President. He was also the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. He used to close the proceedings of the Rajya Sabha every day at 12:00 and go to the mosque to offer namaz and deliver sermons. Fed up with this, Sister Mayawati ji asked him directly, When she was turned down." Vice President Hamid Ansari, nominated by @INCIndia used to leave Rajya Sabha daily at 12:00 to offer prayers. All members sat empty awaiting his return, halting constitutional proceedings. Ms Mayawati raised this issue but Congress didn't support her. And now Congress is… pic.twitter.com/DXOZxDK9ts — Vishnu Vardhan Reddy (@SVishnuReddy) February 10, 2024
Vice President Hamid Ansari, nominated by @INCIndia used to leave Rajya Sabha daily at 12:00 to offer prayers. All members sat empty awaiting his return, halting constitutional proceedings. Ms Mayawati raised this issue but Congress didn't support her. And now Congress is… pic.twitter.com/DXOZxDK9ts — Vishnu Vardhan Reddy (@SVishnuReddy) February 10, 2024
India Today Fact Check found that while Mayawati did call out Ansari for leaving the Parliament at noon every day, her comment had no mention of namaz whatsoever.
With the help of a keyword search, we found that this video is from the 2012 Winter Session of the Parliament when Hamid Ansari was the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha during the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance regime. In this video from December 12, 2012, Mayawati said: "The proceedings are halting every day after 12 o'clock. You are the chairman of the House. You get up at 12 o'clock every day and leave, who will preside over the parliamentary proceedings and ensure that the House remains in order?"Â
In response, Hamid Ansari asked Mayawati to sit down and maintain decorum during the Question Hour. It is worth noting that nowhere in this video did Mayawati mention namaz.
Further, we found that the video in question was shared by the Instagram account of the Bahujan Samaj Party on February 4, 2024. Following this, people on different social media platforms began sharing this video, accusing Ansari and the Congress party of being pro-Islam.
Per media reports from December 2012, Mayawati wished to speak about the issue of reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in government job promotions. However, Parliamentary proceedings were disrupted due to protests from the Samajwadi Party, which infuriated Mayawati. WHAT MAYAWATI SAID ABOUT THIS
The same day, Mayawati spoke about her outburst to the press. She said that Ansari would leave Parliament at noon every day and would then be replaced by the deputy chairman. Due to this, the bill to provide quotas to SCs/STs in government job promotions could not be discussed. She further blamed Ansari and the government for their inability to keep the House in order. WHAT ANSARI SAID ABOUT THIS
Hamid Ansari wrote about this incident in his autobiography "By Many A Happy Accident". According to him, Mayawati expressed regret for her statement the next day. However, the book as well had no mention of namaz.Â
It is thus clear that a misleading communal angle was added to this 12-year-old incident from Parliament. Â - Ends Published By: Aditi Sharma Published On: Feb 13, 2024 23:12 IST

title: Fact Check: Too cool for school? No, this Tripura academy didn't threaten students to get Valentine's dates
content:
This circular was doctored by a student as a prank. However, a Tripura newspaper published it as fact. The school and the local police have refuted this.
Ahead of Valentine's Day, did a school in Tripura threaten its students to find dates for February 14 or face repercussions? This absurd demand appeared to be the subject of a school circular that was shared widely on social media and even published by a local newspaper.Â
On both Facebook  and X , many shared the screenshot of a Bangla newspaper report containing a notice signed by the vice-principal of Saint Arnold's School. It said that students who did not visit school with their romantic partners on February 14 would not be allowed to sit for their board examinations.Â
An X user, sharing the newspaper article's screengrab , wrote: "News coming in from Tripura. A Christian missionary school has released a strange circular regarding Valentine's Day. Saint Arnold's School of Ambassa of Dhalai district directed students to come with partners. If not, 'you will not get a chance to sit for board examination'." News coming in from #Tripura A #Christian #Missionary school has released a strange circular regarding #valentine 's Day. Saint Arnold's School of Ambassa of #Dhalai district, directed students to come with partners. If not, 'you will not get chance to sit for board examination" pic.twitter.com/ixghNL52zo — Omkara (@OmkaraRoots) February 13, 2024
News coming in from #Tripura A #Christian #Missionary school has released a strange circular regarding #valentine 's Day. Saint Arnold's School of Ambassa of #Dhalai district, directed students to come with partners. If not, 'you will not get chance to sit for board examination" pic.twitter.com/ixghNL52zo — Omkara (@OmkaraRoots) February 13, 2024
India Today found that the school, of course, did not issue such a bizarre threat. So, let's look at the chain of events that led to this odd (and false) notice going viral. Â
India Today first contacted Saint Arnold's School in Tripura's Dhalai district. On the condition of anonymity, a senior member of the school administration explained how a prank by a school student blew out of proportion when an Agartala-based Bangla newspaper published a report about it on its front page on February 12.
According to the school administration member, the fake circular came to their notice on February 4. After an internal investigation, the school found a Class 12 student guilty of mischievously editing a school notice and spreading it around. The management member said, "We did not want to spoil the student's educational career. Hence, we just asked him to apologise, which he did." HOW IT BLEW UP
The matter would have ended there. But on February 12, "Tripura Bhabishyat", an Agartala-based Bangla newspaper, published a report about the doctored school notice. The report erroneously claimed that this circular was issued by Saint Arnold's School in Dhalai and that the vice-principal had threatened to not let students sit for board exams if they did not bring their romantic partners to school on Valentine's Day. The report also claimed that when asked about this, the school administration refused to comment.
However, the school administration did issue a rebuttal to these claims in a letter to the newspaper's editor. In a copy of the letter obtained by India Today, school principal Fr. Lourdu Marreddy SVD said, "This is to bring to your notice that the school never issued such a notice and the contents of the notice are totally false, highly objectionable, and evidently in bad taste. The school has never observed Valentine's Day nor does it intend to." Marreddy also asked the newspaper to publish the correct version of events.
India Today reached out to Chandra Roy, the editor of "Tripura Bhabishyat", who told us that they found this notice on social media. She said that since the notice was on the school's letterhead, they believed it to be real.Â
The newspaper retracted the story on February 13, admitting that it had not contacted the school before publishing the report. You can read the retraction here. advertisement POLICE INVOLVEMENT Following the "Tripura Bhabishyat" report, the school also got in touch with the local police. In its letter to the police, the school principal informed that the notice was "false news" and that the school had not issued it. The letter added that the school "mutually found the solution and the student has apologised along with his guardian." The school also affirmed that it did not want to file a police complaint against the student. Image 5 Following that, Dhalai Police on February 12 also issued a statement on its social media accounts , debunking the viral notice. Thus, it is clear that the news of a Tripura school asking students to bring their romantic partners to the campus on February 14 is patently false. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Feb 14, 2024 18:13 IST

title: Fact Check: AI-generated image viral as modified tractors being used in farmers' protests
content:
As the second wave of the farmers' protest began, a photo of vehicles that appeared to be a cross between tractors and tanks was widely shared online. Allegedly, the marching farmers were using these modified tractors in the protests.Â
An X user wrote while sharing the photo : "Just before the election, they want to create hysteria and unrest. Hope this time govt derails their sinister plot by taking stern action against these paid protests which are part of the toolkit." The archive of such a post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that this image is AI-generated. OUR PROBE
Many people shared the screenshot of a February 11 news report titled "Tractors modified to remove barricades, resist tear gas shells will lead Delhi Chalo march by Punjab farmers, intelligence agencies alert police". This screenshot contained the viral image, and the article was credited to ANI.
Using this, we ran a keyword search and found that the viral image was used in an OpIndia report from February 11 with the same headline. The article, however, stated that the image was AI-generated.Â
We also found this report on ANI's website . However, it was published here with a different image. We did not find any report or social media post by ANI which featured the viral image. LOOKING AT THE PHOTO
A close look at the viral photo reveals several clues pointing to it being AI-generated. The colour and texture of the road appear odd. The vehicles on the other side of the road look misshapen. And in one of the tractors, the tracks appear to be wrong.Â
We also ran this image through two detection tools — Sensity AI  and Is it AI . Both tools declared the viral image was AI-generated.Â
It's noteworthy, however, that farmers are reportedly using modified tractors in these protests. "Tractors have been fitted with hydraulic tools to remove barricades, fire-resistant hard-shell trailers being readied to fight tear gas shells. They have also performed drills with these modified vehicles," the news agency ANI quoted a central intelligence agency official as saying.
To sum it up, an AI-generated image of modified tractors is being falsely shared as real.  - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Feb 14, 2024 20:33 IST

title: Fact Check: TN police attacking farmers? Nope, this video shows lathi-charge on BJP workers in Bengal
content:
This video shows West Bengal police assaulting BJP workers in North 24 Parganas.
On February 13, farmers in Tamil Nadu expressed solidarity with the farmer unions participating in the "Delhi Chalo" protests and criticised the police for trying to stop the farmers from entering the national capital.
Following that, a video of police personnel lathi-charging people was shared by many online. Sharing this video, an X user wrote, "Tamil Nadu farmers who stood in solidarity with farmers protest 2024 were brutally beaten by police in Tamil Nadu." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video shows the West Bengal Police assaulting Bharatiya Janata Party workers. OUR PROBE
We noticed the logo of news agency ANI in the video. So, we checked ANI's social media accounts to find out if this happened during the farmers' protest.Â
We found that this viral video was shared on ANI's X account on February 13. As per the post , in West Bengal's North 24 Parganas, police resorted to lathi-charging to disperse protesting BJP workers. We also found this video on The Times of India's X account with the same details .  #WATCH | Police resort to lathi-charge to disperse BJP workers protesting, over the violence in Sandeshkhali, North 24 Parganas. pic.twitter.com/dZ3woybVPs — ANI (@ANI) February 13, 2024
#WATCH | Police resort to lathi-charge to disperse BJP workers protesting, over the violence in Sandeshkhali, North 24 Parganas. pic.twitter.com/dZ3woybVPs — ANI (@ANI) February 13, 2024
 We found multiple reports about this incident published on February 14. As per CNBC-TV18's report , BJP workers and the police clashed in Basirhat in North 24 Parganas on February 13, amid protests over allegations of sexual harassment in Basirhat's Sandeshkhali.Â
Section 144 has been imposed in the area to maintain law and order. Reportedly, women in Sandeshkhali have been protesting for weeks over alleged sexual harassment by Trinamool Congress leader Shajahan Sheikh.Â
In the video, one can see protestors holding BJP flags and Bangla shop signages. People could also be heard speaking in Bangla. We also searched for police lathi-charging farmers in Tamil Nadu and did not find any credible news reports saying that.Â
Thus, it's clear that this video has nothing to do with Tamil Nadu farmers. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Feb 15, 2024 16:14 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of protests supporting Punjabi YouTuber FALSELY shared as 'Delhi Chalo' march
content:
The viral video predates the farmers' protest and shows a gathering in support of Punjabi YouTuber Bhanna Siddhu.
A team of three Union ministers will convene the third round of talks with farmer union leaders in Chandigarh on February 15, following inconclusive outcomes from the two rounds of dialogue. Amidst the persistent standoff between security forces and protesting farmers, a video showing a huge gathering is going viral on social media. The video allegedly shows footage of the ongoing farmers' protest.
The visuals, like shot by a drone, show a sprawling canopy erected at the centre of the gathering. An archive of the viral post can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral post predates the beginning of the farmers' protest. The video shows a gathering organised in support of renowned Punjabi YouTuber Bhanna Sidhu, who was arrested. OUR PROBE
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to several social media posts  containing it, made in the first week of February. Significantly, the farmers' protest began on February 13, several days after these posts were made.
These posts featured hashtags  like "Bhana Sidhu", referring to the popular Punjabi YouTuber, or captions soliciting support for him.
Further, we found videos  matching the visuals  of the viral footage, showing the protest site from various angles. In one such video from January 29, the protest's location was mentioned as Kot Dhunna in the Barnala district of Punjab. Notably, this is Sidhu's hometown.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Tera_____MANI (@gulab_sidhu_0001) Additionally, we came across news reports detailing the protest  in Kot Dhunna, in solidarity with Bhana Sidhu, featuring visuals  similar to the viral video.  WHO IS BHANA SIDHU? Bhana alias Kaka Sidhu, is a social media influencer who boasts over one million followers. His content focuses on rural and youth-centric issues in Punjab. He has also appeared in many Punjabi films and comedy series. Sidhu and his family have ties with the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh. Recently, Sidhu was arrested in connection with an extortion case filed by a female travel agent from Chandigarh. She accused him of coercion, threats, and demanding Rs 10,000 from her. Acting on the complaint, police arrested Sidhu on January 21, leading to protests in his hometown. Thus, it's clear that this video has nothing to do with the ongoing "Delhi Chalo" protest. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Feb 15, 2024 16:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Haryana cop run over by tractor during 'Delhi Chalo' protest? No, this video is from 2023
content:
This video is from August 2023 when a farmer was killed after being run over by a tractor-trolley during a protest in Punjab's Sangroor.
Content warning: The viral video contains disturbing visuals
A shocking video  allegedly showing "Khalistanis" running over a Haryana policeman with tractors during the recent "Delhi Chalo" march was widely shared on social media. The video  showed a tractor running over a man. Meanwhile, a policeman could be seen  sitting on the ground, likely injured, while other cops surrounded the tractor.
The video was shared with captions like, "Khalistani terrorist attacked Haryana police, then after finding out, kept dragging the body for 50 meters. It is clear in the video that a murder conspiracy is going on."Â
India Today found that the video is from August 2023 when a farmer was killed after being run over by a tractor-trolley during a protest in Punjab's Sangroor.Â
Using reverse image search, we found screenshots of the viral video in a Navbharat Times report from August 21, 2023. The report said that clashes erupted between farmers who were planning a protest and the police in Sangroor's Longowal village when farmers tried to block a road and a toll plaza. The clashes led to the death of an old farmer named Preetam Singh who came under the tractor-trolley of a protestor during the disturbance. One policeman also sustained severe injuries in the encounter.
At that time, PTC Punjabi  and the Indian Express  also published the news reports about this incident.Â
Gagandeep Singh, a journalist from Punjab, also tweeted this video on August 21, 2023. His watermark is also somewhat visible in the videos going viral right now, which are of poorer quality. A clash between farmers and the Punjab Police occurred in Sangrur's village Longowal as they were heading towards Chandigarh to participate in a protest. title: Fact Check: Video of Muslim man from Moosewala's funeral FALSELY linked to farmers' protests
content:
The video is from Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala's final prayer ceremony. It has nothing to do with farmers' protests.
Are Muslim men disguising themselves as Sikh farmers to join the ongoing farmers' protest? This allegation is widely shared  alongside a video of a Muslim man taking off his skull cap and in its stead donning a Sikh turban in a large gathering.Â
An X user wrote , "Abdul in the guise of Sikh. That's the reality behind farmer protests 2024 Disgusting!" The word "Abdul" is often used on social media as a euphemism for Muslim men.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala's final prayer ceremony. It is completely unrelated to the ongoing "Delhi Chalo" protests. Our Probe
The viral video contained text written in Gurumukhi. Using Google Lens, we translated it. It reads: "Brother Sidhu Moosewala's final prayer." Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala was murdered on May 29, 2022, near his village in Punjab.Â
A subsequent reverse image search with relevant keywords led us to a Facebook post from June 12, 2022, shared by a page called "Sardarian Trust Punjab". The post contained images of the same man in the viral video. We also noticed a poster of Moosewala in the background, which could be seen in the viral video as well. The post read, "Moosewala's final prayer - Sardariaan Trust put up Turban stall, Both Hindus and Muslims tied turbans." Upon going through Sardarian Trust Punjab's Facebook page, we found the viral video . It was shared on June 10, 2022. Moosewala's final prayer ceremony was held on June 8, 2022, in Punjab's Mansa district, the singer's hometown. Thousands of his fans reportedly gathered for the ceremony . Notably, the same viral video was also widely shared in 2023 during the wrestlers' protest in Delhi with false allegations. India Today Malayalam debunked this at the time. Thus, it's clear that a video from Sidhu Moosewala's final prayer ceremony is being falsely linked to the second wave of the farmers' protests. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Feb 19, 2024 19:46 IST

title: Fact Check: DMK leader beating up cop? Nope, the video from UP shows a BJP councillor
content:
This video is from 2018 and shows a BJP municipal councillor from Meerut beating up a policeman.
A video allegedly showing a Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam MLA beating up a policeman has been widely shared.
On Facebook, the video was captioned , "Tamil Nadu state DMK MLA Mansoor Mohammed beat up a police inspector on duty. This is the hopeless situation of law and order and police in the state of Tamil Nadu. Then, what about the common man?" The archive of such a post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from 2018 and the man beating up the cop is a Bharatiya Janata Party councillor from Meerut in Uttar Pradesh. Our Probe
We performed a reverse search on screengrabs from the viral video and found it shared on the official YouTube channel of Hindustan Times  on October 20, 2018. The report was titled: "BJP corporator thrash Sub Inspector, intimidate lady lawyer in Uttar Pradesh."
As per Hindustan Times, Meerut's Bharatiya Janta Party municipal councillor Munish Chaudhary was arrested on October 20, 2018, for beating up sub-inspector Sukhpal Singh Panwar following an argument over delayed service at Chaudhary's restaurant.Â
ANI UP/Uttarakhand's official X  account also shared the video on the same day. ANI noted that the incident took place on October 19, 2018.Â
We also found multiple October 2018 news reports, featuring screengrabs from the video. As per India Today , the sub-inspector visited the BJP leader's restaurant with a woman lawyer. The woman reportedly got involved in an argument with a waiter about not serving on time. This later turned into the brawl captured in the viral clip. The BJP councillor was arrested by the UP police after the video surfaced online but was soon granted bail . It's noteworthy that some news reports have called the leader "Munish Chaudhary" while others called him "Manish Kumar." In 2019, a video went viral about a Congress MLA beating up a cop. At the time, India Today Fact Check debunked this . - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Feb 19, 2024 20:10 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOESN'T show booze being distributed at farmers' protest 2.0
content:
The video is from the Kaunke Kalan village in Punjab's Ludhiana district, where alcohol is distributed during the Baba Rodu Shah Mela every year. It has nothing to do with the ongoing protests.
Following a new government proposal, farmer leaders have decided to temporarily halt the "Delhi Chalo" march to review the new MSP plan thoroughly.Â
Meanwhile, a video making the rounds on social media purports to show alcohol being distributed to farmers. The video was shared on Facebook with captions like: "On Camera - Emotional Blackmail that we are 'Anndata'. Behind Cameras REALITY- Enjoying  ALCOHOL Daru Langars at 'Protest'."
India Today found that this video is not from the second wave of the farmers' protests. It's an old video from an event in Ludhiana's Kaunke Kalan village where alcohol is traditionally distributed during an annual event at the Baba Rodu Shah Dargah. Our Probe
A reverse search of the viral clip's keyframes led us to a post on X from September 2021 that featured the screenshot of a YouTube video, which appeared similar to the viral clip. The post, which was a response to a now-deleted claim, said: "This video is not related to farmers' protest this is a mela that is organised in a village named Kaunke Kalan. This happens every year. You can search Mela Baba Rodu Shah Ji village Kaunke Kalan and check yourself (an image attached as reference)."Â
Subsequent searches with relevant keywords led us to the Facebook page of "Daily News Punjab", which shared a video on September 7, 2021 . This video too featured scenes similar to the viral clip. According to the video's title, this was from an event at the Baba Rodu Shah Dargah in Punjab.Â
We also found a similar video attributed to the same event shared on YouTube  on September 7, 2021.Â
Upon looking closely, we found a video from September 7, 2021, on the Facebook page "Daily News Punjab". This video too had similar visuals as the viral video and covered the alcohol distribution at the Baba Rodu Shah Ji Mela in Punjab's Kaunke Kalan village.
India Today reached out to Ranjeet Singh Rana, the editor of "Daily News Punjab" and a native of the Kaunke Kalan village where the Baba Rodu Shah Mela is held every year. Rana confirmed that the viral video is from September 2021 and shows the scenes at the Baba Rodu Shah Ji Mela. He said that alcohol distribution happened annually at this event.Â
According to a Dainik Jagran report from September 7, 2021, the Baba Rodu Shah Ji Dargah is situated in Kaunke Kalan village in the Ludhiana district. It is around 50 years old. Here, a fair is organised on September 5 and 6 every year when folk singers sing ditties praising Baba Rodu Shah. The event also includes the traditional offering of alcohol to the saint, which is later distributed among worshippers.
Thus, it is clear that the viral video is not from the farmers' protest but from an annual event in the Kaunke Kalan village of Punjab's Ludhiana district. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Feb 19, 2024 22:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Old, unrelated videos FALSELY linked to Houthi missile attack on British ship
content:
These videos are old and unrelated incidents. One is from 2013 and the other is from Brazil.
Houthi rebels targeted the UK-registered bulk-carrier vessel Rubymar in the Gulf of Aden on February 18. The crew was forced to abandon the ship in the Red Sea after the Yemeni militia group fired two missiles. A Houthi military spokesman said the following day that "the ship was severely damaged, leading to its complete halt… It is now at risk of sinking in the Gulf Aden." Â
Now, two videos of vessels sinking are being shared online with claims that they show the fate of the Rubymar post-Houthi attack. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story THE FIRST VIDEO The first video  shows a ship with a red and black hull gradually submerging in water. A Facebook user, sharing the viral video , wrote, "NEW: Video of the Sinking British ship RubyMar, that was attacked by the Houthis, earlier today." Its archive can be seen here . We conducted a reverse search of keyframes from the viral video and found it in several news reports  and social media posts linking it to the sinking of the M/V Atlantik Confidence in 2013 off the coast of Oman. Allegedly, the ship was intentionally sunk by the crew following instructions from the owner, who orchestrated the incident after setting the engine room ablaze.
The first video  shows a ship with a red and black hull gradually submerging in water. A Facebook user, sharing the viral video , wrote, "NEW: Video of the Sinking British ship RubyMar, that was attacked by the Houthis, earlier today." Its archive can be seen here .
We conducted a reverse search of keyframes from the viral video and found it in several news reports  and social media posts linking it to the sinking of the M/V Atlantik Confidence in 2013 off the coast of Oman. Allegedly, the ship was intentionally sunk by the crew following instructions from the owner, who orchestrated the incident after setting the engine room ablaze.
The ship's owner, Atlantic Maritime Company, was facing a financial crisis and reportedly devised the plan  to sink the ship to claim insurance money. After setting the vessel ablaze, the crew abandoned it, leading to its eventual sinking about 138 miles off the coast of Masirah Island in Oman. Thus, it's clear this video has nothing to do with a Houthi attack.Â
Another video of a vessel sinking was similarly claimed to be the Rubymar. The post claimed: "The British cargo ship Rubymar sinking after it was struck by a Houthis missile today. This is the consequences that everyone told Rishi Sunak there would be. The only solution is de-escalation." Its archive can be seen here .
A reverse search of the keyframes from the clip led us to its extended version on a YouTube channel, where it was uploaded on June 12, 2020. This makes it clear that the video was unrelated to the recent incident.
 The translated caption and description indicated that the vessel was called Steller-Baner and it sank near the state of Maranhao in Brazil. With further searches, we came across multiple reports  from June 2020 that noted that the ship had become unfit and had several safety issues. Eventually, it was decided  that the ship would be scuttled after towing to the middle of the sea.
While there are no recent updates or visuals of the Rubymar following the attack, online vessel trackers last recorded its position  on February 18 at 15.05 UTC. According to United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations , the vessel was at anchor and the crew was evacuated safely. Thus, it's clear that old and unrelated videos of sinking ships are being shared as the Rubymar's fate following a Houthi attack. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Feb 21, 2024 17:43 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT victim of Israel's phosphorous bomb, this woman suffers from rare skin disease
content:
This video shows a woman from Fes, Morocco, suffering from a rare genetic skin disease.
A video of a woman  whose face appeared to be severely burnt has been widely shared on social media as a Palestinian victim of Israel's white phosphorous attacks . Many shared the video  and condemned the United States for being complicit in attacks like these .
Content Warning: This video contains graphic footage. Â
Sharing the video on Facebook , one person wrote, "This woman is a victim of Israel White Phosphorous bomb terrorist attacks. Israel is a malevolent entity."
India Today Fact Check found that this woman is neither from Palestine nor a victim of white phosphorous burns. This woman, a resident of Fes, Morocco, suffers from a rare genetic skin disease. Our Probe
In the viral video, we saw the watermark of the Instagram account "@airisputr8". We then found the viral video shared as a reel  by this account on February 9 without offering any information about the woman in question. In the comments, one person wrote that this was a Moroccan woman suffering from a genetic disease and that the video features the logo of a Moroccan charity organisation called Moonvoice. Using this clue, we found that the viral video was originally shared on February 5 by the Instagram account of Ahmed Zainoun, in collaboration with Moonvoice Association .
Using this clue, we found that the viral video was originally shared on February 5 by the Instagram account of Ahmed Zainoun, in collaboration with Moonvoice Association .
The Moonvoice Association is a Moroccan charity organisation that helps children suffering from Xeroderma Pigmentosum  — a genetic disorder that causes hypersensitivity to ultraviolet light, leaving people prone to eye problems, neurological symptoms, and even skin cancer. Those suffering from this affliction, per reports , are sometimes referred to as "moon children". Ahmed Zainoun is the founder and president of Moonvoice Association , the charity.Â
We found that both accounts had shared several videos of children  suffering from this skin disease , along with more videos of the woman in the viral video . According to the caption of one such post , the woman is Shaima, from Fes, a city in Morocco.
A search for her name and other relevant keywords in Arabic led us to social media videos  and photos of her , shared as early as 2016 and 2017. These mentioned that this Moroccan woman suffered from a skin disease.
India Today reached out to Ahmed Zainoun, who confirmed that the woman in the viral video is Shaima, who suffers from Xeroderma Pigmentosum and is visually impaired. He further added that his organisation, Moonvoice Association, has been trying to help others like her, ever since it was established in 2020.
It is noteworthy that Israel has been accused of using white phosphorous in Gaza . However, the viral video does not have any links to the Israel-Palestine conflict at all. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Feb 22, 2024 13:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of clash over Bhindrawale's poster falsely linked to farmers' protests
content:
This video is not related to the farmers' protests but shows a clash between two groups over Bhindranwale's poster.
As the farmers' protest continues, a video making the rounds on social media purports to show protesters attacking policemen with swords. An X user shared the video  and wrote, "So-called farmer attacking police with swords allowed on them for religious purposes. Are they farmers? Ask yourselves." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video shows a clash between two groups over the removal of Sikh separatist leader Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale's poster at a fair in Punjab in January, weeks before the farmers' protest began. OUR PROBE
In response to the viral post on X, many users pointed out that the incident was not from a farmers' protest but from a clash at a Gurudwara in Punjab's Pahu Wind village on the birth anniversary of Baba Deep Singh, a revered figure in Sikh history.
A search with relevant keywords led us to similar videos  uploaded to Facebook on January 2024. As per the information accompanying these videos , this incident took place in Punjab's Pahu Wind village, where the "pradhan" — a figurehead — was attacked following a dispute over a photo of a "Sikh saint". His car was vandalised.
In these videos, we spotted several similarities, including the number of police personnel at the scene, the attire of the man wielding the sword, and a banner in the background.
We also found multiple media reports featuring screengrabs from the viral video, published on January 29. As per the Hindustan Times , the clash started when the president of the Pahu Wind gurudwara committee, Colonel (Retd.) Harsimran Singh, asked a group of Sikh volunteers to remove a portrait of Sikh separatist leader Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale from the premises of the gurudwara.
Triggered by this, some Sikh youth, who were carrying swords, vandalised Harsimran's vehicle. Policemen there, however, managed to take Harsimran Singh to safety.
In a local television news report, we can see the attack from another angle altogether. In this video as well, one can note several commonalities with the viral clip.
Thus, it's clear that a video of a clash between two groups over Bhindranwale's poster was falsely shared as a scene from the ongoing farmers' protests. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Feb 23, 2024 20:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Farmers cutting a deal for protest? No! Video shows negotiation over tractor
content:
This video has nothing to do with the ongoing protest. The people seen in the viral video were negotiating over a tractor.
A video of turban-clad men aggressively negotiating a deal and exchanging insults is circulating on various social media platforms . Bundles of cash are prominently seen in the viral video. Those sharing it claimed that these men were farmers engaged in a dispute over fees for participating in the ongoing protest.
One person who shared the video on Facebook wrote: "This video exposes these brokers. There is a debate over the fee for occupying space at the border for a month. The person facing the camera demands Rs 40,000, but the broker offering the money insists that Rs 35,000 for a month is sufficient, considering your farming activities and the labourers working on your behalf. If you only intend to sit here, you'll receive food; if you want alcohol, then accept Rs 35,000. This is their reality. Please repost this widely so that the nation understands the true nature of these individuals. Their objective is not to assist farmers but to undermine Modi's popularity, as they have openly stated."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video has nothing to do with the ongoing protest. Instead, the people seen in the viral video were negotiating over the price of a tractor. Our Probe
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a higher-quality version of the viral clip, shared by an Instagram account on January 19 . The caption in Gurmukhi, loosely translated to English, read: "Look at the tractor deal happening." It is worth noting that a few tractors could be seen behind the people in the viral clip as well.
In this better-quality version, two people can be seen seated across from each other at a table and scribbling on a piece of paper. The man on the other side could be heard saying, "We had agreed upon 35 thousand." However, another turban-clad man seated beside him insists on 40 thousand and attempts to leave the negotiations in between. He also can be heard saying, "Look at the tractor as well, it is new." Some onlookers in the background can be seen laughing as they witness the strange deal.
In January, many shared the video in question on social media , indicating that it showed a tractor deal taking place .
A Google search revealed that there are several mandis in Punjab where such tractor deals take place. The largest of these takes place every Wednesday in Talwandi Sabo, a town in the Bathinda district of Punjab. Further, we also found other videos showing aggressive negotiations taking place at this mandi, like the one seen in the viral clip.
We contacted Vicky Dhillon, a farmer from Punjab's Mansa district, who often shares such videos of the Talwandi Sabo Mandi on social media. According to him, the man in the black turban was the seller, while the one in the pink turban was a broker. He added that people negotiating at the Mandi are often just as dramatic , which is why their videos go viral. Vicky also told us that the men can be heard discussing various parts of the tractor in the viral clip.
On searching further, we found that the viral clip was originally posted on an Instagram account on January 17 — almost a month before the farmers' protest began. A comparison between the viral clip and the Instagram post confirms that the caption and the username of the account were cropped out of the viral video. Where did the deal take place? This video was also shared by a Facebook channel called Panj Pani TV . We spoke to its owner, Devkaran, who confirmed that this video is indeed from Talwandi Sabo Tractor market in Bathinda. Devkaran stated, "There are three major tractor markets in Punjab: Patiala, Moga, and Bathinda. By listening to the accent in the viral video it is evident that it is from Bathinda. I have also spoken to people from the Talwandi Sabo market, who confirmed that this video is indeed from there." It is thus clear that an old video of people negotiating over a tractor was falsely associated with the ongoing farmers' protest. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Feb 24, 2024 22:53 IST

title: Fact Check: Did arrival of Kukis turn Manipur hills into Wasteland? No, these images are from Brazil
content:
These images are actually from Brazil, where a couple transformed a barren land into a rainforest with their plantation efforts.
Nearly ten months into the ethnic violence in Manipur, tensions continue to escalate between the Meitei and Kuki communities, exacerbating the crisis.
Amidst this, two images comparing a lush green valley with a barren wasteland are viral on social media. Those sharing these images claimed that the green landscape predated the arrival of the Kuki community in Manipur hills, while the barren one reflected the aftermath of their settlement.
These images also featured texts that read, "Before Kuki arrived Manipur Hills. After Kuki arrived Manipur." An archived version of such posts can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that these images are neither from Manipur nor India. Instead, they show a Brazilian tropical forest planted by a couple.
A reverse image search of the collage led us to a Facebook post from September 1, 2021, featuring both images . According to the post, a Brazilian couple created this forest in Brazil in the early 2000s, a project that spanned nearly 18 years.
Further keyword search led us to a report from Metro UK published on May 4, 2019. The report featured images of a thriving forest and a lush valley while detailing the efforts of Brazilian photojournalist Sebastião Ribeiro Salgado and his wife Lélia to replant a vast plot of land over two decades. Images accompanying the report showed the progress of flourishing forests and valleys resulting from their endeavour. A January 25, 2008, Forbes article highlighted the tree planting initiative called Instituto Terra's Reforestation Project, documenting the progress made over the last eight years of the plantation drive. A June 2019 report by the Daily Mail noted that Salgado and his wife began planting trees in 1998 after discovering the devastation of the tropical forest upon their return to Brazil in 1994. Their laborious efforts transformed the area into a habitat that now supports about 300 species of trees, 170 species of birds, and 45 species of mammals and amphibians. A comparison of the viral images with the actual landscape on Google Earth confirmed their Brazilian origin. Hence, it's evident that a collage of two images from Brazil was falsely attributed to Manipur, perpetuating hostility against the Kuki community. - Ends Published By: Shweta Kumari Published On: Feb 27, 2024 09:40 IST

title: Fact Check: 2-year-old photo of Dhoni at a gurudwara being shared with farmers' stir twist
content:
This is a 2022 photo from Dhoni's visit to London. It has nothing to do with the farmers' protests.
As the farmers' protests entered into its third week, a photo of former Indian cricket team captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni at a gurudwara (a place of worship for Sikhs) went viral. Those sharing it  claimed that the photo was recent, and shot during the ongoing farmers' protests.
An X user shared the photo and wrote, "Mahendra Singh Dhoni didn't go to Ram mandir Pran Prathisthan after being invited but he has visited Gurudwara today during ongoing Farmer's protest. MSD is a man with a spine who is still upholding secular values." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found this photo is from 2022, shot in London, England. OUR PROBE
We performed a reverse search on the viral photo and found that the same photo was uploaded by an X user called Gurpreet Singh Anand on February 26, 2024. According to Anand's bio, he is the president of Khalsa Jatha British Isles , a gurudwara established in London, England, in 1908.Â
In response to the viral post, many X users pointed out that the photo is not recent but from 2022. On Anand's X account, we found a photo similar to the viral one , featuring him with Dhoni, shared on October 1, 2022. The post read: "I met MS Dhoni a couple of months ago at the Gurdwara @khalsajatha in London and noticed he was calm, at one with himself and able to absorb the spiritual moment. It's that inner calmness that gives fortitude in situations which may stress many others out."
We compared this photo and the viral one and noted several similarities, including their attires and the red head-covering Dhoni wore.Â
We also found the viral picture on Anand's Instagram account , shared on July 17, 2022. He captioned the photo: "Bowled over with the legendary @mahi7781." As per the geotag in the Instagram post, the photo was from the Central Gurudwara Khalsa Jatha in London.
We searched for media reports that covered Dhoni's visit to England in 2022 and found many reports of the cricketer roaming the streets of London at the time. As per reports, he also marked his presence in India's second ODI of the series against England at Lord's on July 14, 2022.
We then checked Dhoni's social media accounts and media reports to find out if he had recently visited any gurudwara. We, however, found no credible media reports that could confirm the viral claim. Thus, it's more than clear that a two-year-old picture of Dhoni's visit to a London gurudwara was falsely shared as a recent incident amid the ongoing farmers' protests. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar.) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Feb 28, 2024 19:34 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of half-naked Hamas leader with woman is old, unrelated to current Gaza conflict
content:
The video is from 2021 and predates the ongoing Gaza conflict by over two years.
On February 27, US President Joe Biden indicated that Israel may halt attacks  in Gaza during the Muslim holy month of Ramadan if a hostage-release agreement is reached by then. Amidst hopes of a temporary truce, a video going viral on social media shows a semi-nude man caught in a compromising position with a woman in what appears to be a hotel room. Allegedly, this was a Hamas leader.
Sharing the viral video, an X user wrote , "A Hamas leader with a woman at a hotel while Gaza is burning. He's having a different jihad." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today found that the viral video dates back to 2021 and is not recent. It shows Hamas leader Abdel Rahim Abou Fanah, chairman of Zakat, the fundraising arm of the Palestinian militant organisation, half-naked in the company of a woman. Our Probe
Responding to the viral post, an X user stated  that the video was from 2021. Taking this cue, we ran a keyword search and found several news reports  from June 2021 containing screengrabs of the viral video.Â
According to a report in Global Watch Analysis , Hamas leader Abdel Rahim Abou Fanah, chairman of Zakat, was caught half-naked with a sex worker in an Israeli hotel. A Moroccan news outlet  reported at the time that following the video leak, the Iranian Revolutionary Guard instructed Hamas leaders to remove Abou Fanah.Â
The report cited an official letter from Ismail Qaani, commander of the Quds Force of the Iranian Revolutionary Guard, to Yahya Al-Sinwar, Hamas leader in Gaza, ordering Abou Fanah's immediate removal. A copy of the letter can be seen below.
Similar reports confirming the incident's date and origin can be seen here  and here .
In the aftermath of this scandal in 2021, the Gazan public was dismayed to witness a Hamas leader spending his life in a lavish hotel within Israeli territory. The video elicited strong reactions from the community at that time.
So, while the video does appear to show a Hamas leader in a compromising position, it's clear that it has nothing to do with the ongoing conflict that began on October 7, 2023. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Feb 29, 2024 13:58 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of snow geese frozen over a lake is NOT from China
content:
This video is not from China but from South Dakota in the US.
Around the middle of February, parts of China experienced its harshest cold in more than six decades. According to reports , temperatures dived to negative 52.3 degrees Celsius in China's Xinjiang region around February 18. In its aftermath, a video of hundreds of dead birds lying on a frozen lake was widely shared on social media. Allegedly, the video showed waterfowl that froze to death in a lake in Xinjiang.
A Facebook user wrote : "Large numbers of waterfowl died off due to the temperature suddenly dropped to -52℃ in some regions in Xinjiang, China." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today found that the video shows snow geese found over a frozen lake in South Dakota, US. Our ProbeÂ
Several people reacting to the video on X claimed that this incident was from South Dakota. A subsequent keyword search led us to the video shared on Instagram  by photographer Sean Weaver on February 18. Weaver wrote in the video's caption that it was recorded by his friend Nate in South Dakota.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Sean Weaver (@seanweaverdwc)
A post shared by Sean Weaver (@seanweaverdwc)
The February 18 post's caption also noted: "These birds are from a die-off two months ago. The video was recorded two days ago and was the worst die-off I had seen."
Further searches led us to the publication Outdoor Life  which had reported this incident. The publication spoke to Weaver's friend Nate Phinney, who shot the video. Phinney said that he came across the dead snow geese when he went for ice fishing near a lake in South Dakota. He said: "Usually, those geese would be spread out all over the lake, and you wouldn't see them until spring because they'd be covered up by snow."
He further explained that avian influenza during recent migrations left lots of dead geese scattered across the state, adding, "Except we don't have any snow this year, and the lakes sort of thawed back out in early December, so you get that effect of windrows of dead geese on one side of the lake. It's kind of a shock."
Weaver, on the other hand, told Outdoor Life  that these birds probably died during December and had been stuck in the ice for months. "I recorded several lakes in early December with huge die-offs like this. There were dozens if not hundreds of lakes in eastern South Dakota that had dead snow geese on them in early December," he said.
Previously, both India Today and Aaj Tak had misattributed this video to the cold spell in Xinjiang, China. This error has since been rectified.
Notably, we found no credible news reports about birds flash-freezing in China's Xinjiang region because of the cold weather. Thus, it's clear that this video has nothing to do with China at all. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Mar 1, 2024 14:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Virat-Anushka attending Anant Ambani's pre-wedding? No, this video is from 2022
content:
This video is from June 2022. Both Kohli and Sharma are currently in London and will not attend the pre-wedding.
Anant Ambani and Radhika Merchant's three-day pre-wedding extravaganza in Gujarat's Jamnagar will see celebrities from India and around the world. Singer Rihanna, actor Ranbir Kapoor, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerburg, and cricketer Mahendra Singh Dhoni are some of the big names attending the event.Â
However, one viral video that's caught everyone's attention purports to show Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma allegedly on their way to attend the festivities. Its archive can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found the viral video is from June 2022. Both Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma are currently in London and will not be attending the pre-wedding event. Our Probe
We performed a reverse search on the screengrabs of the viral video and found that a similar video was shared by paparazzo Manav Manglani on his Instagram account on June 8, 2022. He captioned the video, "Beautiful Couple, Virat Kohli, Anushka Sharma at the airport today." In both videos, Sharma could be seen sporting an oversized shirt with denim shorts, and Kohli, a t-shirt with white trousers. We found several other similarities, including Sharma's Christian Dior bag.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Manav Manglani (@manav.manglani)
A post shared by Manav Manglani (@manav.manglani)
We also found several media reports from the same day, about the couple's trip to the airport. As per India Today, "Virat Kohli and Anushka Sharma arrived at Mumbai airport walking hand in hand while their daughter Vamika was missing." On February 20, the couple announced the birth of their second child, Akaay. Reportedly, both Kohli and Sharma have been in London since the birth of their child on February 15. In January, Kohli also withdrew from the Indian test squad for the first two matches against England, citing personal reasons.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by AnushkaSharma1588 (@anushkasharma) India Today's sports editor Vikrant Gupta also confirmed that the couple is currently in London and will not be visiting Jamnagar for the Ambani pre-wedding event. Thus, it's more than clear that this old video was shared with a false claim. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Mar 1, 2024 21:39 IST

title: Fact Check: Old AND photoshopped! This photo doesn't show INDIA rally in Patna
content:
Not only is this photo old — it's from a 2017 rally — it's also been edited to make the crowd bigger.
On March 3, INDIA bloc leaders including the Congress party's Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, the Rashtriya Janata Dal's Tejashwi Yadav, and the Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav converged in Bihar's capital Patna for the Jan Vishwas Maharally. In its aftermath, many shared a photo  of the sea of people who arrived to watch the leaders speak.Â
On X, one person wrote : "Tsunami of crowd at the iconic Gandhi Maidan in Patna. Over 12 lakh people joined the historic rally today."Â
India Today Fact Check found that this photo is old and shows a different Rashtriya Janata Dal rally. it's also been digitally altered to show a bigger crowd. OUR PROBE
A reverse search of the photo led us to a Financial Express photo gallery  from August 27, 2017, titled "Unprecedented gathering at BJP Bhagao, Desh Bachao rally at Gandhi Maidan of Patna? Lalu shares pics". In it, we found the viral photo.
It was captioned, "Lalu Prasad Yadav rally in Patna: In a show of strength against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and a friend turned foe Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, RJD president Lalu Prasad Yadav is holding a rally at iconic Gandhi Maidan today. Prominent oppositions like West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and former Uttar Pradesh CM Akhilesh Yadav were a part of this event. Patna's historic Gandhi Maidan witnessed a historic moment after lakhs of people gathered at the venue."
The caption, however, also noted that "there are several tweets doing the rounds claiming that the image tweeted by RJD chief Lalu was Photoshopped," and that the Financial Express "doesn't vouch for the authenticity of the pictures".
Subsequent searches led us to other articles  about the photo being digitally retouched. India TV's report noted that the news agency ANI first pointed out the discrepancy in the image shared by Lalu Prasad Yadav . ANI also shared other photos  captured "from the same point where Lalu Prasad Yadav's purported picture was taken", noting that "crowd sizes are different". RJD's Patna rally: Picture taken from same point where Lalu Prasad Yadav's purported picture was taken; crowd sizes are different. pic.twitter.com/3QuEsBlQua — ANI (@ANI) August 27, 2017
RJD's Patna rally: Picture taken from same point where Lalu Prasad Yadav's purported picture was taken; crowd sizes are different. pic.twitter.com/3QuEsBlQua — ANI (@ANI) August 27, 2017
Further searches led us to the photo that was digitally edited to make the crowd bigger. It was part of a Jansatta report  on the August 2017 RJD rally. It was also shared on social media by a few people around the same time.Â
A comparison of this photo and the viral one makes it clear that it was indeed edited.Â
Thus, while the recent Patna rally reportedly saw a sizable crowd, it's clear that the viral photo is not just old but also edited. Notably, another photo from the same August 2017 rally has also been shared widely as sights from the Jan Vishwas Maharally. Here's Aaj Tak's fact-check of that. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Mar 4, 2024 18:28 IST

title: Fact Check: German navy missile misfire in Red Sea? This video is 6 years old
content:
This incident occurred on June 21, 2018, during a naval exercise near the coast of Norway.
Recently, a German warship called the Hessen accidentally opened fire on a US military combat drone near the Red sea. However, the drone did not sustain any damage and the incident is now under investigation. Â
Now, a video allegedly showing missiles misfired from a German ship in the Red Sea has gone viral on social media. In it, one can see a large fireball erupting from a ship in the sea, followed by thick smoke.Â
An X user shared the clip and wrote, "The German navy appears unprepared to engage with the Houthis in Yemen as evidenced by the malfunctioning missiles from their frigate exploding in the Red Sea prior to launch."Â
India Today found that this video is neither recent nor from the Red Sea. This clip is from June 21, 2018, and shows a German warship during a naval exercise near the coast of Norway.
We noticed that many people reacting to the video pointed out that this was the German ship Sachsen, which suffered a missile launch failure in 2018. A subsequent keyword search led us to a June 27, 2018, report by the US science and technology magazine Popular Mechanics. This report featured the same video and said that a German warship was damaged in a missile-firing incident off the Norwegian coast. Â
News websites like Newsweek  and Express  also reported this incident in 2018 and carried screenshots from the viral video in their reports.Â
Per Newsweek , this incident took place on June 21, 2018, when a failed missile launch ended up showering one of its frigates, the FGS Sachsen, with sparks and debris. Two sailors were injured in this incident and an investigation was launched to determine the cause of this failure.Â
Thus, it's clear that the video in question is being shared with false claims.   - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Mar 4, 2024 23:25 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT north California blizzard — this is from China!
content:
While there was a blizzard attack in North California, this image dates back to January 2023 and shows the aftermath of an avalanche in China's Xizang (Tibet) region.
Northern California in the United States was hit by a snowstorm  over the weekend. Reportedly, this was the biggest snowstorm of the season (with more snow on the way) and interstate highways remained closed because of the blizzard even on March 4.Â
Now, images of cars buried in heavy snow with passengers inside are circulating on social media, with captions like, "Snowpocalypse in Northern California buries motorists." Many also shared a video of the same incident with similar claims.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the visuals are more than a year old and from China. Revealing the truth beneath the snow
A reverse image search of the viral photo led us to an X post shared on January 19 , 2023. This post featured the viral image but stated that this was an avalanche that occurred on January 17, 2023, in Linzhi to Pai, China. The post mentioned that an accident occurred at the exit of the Duoxiongla Tunnel, resulting in eight deaths. An avalanche occurred on the evening of January 17 on the road from Linzhi to Pai. The accident occurred at the exit of the Duoxiongla Tunnel,8 people have been killed and many are missing.The temperature in Tibet is abnormally high recently, the avalanche may be related to it. pic.twitter.com/ovnBMuW5M6 — Jim yang (@yangyubin1998) January 19, 2023
An avalanche occurred on the evening of January 17 on the road from Linzhi to Pai. The accident occurred at the exit of the Duoxiongla Tunnel,8 people have been killed and many are missing.The temperature in Tibet is abnormally high recently, the avalanche may be related to it. pic.twitter.com/ovnBMuW5M6 — Jim yang (@yangyubin1998) January 19, 2023
This clarified that the images of cars buried under snow are unrelated to the recent North California blizzard.
An advanced search using keywords led us to a Chinese news report dated January 19, 2023, featuring several other images from the incident. According to the report, locals refer to the area where the accident occurred as "Ghost Gate" due to numerous avalanches over the years resulting in casualties.
Global Times, China's state-owned news outlet, covered the incident on January 20 , 2023. According to the report, a total of 28 people were killed after being trapped in the snow in China's Xizang (Tibet) region.
Thus, it is clear that an old and unrelated image was falsely shared as visuals of Northern California's blizzards. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Mar 4, 2024 23:37 IST

title: Fact Check: Woman burns national flag in France? Nope, this clip is from Morocco!
content:
The incident occurred in Morocco in 2023, not in France. It was during a protest against France for supporting Israel.
On February 23, Imam Mahjoub Mahjoubi was expelled  from France's national territory and deported to Tunisia. Mahjoubi had allegedly delivered violent and bigoted sermons that referred to the Jewish people as the enemy, called for "the destruction of Western society", and described the French flag as "satanic" and of "no value with Allah".
Now, a video of a woman burning the French tricolour during a protest is being widely shared. An X user shared the video  and wrote, "Muslim woman BURNS the French flag in France. An Imam who recently called the French flag 'satanic' was deported within 12 hours of his arrest. Should this woman also be immediately deported?" The archive of this post can be seen here .
India Today found that neither did the incident occur in France nor was it recent. The viral video shows a pro-Palestinian protest in Tangier, Morocco, from October 2023. OUR PROBE
We noticed that several people responded to the viral video and claimed that the incident occurred in Morocco, not France. Taking this lead, we conducted a keyword search in Arabic and found the extended version of the viral video in several news reports on YouTube from October 2023.Â
TanjaNews TV, a Morocco-based media platform, shared the viral video  on October 25, 2023, stating it showed the burning of the French flag outside the French consulate in Tangier, Morocco.
We also found another video  of the same woman burning the French flag , also filmed outside the French consulate in Tangier and uploaded on October 25, 2023.  Protestors had reportedly assembled outside the Consulate General of France in Tangier to condemn France's support for Israel in the Israel-Hamas conflict. In the viral video, we observed that the police officers were wearing a badge. On close perusal, we found that it resembled the Moroccan police badge and not French. We also geolocated the site of the protest site on Google Maps , which confirmed that the viral incident occurred outside the French consulate in Tangier, Morocco, and not in France. Thus, it's clear that this video doesn't show a woman in France burning the French flag. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Mar 5, 2024 18:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Don't fall for half-baked lies! Giant castle cake NOT from Ambani pre-wedding
content:
This video has been online since as early as June 2023 and predates Anant Ambani and Radhika Merchant's pre-wedding festivities.
Anant Ambani and Radhika Merchant's three-day pre-wedding celebrations in Jamnagar, Gujarat, ended on March 3. The event's extensive menu was crafted by top chefs and featured more than 2,500 dishes  including Thai, Japanese, Mexican, Parsi, and pan Asian cuisines.
As videos and photos from the mega event flooded social media, one particular clip of a gigantic multi-tiered cake caught the attention of more than eight lakh people. Allegedly, this cake too was part of the extravaganza.Â
India Today Fact Check found that this has been on the internet since as early as June 2023 and therefore predates Anant Ambani and Radhika Merchant's pre-wedding celebrations. OUR PROBE
We performed a reverse search on screengrabs of the viral video. This led us to the same video  uploaded on October 30, 2023, to the official Instagram account of UNILAD, a British Internet media company. The post read: "Looks like something from Hogwarts." The video was credited to TikTok user @fill220812⁠.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by UNILAD (@unilad)
A post shared by UNILAD (@unilad)
We found that this video was uploaded to the same TikTok account on October 21, 2023, and had been viewed over ten million times at the time of writing this. We searched for media reports that covered this occasion and found many reports published in October 2023 about the castle-themed cake. title: Fact Check: New Pak leader slapped in public? NO, this clip is from 2019
content:
This video does not show a recent incident. It is from a public gathering in Pakistan in 2019.
Pakistan's newly formed Parliament elected Shehbaz Sharif as Prime Minister for a second time on March 3Â after a coalition government was formed following national elections that were marred by allegations of large-scale rigging. The declaration was met with loud protests from the Sunni Ittehad Council, a party backed by Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf. Lawmakers reportedly called for Khan's release and continued to protest throughout Sharif's speech.Â
A video of a public gathering is now making the rounds on social media, in which a man shaking hands with people gets slapped. Those sharing the clip, claimed that this was a recent incident where a man expressed his anger against a political leader by slapping him.Â
One person tweeted the video writing , "Spit, slap and stick movement has been started with Lotas. This is just the beginning," along with hashtags such as "Mandate Belongs To Kaptan", referring to Imran Khan, and "Free Leader Of The Nation". Defectors are often colloquially referred to as "lotas" in Pakistan.
India Today Fact Check found that this video does not show a recent incident, it is from 2019.Â
Reverse searching keyframes of the viral video led us to the same video shared on multiple YouTube channels back in April 2019. This made it clear that the video does not show a recent incident.Â
The descriptions of these YouTube videos stated that the clip featured a young man slapping a PTI minister in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province of Pakistan. Some social media posts also added that this young man was unemployed, and hence angry at the minister.Â
News outlet "Al Arabiya Urdu" also shared the video on April 21, 2019, titled in Urdu: "During a ceremony in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the provincial minister was slapped hard by a young man who was angry with the performance of the provincial government."
We then found a 2019 news report about this incident that said the video did not feature a political leader. Quoting officials of the Prime Minister's office, it said that the video showed Afghani refugees getting into a scuffle with locals in the Mohmand Tribal district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
While we could not independently verify the location of the video, it is clear that it does not show a recent outburst of people against political leaders in Pakistan. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Mar 7, 2024 18:25 IST

title: Fact Check: Ironic image of damaged street in front of 'Department of Roads' is NOT from India
content:

A photo of an unpaved waterlogged road allegedly in front of an Indian "Department of Roads" building was filed under irony and shared widely online.Â
An X user wrote , "Department of roads. It happens only in India." Its archive can be seen here .
Many who shared the photo also tagged Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari  on X.Â
India Today Fact Check found that this image is from Nepal, not India.Â
We noticed that many people reacting to the viral image claimed it was from Nepal. Next, we reverse searched it with relevant keywords and found it in a March 4 report published on the Nepali news portal "Bizness News". Per this report, the image was first shared by an X user called Deependra Chaulagai, who shared this photo on March 3 and wrote in Nepali, "Road department sir! The pressure to travel here!" Â
We noticed that several people congratulated Chaulagai saying that the picture he shared had become world famous, to which he replied with the folded hands emoji. सडक विभाग हजुर! दबाब यात्रा यता पो गर्ने की! नजिकै 😂🫢 pic.twitter.com/4hP4URpwK6 — Deependra (DC) (@deependradc) March 3, 2024 On March 4, Chaulagai also shared a press release issued by the Road Division in Kathmandu. Later, in 2023, it was re-shifted to its old building in Babar Mahal, Kathmandu.   According to a report by Nepali news website "ratopati.com" , the contract for the Road Department building's renovation did not include the work of repairing the road in the premises. Another report stated that the road became muddy because of rains . India Today also contacted Nepal-based journalist Nakul Aryal, who confirmed that this photo showed the Road Department compound in Kathmandu's Babarmahal.   He also sent us the latest image and video of the Road Department compound.
