title: Fact Check: Viral video of baseball fans celebrating falsely interpreted as anti-Biden chants in Texas Primary
content:
The video actually shows baseball fans celebrating the Texas Rangers' victory with chants of "Let's Go Rangers" in November 2023.
In the 2024 Texas primary elections, Democratic President Joe Biden secured the nomination, while former Republican President Donald Trump emerged victorious in the Republican primary. These results will set the stage for a high-stakes national showdown in November.
Amidst this political landscape, a video has gone viral that shows a huge crowd chanting slogans. Social media users claimed that a crowd gathered during the recently held primary in Texas chanted expletives directed at President Biden. Wow! Huge crowd in Texas chants FJB. It's over. pic.twitter.com/3YN3n9i7Z6 — PAMELA HENSLEY🇺🇸 (@PamelaHensley22) March 6, 2024
Wow! Huge crowd in Texas chants FJB. It's over. pic.twitter.com/3YN3n9i7Z6 — PAMELA HENSLEY🇺🇸 (@PamelaHensley22) March 6, 2024
An X user while sharing the viral video wrote , "Wow! Huge crowd in Texas chants FJB. It's over." An archived version of the viral post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is old and actually shows baseball fans chanting "Let's Go Rangers" to celebrate their team's victory in Phoenix, Texas.
In response to the viral tweet, a user clarified that the crowd was chanting "Let's Go Rangers" during the World Series parade in Arlington.
Taking this cue, we searched YouTube and found the viral video posted on the YouTube channel of Texas News Hub  on November 4, 2023. The caption accompanying the video read, "Rangers World Series win Parade in Arlington turn out 500 - 700 thousand fans."
On searching further, we found another video posted on the same date . The caption to it read, "Fans chant 'Let's go Rangers!' at World Series parade." The description noted that the video shows the 2023 World Series parade in Arlington, Texas. In the video, an announcer requested the crowd to chant "Let's Go Rangers", to which they obliged.
Upon examination, we observed that the video features the same location and a crowd wearing similar clothes.
We found similar videos shot from different angles  of the event that took place in November 2023 and all describing the chants as "Let's Go Rangers."
News reports from the same date  also corroborated the context of the video , confirming that it is from the Arlington Entertainment District where fans celebrated the Texas Rangers' first World Series championship in franchise history.
Thus, chants of "Let's Go Rangers" during the championship celebrations of the Texas Rangers baseball club were falsely interpreted as the crowd shouting expletives at US President Joe Biden. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Mar 8, 2024 15:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Pakistani market falsely linked to UK goes viral
content:
This video is unrelated to Bradford but instead shows Resham Bazar in Sindh, Pakistan.
A video of a local market scene with women in burqas and Urdu signage outside shops is viral on social media. Many social media users linked this video to increasing immigration in Europe.
One user on X while sharing the video wrote , "The British city of Bradford is completely unrecognizable due to mass immigration. The picture is the same in many other European cities. Mass immigration is absolutely one of the greatest crimes against European people and civilization." An archived version of the post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video has nothing to do with the British city of Bradford; rather it shows Resham Bazaar in Sindh, Pakistan. OUR PROBE
Responding to the viral post , some users believed it to be true and criticised the British government, while others identified  the location as a suburb in Pakistan.
The video opens with a glimpse of a shop named "Sakhi Jewellers". We carried out relevant keyword searches, which led us to an extended version of the viral clip on YouTube , uploaded on Feb 10, 2022. The description of the video clearly states its setting as Resham Bazaar in Hyderabad city of Pakistan. This historic marketplace stretches over two kilometres and is considered one of the longest in Asia. The 400-year-old market extends from Pakka Fort to Market Tower.
The viral segment features in the beginning at the 0:07 minute mark . It features several distinct landmarks that can be seen in other videos  of the Resham market, confirming its Pakistani origin. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Mar 9, 2024 20:20 IST

title: Fact Check: 2023 video from Punjab FALSELY shared as Christian man being attacked in UP
content:
This video is more than a year old and from Sangrur, Punjab. There is no communal angle to the incident.
A video allegedly showing a mob beating up a Christian man with rods in Uttar Pradesh has been widely shared online. A Facebook user wrote , "My dear brothers and sister be aware of what is happening to our fellow Christians in Central India. If you don't pray now, then when will you pray. Heartbreaking sight of anti-evangelicals harassing God's servants in Uttar Pradesh."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is more than a year old and from Sangrur, Punjab. It also doesn't have a communal angle. Our Probe
We performed a reverse search on screengrabs from the viral video. This led us to several news reports published in February 2023. As per the Punjab Kesari, a person identified as Sonu Kumar was attacked by four or five people in Sunam, Punjab. The assailants fled from the spot and the victim was admitted to the hospital.
The report mentioned that Kuldeep Singh, an accused, was subsequently arrested. The other five accused, including a woman, were identified as Mani Singh, Malkit Kaur, Lavi Singh, Amrik Singh, and Gopal Singh, from the Jagatpura village.
According to the Indian Express, on February 19, 2023, Sangrur police arrested one of the six people booked for beating up 37-year-old Sonu Kumar over personal enmity on February 15.Â
Kumar, in his complaint, said that he was travelling with his son Buta Singh to fetch a geyser from his father Gurcharan Singh's house. When they reached Bajigar Basti, Malkit Kaur allegedly gathered people to teach him a lesson, who attacked him using iron rods.Â
We searched about this incident on YouTube and found that multiple local media channels had covered this incident at that time. As per News18 Punjab/Haryana/Himachal's video report , the viral video was dated February 15, 2023. The police reportedly registered a case of attempted murder under Section 307 of the Indian Penal Code.
Thus, it's more than clear that an old incident of personal enmity from Sangrur, Punjab, was falsely shared as a Christian man being attacked by a mob in Uttar Pradesh. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Mar 11, 2024 22:25 IST

title: Fact Check: Big B didn't snub Boman Irani, viral clip clipped out of context
content:
This video is edited. In the full video, Bachchan shook Irani's hand and spoke to him afterwards.
Did Amitabh Bachchan snub fellow actor Boman Irani during a recent event? A video making the rounds online purports to show Big B ignoring Irani as he extended his hand for a shake.
The clip  shows Irani standing in a stadium right in front of Bachchan with his hand out. Bachchan, however, moves ahead to shake hands with Sachin Tendulkar. After this, he could be seen hugging other actors present at the event, namely Akshay Kumar, Ram Charan, and Suriya, and even turning around to look at dancers performing in the stadium.
One person shared this video on Facebook , writing, "Amitabh Bachchan ignored Boman Irani. During an event, Boman Irani looked super excited to meet Amitabh Bachchan, but the superstar did not radiate the same vibe. As Boman waited with his hand out for a handshake, he was ignored in public." Many in the comments, called out Bachchan for this.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video was edited. In the full video, Bachchan shook Irani's hand and spoke with him afterwards.
In the viral video, we noticed "ISPL" written at the boundary of the stadium. Using this clue, we found the full video of this event , uploaded to YouTube on March 6. According to its description, Amitabh Bachchan, Akshay Kumar, Ram Charan, and Suriya were present at an ISPL cricket match.
Per news reports, the Indian Street Premier League  is a T10 tennis ball cricket tournament that was inaugurated on March 6  at the Dadoji Kondadev Stadium in Thane, Maharashtra. There are six teams in this league, all owned by Bollywood actors.
In the full video, Amitabh Bachchan, around the 47-second mark, entered and hugged Akshay Kumar, who then asked him to turn around and look at the people performing. After that, he greeted Akshay Kumar, Ram Charan, and Suriya.Â
Following this, Boman Irani extended his hand to greet Bachchan, who shook Sachin Tendulkar's hand instead. But, within a few seconds, Bachchan shook Irani's hand and hugged him. After that, Irani also interviewed Bachchan  about his ISPL Team, "Majhi Mumbai".
We also found an ANI report  about this event. According to it, the inaugural edition of the Indian Street Premier League kicked off with a star-studded opening ceremony in the presence of Sachin Tendulkar, Amitabh Bachchan, Akshay Kumar, Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor-Khan, Suriya, and Ram Charan, who are also team owners. The six teams are Majhi Mumbai, Srinagar ke Veer, Chennai Singams, Tigers of Kolkata, Falcon Risers Hyderabad, and Bangalore Strikers.
We also found photos  and videos  of the inaugural ceremony, featuring these celebrities, on the Instagram page of ISPL T10.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by ISPL (@ispl_t10)
A post shared by ISPL (@ispl_t10)
It is thus, clear that an edited video was shared to claim that Amitabh Bachchan ignored Boman Irani at an event. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Mar 11, 2024 22:44 IST

title: Fact Check: Pak PM didn't announce CAA for Indian Muslims, viral post is fake!
content:
Shehbaz has not posted such a claim on his social media accounts. The post was created digitally.
The Centre, on March 11, notified the rules for implementing the contentious Citizenship Amendment Act, 2019. Immediately, the announcement was met with both applause and outrage from citizens and political leaders alike.Â
Amid this, a screenshot purportedly showing a post made by Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on X began making the rounds on social media. The alleged post, dated March 11, announced  that Pakistan was coming up with its version of the CAA to expedite citizenship for "persecuted Indian Muslims."Â
It read , "To counter Indian Govt's undemocratic and communal CAA, the Govt of Pakistan has decided to notify Pakistan's own CAA, in which Indian Muslims who feel persecuted in India will be given the citizenship of Pakistan." The archive of one such post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found the viral post was fabricated.
The purported post on X was dated March 11, 2024. We examined Sharif's official X account  but found no activity after March 10. Additionally, a perusal of his account's archived versions on the Wayback Machine only yielded  records up to March 8, 2024. Despite searching his other social media profiles , we found no evidence of such a post .
We tracked the earliest appearance of this screenshot to the X user " The Poll Lady ", who shared it on the night of March 11, writing: "Full support to Pakistan PM." However, the account later shared a post saying , "Only a very bitter individual would propose a community note for this thoughtful tweet," implying that it was intended for satire. However, India Today could not conclude if the viral photo originated from this account. Only a very bitter individual would propose a community note for this thoughtful tweet. 🤣
— The Poll Lady (@ThePollLady) March 12, 2024
Only a very bitter individual would propose a community note for this thoughtful tweet. 🤣
— The Poll Lady (@ThePollLady) March 12, 2024
We searched for media reports to verify if Sharif had made such a statement about Pakistan drafting a CAA-like law. However, our search yielded no credible sources supporting the viral claim. If true, such an announcement would have garnered significant media attention and been reported in both countries.
India Today further reached out to multiple Pakistani journalists. Rai Shahnawaz, a multimedia journalist working with the Islamabad-based Urdu News refuted the screenshot, calling it fake. This story will be updated as and when other reporters respond.Â
Therefore, It's clear that the post attributed to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is not real — it was digitally created. - Ends Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Mar 12, 2024 18:11 IST

title: Fact Check: This isn't from Spain! Old stabbing video from Turkey viral with anti-immigrant spin
content:
