title: Fact Check: Another day, another Mukesh Ambani deepfake selling a get-rich-quick scheme
content:
A video of Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani advising people about a get-rich-quick scheme has been making the rounds on social media. In the video, India's and Asia's richest man can be seen persuading people to follow his "student" Veenit on social media to get free-of-cost investment advice for wealth multiplication.Â
A Facebook user shared the video and wrote, "Benefits are coming! Could 'it' be the next high-growth stock to soar 200%? Get free daily access to high-growth stocks! Hungry for high returns? We provide real-time trading advice and free stock information." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that this video is a deepfake. OUR PROBE
A quick reverse search of the viral video keyframes led us to a December 30, 2022, report by Business Today  that featured a snippet of Mukesh Ambani's speech on the 90th birth anniversary of Reliance India Limited founder Dhirubhai Ambani. As per the report, this video was recorded on December 28, 2022. Â
In the video, Ambani can be seen wearing the same outfits as in the viral clip and standing against the same backdrop. We also found the video of the entire speech which can be seen below. In it, nowhere did Ambani mention his "student" Veenit or any of the contents of the viral clip.   Â
Additionally, in the viral clip, we observed several irregularities in Ambani's lip movement. This made it clear that the 2022 video was digitally altered to create the viral clip. THE CURIOUS CASE OF VEENIT The viral clip featured a photo of the man referred to as Veenit. A reverse image search of the photo led us to a Money Control report  about Nitin Bhasin, the co-head of Institutional Equities, and the head of equity research at Ambit Capital. We noticed that Bhasin's photo was used in the viral clip, but his face had been altered. We didn't find the source of the man's face in the viral clip. Last year, India Today debunked a similar deepfake video featuring Mukesh Ambani.    - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Mar 12, 2024 23:39 IST

title: Fact Check: Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah DIDN'T say that he wished to be reborn as a Muslim
content:
This video is clipped. He attributed this statement to former PM HD Deve Gowda in the full video.
A video of Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah allegedly saying that he wishes to be reborn as a Muslim in his next life is being widely shared online.
An X user shared the short clip and wrote, "If I am born again, I would like to be born as Muslim - Siddaramaiah."  Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that this video has been clipped out of context. The complete video shows him taking a dig at former Prime Minister HD Deve Gowda, claiming that he (Deve Gowda) had once expressed his desire to be reborn as a Muslim. OUR PROBE
Siddaramaiah's statement in the video roughly translates to: "In the event I am reincarnated, I would like to be born as a Muslim." He says it twice in the viral clip.
We noticed the logo of TV9 Kannada in the video. Using this clue, we ran a keyword search and found the longer version of this clip on the news outlet's YouTube channel, uploaded on March 10.
The video's caption stated, "Siddaramaiah: He said that he wants to be reborn as a Muslim. Siddu lashed out on Gowda". This suggests that Siddaramaiah attributed this statement to someone else. This video was from an event held on March 10 in the Mandya district of Karnataka. The complete video of Siddaramaiah's speech can be seen below. The viral clip can be seen at the 18-minute-35-second mark.  The full context of the statement is revealed in the longer video. Siddaramaiah says, "It is quite surprising to me that Mr Gowda has now aligned himself with the BJP and has been expressing admiration for the party. He had once said that he wished to be born as a Muslim in his next birth. He also used to say that he would always oppose the BJP because it is a communal party." Thus, it's clear that the portion of the video in which Siddaramaiah said Deve Gowda's name was removed from the viral video. As per a March 11 report in the Hindustan Times , Siddaramaiah criticised Deve Gowda, saying that he aligned with BJP for the survival of his party. Per the report, he also recalled that Deve Gowda had once said that he wanted to be reincarnated as a Muslim. Reports by ETV Bharat  and The Hindu  also included Siddaramaiah's statement on Deve Gowda's wish of being reborn as a Muslim.  We also did not find any reports corroborating the claim that Siddaramaiah expressed his wish to be reborn as a Muslim. - Ends (With inputs from Sagay Raj in Karnataka) Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Mar 13, 2024 21:38 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Halloween in China VIRAL as evidence of Haiti's cannibalism
content:
The video is from Halloween celebrations in a Chinese amusement park.
Haiti descended into chaos  after Prime Minister Ariel Henry's resignation, with gang leader Jimmy Cherizier, also known as "Barbecue", gaining the spotlight amidst the violence.
Social media was flooded with videos allegedly showing cannibalism  on the streets of Haiti .
One particularly viral video  purportedly shows two human bodies tied to a rotisserie, being barbecued over charcoal. This video was also shared by Donald Trump's supporters, who connected it with the US immigration crisis.
An X user sharing the viral video  wrote, "Hey Libtards! By Letting In Millions Of Undocumented And Unvetted Illegal Immigrants Means Many People LIKE THIS! Are Being Let Into Our Country! Use Damn Common Sense!! We Are Letting Killers, Rapists. Pedophiles and Cannibals Into Our Country!"Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video has no connection to either the US or Haiti. Instead, it shows a Halloween party at a Chinese amusement park. OUR PROBE
In response to one such viral post, an X user identified the location of this clip as the Chimelong Amusement Park in China. A subsequent keyword search led us to the viral video shot from another angle on the Instagram account  named, "Galaxychimelong", uploaded on October 31, 2018.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by galaxy-vladlen (@galaxychimelong) Further searches also led us to a similar video on Facebook, dated October 17, 2018, emphasising its origin at the Chimelong Ocean Kingdom in Zhuhai, China, during Halloween celebrations. In the video, people in eerie costumes and Halloween installations could also be seen. Chimelong Ocean Kingdom  is a theme park situated in Zhuhai, China. It hosts elaborate themed events. We came across many visitor-uploaded photos  that matched the decor as seen in the viral video . Thus, it's clear that an old video of Halloween celebrations in an amusement park in China has been falsely associated with recent developments in Haiti and the US. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Mar 13, 2024 22:13 IST

title: Fact Check: Gayatri Mantra at Pak PM's swearing-in? No, this 2017 clip is from a Holi event in Karachi
content:
Narodha Malni, a Karachi-based singer, recited the Gayatri Mantra at a Holi celebration in 2017 where then PM Nawaz Sharif was present. She confirmed to India Today that the viral claim is untrue.
After a contentious election, amid allegations of fraud, Shehbaz Sharif of the Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz) became the Prime Minister of Pakistan for the second time on March 4.
In its aftermath, a video of a woman reciting the 'Gayatri Mantra' , a Hindu holy chant, was widely shared, with many claiming that this was from the Pakistani PM's swearing-in ceremony. In the video's backdrop , a poster of Pakistan 's founder, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, was visible.
A Facebook user wrote while sharing the video : "Pakistan prime minister's swearing-in ceremony starting with 'Gayatri Maha Mantra' by Smt. Naroda Malini sahiba. Now Pakistan has officially recognised the importance & it's recited in all functions." The archive of this post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is not from the Pakistani PM's swearing-in ceremony. It is from a 2017 Holi celebration where then Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif was present.
We reverse-searched keyframes from the viral video and found the clip shared on X  on March 18, 2017, which read, "Hindu Girl recites highly revered Universal Gayatri Mantra in the presence of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif at Holi Celebrations in Pakistan". Its archive can be seen here .Â
Nawaz Sharif could be seen in both clips, clapping as the Gayatri Mantra recitation ends. This made it clear that the video is not recent but at least seven years old. Using this information, we searched with relevant keywords and found a news report in Pakistan's Dunya News , in which Nawaz Sharif could be seen attending the same event as the viral video. In the video there we observed the Jinnah poster seen in the viral video. It said: "Happy Holi. Warm Welcome to Muhammad Nawaz Sharif (Prime Minister of Pakistan)". According to this report, the event took place on March 14, 2017, in Karachi, on the Hindu occasion of Holi. Nawaz Sharif had joined the festivities. To further corroborate the facts, we contacted the singer Narodha Malni, whose name was mentioned in the viral post, who also introduced herself in the viral clip. Her official Facebook page , which features multiple videos of her performances, mentions that she lives in Karachi, Pakistan. Speaking to India Today, the singer recalled her performance from 2017 when she recited Gayatri Mantra in front of Nawaz Sharif. Talking about the viral claim, Malni said, "The viral claim is fake news and it is an old video from 2017". Malni had previously spoken to the BBC about her Gayatri Mantra performance in a 2017 interview. As per a Dawn report , Nawaz Sharif spoke at the Holi event and said about Pakistan's Hindu community, "A very Happy Holi to everyone. Two years ago, I became yours and you all became mine and today our bond has become even more stronger". It is thus clear that this video doesn't show the Gayatri Mantra being recited at the swearing-in ceremony of the Pakistan Prime Minister. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Mar 14, 2024 19:15 IST

title: Fact Check: Don't fall for this scandalous BBC scoop on Ambani jr! These are just scammers at work
content:
Neither has the BBC published such a report nor has Sharan Hegde interviewed Anant Ambani.
Just days ago, Anant Ambani was dancing, celebrating, and rubbing shoulders with celebrities from across the country and the world. The global press covered the Reliance Industries scion's ostentatious three-day pre-wedding bash. But days later, it would seem that his fortunes have turned.Â
Sensational headlines about how the Bank of India sued Anant Ambani "for his remarks on live television shows" began making the rounds. And you couldn't be blamed for believing them. After all, why would you doubt something like this, if it came from an organisation as prestigious as the BBC?
But just because something looks like the BBC, and feels like the BBC, doesn't mean it is the BBC. For these ' news articles ' merely imitate the British news outlet. Just have a look at them. From the sections to the comments, you can't interact with anything. They're set dressing.Â
These facsimiles of news articles are a dime a dozen. You may have seen similar ones featuring other celebrities or news anchors. Here's another one about Anant Ambani and "what the son of India's richest man has blabbed about". This purports to be a Money Control news report. You can see other similar ones here , here , and here .Â
The BBC of course never published anything like this. Former BBC journalist Jane Wakefield whose byline is in these 'news reports' confirmed to India Today that she never wrote them.Â
So, why do these exist? To scam you, of course. Let's take a look at what's going on then, shall we?
What tales do these lurid headlines tell?
The first thing you notice when you click on such links — often promoted ads on Facebook — is that the URLs don't mention the news outlets they are imitating. The Anant Ambani links, for example, redirect you to ' escapekpom.com '.
In it, you will see a fake article about how CNBC TV18 journalist Anand Narasimhan, during the live broadcast, got into a heated discussion with Anant Ambani, and "called him a liar right in front of thousands of live viewers". But soon, Ambani reportedly convinced Narasimhan to register on a website to earn more money, and like clockwork, the news anchor made a profit.Â
Interestingly, refreshing the page leads you to another fake interview; this one on the photoblog Humans of Bombay, between financial influencer Sharan Hegde and Ambani. This interview also follows a similar script.Â
Of course, Narasimhan's actual interview with Anant Ambani did not go this way at all. It had zero mention of investment platforms. You can see that interview right here .Â
And Sharan Hegde's PR manager Bhavika Valecha confirmed to India Today that he never interviewed Anant Ambani. Additionally, Anupriya Akhade, the group solutions manager at Humans of Bombay, also told us that they have never conducted such a talk.Â
What are these "investment" platforms?
The investment website that Anant Ambani supposedly boasts of in these fake news articles is 'Immediate A8 Alrex'. It's hyperlinked. As soon as you click on the link (and you absolutely never should), you will be redirected to a new page where you are asked to enter your personal details.Â
As soon as you enter this information (which, again, you never should), you'll receive a message that your application has been accepted. However, the next website that pops open may get blocked if you have antivirus software. You receive the warning that this site may potentially steal your passwords, emails, or even credit card details.
Examining the URL of this "investment platform" discloses much. According to DomainTools, 'Immediate A8 Alrex' was created on March 4 — less than two weeks ago. And already, DomainTools reveals, it has been reported 60 times for spamming and 69 times for phishing attempts. Phishing is a form of social engineering, where bad actors try to deceive you into revealing sensitive information or installing malware. It can lead to data mining, financial scams, and often, both.Â
So, it's more than clear that these fake news articles about Anant Ambani are just another way to scam people.Â
India Today has reached out to Meta, enquiring about what steps the tech giant is taking to curb misleading articles like these that are promoted as ads. This story will be updated as and when we receive a response. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Mar 14, 2024 23:04 IST

title: Fact Check: 2022 video of Bharat Jodo Yatra shared as Congress's recent Nashik rally
content:
The video is from December 2022 and shows Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra in Dausa, Rajasthan.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra entered Maharashtra's Nandurbar district  from Gujarat on March 12. Subsequently, there was a Congress rally in Nashik on March 14, which included Maha Vikas Aghadi leaders.Â
Now, a video of a huge crowd allegedly from the Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra in Maharashtra is being shared online. An X user wrote , "Tsunami of the crowd at Rahul Gandhi's Nyay Yatra in Nashik today. Lakhs & lakhs of people are joining his Yatra but media won't show this." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from December 2022 and shows Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra in Dausa, Rajasthan. OUR PROBE
We performed a reverse search on screengrabs of the viral video. This led us to the same video uploaded to Rajasthan's Congress leader Sachin Pilot's X  account on  December 16, 2022. The post reads: "As the Bharat Jodo Yatra entered Dausa on its 100th day, the response and participation of the people was overwhelming." Dausa is the political stronghold of Sachin Pilot. At the time, many accounts associated with the Congress party  also shared the video with similar information. As the #BharatJodoYatra entered Dausa on its 100th day, the response and participation of the people was overwhelming! pic.twitter.com/ZIyX8l6SLR — Sachin Pilot (@SachinPilot) December 16, 2022
As the #BharatJodoYatra entered Dausa on its 100th day, the response and participation of the people was overwhelming! pic.twitter.com/ZIyX8l6SLR — Sachin Pilot (@SachinPilot) December 16, 2022
We compared this video and the viral one and noted several similarities, including shop signages, motor vehicles, and posters on the road.
We searched for media coverage of the event and found several such reports published in December 2022. As per ABP news , Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra reached Rajasthan's Dausa on December 15, 2022. There, he listened to the local farmers' problems.
We also found a Navbharat Times video report uploaded to YouTube in December 2022, which contained screengrabs from the viral video. As per the report, the Bharat Jodo Yatra reached Dausa in Rajasthan on its 100th day, Where a huge crowd gave a grand welcome to Rahul Gandhi.
We tried to look for videos of Gandhi's recent Nashik visit during his Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra. We found a live stream ( https://www.youtube.com/live/aFkEv08iKUE?si=higoFM68Oe60jgkX ) on Gandhi's official YouTube account from March 14. While a large number of people gathered for the rally, it appeared smaller compared to the viral video. Also, we did not find any similarities between this video to the viral video.
Thus, it's more than clear that a 2022 video from Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra in Rajasthan was falsely shared as his recent rally in Nashik, Maharashtra. - Ends Written by Ashish Kumar Published By: Ajmal Published On: Mar 15, 2024 18:12 IST

title: Fact Check: Rahul Gandhi didn't refuse Lord Vitthal's idol, viral video is clipped
content:
This is a clipped video circulating. In the full-length video and photographs, Gandhi can be seen accepting the idol.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi addressed the Kisan Mahapanchayat in Nashik , Maharashtra, as part of his ongoing Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra. Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar and Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut were also in attendance.
A video now going viral allegedly shows Gandhi refusing to accept a Lord Vitthal idol presented by one of his party workers. Lord Vitthal is a revered local deity in Maharashtra and Karnataka.
Bharatiya Janata Party's Amit Malviya  and the BJP's official Maharashtra account  shared the video on X. Malviya wrote, "Rahul Gandhi refuses to accept idol of Bhagwan Vitthal on stage. This is an insult to not just the Warkaris but millions of Hindu devotees, who revere the Lord. From DMK to the Congress, Hindu hate is what binds the I.N.D.I Alliance. Rahul Gandhi suffers from Hindumisia."Â
Many others shared the clip with the same accusation.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video was clipped. In the full clip, Gandhi can be seen accepting the idol from a supporter on that dias and was also photographed while doing so. Our Probe
Upon reverse-searching keyframes of the viral video, we found a video posted on X on March 14 by the President of the Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee, Nana Patole. In this video, Rahul Gandhi can be seen accepting the idol and posing with it for a photograph.Â
Patole, while sharing the video, alleged that BJP members were sharing the viral clip alongside falsehoods. धरीला पंढरीचा चोर | गळा बांधुनिया दोर || हृदय बंदिखाना केला | आंत विठ्ठल कोंडीला शब्दे केली जडाजुडी | विठ्ठल पायी घातली बेडी सोहम शब्दाचा मारा केला | विठ्ठल काकुळती आला आम्ही रामाचे पुजारी, हे तर रामाचे व्यापारी... ही संत जनाबाई ह्यांच्या अभंगाची ओळ या भाजपावाल्यांसाठी… https://t.co/2Y3P8E49Ag pic.twitter.com/DdBulBA14w — Nana Patole (@NANA_PATOLE) March 14, 2024
धरीला पंढरीचा चोर | गळा बांधुनिया दोर || हृदय बंदिखाना केला | आंत विठ्ठल कोंडीला शब्दे केली जडाजुडी | विठ्ठल पायी घातली बेडी सोहम शब्दाचा मारा केला | विठ्ठल काकुळती आला आम्ही रामाचे पुजारी, हे तर रामाचे व्यापारी... ही संत जनाबाई ह्यांच्या अभंगाची ओळ या भाजपावाल्यांसाठी… https://t.co/2Y3P8E49Ag pic.twitter.com/DdBulBA14w — Nana Patole (@NANA_PATOLE) March 14, 2024
In the video, Gandhi and his associates could be seen gesturing at the party worker to step aside while he was being photographed with someone else. Later, Gandhi accepted the idol, posed for a photograph with the presenter, and then passed it on.
Many Congress leaders issued similar rebuttals to Amit Malviya's post on X.
We also found a video of the entire event shared by Oneindia News on March 14. The relevant section appears between the 13-minute and 14-minute-30-second mark. The sequence of events that happened is as follows.Â
First, someone wrapped a turban around Rahul Gandhi's head. At the time, the person with the idol tried to present it to him but was stopped twice by others on the stage as people garlanded Gandhi. Then the Congress leader removed the turban and the garlands and accepted the idol.Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral video was clipped to give it a false spin. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Mar 15, 2024 19:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Hub Power Company from Pak buy electoral bonds? The truth behind this shocking claim
content:
Hub Power Company, which made political donations through electoral bonds, has no known Pakistani links. It's a Delhi-based company.
As the nation pored over the massive electoral bonds data released on March 14, many fixated on one particular set of entries. On April 18, 2019, Hub Power Company donated Rs 95 lakh through 14 electoral bonds. But what was so special about this? Allegedly, this was a Pakistani company, and these purchases were linked to the February 2019 Pulwama terrorist attack that killed 40 Indian Central Reserve Police Force personnel.Â
"SHOCKING. Pakistan-based company, Hub Power Company, donated Electoral Bonds weeks after the Pulwama attack," alleged the official Facebook page of Indian National Congress Chandigarh on March 15 . "When the entire country was mourning the loss of 40 brave soldiers, someone was enjoying funding from Pakistan. Now you know why no proper investigation of Pulwama attacks was ever done & no culprits are caught yet."
Another Facebook user , while sharing a photo of the released electoral bond data and the screengrab of the Wikipedia page of Hub Power Company, wrote: "Pakistani Company has also bought Electoral Bonds. These bonds issued to Hub Power Company during Pulwama attack happened where our soldiers were died. Is it just coincidence?"Â
The Wikipedia page mentioned that Hub Power Company Limited or HUBCO was the first and largest Pakistani Independent Power Producer. Â
India Today Fact Check found that while there is a Pakistani company by this name, the Hub Power Company listed in the electoral bonds list is a Delhi-based company with no known Pakistani links. The Pakistani HUBCO has refuted all allegations of donating to Indian parties through electoral bonds. All you need to know about the Indian 'Hub Power Company'Â
Through a keyword search, we found the Indiamart page for Hub Power Company. The page listed the business as a "wholesaler of deepawali lights, rechargeable bulb & ormit led bulb in Delhi." Among other details such as an annual turnover of Rs 50 lakh to 1 crore, Indiamart also listed a GST number for the company: 07BWNPM0985J1ZX.
In the official Goods and Services Tax portal , the GST number listed above led us to the following details: Hub Power Company is owned by a person called Ravi Mehra. It was registered on November 12, 2018. Its principal place of business was an address in New Delhi's Geeta Colony. Nothing in these details hinted at the company having any Pakistani links. According to the Election Commission of India , the Hub Power Company purchased 14 electoral bonds worth Rs 95 lakh on April 18, 2019. However, which political party was the recipient of this donation, or if there was more than one political party that received the money, cannot be ascertained from the data that has been released at this time. According to the Department of Economic Affairs under the Union Ministry of Finance , "Electoral Bonds would have a life of only 15 days during which it can be used for making donation only to the political parties registered under section 29A of the Representation of the Peoples Act, 1951 (43 of 1951) and which secured not less than one per cent of the votes polled in the last general election to the House of the People or a Legislative Assembly." advertisement It is noteworthy, however, that there is a Pakistan-based Hub Power Company . But this company, in the aftermath of these allegations, took to X to "categorically state that we are not affiliated with the company named in this matter or any other company based in India. The payments which are being highlighted on the media have no connection whatsoever with HUBCO." pic.twitter.com/TIed2fBYvj — Hubco (@TheHubPowerCo) March 15, 2024  Can foreign companies donate to Indian parties through electoral bonds? Trilochan Sastry, the chairman and founder member of the Association for Democratic Reforms told India Today that before 2017, only foreign companies which had an Indian business partner with at least a 51 per cent stake could make such a donation. But this roadblock was removed thanks to the amendment to FCRA rules in 2017 . This amendment made it technically possible for foreign companies to make donations through electoral bonds. They needed to fulfil only two criteria: first, the company should fulfil all applicable rules to conduct business in India; and two, they should have a registered office in India. advertisement This amendment was subsequently challenged in the Supreme Court. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Mar 15, 2024 23:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Chief Election Commissioner didn't skip this journo's question, clipped video viral
content:
The viral video is clipped. In the full video, CEC Rajiv Kumar can be seen answering the journalist's question, along with other queries later.
The schedule for the Lok Sabha elections 2024 is out now , according to which the world's biggest electoral exercise will be held in seven phases from April 19 to June 1, with counting of votes on June 4. Chief Election Commissioner Rajiv Kumar along with Election Commissioners Gyanesh Kumar and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu , announced this schedule along with dates for assembly elections and By-Elections in 26 Assembly Constituencies, in a press conference held on March 16 .Â
A video clip from this press conference  is now making the rounds on social media platforms, in which a journalist can be seen asking whether the election commission will take action against the ruling party for violation of the model code of conduct (MCC), or only leaders of the Opposition party will bear the brunt . Those sharing the clip claimed the Election Commissioners dodged her query, calling them biased .Â
The text inside the viral video read : "Hats off to her guts. A brave journalist asked, 'Why isn't the ECI taking action against Modi & Shah for their hate speeches?' But the spineless ECI skipped the question." India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is clipped. In the full video, CEC Rajiv Kumar can be seen answering the journalist's question, along with other journalists' queries at the conference later. Our Probe We found the live streaming of the press conference shared on the official YouTube channel of the Election Commission of India  on March 16. The conference was led by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Rajiv Kumar, who first shared slides containing detailed electoral statistics along with advisory to the contesting political parties. This was followed by the schedule of bypolls on 26 ACs, Assembly elections in four states, namely Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, and Odisha, and the schedule of Lok Sabha polls. Following that, journalists at the conference raised their questions . The clip of the viral video can be seen in this footage at the mark of 1 hour 54 seconds . The woman introduced herself as Ashlin Mathew from the National Herald .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is clipped. In the full video, CEC Rajiv Kumar can be seen answering the journalist's question, along with other journalists' queries at the conference later.
We found the live streaming of the press conference shared on the official YouTube channel of the Election Commission of India  on March 16. The conference was led by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Rajiv Kumar, who first shared slides containing detailed electoral statistics along with advisory to the contesting political parties. This was followed by the schedule of bypolls on 26 ACs, Assembly elections in four states, namely Andhra Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, and Odisha, and the schedule of Lok Sabha polls.
Following that, journalists at the conference raised their questions . The clip of the viral video can be seen in this footage at the mark of 1 hour 54 seconds . The woman introduced herself as Ashlin Mathew from the National Herald .Â
As journalists asked their queries, CEC Rajiv answered the first round of five questions, including the one from the viral video at the mark of 1 hour 10 minutes and 22 seconds .Â
Addressing the allegation of bias in dealing with the violation of the MCC, he said, "Wherever there will be a case of violation against anyone, no matter how renowned the politician may be, we will take action against him or her."Â
This answer by the CEC was also reported by the Hindustan Times in a report about the conference . It further added that an individual named Professor DS Agarwal, who introduced himself as a nominee of ex-President Pranab Mukherjee in 2012, also asked questions from the poll body officials.
The man was, however, led away from the conference, as he was not a member of the press. The video of the incident was also tweeted by the news agency ANI . #WATCH | During the press conference of the Election Commission of India, a person not belonging to the Press, raises questions against the Election Commission. He was led away from the press conference which was for journalists. pic.twitter.com/kYUWfmO0Bf — ANI (@ANI) March 16, 2024
#WATCH | During the press conference of the Election Commission of India, a person not belonging to the Press, raises questions against the Election Commission. He was led away from the press conference which was for journalists. pic.twitter.com/kYUWfmO0Bf — ANI (@ANI) March 16, 2024
Thus, it is clear that a trimmed video was shared to claim that the ECI skipped a journalist's question at a press conference. - Ends Published By: Srishti Jha Published On: Mar 17, 2024 16:57 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Rahul's Nyay Yatra in Maharashtra, this clip shows bullock cart race in Karnataka
content:
The video is not from Rahul Gandhi's rally. Instead, it is from a bullock cart race on March 5 in Karnataka.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra concluded in Mumbai's Dharavi on March 16. In its aftermath, a video of a huge crowd, allegedly from Gandhi's rally in Maharashtra, was shared by many on social media platforms.
A Facebook user shared the viral clip and wrote, "Crowd at #RahulGandhi's rally in  Maharashtra , now." Its archive can be seen here .
Additionally, the viral clip was shared on the official Facebook page of Uttarakhand Congress . The caption read, " Rahul Gandhi 's first big rally after the #ElectoralBondScam expose." Its archive can be seen here . The video was also shared by a news platform called "Molitics India" , claiming it to be from Maharashtra.
India Today Fact Check found that the viral clip is not from a Rahul Gandhi rally. It is from a bullock cart race from March 5 in Karnataka .
By performing a reverse search on screengrabs from the viral video, we found a similar video  uploaded to YouTube on March 11. The video was also shared on Instagram  on March 10. In this video, a bullock cart could be seen trampling people as it moved.
The caption along with these videos claimed they showed a bullock cart race. This suggested that the viral clip may not have been related to Rahul Gandhi's Maharashtra rally because the Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra entered the state on March 12.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Aashish (@aashish.8624_)
A post shared by Aashish (@aashish.8624_)
These videos also featured a huge poster of a man, which was also visible in the viral clip. Upon comparison, it became clear that these videos were from the same place.
We then found the viral video in an Instagram post  from March 5, shared by a person called Abhijeet Kalage. We contacted Kalage, who told us he shot this video the same day at a bullock cart race in Karnataka's Belagavi district.
Kalage, who hails from Maharashtra's Kolhapur district, which borders Karnataka's Belagavi district, mentioned that a bull named Haranya from his region was announced as the winner.
India Today's Kolhapur correspondent Deepak Suryavanshi confirmed that the viral video was from Chikodi village in Karnataka's Belagavi district. The race was organised on March 5 on Congress MLA Prakash Hukkeri's birthday.
We then spoke to Sachin Patil, the winning bull's owner. He told India Today that the race was organised by Prakash Hukkeri's son Ganesh Hukkeri. After Haranya won the race, Patil was awarded Rs 17 lakh. He also told us that the man in the poster in the viral video was Ganesh Hukkeri. Patil also sent us a few photos of the race which can be seen below.
A Belagavi-based news portal live-streamed the whole programme. The video can be seen below. We spotted many similarities between this video and the viral one, including the aforementioned poster.
Thus, it is clear that the viral video is not from Rahul Gandhi's Maharashtra rally but from a bullock cart race in Karnataka. - Ends (with inputs from Deepak Suryavanshi in Kolhapur) Published By: Prateek Chakraborty Published On: Mar 18, 2024 16:23 IST

title: Fact Check: Digitally made photo of fire VIRAL as Ukrainian attack on Russia
content:
This image was created by a Ukrainian artist. It doesn't show a real incident.
As Vladimir Putin secured his term for another six years, reportedly winning 87 per cent of the vote , a number higher than in the four previous elections he participated in, Russia's defence ministry said its forces destroyed dozens of drones in several regions across the country, including Moscow. Reportedly, these attacks happened in the Russian region of Krasnodar and the port city of Odesa.
Now, an image  of a massive fire and thick smoke behind a billboard featuring Putin's photo and Russian language text is being shared online. A Facebook user shared the photo and wrote, "More hits in Russia… including Domodedovo Airport in Moscow. the billboard says 'stability'."
"A genuine photo taken following a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian oil refinery. the billboard states 'STABILITY'," wrote an X user . Its archive can be seen here . Â
We found that a Ukrainian artist digitally created the image in question, who confirmed this to India Today. OUR PROBE
A quick reverse search led us to an X post  that noted that this image was created in the backdrop of the presidential election and other recent developments in Russia. It attributed the photo to Telegram user "@khersondesigner". Its archive can be seen here .Â
A keyword search led us to X user @khersondesigner, who shared an extended version of the viral image on March 14. Its archive can be seen here . A comparison can be seen below.
Next, we looked for this image on the Telegram channel of "@khersondesigner". We found it posted on January 23 , alongside the Ukrainian language caption: "All posters here are HD posters".Â
It was reposted on the channel on March 18  with the text, "Who would have thought that this picture would become popular all over the world? Journalists from abroad ask 'Is this a real photo or a processed one?' Unfortunately, the picture became popular without indicating the author's name, and people really think that it is a photo."Â
India Today reached out to "@khersondesigner", who said that this image was created by him using multiple photo editing tools, including some AI tools. He added that he is a designer from Ukraine who hails from Kherson.Â
Thus, it's clear that a digitally created image is being falsely shared as a Ukrainian attack on Russia. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Mar 19, 2024 15:31 IST

title: Fact Check: Did CJI walk away while Tushar Mehta was speaking? NO, viral claim is false
content:
The viral claim is false. In the complete video, it's visible that the CJI did not walk away and was present for the complete session.
Did Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud walk away while the Solicitor General was presenting his arguments? A video from the Supreme Court hearing on the electoral bonds case was shared with this allegation.Â
The clip showed Solicitor General Tushar Mehta speaking on the matter. Near the end of the video, while Mehta was still speaking, it appeared as if Chandrachud was about to get up and leave. This is where the video ended.Â
A Facebook user while sharing the viral clip wrote, "How can the CJI behave in this manner? SG is presenting his arguments before him and without adjourning, he and other judges simply walked away. This is gross humiliation and insult to the Govt of India. All the judges including the CJI Chandrachud, should be hauled up and, forced to resign by the President of India. Totally mannerless and ARROGANT this man Chandrachud is. He and other judges are taking vengeance against the Govt of India." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral claims are not true. Neither the CJI nor the other judges walked away in the middle of the Solicitor General's arguments. The CJI was adjusting his chair and the court was in session for another 20 minutes.
Under the viral post, many pointed out that the allegation was false. We noticed that the video featured the logo of Law Today. Based on this, we checked and found it was shared on the news outlet's X account  on March 18. It was taken from the live stream of the apex court's proceedings inside courtroom number one.
Law Today's video was the same as the viral clip, even in length. Near its end, Tushar Mehta can be heard saying, "My purpose is to inform you that there is something else that is playing out, something that neither the Supreme Court intended, nor the Electoral Bonds scheme intended."
On the Supreme Court of India's official YouTube channel, we found the full version of the video . The clip was live-streamed on March 18 and was 47 minutes long.
The viral clip can be seen beginning at the 23-minute mark. At 27 minutes and 4 seconds, the CJI can be seen talking to his colleagues and adjusting his position. This is where Law Today's clip ended. Watching the complete video, one can see that the CJI did not get up from his chair. After this, Mukul Rohatgi, the Former Attorney-General for India started speaking. The CJI could be seen seated for the remainder of the proceeding.Â
To further corroborate the facts, we spoke to Delhi-based journalist Awstika Das, the Supreme Court Correspondent at LiveLaw, a legal news portal. Das, who covered the March 18 proceedings, told India Today she was also taken aback when she saw the viral clip. She said, "Having covered the entire hearing, I can confirm that it continued for another twenty minutes or so. The entire proceeding was live-streamed on YouTube. A quick look at the full footage is all it takes to dispel these unfounded and inaccurate claims."
Thus, it is clear that the viral claim about the CJI walking away is false. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Mar 19, 2024 18:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Canada DIDN'T shame Indians for open defecation, these ads are Photoshopped
content:
The picture has been digitally altered. It has nothing to do with Indians living in Canada. The actual image of the billboard is old and from Accra, Ghana.
A billboard featuring a man defecating in the open is making rounds, with many claiming  that Canadian municipalities have issued these ads in Hindi for Indians living there.Â
Sharing this photo, an X user wrote , "Municipalities across Canadian cities with high Indian population have put posters in Hindi across the park and beaches asking Indians not to defecate in the open. It is normal in India as Millions of them still don't have the facility of a washroom and they defecate in the open." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the picture has been digitally altered. It has nothing to do with Indians living in Canada. The actual ad is old and from Accra, Ghana. OUR PROBE
We performed a reverse search on the viral photo and it led us to the stock image website Shutterstock where a photo resembling the viral one can be seen. We compared both photos and found several similarities. As per Shutterstock , the photo was taken on May 1, 2018. The photo was captioned: "The billboard "Beaches are not toilets" on the street of Accra."
However, the only differences we found between the Shutterstock photo and the viral one were that the face of the man defecating appeared to have been digitally altered, and the text "Gyae Ennfatawo" was replaced with the Hindi translation of "stop open defecation". We also found many media reports published in 2018 that contained the Shutterstock image. As per BusinessGhana , these billboards were part of a public health sanitation project funded by Canada and the United Nations. On the billboard, a logo of the Government of Canada can be seen at the bottom alongside the logos of the Ghanaian government and UNICEF. Canada has been working with UNICEF since 2012 to eradicate open defecation in the African country.
We also found many media reports published in 2018 that contained the Shutterstock image. As per BusinessGhana , these billboards were part of a public health sanitation project funded by Canada and the United Nations. On the billboard, a logo of the Government of Canada can be seen at the bottom alongside the logos of the Ghanaian government and UNICEF. Canada has been working with UNICEF since 2012 to eradicate open defecation in the African country.
The reports mentioned that the Canadian Government gave about $850,000 to fund one of Ghana's most "significant" development challenges. An official said at the time that the money had been instrumental in getting Ghanaians to change habits and build proper toilets.
We then searched if Canadian municipalities had employed similar ad campaigns to encourage Indians not to defecate in the open. We found no credible news report about this.Â
Thus, it is more than clear that a billboard of an open defecation campaign in Accra, Ghana, was digitally altered to falsely link to Indians living in Canada. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ajmal Published On: Mar 19, 2024 20:32 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of failed fighter aircraft take-off is old and not from Russia
content:
This video dates back to February 2017 and is from Belarus. The accident occurred during military training by the Belorussian air forces.
A video showing a failed take-off by a fighter aircraft has been circulating on social media, with claims suggesting it was a mishap involving the Russian Air Force.
The video begins with the aircraft accelerating on the runway. However, as it attempts to lift off, its landing gears retract, causing the tail to scrape against the runway. The aircraft eventually catches fire due to heavy friction. Despite the harrowing situation, the pilot managed to save himself by ejecting safely.
While posting the video on social media platforms , many users claimed the incident was from Russia and questioned its Air Force's competence. A user wrote, "Top Gun: Russia. Either Russia is running out of qualified pilots or they're having another go at the ekranoplane."
Others shared this video on X with a caption that read, "Russia ripping off the Houthis now."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is six years old and not from Russia. Russia ripping off the Houthis now pic.twitter.com/ujPWK76Sg1 — FriendlyKozak 🇺🇦 (@KvotheTheArcane) March 11, 2024
Russia ripping off the Houthis now pic.twitter.com/ujPWK76Sg1 — FriendlyKozak 🇺🇦 (@KvotheTheArcane) March 11, 2024
A reverse search of a keyframe from the video led us to an article published on The Aviationist website , dated July 15, 2017. According to the report, the incident involved a MiG-29BM Fulcrum belonging to the Belarusian airforce and occurred in Bobruisk, Belarus on Feb. 27, 2017. With subsequent searches, we came across several news reports that featured screengrabs from the mishap, corroborating the details of the incident. The Mirror UK report highlighted that the MiG-29 caught fire during military training conducted by the Belorussian air forces at an airfield in Bobruisk, Belarus. A report from The Sun quoted local sources indicating that the fire likely started in the engine, although no official confirmation regarding the cause was provided. The report also added that the pilot emerged unscathed. Nearly five months after the incident, in July 2017, the Belarusian Ministry of Defense officially acknowledged the accident and announced the commencement of an investigation. It is worth noting that MiG fighter aircraft are of Russian origin and are used by several countries including India, Ukraine, and Germany for air combat. The viral video doesn't show a mishap involving the Russian Air Force but rather an incident from Belarus in February 2017. - Ends Published By: Shweta Kumari Published On: Mar 21, 2024 17:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Muslim man molesting school student is from Bangladesh, NOT India
content:
This incident is from Bangladesh's Dinajpur district. The accused was arrested on March 18.
CCTV footage of a Muslim man sexually assaulting a school student has been shared widely on social media, with many claiming this incident  happened in India . An X user  shared the video and wrote, "A Muslim man tried to molest a school girl caught on CCTV in India".Â
Another wrote, "India slowly becoming Pakistan for Hindus," implying that the school student in the video  was Hindu. The archives of these posts can be seen here  and here .
India Today found that this incident happened on March 17 in Bangladesh's Dinajpur district. Shah Iftekhar Ahmed, Dinajpur's superintendent of police, confirmed this to India Today. Our ProbeÂ
Responding to the viral post, many social media users pointed out  that this incident was from Bangladesh. A reverse search of the viral video's keyframes along with relevant keywords led us to a March 18 video report by Bangladeshi news outlet Jamuna TV. As per the Bangla language caption written alongside this report, this incident happened in Bangladesh's Dinajpur.
We subsequently found several Bangladeshi news reports about the incident. According to Bangla News 24 , this incident happened on March 17, when the school student was walking to her sister's house. Following this incident, her father filed a complaint with the police.Â
Per a report by CNI Asia , the victim was a class 6 student. The accused reportedly was the son of Ariful Islam Mintu of the Baluadanga locality in Sakhawat, Bangladesh. His family as per the report asserted that the accused suffered from mental issues and was getting treatment for the same.
India Today then got in touch with Shah Iftekhar Ahmed, the superintendent of police in the Dinajpur district, to know more. He said that a 12-year-old Hindu girl was molested on March 17 by Sakhawat Hossain, 20. Ahmed added, "Upon receipt of a complaint from the victim's father, a case was filed in the Kotwali police station of Dinajpur under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act, 2000. On March  18, the criminal was duly arrested and sent to prison."
Bangladesh-based reporter Shahidul Hasan Khokan also corroborated that this incident happened in Bangladesh.
Thus, it's clear that this video is not from India. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Mar 22, 2024 15:34 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of TMC leader being chased by crowd goes viral before Lok Sabha polls
content:
While TMC's Bishnupur candidate, Sujata Mondal, did indeed threaten voters, the video in question dates back to July 6, 2021, from the West Bengal assembly elections.
Amidst the fervour of Lok Sabha poll campaigns in West Bengal, a shocking video showing villagers wielding bamboo sticks and chasing a woman has gone viral on social media.  Sujata Khan, TMC candidate from Bishnupur was threatening voters of Arambagh to vote for TMC or they will face consequences. Voters of Arambagh beat up Sujata Khan and other party workers and chased them away from there. Hindus of Bengal are fighting!! pic.twitter.com/wqfxCQy6ho — Sunanda Roy 👑 (@SaffronSunanda) March 21, 2024
Sujata Khan, TMC candidate from Bishnupur was threatening voters of Arambagh to vote for TMC or they will face consequences. Voters of Arambagh beat up Sujata Khan and other party workers and chased them away from there. Hindus of Bengal are fighting!! pic.twitter.com/wqfxCQy6ho — Sunanda Roy 👑 (@SaffronSunanda) March 21, 2024
The video was shared with claims  suggesting that Sujata Khan, the TMC candidate from Bishnupur, incurred the wrath of villagers for allegedly intimidating voters. Sujata Mondal, formerly known as Sujata Khan and the ex-wife of Bishnupur BJP MP Soumitra Khan, allegedly threatened voters to stop civic amenities if they voted for BJP in the upcoming Lok Sabha polls. This incident is being claimed as the aftermath of her threat.
A user while sharing the viral video , wrote, "Sujata Khan, TMC candidate from Bishnupur, was threatening voters of Arambagh to vote for TMC or they will face consequences. Voters of Arambagh beat up Sujata Khan and other party workers and chased them away from there. Hindus of Bengal are fighting!"
India Today Fact Check found that the video dates back to April 2021, during the West Bengal assembly elections.
A reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video took us to a report by The Quint from April 6, 2021, detailing the assault on TMC's candidate Sujata Mondal.
The report, featuring screenshots from the viral video, highlighted that TMC's candidate from Arambagh, Sujata Mondal, was allegedly assaulted by a group at Arandi's booth number 263. TMC accused the BJP of orchestrating the attack.
According to reports from India Today  and NDTV , TMC supremo Mamata Banerjee responded to the incident by taking a jibe at it. She remarked, "We shall take legal action against such central force personnel. We shall file an FIR. They talk about Beti Bachao and beat up my woman candidate Sujata Mondal, who is also an SC candidate."
On April 6, 2021, news agency ANI tweeted Sujata's statement following the incident, where she alleged that at booth number 45, votes intended for TMC went to BJP. Situation is fine at many places but not okay where we're strong. At booth 45, people voted for TMC but it's going to BJP. In Arandi-ii, our workers were beaten. Central Forces are also not neutral.They're telling people to vote for BJP: Sujata Mondal, TMC candidate from Arambagh pic.twitter.com/bmMi3vuAJ7 — ANI (@ANI) April 6, 2021
Situation is fine at many places but not okay where we're strong. At booth 45, people voted for TMC but it's going to BJP. In Arandi-ii, our workers were beaten. Central Forces are also not neutral.They're telling people to vote for BJP: Sujata Mondal, TMC candidate from Arambagh pic.twitter.com/bmMi3vuAJ7 — ANI (@ANI) April 6, 2021
Furthermore, we also found the extended version of the original video, posted by the official YouTube channel of Anandabazar Patrika. It shows Sujata Mondal engaging with some villagers, who subsequently confront her with bamboo sticks.
Ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, the TMC fielded Sujata Mondal against her former husband, BJP MP Soumitra Khan, in Bishnupur. While she did initiate her campaign by allegedly issuing threats to villagers, the video in question is three years old. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Mar 22, 2024 17:06 IST

title: Fact Check: 2013 video of Syrian rebels shooting down fighter jet viral as Ukrainian F-16 under attack
content:
The viral video from Syria is more than 11 years old. It has nothing to do with the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.
A video allegedly showing Russian forces shooting down a Ukrainian F-16 fighter jet has been widely shared online. Sharing this video, an X user wrote , "Russia shoots down F-16. Using new state-of-the-art S-500 air defence in Ukraine. This will be the fate of all Western planes sent to Ukraine." Archives of such posts can be seen here  and here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video from Syria is more than 11 years old. It has nothing to do with the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.
It's noteworthy that in an interview in February, NATO Secretary General Jens Stoltenberg said that the alliance wants F-16 jets to be available to Ukraine as soon as possible without specifying the timeframe. Also, on March 20, a Greek F-16 fighter aircraft crashed in the Aegean Sea during a training mission  near Psathoura island, 175 kilometres northeast of Athens, Greece. The pilot was reportedly rescued. OUR PROBE
We performed a reverse search on screengrabs of the viral video. This led us to the same video  uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Euronews (Turkish) on February 4, 2013. As per the video report, it showed clashes between pro-regime forces and rebels across Syria. Rebels reportedly shot down a Syrian MiG-23 warplane during the clashes near the west-central Syrian city of Hama.Â
In February 2013, many international media outlets and channels reported this incident with the same information.Â
We searched about this incident using Arabic keywords and found a similar video uploaded to the YouTube channel of Ugarit News - Syria in February 2013. Ugarit News is an online Syrian rebel news outlet.Â
As per the video's title, rebels shot down a MiG-23 plane in the city of Karnaz, located northwest of Hama. This means the video predates the ongoing war in Ukraine.
In 2023, the United States approved sending F-16s to Ukraine from Denmark and the Netherlands to power its defence against Russian aggression. But Ukraine has yet to receive any ( https://www.nytimes.com/2024/03/11/world/europe/ukraine-f16-pilots.html ) F-16 jets officially from the NATO allies. Also, the artillery gun used in the viral video does not match the Russian anti-ballistic missile system S-500.
Thus, it's more than clear that an 11-year-old video from Syria was falsely linked to the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ajmal Published On: Mar 22, 2024 17:46 IST

title: Fact Check: 'No Vote To BJP' video from Bengal polls viral again ahead of Lok Sabha election
content:
This video is more than three years old and from the 2021 West Bengal elections. It's not related to the upcoming Lok Sabha elections.
Around a billion India will vote for the 18th Lok Sabha from April 19 to June 1 in seven phases to elect their representatives in the lower house of the Parliament. In its run-up, a video  of several people holding placards proclaiming "No Vote To BJP" at different locations began making rounds online. Those sharing the video linked it to the ongoing Lok Sabha elections. The archive of such a post can be seen here. Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is more than three years old, from the 2021 West Bengal elections. Our Probe
A quick reverse search of screengrabs from the viral video led us to the same video uploaded to the YouTube channel "No Vote To BJP" on February 13, 2021. As per the video's description, a large number of people unanimously expressed their views to not vote for the Bharatiya Janata Party at several iconic places in Kolkata.Â
The same video was uploaded to the Instagram account "No Vote To BJP" on February 16, 2021, with captions related to the 2021 West Bengal Assembly elections. This made it clear that the video was more than three years old and had nothing to do with the upcoming general elections.Â
There are multiple anti-BJP and "No Vote To BJP" campaign videos on the YouTube channel. However, their channel has been inactive since April 2021. We searched about this campaign online  and found that it was set up by a group of political and civil rights activists in January 2021. It was launched ahead of Bengal state polls and its main motive was discouraging people from voting in favour of the BJP. As per The Hindu's report after the Bengal elections, the campaign "No Vote To BJP" helped Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress to register a massive victory over the BJP. the TMC won over 200 seats as compared to just 77 by the BJP. It's noteworthy that during the Karnataka Assembly elections in 2023, videos of this campaign went viral. At the time as well, India Today Fact Check debunked these claims. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Mar 22, 2024 23:16 IST

title: Fact Check: Old Video passed off as Afghan Forces seizing Pak Army post amid clashes
content:
This video is unrelated to the current clashes and has been online since at least September 2023.
Four civilians and three military personnel were reportedly injured in Pakistan on March 18 due to shelling from across the Afghanistan border. Tensions escalated between the two countries as Pakistani fighter jets conducted airstrikes inside the Afghan provinces of Paktika and Khost. This retaliation came after a suicide bombing attack on March 16 against Pakistani security forces in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The Jaish-e-Fursan-e-Muhammad militant organisation claimed responsibility for the deadly ambush .
Amid these events, a video surfaced on social media  showing a bunch of armed men throwing stones at Pakistani flags, painted on the walls of an old and worn building. Those sharing the video alleged that Afghan forces had seized a Pakistan Army post during the ongoing clashes. For instance, a social media user sharing the video , wrote, "Video: A Pakistan Army post captured by Afghan forces in ongoing border clashes." An archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is unrelated to the ongoing clashes. The video has been on the internet since at least September 2023.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a YouTube video  dated September 12, 2023. The video shared on a channel called "Pashton Plus" carried a screenshot from the viral video. The accompanying caption stated that the video showed the Taliban seizing a Pakistani outpost and hurling stones at the Pakistani flag. This finding confirms that the video predates the ongoing clashes between Pakistan and Afghanistan.
Further searches led us to an extended version of the video in question , which was shared on Facebook on September 11, 2023, with similar information.
With subsequent searches, we found several media reports from September 2023, including those from Hindi News18  and India Today , regarding the video. According to them, the video showed Tehrik-e-Taliban-Pakistan (TTP) militants reportedly seizing control of the Pakistan army's headquarters in Chitral, a city located in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. On September 6, 2023, militants affiliated with the Taliban in Pakistan launched a large-scale assault in Chitral, overruning several villages and resulting in the loss of many soldiers' lives.
At the time, several people shared the viral video  on social media platforms, accompanied by similar claims .
While we could not independently verify the location of this video, it is clear that it predates the ongoing clashes. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Mar 23, 2024 20:00 IST

title: Fact Check: 2009 video of US airstrike falsely shared as Pakistan's crackdown on BLA militants
content:
This video has been on the internet since as early as 2009 and likely shows a US military helicopter attack.
Pakistan's second-largest naval air station, PNS Siddique in Turbat, Balochistan, came under attack on the night of March 25. Reportedly, during the attack by the Baloch Liberation Army, at least one paramilitary soldier and five militants were killed .Â
Now, a video allegedly showing Pakistani forces shooting down the BLA attackers has been widely shared online. An X user wrote , "Footages of BLA Terrorist Pakistan Zindabad," alongside hashtags "Turbat" and "Balochistan". Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video has been online since as early as 2009. It has nothing to do with the recent attack on the Pakistani naval air station in Turbat, Balochistan. OUR PROBE
We performed a reverse search on screengrabs of the viral video. This led us to the same video  uploaded to YouTube on September 9, 2009. The video was titled, "Military US Helicopter Killing Terrorists HD." This means the video predates the recent BLA attack by more than a decade.Â
We searched about this incident using keywords and found screengrabs from the viral video in several media reports. As per some reports , the footage allegedly shows US choppers across the then-war-torn Iraq. Several videos on YouTube claimed this to be an Apache helicopter operation  in Iraq. We also found the same video clip  posted in June 2015 on the website "Military.com", which publishes news and information about the United States military, veterans, and foreign policy. The video here was titled, "Apache Helicopter Engages Terrorists." No further information was given in the article. Apache helicopters are American twin-turboshaft advanced attack helicopters and are currently operated by several countries, including India, Japan, and South Korea. Currently, Pakistani forces do not have an Apache fleet, so using them against the BLA insurgents in Balochistan would be impossible. No video had been released by Pakistani authorities about the BLA attack at the time of publishing this story. So, while India Today could not independently verify the actual location of the viral video, it's more than clear that it has nothing to do with the recent BLA attack on a Turbat naval air base in Pakistan. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Ajmal Published On: Mar 27, 2024 14:06 IST

title: Fact Check: US transport secretary DID NOT blame racist design for Baltimore bridge tragedy
content:
This video of Pete Buttigieg is from November 2021. He was speaking about the Infrastructure Bill.
On the night of May 26, a bridge in Baltimore, US, collapsed after a container ship hit it, killing at least six people  and injuring others. Following the accident, a video of United States Secretary of Transportation Pete Buttigieg was widely shared.Â
Those sharing the video  claimed that Buttigieg blamed the racist design and construction for this collapse. "Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg is taking zero blame for the accident today that occurred in Baltimore at the Francis Scott Key Bridge. Instead, he is blaming those that constructed the bridge, saying it was designed with racism, just like racist bridges in New York," read one such post.
Others shared this clip on X stating, "Transportation Secretary In Response To Bridge Disaster: Maybe Some Bridges Were Made By Racists." An archived version of such a post can be seen here . At first my wife and I thought he was kidding but then she realised he was serious! "He's a sick man", she said. "He's seriously a mentally impaired man", she said again, as we replayed the video clip of Pete Buttigieg blaming the bridge collapse in Baltimore on racism against… pic.twitter.com/9UzyjIoPFm — 𝔹𝕦𝕕… (@bud_cann) March 27, 2024
At first my wife and I thought he was kidding but then she realised he was serious! "He's a sick man", she said. "He's seriously a mentally impaired man", she said again, as we replayed the video clip of Pete Buttigieg blaming the bridge collapse in Baltimore on racism against… pic.twitter.com/9UzyjIoPFm — 𝔹𝕦𝕕… (@bud_cann) March 27, 2024
In the video, Buttigieg could be heard saying, "If an underpass was constructed such that a bus, carrying mostly black and Puerto Rican kids, was designed too low for it to pass by, that obviously reflects racism that went into those design choices. I don't think we have anything to lose by confronting that simple reality, and we have everything to gain by acknowledging it and then dealing with it."Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video is unrelated to the Baltimore bridge collapse. It is from November 2021 and shows Buttigieg speaking about the Infrastructure Bill. OUR PROBE
An advanced search with keywords from Buttigieg's purported statement took us to an Independent UK report from November 9, 2021, quoting the transport secretary uttering these exact words.Â
According to this report, Buttigieg was asked about the bipartisan Infrastructure Bill during a press conference. He responded, saying that the highway designs in the country were "racist". He went on to add that the Infrastructure Bill would help fix this.Â
The YouTube channel of the New York Post also uploaded the extended version of this clip, where Buttigieg can be heard speaking about this project and plans to build new infrastructure that would supposedly fix the issue. BUTTIGIEG'S TAKE ON BALTIMORE MISHAP
A subsequent search with keywords led us to several reports from the Daily Mail, quoting Buttigieg as stating that the Baltimore bridge was not an ordinary construction and was one of the cathedrals of American infrastructure. He added that the path to normalcy would not be easy. Buttigieg's complete statement following the Baltimore tragedy can be seen in the video uploaded by NBC News.
Thus, it is more than evident that a two-year-old comment by the US transport secretary is being misattributed to the Francis Scott Key Bridge tragedy. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Mar 27, 2024 15:47 IST

title: Rome's Iron Bridge on fire after Baltimore bridge collapse? NOPE, old video viral
content:
This video of the Iron Bridge is from October 2, 2021.
Days after a cargo ship rammed into Baltimore's Francis Scott Key Bridge on March 26, causing it to collapse, a video featuring a burning bridge  went viral on social media. Those sharing it claimed that the "Iron Bridge", which spans the river Tiber in Rome, caught fire on March 28, two days after the Baltimore bridge collapse.Â
Some social media users called the incident "suspicious" , demanding an investigation  into the targeting of critical infrastructure .
One person shared the video on X  writing, "2 Bridges in 1 week. Color me surprised. Not. The 'Iron Bridge' in Rome, Italy burned down and collapsed yesterday evening." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is not recent. It is from October 2, 2021.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip shared on X back in October 2021. With the help of a keyword search, we found several media reports about this incident.Â
A report by Reuters  stated that a huge fire broke out on the night of October 2, 2021, damaging Rome's Iron Bridge. The bridge was subsequently closed indefinitely for safety checks.Â
A video shared on the YouTube channel of "Fanpage.it", an Italy-based newspaper, showed parts of the bridge falling into the river while still ablaze.
Quoting the firefighters, the Independent reported  that the fire erupted before midnight on October 2, 2021, near the Ostiense neighbourhood and was extinguished by 4 am the next day. This happened on the eve of the mayoral elections. The fire destroyed parts of the Iron Bridge, which plunged into the River Tiber. Three nearby nightclubs were reportedly evacuated. However, no injuries were reported.
It is thus clear that a 2021 video of Rome's Iron Bridge on fire was falsely shared as a recent incident. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Mar 29, 2024 16:19 IST

title: Fact Check: This hilarious courtroom exchange during Kejriwal's hearing DID NOT take place at all!
content:
There is no evidence of the purported exchange taking place during CM Kejriwal's March 28 court appearance.
Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal's remand in the liquor policy case  has been extended to April 1 following his appearance in Delhi's Rouse Avenue court on March 28. Kejriwal, in person, opposed the Enforcement Directorate's request for further custody and called the alleged scam a political ploy against the Aam Aadmi Party.
Since then, several excerpts of a heated courtroom exchange between Kejriwal and the ED's lawyers have surfaced on social media. One such exchange purportedly between Kejriwal and Additional Solicitor General SV Raju was widely shared, where Kejriwal took a dig at the evidence presented by the domestic law enforcement agency.
The exchange in question went as follows:
"Arvind Kejriwal in court: Why have you arrested me?Â
ASG Raju: We have a statement against you.
Kejriwal: So if I say I gave 100 crores to Modi and Amit Shah, will you go and arrest them based on my statement?Â
Judge and ASG both went quiet."
India Today Fact Check found that the purported exchange never happened. Our Probe
A keyword search yielded no news reports from credible sources about the hearing that confirmed the viral exchange happened. LiveLaw and Bar & Bench, two legal news outlets known for in-depth live courtroom updates, did not report such an exchange.
We then came across journalist Tanishka Sodhi's post on X , who was present in the courtroom during the proceeding, refuting the viral claim, stating it did not occur. She wrote, "Several accounts have tweeted this exchange & it has gone viral. But as someone who was in court, along with a dozen other reporters, can confirm that it certainly did not happen. Please stop RTing fake news!" Several accounts have tweeted this exchange & it has gone viral. But as someone who was in court, along with a dozen other reporters, can confirm that it certainly did not happen. Please stop RTing fake news! Read what actually happened in court here ⬇️ https://t.co/0MiINvvXHh https://t.co/RtxABlerab — Tanishka Sodhi (@tanishka_s2) March 29, 2024 India Today's legal reporter Kanu Sarda, who was also present in the court during the hearing, confirmed that the viral exchange was fake. Sarda said that no such statement was made by Kejriwal referencing Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. Additionally, leaked footage of Kejriwal's courtroom testimony as reported by Mojo Story  further verified the absence of such a statement. No statement made by the Delhi CM resembled the viral exchange. Thus, it's more than clear that the viral exchange between Delhi CM Kejriwal and ASG Raju did not occur at all. - Ends Published By: chingkheinganbi mayengbam Published On: Mar 29, 2024 19:40 IST

title: Fact Check: Last rites of Sufi saint FALSELY viral as Mukhtar Ansari funeral
content:
The footage shows the last rites of Indian Sufi scholar Saqlain Miyan in Bareilly in 2023.
Gangster-turned-politician Mukhtar Ansari's final rites were held in Ghazipur on March 30, amidst tight security. Following this, a video of a large crowd began making the rounds on social media with claims that it showed people gathered in Ghazipur to pay their last respects to Ansari. An archive of the post can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video actually shows the funeral procession of Indian Sufi scholar Saqlain Miyan in Bareilly, in October 2023. Our Probe
We noted distinct elements in the video, including a mosque-like structure and a signboard for Gandhi Medicos. A user on platform X identified the video as footage from the funeral of Islamic scholar Saqlain Miyan in Bareilly.
Using this information, we carried out keyword searches and found many YouTube videos from October 2023 . All these videos were stated to be from Saqlain Miyan's funeral .
We noticed a mosque in these videos resembling the one in the viral video and several other common elements. We then geolocated Gandhi Medicos and found it to be in proximity to Dargah Hazrat Shah Sharafat Ali Miyan, where the Sufi scholar was buried. Additionally, we found the same signboard in the photos tagged to this location on Google Maps.

title: Fact Check: This aerial shot shows 2019 rally in Kolkata, not INDIA bloc rally in Delhi
content:
This image dates back to February 3, 2019, and shows the Brigade Parade ground in Kolkata during a Left rally.
For the first time since the formation of the INDIA bloc, a mega rally showcasing Opposition unity was organised by the Aam Admi Party on March 31 at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan. Members of Congress, Samajwadi Party, Trinamool Congress, Communist Party of India (Marxist), Nationalist Congress Party (Sharad Pawar), Shiv Sena (Uddhav), and the Rashtriya Janata Dal, among others, participated in this event.
Meanwhile, a bird's-eye-view photo allegedly showing this mega rally was widely shared. Some of these posts claimed, "Scenes from today at the Ramlila Maidan Alliance Rally. Modi toh giyo. #INDIAAlliance."Â
One Facebook user wrote : "Massive crowds today at the INDIA alliance rally at the Ramlila Maidan New Delhi. Godi Media won't show you these visuals." The archives of such posts can be seen here and here . BIG BREAKING Massive crowds today at the INDIA alliance rally at the Ramlila Maidan New Delhi. Godi Media won't show you these visuals. pic.twitter.com/plWApaMMHa — Ravinder Kapur. (@RavinderKapur2) March 31, 2024
BIG BREAKING Massive crowds today at the INDIA alliance rally at the Ramlila Maidan New Delhi. Godi Media won't show you these visuals. pic.twitter.com/plWApaMMHa — Ravinder Kapur. (@RavinderKapur2) March 31, 2024
Even a few online news outlets shared this image , linking it to the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the image dates back to February 2019 and shows a mega Opposition rally in West Bengal, right before the Lok Sabha elections. Our Probe
Running the viral image through Google Lens, we found that this was shared by Mohammed Salim, the State Secretary of CPI(M) West Bengal, on February 23, 2021. He wrote on X: "The #PeoplesBrigade on 28th February is going to be the mother of all rallies. The huge turnout of anti-TMC & anti-BJP voters will once again force Narendra Modi to put up sheds to hide the poor turnout during BJP's Brigade rally. #BengalNeedsLeft #BengalRejectsBJP."
