title: Fact Check: Did Congress leaders ignore Karnataka councillor whose daughter was killed?
content:
The Minister of Women and Child Development Minister Laxmi Hebbalkar visited Neha Hiremath's house on April 20, a day before JP Nadda's visit.
The murder of Neha Hiremath, daughter of Karnataka Congress Councillor Niranjan Hiremath, on April 18, has triggered a political slugfest in the state. While the ruling Congress attributed the motive behind the murder  to personal reasons, the Bharatiya Janata Party alleged this was a case of "love jihad", a far-right conspiracy theory that claims Muslim men target Hindu women and convert them to Islam through marriage.
Niranjan Hiremath had earlier complained that if the Karnataka police could not conduct the investigation, the state government should transfer the case to the Central Bureau of Investigation. Then, following a phone call with Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, Niranjan Hiremath apologised for speaking against the state government and said that courts should fast-track such heinous cases.
Amid protests and calls for a bandh in Karnataka following the murder, several social media posts alleged that no Congress leader visited the Hiremath home to pay their condolences.Â
These posts featured a video of BJP National President JP Nadda and Karnataka BJP chief Vijayendra meeting the grieving family. They  claimed : "Hubbali: After JP Nadda ji, Karnataka BJP chief Vijayendra visited Neha Hiremath's house and met his father and Congress leader Niranjan Hiremath. Still, not a single person from Congress visited Neha's house. Not even for formality. Muslim appeasement at the highest level. Shame!" An archive of such a post  can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that before JP Nadda's visit, Karnataka State Women's Commission Chairperson Nagalakshmi Choudhary and Women and Child Development Minister Laxmi Hebbalkar had visited Hiremath's house. OUR PROBE
Keyword searches in English and Kannada led us to several news reports predating Nadda's visit to the Congress corporator's home. The BJP president visited Hiremath's residence on April 21 . A day before, on April 20, Karnataka Minister for Women and Child Welfare Lakshmi Hebbalkar offered condolences at the residence of the Congress councillor for the Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation. During her visit, she assured Neha's family of justice .
Karnataka State Women's Commission chairperson Nagalakshmi Choudhary also reportedly visited  the residence of the murdered 23-year-old on April 21. Offering condolences to her family, she expressed concern for their well-being and urged them to prevent anyone from exploiting the incident for selfish or political reasons. She reportedly said , "I am worried about the family and has asked the family not to allow anyone to use the incident for their selfish and political reasons."
After Nadda's visit, Congress General Secretary and Karnataka in-charge Randeep Singh Surjewala, accompanied by Law Minister HK Patil, also paid a visit to Hiremath's residence on April 24 . Surjewala paid his condolences and reaffirmed to the family that the accused would be swiftly brought to justice. Chief Minister Siddaramaiah too visited the family on April 25. title: Fact Check: This clip of Anthony Blinken praising Chinese economy has synthetic audio
content:
This clip was edited to add synthetic audio. During his address, he spoke about cooperation to help prevent the entry of ingredients of one of the most abused drugs Fentanyl in the US and dealing with other differences with China.
US Secretary of State Antony Blinken met Chinese President Xi Jinping and senior Chinese officials on April 26 to discuss bilateral, regional, and global issues, including China's support for Russia in the Ukraine war, Taiwan and the South China Sea, and human rights.Â
Now, a video going viral on social media shows Blinken extolling the Chinese economy and its technological advancements. An X user sharing this video wrote, "Have you listened to Anthony Blinken's speech from Shanghai?" Its archive can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that the audio in this clip was altered. During his address, he spoke about cooperation to help prevent the entry of ingredients of one of the most abused drugs, fentanyl, in the US and dealing with other differences with China.
It's easily observable that the audio and video in the viral clip are out of sync, clearly suggesting alterations were made to the video.
We also found the original video on the official X account of Blinken , which was shared on April 24 with the following text, "I'm in China to make progress on issues that matter most to the American people, including curbing fentanyl trafficking. We will discuss the work underway to fulfil commitments made by @POTUS and President Xi last fall, as well as the areas where we have significant disagreements."
In the video, he spoke about cooperation to help prevent the entry of ingredients of fentanyl into the US and dealing with other differences with China. I'm in China to make progress on issues that matter most to the American people, including curbing fentanyl trafficking. We will discuss work underway to fulfill commitments made by @POTUS and President Xi last fall, as well as the areas where we have significant disagreements. pic.twitter.com/YMVN4LA6uD — Secretary Antony Blinken (@SecBlinken) April 24, 2024
I'm in China to make progress on issues that matter most to the American people, including curbing fentanyl trafficking. We will discuss work underway to fulfill commitments made by @POTUS and President Xi last fall, as well as the areas where we have significant disagreements. pic.twitter.com/YMVN4LA6uD — Secretary Antony Blinken (@SecBlinken) April 24, 2024
The text of his speech is produced below:
"I've just arrived here in Shanghai, in the People's Republic of China, to work on issues that matter to the American people. One of those is fentanyl, a synthetic opioid, the leading killer of Americans between the ages of 18 and 49.
President Biden and President Xi, when they met in San Francisco at the end of last year, agreed to cooperate to help prevent fentanyl and the ingredients that make it from getting to the United States.
We'll be working on that. Besides my counterparts in the Chinese government, I'll be talking to students, academics, business leaders, and the people who are building bridges and ties between our countries.
And of course, we'll be dealing with areas where we have real differences with China, dealing with them directly, communicating clearly, face-to-face diplomatic matters. It's important to avoid miscommunications and misperceptions, and to advance the interests of the American people."
Thus, it's clear that an edited video of US Secretary of State Blinken overlaid with synthetic audio is being shared online amid his Chinese visit. - Ends Published By: Shweta Kumari Published On: Apr 27, 2024 14:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Amit Shah did NOT talk about scraping ST/SC/OBC reservation, viral clip is doctored
content:
The viral video is doctored. The original video is from his rally held in Telangana, in which Shah announced that if the BJP is voted to power in the state, it would end the Muslim reservation.
Addressing a rally in Telangana's Siddipet on April 25, in support of BJP's Lok Sabha Poll candidate M Raghunandan Rao, Union Home Minister Amit Shah accused the Congress party of corruption and raised questions on the reservation policy of the state.Â
Amid this, a video of the Home Minister's speech started making the rounds on social media , in which he could be heard saying, "If BJP comes to power, it will end the unconstitutional SC, ST, and OBC reservation."
One social media user shared the video of Shah on Facebook , writing: "Will cancel ST, SC reservations if BJP govt is formed again: Amit Shah. #NoMoreBJP." An archived version of this post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video was doctored. The original video is from his rally held in Telangana in 2023, in which Shah announced that if the BJP is voted to power in the state, it will end the Muslim reservation. OUR PROBE
With a keyword search, we found a video shared on the YouTube channel of NDTV  back in 2023. The title of the video read: "Amit Shah Vows To Scrap Muslim Quota in Telangana."
According to its description, while addressing a rally at Chevella near Hyderabad on April 23, 2023, Shah slammed religion-based reservations. Calling them "unconstitutional," he vowed to scrap the reservations for Muslims in Telangana if the BJP formed the government in the state. Â
The colour pattern of the stage and the colour of the podium in this video match those in the viral clip. Additionally, Amit Shah could be seen wearing a scarf of the same colour and design in both videos.
The video of this rally was also shared on the official YouTube channel of Amit Shah on April 23, 2023. The part seen in the viral video can be found at the mark of 14:30  in the video. It is clear that Shah was not talking about scrapping reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes. Instead, he talked about ending the 4 per cent reservation given to Muslims in the state. Contrary to the claim, he spoke about scrapping the reservation given to Muslims and reallocating it to the SC, ST, and OBCs.
It is noteworthy that Shah recently talked about ending the reservation given to Muslims in his rally in Telangana's Siddipet on April 25.
Muslims in Telangana reportedly get 4 per cent reservation in education and employment under the category of Other Backward Classes. However, this quota doesn't form a part of the existing reservation of OBCs but comes under a separate category called BC-E.
It is thus clear that an old video of Amit Shah was doctored to falsely claim that he talked about scrapping ST/SC/OBC reservation in a rally. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Apr 27, 2024 22:21 IST

title: Fact Check: Modi DID NOT accuse Karnataka people of committing sin, viral clip was cut out of context
content:
The viral video has been clipped out of context. In the full video, PM Modi could be seen criticising the state's Congress government, not the people of Karnataka.
Did Prime Minister Narendra Modi call the people of Karnataka "sinners" during a campaign speech? With people gearing up for the third phase of the Lok Sabha elections, many on social media shared a video of PM Modi  claiming the same. In it, Modi can be heard asking people to punish the "Karnataka waalon" during the elections for committing sin.Â
Sharing the video on Facebook , one person wrote, "As expected, he is attacking an entire state now, not even sparing the people who supported BJP. 'Ye Karnataka wolo ne jo paap kiya hai' He is questioning the intelligentsia of the entire state." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is clipped. In the full video, PM Modi could be seen criticising the Congress party, not the people of Karnataka. OUR PROBE
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an Asianet News report  containing a screenshot of the viral clip. According to it, Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a rally in Karnataka's Belagavi on April 28, in which he accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of insulting Hindu kings and glorifying Muslim rulers among several other things.Â
Using this clue, we found the live stream of this rally shared on the YouTube channel of PM Modi. In this video, the portion of the viral clip can be seen at the 32-minute mark . Right before PM Modi made this statement, he talked about how Congress allegedly betrayed the farmers of Karnataka.Â
"The betrayal that the Congress has committed with the farmers here, that's an enormous sin. When the BJP was in power here, Rs 10,000 would get deposited in farmers' bank accounts. The Congress government, the moment it came to power, stopped paying Rs 4,000. They received the votes. Now they don't care about the farmers. Farmers now only receive the Rs 6,000 that Modi sends them. They cut their share. But you will continue to receive the money under the PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi," said Modi.Â
He then made the viral comment. This made it clear that Modi did not refer to the people of Karnataka when he said "Karnataka waalon". Rather, he was referring to the Congress government in the state.Â
We also found several media reports about this rally. A report by Deccan Herald  quoted this PM Modi statement about the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi Scheme where he criticised the Congress of letting the farmers down.Â
In the same rally, Modi also attacked Rahul Gandhi  for allegedly insulting Hindu kings but keeping mum on atrocities committed by Muslim rulers. He also accused Congress of prioritising appeasement while atrocities and crimes were being committed in the state.Â
It is thus, clear that a clipped video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi was shared to falsely claim that he accused the people of Karnataka of committing a sin. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Apr 29, 2024 15:04 IST

title: Fact Check: Congress workers DID NOT obstruct Uddhav's speech. Here's what happened
content:
The viral video is edited to change its context. At Wardha, Thackeray was in a hurry and wanted to deliver only a small speech. The viral clip shows party workers requesting him to speak for longer.
Did Congress party workers obstruct Uddhav Thackeray's speech  during a recent rally in Wardha, Maharashtra?Â
Attacking the Maha Vikas Aghadi — the Maharashtra alliance comprising Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray), the grand old party, and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharad Pawar) — many shared a video  in which Thackeray could be seen attempting to speak as several men interrupted him .Â
Sharing the video on X , one person wrote, "What a fall! Uddhav Thackeray is the other name of shamelessness. Watch how congress workers of Wardha denied Uddhav to even make speech in a rally. Ye log ladenge Modi se (These people will fight Modi)?" Some also commented  that no one would have dared to do the same to Bal Thackeray. The archive of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video was edited. At the Wardha rally, Uddhav Thackeray was short on time and thus wanted to deliver only a small speech. The viral clip shows party workers requesting him to speak for longer.Â
With the help of a keyword search, we found an extended version of the viral video on the YouTube channel of ABP Majha . Its title in Marathi stated that Uddhav Thackeray attacked Nitin Gadkari in his speech at a rally in Maharashtra's Wardha.Â
The video begins with the part seen in the viral video, featuring Thackeray speaking to other leaders on the stage. However, after the conversation, Thackeray gave his speech, uninterrupted by anyone.
As per reports , this was from an April 22 rally in Hinganghat in the Wardha district for Amar Kale, a three-time MLA from the NCP (Sharad Pawar) and the Maha Vikas Aghadi candidate from Wardha. Aside from Thackeray, Sharad Pawar, Amar Kale, and other local leaders spoke at the event.Â
We then found the live stream of this rally on the YouTube channel of Mumbai Tak . Right after the 50-minute mark, Amar Kale could be seen speaking on the stage. Midway, one person approached the leader and interrupted him. After this, Kale moved away from the podium and Uddhav Thackeray was invited to the stage.Â
As Thackeray reached for the mic, some party workers could be seen speaking to him. Thackeray could be heard saying, "Five minutes," while the other leaders could be heard saying, "No, 15 minutes," during this. One of the people on the stage even folded his hands in front of Thackeray, who smiled. Following this, Thackeray made a 10-minute-long speech without any interruption.Â
India Today spoke to Atul Wandile, the State Secretary General of the NCP (Sharad Pawar), who organised this rally. Wandile called the viral claims baseless and explained what happened.Â
He said, "Some of our leaders' speeches got extended and Uddhav Thackeray had a few programs lined up in Nagpur. Uddhav Thackeray said I have to leave early for the Nagpur programs, so I will just speak for five minutes. We then requested him that a huge number of people have come here to listen to you, so don't speak for five minutes; speak for 10 to 15 minutes or as long as you can."
Thus, it's clear that Congress workers did not obstruct Uddhav Thackeray's speech in Wardha. - Ends (With inputs from Surendra Ramteke in Wardha, Maharashtra.) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Apr 30, 2024 20:30 IST

title: Fact Check: Decade-old video viral as flash floods hit Kashmir
content:
Though flash floods hit Kashmir recently, this video is from 2014 when deadly floods hit the valley, killing about 300 people.
Torrential rains in late April have triggered floods in northern parts of Kashmir, causing damage to buildings and roads. A video comprising multiple clips of people wading through flooded streets has now gone viral.
Allegedly, these clips showed the recent floods in Kashmir. A Facebook user shared the video and wrote, "Deadly flooding in Kashmir." Many others also shared the same video , claiming the same. The archive of the viral post can be seen here.Â
India Today found that while from Kashmir, the viral video is almost 10 years old! Our Probe
A keyword search led us to the viral video shared on the YouTube channel of the international news agency Associated Press. The video was uploaded on September 4, 2014. As per the video's description, it showed Kashmir's worst flood in 22 years, which hit the valley in September that year.Â
The same footage can also be seen on the website of the Associated Press.Â
The 2014 Kashmir floods caused heavy damage to the valley, leaving more than 300 dead  and thousands with damaged homes. The floods reportedly cost the economy more than Rs 100 crore, a Greater Kashmir report said.Â
As per an NDTV report,  the recent floods in Kashmir have resulted in at least five deaths so far. The news agency ANI also shared a video of flash floods in Kupwara on April 29. #WATCH | Roads and buildings damaged in flash floods in J&K's Kupwara due to sudden heavy rains in the area pic.twitter.com/wRjcXQoa1Y — ANI (@ANI) April 29, 2024
#WATCH | Roads and buildings damaged in flash floods in J&K's Kupwara due to sudden heavy rains in the area pic.twitter.com/wRjcXQoa1Y — ANI (@ANI) April 29, 2024
Thus, it's clear that the viral video has nothing to do with the recent floods. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Apr 30, 2024 20:33 IST

title: Fact Check: No, this video DOES NOT show Goldy Brar being murdered in broad daylight
content:
The video shows an unrelated shootout incident in New Orleans from July 2023. US police refuted claims of Goldy Brar's murder.
Social media is buzzing with reports of gangster Goldy Brar's alleged murder, the main suspect in the 2022 killing of Punjabi singer and Congress leader Sidhu Moose Wala.Â
A video now going viral shows a shootout, with many claiming it showed Brar being shot in broad daylight in the US. While sharing the viral video , an X user wrote, "Goldy Brar shootout."Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video has no connection to the purported murder of Goldy Brar. Instead, it shows a shootout in New Orleans in July 2023. Conflicting reports have surfaced regarding the death of the notorious gangster. OUR PROBE
Upon conducting a reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video, we came across a video report by New Orleans' CBS affiliate , WWL-TV Channel 4, from July 2023. The video caption stated that it shows a shooting on Industry Street that resulted in two women being injured.
Using this lead, we performed keyword searches and found several reports from July 31, 2023. Louisiana-based WDSU News carried the viral video in its report, noting that around 5:15 pm, a black car arrived at Industry Street, where two men got out and opened fire on people sitting on the front porch of a home. Two women were reportedly injured.
Another report featuring the viral video said that a felon in possession of a firearm was arrested at the scene of the crime. IS GOLDY BRAR DEAD?
Earlier reports suggested that Goldy Brar, along with other gangsters, was involved in a scuffle at a club in Fresno, California. The altercation escalated and resulted in gunfire, leading to Brar's death. Gangster Arsh Dalla allegedly claimed responsibility for the murder.Â
Now, conflicting reports regarding Brar's fate have emerged amid speculation, with police refuting the claim that he was killed in a shootout in California on April 4.
The US police clarified that the news about Brar being shot dead in the country was not true. The notorious gangster is the prime suspect in the murder of singer Sidhu Moose Wala and has also been implicated in attacks on Salman Khan.
Thus, it's clear that an old video of an unrelated shootout in the US is being shared with false claims linking it to the alleged murder of gangster Goldy Brar. - Ends Published By: Prateek Chakraborty Published On: May 2, 2024 21:19 IST

title: Did empty chairs greet PM Modi in Jamnagar? No, this video is NOT from Gujarat at all
content:
This video is not from Jamnagar but from Pune, Maharashtra, where Modi addressed a rally on April 29.
As Narendra Modi and Bharatiya Janata Party leaders continue to campaign ahead of the third phase of the Lok Sabha polls, a video going viral purports to show rows and rows of empty seats at the prime minister's rally in Jamnagar, Gujarat. The video , recorded in the evening, showed several people leaving the venue while PM Modi spoke.
One Facebook post read, "Gujarat Model. A crowd of lakhs gathered at Modiji's rally to see him. The chairs remained empty, but Modiji finished his work and left. Modiji, maybe the people need more money to attend the rally. Lakhs of people gathered to listen to Modi ji's speech in Jamnagar, Gujarat. See how the crowd is jam-packed!" This clip was also shared with similar claims in Hindi . The archive of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check has found that the video is not from the Prime Minister's Jamnagar rally. It is from Pune, Maharashtra. Our Probe
We found a video of Modi's Jamnagar rally uploaded to his official YouTube channel. Streamed on May 2, 2024, it showed the PM was wearing a golden turban and a grey jacket.
In the viral video, however, Modi's turban was red and his jacket sky blue. The Jamnagar rally also took place in the daytime. But the viral video showed the evening sky, clearly suggesting that it was from the same rally.
Subsequently, a reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip shared on X  on April 30. The post noted that this rally was from Pune, Maharashtra.
The Prime Minister's official YouTube channel featured the video of his address in Pune on April 29, where he could be seen wearing a red turban and a sky-blue jacket, similar to the viral video.
A comparison between this and the viral clip made it clear that it was from Pune. We noticed the same tents and LED projector screens positioned at the exact spots in both. Rohit Pawar, the Nationalist Congress Party MLA from Karjat-Jamkhed also shared another video  of this rally, where people can be seen leaving their seats while the PM spoke. पुणे, बारामती, शिरुर आणि मावळ या चार मतदारसंघांसाठी पंतप्रधान नरेंद्र मोदी साहेबांनी एकत्रित घेतलेल्या सभेतील मोकळ्या खुर्च्यांचा हा बोलका व्हिडिओ… बेरोजगारी, महागाई, जाती-धर्माचं राजकारण आणि केवळ पोकळ स्वप्नांना आता लोकंही कंटाळले असून भाड्याने यायलाही नकार देत आहेत. पुणे… pic.twitter.com/a9qGtw9GUk — Rohit Pawar (@RRPSpeaks) April 29, 2024 Therefore, it is clear that the viral video is from neither Jamnagar nor Gujarat but from Pune, Maharashtra. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: May 3, 2024 16:07 IST

title: Fact Check: NO terror angle in Kalyan Jewellers blast in Karnataka, here's what happened
content:
Bellary SP Ranjit Kumar Bandaru told India Today that this explosion happened during gas refilling in an air conditioner and there was no terror link.
A video allegedly showing a bomb blast in a Kalyan Jewellers store in Karnataka has been widely shared on social media. In it, a severely injured man is seen being escorted out of the smoke-filled store to a car, as others escape in panic.Â
Those sharing this video  claimed this was a second blast in Karnataka since the Congress party came into power, the first being the Rameshwaram Cafe blast .Â
An X user wrote , "Breaking Alerts. Bharat. There has been an IED blast in the showroom of Kalyan Jewelers in Bellary, Karnataka. Due to the horrific blast, many people are reported to have been seriously injured.It's Islamist Attack?" Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that this was not a bomb blast but an accident at a Kalyan Jewellers store in Bellary, Karnataka.Â
A keyword search led us to the viral clip in a video report by Hindustan Times Kannada, titled "AC blast at Kalyan Jewellers, Bellary." The report also showed policemen, firefighters, and locals standing outside the showroom, with glass shards scattered everywhere.
As per Asisnet News , there was an explosion during the gas refilling process in the central air conditioning system at a Kalyan Jewelers store. Among the injured were Ahmmed Basha, Saiyad Tabrej Basha, Saiyad Juber, Arun, and Ningappa, and they all were admitted to the VIMS Hospital. The report said that no foul play was found.
Reports by Kannada Prabha  and Times Now News  also corroborate this. WHAT DO POLICE SAY?
The Karnataka police issued a clarification regarding this incident on X. The post reads, "The cause was an air conditioner gas explosion, and @BallariSp has already visited, and an investigation is continuing. Don't spread rumors and don't listen to rumours." The cause was an air conditioner gas explosion, and @BallariSp has already visited, and an investigation is continuing. Don't spread rumors and don't listen to rumours, https://t.co/16ANMApSRU — ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ರಾಜ್ಯ ಪೊಲೀಸ್ Karnataka State Police (@KarnatakaCops) May 3, 2024
The cause was an air conditioner gas explosion, and @BallariSp has already visited, and an investigation is continuing. Don't spread rumors and don't listen to rumours, https://t.co/16ANMApSRU — ಕರ್ನಾಟಕ ರಾಜ್ಯ ಪೊಲೀಸ್ Karnataka State Police (@KarnatakaCops) May 3, 2024
 We got in touch with the Bellary's Superintendent of Police Ranjit Kumar Bandaru, who rubbished the claims of a terror link in this incident. "Air conditioning repair work was going on in the store. Technicians were refilling gas in it. Suddenly, the cylinder being used to refill gas exploded. Five people have been injured in this incident. A case has been registered against the Kalyan Jewelers store and the concerned AC service center," he told India Today.

title: Fact Check: Karnataka Congress workers DIDN'T burn themselves while setting Modi effigy on fire
content:
The 2012 video is from Pathanamthitta, Kerala, and shows Kerala Students Union activists protesting against the vice chancellor of MG University.
A video making the rounds  on social media purports to show Karnataka Congress workers accidentally setting themselves on fire while attempting to burn Prime Minister Narendra Modi in effigy.
Sharing the video, an X user wrote , "Lungi of five Congressmen caught fire while burning Modi's effigy in Karnataka! See how all this happened. Now Modi ji's effigies have also started teaching a lesson. This is Modi ji power." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today found that this 2012 video from Kerala shows student activists burning the effigy of MG University's vice-chancellor. Our Probe
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook post  containing the same video but of better quality, dated September 1, 2012. The post claimed that the clip was from Kerala. We also observed shop signages written in Malayalam in this video.
As per the report, Kerala Student Union workers were burning the vice chancellor of MG University in effigy, and while doing so, their clothes also caught fire. In the video, the protesters can also be seen carrying KSU flags. We also found a Times of India report  from July 2012 that noted students were protesting the vice chancellor of MG University over alleged corruption charges. The report added that some protesters were injured in the fire and were hospitalised.
We also found a Times of India report  from July 2012 that noted students were protesting the vice chancellor of MG University over alleged corruption charges. The report added that some protesters were injured in the fire and were hospitalised.
Thus, it's more than clear that a 12-year-old video of student protests from Kerala was falsely shared as an anti-Modi protest by the Congress in Karnataka. Â - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: May 6, 2024 18:43 IST

title: Fact Check: Another Alia Bhatt deepfake! Face of actor added over Wamiqa Gabbi's
content:
This is a deepfake video. The original video features actor Wamiqa Gabbi, not Alia Bhatt.
On May 7, Alia Bhatt dazzled Met Gala attendees in New York in a Sabyasachi saree . Meanwhile, another video of the actor, this time in a red saree, caught several eyes on social media. Shared from an Instagram account called Unifixface , this video featured Bhatt posing for what appeared to be a photo shoot.
The post's caption read, "Alia Bhatt off-screen," along with hashtags like "trending reels", "trending", "viral", and "alia bhatt". Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found this video is a deepfake. Alia Bhatt's face was digitally added over the video of actor Wamiqa Gabbi. THE REAL VIDEO
A simple reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the verified Instagram account of Wamiqa Gabbi , an actor, who debuted with a small role in the Imtiaz Ali flick "Jab We Met", and has since worked in movies like "83" and shows like "Jubilee". The original video of the photo shoot, which did not feature Alia Bhatt, was shared by Gabbi on April 27 with the caption: "Your Premiqa is indeed a Chamkila fan."     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Wamiqa Gabbi (@wamiqagabbi)
A post shared by Wamiqa Gabbi (@wamiqagabbi)
A comparison between different keyframes from both videos makes it clear that the Bhatt version is nothing but a deepfake.
We also observed that the Instagram account Unifixface, which shared Bhatt's video, shares other deepfake videos regularly, usually featuring Alia Bhatt in most of them. While many such deepfake videos often feature hashtags like " AI " or " transition ", most of them do not include the proper context.Â
It is also noteworthy that the bio of this account  mentions that it is for editing works and that the videos are for entertainment purposes only. However, a lack of proper context in posts may leave viewers confused or mistaken.Â
This is also not the first time Alia Bhatt has been a victim of a deepfake video. In November last year , the actor's face was incorporated into a video of another woman, making various gestures on camera. - Ends Published By: Karishma Saurabh Kalita Published On: May 7, 2024 22:24 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOESN'T show Rahul Gandhi visiting Ram Mandir after Raebareli nomination
content:
The viral video is from February 3, and shows Rahul Gandhi visiting Baba Baidyanath Dham in Jharkhand's Deoghar during his Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra.
Former Congress leader Acharya Pramod Krishnam on May 6 accused Rahul Gandhi of planning to overturn the Supreme Court verdict of the construction of Ayodhya's Ram Mandir "once voted to power". Amid these allegations, a video of Rahul Gandhi donning a pink dhoti and stole, tilak on his forehead, and a garland on his neck, seemingly walking out of a temple is making the rounds on social media. In the clip, chants of "Modi Modi" and "Jai Shri Ram" can be heard.Â
Sharing the video, many claimed that the video showed people sloganeering against Rahul Gandhi as he visited Ayodhya's Ram Temple after his Raebareli nomination on May 3.Â
One person shared the video on Facebook  writing, "Seasonal Hindu Rahul Gandhi visits Ayodhya Ram Mandir after filing his nomination from Rae Bareli. Crowds chant Jai Sri Ram, shout Modi Modi." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from February 3, when Rahul visited Baba Baidyanath Dham in Jharkhand's Deoghar during the Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra.
We first looked for news reports about Rahul Gandhi visiting Ayodhya after his Raebareli nomination, but could not find any. We then reverse-searched keyframes of the viral video, which led us to a post dated February 3. According to it, the video showed Rahul Gandhi visiting a temple in Deoghar, a city in Jharkhand.
We then found a longer version of this video shared by ANI on February 3. It stated that Rahul Gandhi visited Deoghar's Baba Baidyanath Dham temple, where people raised slogans of "Narendra Modi Zindabad" and "Rahul Gandhi Zindabad". #WATCH | Slogans including "Narendra Modi Zindabad", "Rahul Gandhi Zindabad" raised by some people during Congress MP Rahul Gandhi's visit to Baba Baidyanath Dham temple, in Deoghar, Jharkhand pic.twitter.com/FEInvJOLfV — ANI (@ANI) February 3, 2024
#WATCH | Slogans including "Narendra Modi Zindabad", "Rahul Gandhi Zindabad" raised by some people during Congress MP Rahul Gandhi's visit to Baba Baidyanath Dham temple, in Deoghar, Jharkhand pic.twitter.com/FEInvJOLfV — ANI (@ANI) February 3, 2024
Per reports , Rahul Gandhi visited Baba Baidyanath Dham in Deoghar on February 3 during his Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra in Jharkhand. The march began in Manipur on January 14 and entered Jharkhand on February 2. In Deoghar, Gandhi performed "Rudrabhishek" at a temple. There, people chanted "Modi Modi" and "Modi Zindabad" in front of the Congress leader . Videos  and photos  of his visit to Deoghar were shared by many Congress leaders at the time. हर हर महादेव 🔱 pic.twitter.com/83XVv1INie — Supriya Shrinate (@SupriyaShrinate) February 3, 2024
हर हर महादेव 🔱 pic.twitter.com/83XVv1INie — Supriya Shrinate (@SupriyaShrinate) February 3, 2024
India Today also contacted Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate, who confirmed that Gandhi did not visit the Ayodhya Ram Mandir following his Raebareli nomination. She said, "After his nomination, he flew for a rally in Pune. Wherever he has gone is publicly available on the social media handle of Congress."
It is noteworthy that after his nomination, Rahul Gandhi visited the Lalbai Fulbai temple in Madhya Pradesh's Khargone on May 6. However, there are no reports of people sloganeering against him during this visit. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: May 8, 2024 15:54 IST

title: Fact Check: This video is from 2019 and DOESN'T show soldiers promoting BJP at poll booths
content:
This video dates back to 2019. The Army at the time clarified that miscreants obstructed soldiers from casting their votes in MP's Jabalpur.
A video of soldiers being publicly called out for allegedly asking people to vote for the Bharatiya Janata Party has been widely shared. In it, a man in a white shirt can be seen interrogating soldiers standing beside a military vehicle.Â
The man in a white shirt said, "They were asking people to press button number 1 to ensure BJP's victory." The man recording the video then said, "They were promoting the BJP inside the polling booth." They also accused the soldiers of bringing people to cast proxy votes, adding that when the general public objected, they (the soldiers) had to run away. Â
Those sharing the video used hashtags like "BIG BREAKING" and "LokSabhaElection2024". An X user wrote , "Indian Army Tarnished by Modi & His Sanghi Gang. The Army is being used by the #BJP to cast Fake Votes. The Indian Army has been assigned the task of carrying out illegal and fraudulent work for the BJP. Caught red-handed inside Election booth for influencing voters to cast Fake Votes for #BJP." Its archivecan be seen here .Â
India Today found that the video in question dates back to 2019 and has nothing to do with the ongoing elections. At that time, the Indian Army filed a complaint against the people who created this video, alleging that they were trying to defame it. The complaint stated that people also tried to stop some soldiers posted at the Jabalpur cantonment from casting their votes.  Â
We observed "Jabalpur" written on the army vehicle seen in the viral video. Some social media users also pointed out  that this incident from Madhya Pradesh's Jabalpur happened in 2019.Â
Based on these clues, a keyword search led us to an ANI post on X from May 1, 2019. Per this tweet, army officials in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, filed a complaint against unidentified miscreants for trying to snatch voter ID cards of general voters, obstructing soldiers from voting, and circulating videos to defame the Indian Army. Army officials in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, have filed a complaint against unidentified miscreants for trying to snatch voter ID cards of general voters, obstructing Army voters posted in Cantonment there and circulating videos to malign Army image, on April 29. pic.twitter.com/ByXwNR4EHz — ANI (@ANI) May 1, 2019
Army officials in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, have filed a complaint against unidentified miscreants for trying to snatch voter ID cards of general voters, obstructing Army voters posted in Cantonment there and circulating videos to malign Army image, on April 29. pic.twitter.com/ByXwNR4EHz — ANI (@ANI) May 1, 2019
According to this complaint, this incident happened on April 29, 2019, when soldiers and their spouses of the Grenadiers Regimental Centre went to cast their votes at Booth No 146 at the Swamy Vivekananda Higher Secondary School in Katanga, Jabalpur.Â
The Times of India reported this incident , and The Quint fact-checked  a similar viral claim at the time as well.Â
The Quint report contained an Indian Army statement that said that the soldiers "rung up Commandant when they were videographed and he told them not to get into any altercation and exercise their right of franchise and get back peacefully", adding that a "total of 1,386 application for all ranks and dependents were applied from the Centre to ECI as General Voter ID Cards, out of which, 1304 voted today". The Army also clarified that the heavy vehicles seen in the video were provided to facilitate the movement of troops and families to vote.Â
In light of the video going viral again amid the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, the Indian Amry issued another statement: "In the light of recent Lok Sabha Elections, an old video of year 2019 is being circulated on Social Medial Platforms with a malicious intent to defame Indian Army. The video is of last elections wherein troops from The Regimental Centre had collectively gone to cast their votes. This was propaganda spread by a few persons at that time."
The statement further said, "Necessary rebuttal was issued post investigating the facts. The video has again resurfaced backed and being circulated with malicious intent. Everyone is requested not to pay attention to this message as the same may lead to projection of incorrect image of the Army."
Thus, it is clear that the viral claim is false. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: May 8, 2024 19:10 IST

title: Fact Check: UAE, not UP! Dubai clip viral as Noida's development
content:
The second clip in the viral video is from Dubai, not Noida in Uttar Pradesh.
A video that's been widely shared on social media purports to show how Noida in Uttar Pradesh has developed in the last decade. It shows two aerial shots of a city, one allegedly from 2015 and the other from 2024. Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that while the first shot shows Noida, the second video clip is actually from Dubai. OUR PROBE
The first clip, allegedly shot in 2015, shows a highway junction. We compared it to similar areas in Noida on Google Maps and found the exact location: the Noida-Greater Noida Link Road. Several features visible in the video are there in the satellite image.Â
A comparison of the Google Maps satellite image  and a screenshot from the viral video clip can be seen below:
We reverse-searched grabs from the second clip in the viral video. We discovered that similar visuals have been shared as sights from Dubai in various posts .Â
Although these posts did not specify which part of Dubai they showed, we observed a distinctive building roof in the video, with a metro line passing underneath. We looked at various Dubai metro station buildings and found one that appeared very similar to the viral video.Â
We geolocated the metro station shown in the viral video as the Mashreq Metro Station on Sheikh Zayed Road, Dubai. We confirmed the location through street view and by examining nearby places and constructions.Â
A comparison of screenshots from the viral video and Google Maps  can be seen below:
Thus, it is clear that the video doesn't show Noida's development in the last decade as one video is not from India at all! - Ends (Written by Deenadayal Kalarikkal) Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: May 9, 2024 22:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video falsely shared as protest in Sweden against Israel's Eurovision participation
content:
This video has nothing to do with the ongoing protests in Sweden. It shows an anti-Israel protest staged at a Sweden tennis match back in 2009.
Thousands of pro-Palestinian demonstrators, along with Climate activist Greta Thunberg, gathered in the Swedish city of Malmo to protest  against Israel's participation in the Eurovision Song Contest on May 9. Singer Eden Golan from Israel had qualified for Eurovision's grand finale , scheduled for May 1, amid heightened security.
Now, a video of several masked men hurling smoke bombs and vandalising police vehicles is going viral on social media . These men could be seen throwing bricks at the vehicles and attacking those attempting to intervene.
Those sharing the video  claimed that it shows the Eurovision protesters in Malmo resorting to violence  and damaging public property in Sweden. One person shared the video on Threads, and wrote, "Hamas supporters tried to attack an Israeli singer at Eurovision. They had rope." An archived version of one such post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video has no connection to the ongoing protests in Sweden. Instead, it shows an anti-Israel protest staged during a Sweden tennis match in 2009.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a media report  dated March 7, 2009. It contained a screenshot of the video in question. According to the report, dozens of anti-Israel protesters clashed with police outside the Baltic Arena in Malmo, Sweden. The protesters reportedly attempted to storm the stadium where the home country was playing a Davis Cup tennis match against Israel.
Davis Cup , or the World Cup of Tennis, is the world's largest annual team sporting competition.
We also found the full video of the violent protest, in which the viral clip could be seen at the beginning.
Per reports , hundreds of left-wing activists joined the pro-Palestinian demonstration of about 6,000 people and began hurling stones, fireworks, and paint bombs at police vans. About a thousand police officials were deployed in Malmo to prevent the protesters from entering the stadium, using barricades and truncheons to push the rioters back. The protesters wanted to disrupt  the match, which was reportedly being played without any fans in Malmo due to security concerns.
The match went ahead as planned amid heavy protests outside the arena. Police reportedly arrested eight protesters and detained more than a hundred others. No injuries were reported in the incident.
It is thus clear that an old video from 2009 is being falsely linked to the ongoing protest in Sweden against Israel's participation in Eurovision. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: May 10, 2024 17:27 IST

title: Fact Check: This Aaj Tak show about doctor being attacked on air is a DEEPFAKE
content:
India Today found the video to be fake. Unrelated videos were edited with voice cloning technology and an Aaj Tak logo was added to give it credibilty.
A video featuring the Aaj Tak logo purports to show a news segment, where a news anchor explains that a doctor was assaulted during a news debate by a fellow panelist. The video shows the assault and then cuts to the doctor in question speaking about the attack, and then claiming he had developed a new heart medicine that would help prevent cardiovascular diseases.
A Facebook user, sharing the viral video , wrote, "Shocking incident of attack on Dr Deviprasad Shetty, famous cardiologist. Please make it viral. He should be shot dead." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video was fake. There is no record of a Dr Devi Shetty being attacked during a live show. The voices of both, the news anchor and the doctor, were altered. OUR PROBE
A search online revealed that the anchor in the viral video is India TV's Prachi Parashar — not an Aaj Tak or India Today anchor. Â
We observed that the words spoken by either the anchor or the doctor did not sync with their lip movements. This hinted at the audio having been digitally manipulated, likely using AI tools.
We then reverse-searched keyframes from the brawl shown in the viral video, which led to the original clip shared by the YouTube channel of News Nation. The January 13, 2017 video featured the controversial religious figure and former "Bigg Boss" contestant Swami Om getting into a fight during a television debate. Dr Devi Shetty was not mentioned in the YouTube video even once.
When we reverse-searched keyframes from the segment of the viral video that featured the doctor speaking about his new medicine, we found an NDTV Profit interview from November 24, 2022, titled: "BQ Exclusive: Dr. Devi Shetty on Health, Heart & Healing."Â
In this interview, Dr Shetty discussed several health-related topics like cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, lack of doctors and health insurance. But, there was no mention of pharmaceutical companies or an endorsement of any medication as shown in the viral video. We also searched the internet to verify if Dr Shetty had endorsed any medicine for cardiovascular diseases, but it didn't yield any results suggesting the same.
Thus, it's clear that this is not a real news segment at all. The Aaj Tak logo was added to unrelated videos where the speakers' voices were manipulated to present a false narrative.
Update: An earlier version of this story did not feature the anchor's name. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: May 12, 2024 15:33 IST

title: Fact Check: 'PoK'-ing holes in the Tiranga story - Indian flag NOT waved at Pak protests
content:
The viral image from Rawalakot was edited to add the Indian flag. The Tricolour was not raised during protests in PoK.
Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, or PoK, has been witnessing widespread and violent protests against rising inflation in the country and the Shahbaz Sharif government's economic policies since May 10. But are protestors going so far as to wave the Indian flag  at these rallies to voice their anger against the regime? A photo going viral right now purports to show just that.
An X user claimed : "The Indian flag was hoisted in Rawalkot (POJK), Pakistan Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, during a protest against the Pakistan Army and Police." The same photo was shared by many on Instagram  and Facebook  with similar claims. Their archives can be seen here , here , here , and here .
Indian media outlets like News Nation , Punjab Kesari , and Gujarati Mid-Day  also published reports about the Indian flag being raised in PoK during ongoing protests. And outlets like Wion  and Siasat Daily  used the viral image while reporting about the protests.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral image from Rawalakot was edited — the Indian flag was overlaid digitally. The Indian flag was not waved at the rally in PoK.
Here's how we reached this conclusion: CONFIRMING THE PHOTO'S LOCATION
While trying to locate the origin of the viral photo with the Tricolour in it, we discovered that the photo was flipped horizontally. Many X users, responding to the viral posts, also pointed this out while sharing the original photo . Often, images or videos are flipped or laterally inverted to make them harder to reverse-search. A mirrored image for third class projection and reach. Here is the original one. pic.twitter.com/0lRMWDUsyc — Jeem Alif (@juneerulz) May 11, 2024 We confirmed that the photo was flipped by closely examining the text visible in it: an autorickshaw had "BAZGAR" written on its back in the original photo. The letters Z and G can be seen laterally inverted in the viral image. A comparison between the two photos can be seen below. PHOTO LEADS TO BANK ROAD IN POK'S RAWALAKOT A keyword search in Urdu about the ongoing protests in PoK led us to a Facebook reel  from May 12, which contained visuals from multiple demonstrations. The video at the top left corner appeared similar to the viral image. It also featured the text: "Rawalakot Tourism Hotel". Rawalakot is the capital of the Poonch district in PoK. A comparison between this video and the photo makes it clear this is the same location. While searching for the Rawalakot Tourism Hotel on Google Maps, we found another nearby hotel called Green Valley located on the same road. On the Google Maps page for this hotel, a user shared a video in 2023. This video further confirms its location as Rawalakot's Bank Road. WHEN DID THIS PROTEST TAKE PLACE? India Today Fact Check spoke to Waqar Khan, the proprietor of the Kashmir General Store at Bank Road in Rawalakot about the viral photo. He said that demonstrations happened in front of his shop on May 10. Khan refuted any claims about the Indian flag being raised during this rally. We found a May 10 Facebook post  and a video uploaded on May 11  covering the same protest. It is important to note that neither had the Indian flag in them, confirming what Waqar Khan told India Today. NO PAK MEDIA REPORTS ABOUT TIRANGA Raising the Indian flag during an anti-government protest in PoK would cause the flutter and would surely be covered by the Pakistani media. And while the protests were covered widely by the country's news outlets, we could not find any mention of the Indian flag. Incidentally, many Pakistani news reports  used the original photo (which did not feature the Indian flag). advertisement Additionally, Jabbar Chaudhary, the executive editor of Pakistan-based news outlet Samaa TV told India Today Fact Check: "The image being shared over social media is totally fabricated. The Indian flag was not hoisted in Rawalakot or other parts of PoK. There are ongoing protests in Kashmir, but no one has taken such extreme steps." PHOTO FORENSICS REVEALS MANIPULATION We used the InVid tool to check for manipulation in the viral image. As you can see in the GIF below, the light-green-coloured marks indicate the areas where the photo was doctored. This is exactly where the Indian flag could be seen in the viral image. This makes it amply clear that the Indian Tricolour was photoshopped into a PoK protest to give it an Indian connection. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: May 13, 2024 20:07 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral post mixes two separate cases from 2018 to fuel communal narrative in Bengal
content:
The image is related to a 2018 Bhopal incident where a Hindu man called Rohit Singh held a Hindu woman hostage for several hours.
A post going viral on social media right now alleges that a Muslim man called Sultan Shaikh killed his Hindu fiancee Shubhalagna and injured her parents in West Bengal's Howrah after his "false Hindu identity was discovered. The post featured a photo of a man and a woman, with the latter's face blurred. The photo and the news were credited to ABP News. The archive of such a post can be seen here .Â
India Today found that the photo shows a Hindu man called Rohit Singh who held a Hindu woman hostage for several in 2018 in Madhya Pradesh's Bhopal. However, the same year in West Bengal's Hooghly district, a man called Sheikh Sultan had killed a woman named Shubhalagna. OUR PROBE
Many people responded to the viral posts pointing out that the image was related to a 2018 incident from Bhopal. Reverse-searching the photo led us to a July 14, 2018 report by the Navbharat Times . According to it, in Bhopal's Misrod area, a man called Rohit forcefully entered the apartment of a woman called Vibha Srivastav and held her hostage for hours. The ordeal went on for about 12 hours, after which Rohit was arrested.Â
According to The Times of India , the accused, Rohit Singh aka Regal, allegedly stabbed the woman and locked himself in her bedroom. Reportedly, he threatened her to marry him. The hostage was later rescued and admitted to a hospital. Â
Many news outlets had reported this incident in 2018 and all named the accused as Rohit Singh. As per a report by Patrika , the woman who was held hostage later demanded strict punishment for Rohit claiming that he had motives to kill her and her family.Â
We contacted Rahul Kumar Lodha, currently serving as the superintendent of police in Ratlam, who was posted in Bhopal in 2018 and was present at the spot when this incident happened. He told India Today Fact Check that both the accused and the victim in this case were Hindus. He said, "I spoke to the accused Rohit for around four hours to convince him to open the door. Rohit, a resident of Uttar Pradesh had befriended that girl (victim) in Mumbai. There was some dispute between them, following which she came back to Misrod and the said incident happened."Â
He added, "The girl had visited me with her mother a few days after this incident," which disproves the claim of the woman being murdered. THE SHEIKH SULTAN AND SHUBHALAGNA STORY
Using a keyword search, we found a July 2018 report  by Business Standard that said a 35-year-old woman named Shubhalagna was shot dead by her "jilted lover" Sheikh Sultan, who also beat up her parents in West Bengal's Hooghly district.
We also shared the viral post with Partha Sikdar, the additional commissioner of police at the Uttar Para Police Station, who told India Today, "This incident happened in July 2018. Sultan was convicted and was sent to lifetime imprisonment. I don't have any idea about the people in the viral post."  - Ends (With inputs from Riddhish Dutta) Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: May 13, 2024 21:58 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of man alleging voter suppression is from Bhopal, NOT Uttar Pradesh
content:
The video was shot in the Narela ward of Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh, during the third phase of voting — not in Uttar Pradesh.
The fourth phase of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections saw several videos alleging voter suppression being widely shared on social media. One such video shows a man alleging Bharatiya Janata Party members halted voting at his centre and the police did not intervene. The video shows many burqa-clad women present at the scene.
Those sharing this clip alleged that it was from Uttar Pradesh. A Facebook user  wrote, "Voting is being stopped in Uttar Pradesh because Muslims are voting more and more. Look at the situation here, how democracy is being murdered." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral clip is from Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh, not Uttar Pradesh.Â
In the comments of one of the viral posts, some claimed that the man in the video was Isa Ahmad. We searched for this person on social media and found a Facebook account, whose display picture matched the person in the viral video. India Today Fact Check contacted Ahmad using the mobile number on his Facebook profile, who confirmed he was the man in the clip.
A local journalist, Ahmad called the viral posts false and clarified that the incident did not occur in Uttar Pradesh but in the Narela ward of Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh. Bhopal went to polls in the third phase of the Lok Sabha polls on May 7.Â
Speaking to India Today Fact Check, Ahmad alleged that BJP workers disrupted voting at booth number 194 at the NM Convent School after sensing a high turnout of Muslim voters. He said that these workers alleged fake voting and insisted on halting the polling until a woman constable could verify the identity of the burqa-clad women.Â
Consequently, election officers stopped polling, stating it would only recommence after the sub-divisional magistrate's inspection. Ahmad said that it was after this that he recorded the viral video. He added that following the SDM's visit, polling resumed within 20-25 minutes. Geolocating the polling booth
We located NM Convent School in Bhopal on Google Maps . Photos tagged to the location matched visuals from the viral video, as seen in the comparison below.
While verifying the viral video's allegations of voter suppression is beyond the scope of India Today Fact Check, it is nonetheless clear that this incident is not from UP at all. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: May 14, 2024 22:44 IST

title: Fact Check: Was Shreyas Iyer dropped for refusing to shake PM's hand? Nope, viral video is edited
content:
This video is clipped. Iyer shook hands with PM Modi in the original video.
Despite a tremendous run at the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup with more than 500 runs, Kolkata Knight Riders skipper Shreyas Iyer was excluded  from the annual contract of the BCCI in February. Now, a video going viral on social media claims to show him refusing to shake hands with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, with those sharing it  alleging this was why he was dropped.Â
An X user wrote: "Remember when Indian cricketer Shreyas Iyer had refused to shake hands with Modi after CWC Final? He was later dropped from BCCI central contact by Jay Shah. Today he has followed Dhruv Rathee on Instagram  One of the very few cricketers with a spine, Shreyas Iyer." The archive version of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that Iyer shook hands with the prime minister, but that part was edited out in the viral video. OUR PROBE
After India's heartbreak at the World Cup Finals, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah paid a visit to the dressing room of the Indian team. They reportedly consoled the players and also praised their performance throughout the campaign.Â
With the help of a search with keywords, we found the complete video of the PM's interaction with the players on the official YouTube channel of Narendra Modi . Uploaded on November 21, 2023, the caption of this video reads, "PM Modi Meets the Men in Blue, Comforts Indian Cricket Team After World Cup Final." Here, the PM could be seen consoling the Indian players and the support staff.
Uploaded on November 21, 2023, the caption of this video reads, "PM Modi Meets the Men in Blue, Comforts Indian Cricket Team After World Cup Final." Here, the PM could be seen consoling the Indian players and the support staff.
At the 1 minute 20 seconds mark in the viral video, the PM could be seen shaking hands with Indian middle-order batter Shreyas Iyer, followed by Suryakumar Yadav, Kuldeep Yadav, and KL Rahul. This frame can be seen below.Â
The reason behind Shreyas Iyer's exclusion from the BCCI's annual contract remains foggy. According to some reports , Iyer and Ishan Kishan's contracts were axed for not playing in the Ranji Trophy. The top cricket body also issued a statement  which noted, "The BCCI has recommended that all athletes give precedence to participating in domestic cricket during periods when they are not representing the national team."Â
It's noteworthy that various screenshots going viral on social media claim to show the cricketer had followed YouTuber Dhruv Rathee on Instagram. However, at the time of writing this on May 15, Iyer's following list did not feature Rathee's name.Â
Regardless, it is abundantly clear that he never refused to shake hands with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: May 15, 2024 20:25 IST

title: Fact Check: No 'Pallywood', this 2018 video shows a medical drill in Gaza
content:
The video does not show Gazans faking injuries during the ongoing conflict but rather depicts a medical exercise conducted by the Islamic University in the Gaza Strip back in 2018.
The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees  stated that amid Israel's bombing of Rafah, about 3,60,000 Palestinians fled the city.
Now, pro-Israel accounts on social media are sharing a video alleging crisis actors are pretending to be injured Gazans.Â
Sharing the video, an Instagram user wrote, "And the award for worst performance goes to Hamas. This is the kind of lies and propaganda Israel is up against. Just ask the UN who just brought half the women and children killed in the war back to life. And they expect the world to trust the news. Israel has the most moral army in the world."     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by MELISSA MAYO - Food Network Chef (@themelissamayo)
A post shared by MELISSA MAYO - Food Network Chef (@themelissamayo)
India Today Fact Check found that the video shows a medical exercise conducted by the Islamic University in the Gaza Strip in 2018. It is unrelated to the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the video, we came across a Facebook post by the Islamic University in the Gaza Strip from March 11, 2018. The post detailed that a medical exercise was conducted by the university's Faculty of Medicine on Medical Awareness Day. Visuals from the post matched those in the viral video, with the two injured men seen in both clips wearing the same clothing. Further search led us to another Facebook video of the same exercise from March 2018. This video documented the entire exercise and showed university representatives and faculty explaining its objective of raising medical awareness. Participants simulated injuries with fake blood and even lighting their clothes on fire. Additionally, we found a report from the local news outlet called "Palestinian Online" dating March 12, 2018. It stated that the exercise was aimed to recreate scenes from past attacks on Gaza as part of Medical Awareness Day. It further noted that the University's College of Medicine conducted the exercise in collaboration with the Hayat Centre for Training in Emergency and Crisis Management. In conclusion, the video in question, falsely linked to the ongoing conflict, really depicts an old medical exercise conducted by the Islamic University in Gaza. Claims of Gazans faking injuries during the current conflict were unfounded. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: May 15, 2024 21:20 IST

title: Fact Check: These clips DON'T show Lucknow Super Giants owner Sanjiv Goenka apologising to KL Rahul
content:
These videos are old and have nothing to do with this incident.
After the Lucknow Super Giants' defeat against the Sunrisers Hyderabad in the current season of the Indian Premier League on May 8, a video allegedly showing the former's owner Sanjiv Goenka publicly scolding team captain KL Rahul went viral.Â
As social media debated and dissected this video, two other videos purporting to show the owner now apologising to the captain cropped up. But do these videos actually show that? Let's look at them one at a time. THE FIRST VIDEO
One video  shows Sanjiv Goenka saying, "All the fans, to the players, to the coach, and the entire coaching staff," before the video switches to a voiceover that says he apologised to KL Rahul and others. The video was shared with claims like, "Sanjiv Goenka apologises to KL Rahul and the supporting staff of Lucknow Super Giants !! Great Gesture." Its archive can be seen here .Â
Using a keyword search, we found that this video was first shared on the official X account of the Mohun Bagan Super Giant football club on April 15. Goenka is the chairman of this club. In the video, Goenka can be heard saying that it was a historic day as Mohun Bagan had won the league trophy for the first time. Warm wishes coming in from our Chairman Dr Sanjiv Goenka! 💚♥️ #MBSG #JoyMohunBagan #আমরাসবুজমেরুন #ISL10 pic.twitter.com/mo0qR0QppS — Mohun Bagan Super Giant (@mohunbagansg) April 15, 2024
Warm wishes coming in from our Chairman Dr Sanjiv Goenka! 💚♥️ #MBSG #JoyMohunBagan #আমরাসবুজমেরুন #ISL10 pic.twitter.com/mo0qR0QppS — Mohun Bagan Super Giant (@mohunbagansg) April 15, 2024
According to the official website of the Indian Super League , Mohun Bagan defeated the Mumbai City Football Club to win its first ever League shield on April 15. Thus, it's clear that this video has nothing to do with KL Rahul. THE SECOND VIDEO
In the second video , Goenka can be heard saying, "Anyone who knows the stand, that we are going to play to win. So, you will see an approach of wanting to win in any game. Believe in us, back us, we won't disappoint you." Its archive can be seen here .Â
We found that this clip was first shared by Sanjiv Goenka's official Instagram account on December 19, 2023, the day when the 2024 Indian Premier League actions were held in Dubai . The video was shared with hashtags like "#LucknowSuperGiants" and "#IPLAuction".     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Lucknow Super Giants (@lucknowsupergiants)
A post shared by Lucknow Super Giants (@lucknowsupergiants)
Thus, it's clear that this video too is unrelated. GOENKA AND KL RAHUL
As per a Times of India report  Sanjiv Goenka hosted KL Rahul for dinner on May 13 and a picture of him hugging Rahul on the occasion was widely shared. However, we did not find any video of Goenka apologising to Rahul. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: May 16, 2024 16:36 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show Afghan forces shooting down a Pakistani chopper
content:
This video is not from Afghanistan or Pakistan. It shows a Kurdish militant shooting down a Turkish helicopter in May 2016.
A video  making the rounds on social media purports to show an Afghani soldier shooting down a Pakistani chopper using a shoulder-fired missile. #WATCH | Afghan forces shot down Pakistan Army Helicopter along the disputed Durand line in Kurram. #Afghanistan #Pakistan pic.twitter.com/q0sUGOcHEb — MR Obito (@MrObito777) May 15, 2024
#WATCH | Afghan forces shot down Pakistan Army Helicopter along the disputed Durand line in Kurram. #Afghanistan #Pakistan pic.twitter.com/q0sUGOcHEb — MR Obito (@MrObito777) May 15, 2024
The video shows the missile striking the helicopter's tail, causing it to spin out of control, explode, and plunge to the ground. An X user wrote with sharing it: "Breaking News‌. Afghan forces shot down Pakistan Army Helicopter along the disputed Durand line in Kurram." The archive of a similar Facebook post  can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is eight years old and shows a militant group taking down a Turkish army helicopter. OUR PROBE
We found no credible news reports about any recent attack on a Pakistani chopper by Afghan forces. However, a Reuters report  noted that a helicopter used by the Afghanistan army crashed while attempting an emergency landing in central Afghanistan on May 15, killing one person and injuring 12.Â
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Mirror UK report  dated May 24, 2016, which featured the same video. According to the report, it showed a Kurdistan Workers' Party or PKK militant launching an attack on a Turkish army helicopter. The PKK is a militia group that operates in Iran, Iraq, Syria, and Turkey — it's been designated a terrorist organisation in the latter.Â
We also found a Washington Post report  from May 14, 2016, which mentioned that the attack took place in the mountains of southeastern Turkey.Â
The Washington Post reported that Turkish officials initially attributed this helicopter crash in the Hakkari province to a technical failure. However, they refused to comment after the video of this attack was uploaded to the YouTube channel Gerilla TV, reportedly affiliated with the militant group. Although the video has since been deleted, its archive can be seen here .
Thus, it is evident that an old video from Turkey was falsely shared as Afghan forces taking down a Pakistani helicopter. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: May 16, 2024 18:49 IST

title: Fact Check: This ISN'T Iranian President's crashed helicopter, these photos are 4 years old
content:
These photos show a 2020 training plane crash in Iran, not the Ebrahim Raisi helicopter crash.
Iranian state media confirmed that Iran's President Ebrahim Raisi, Foreign Minister Hossein Amirabdollahian, and other senior officials died in a helicopter crash on May 19 . Raisi was reportedly returning from his visit to Azerbaijan when the helicopter crashed near Jolfa, a city on the border with Azerbaijan. Now photos going viral claim to show the debris from this crash. In this story, we will debunk two such photos: advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story THE FIRST PHOTO: Sharing this picture, an X user wrote , "Many Bodies of those who died in the Iran President Raisi helicopter crash have been burnt and cannot be identified." Its archive can be seen here . A reverse search led to Iranian media reports published in April 2020 that contained the viral picture. As per Jahan news , the image shows a training plane flying from Bisheh Kolah to Tehran. It crashed near Mutalaq (Salman Shahr) and the wreckage was found in Iran's Kila Kala Abbas Abad area. The plane reportedly crashed during a police operation due to adverse weather conditions. The report was published in the Persian year 1399, which is the same as the year 2020. Currently, only Iran and Afghanistan follow the Persian calendar.Â
Sharing this picture, an X user wrote , "Many Bodies of those who died in the Iran President Raisi helicopter crash have been burnt and cannot be identified." Its archive can be seen here .
A reverse search led to Iranian media reports published in April 2020 that contained the viral picture. As per Jahan news , the image shows a training plane flying from Bisheh Kolah to Tehran. It crashed near Mutalaq (Salman Shahr) and the wreckage was found in Iran's Kila Kala Abbas Abad area. The plane reportedly crashed during a police operation due to adverse weather conditions.Â
The report was published in the Persian year 1399, which is the same as the year 2020. Currently, only Iran and Afghanistan follow the Persian calendar.Â
We also found several other local media reports published around the same time that said the viral photo showed the crash in Kila Kala Abbas Abad. The screenshot of such a news report can be seen below along with the date it was published. THE SECOND PHOTO Another photo of what appears to be a crashed aircraft's wreckage was widely shared on social media linking to the Iranian president's helicopter crash. The viral post's archive can be seen here . A reverse search of this photo as well led us to news reports about the 2020 plane crash mentioned above. We found this in a report published in 2020 on the official website of the Mizan News Agency. As per the report , the wreckage of the plane was found in the Kila Kala Abbas Abad area. Thus, it's clear that both photos going viral are unrelated to Ebrahim Raisi's helicopter crash. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar.) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: May 20, 2024 19:39 IST

title: Fact Check: 6-year-old video VIRAL as RCB fans harassing CSK supporters
content:
This video is from 2018 and shows Saravanan Hari, a Dhoni fan, being attacked in Chennai.
In the ongoing Indian Premier League season, Chennai Super Kings' fans accused Royal Challengers Bengaluru fans of harassment after CSK lost to RCB on May 18. Now, a video of people chasing and hitting a man with yellow body paint and "Dhoni" written on his chest has gone viral on social media.Â
Allegedly, the video shows RCB fans misbehaving with CSK fans. Those sharing it used hashtags like "IPL2024" "CSK" and "RCB". Archives of two such posts can be seen here and here and here .Â
India Today found that this video is from April 2018.Â
Many X users pointed out in response to these viral posts that this video dates back to 2018. A subsequent keyword search led us to a video shared by the Times Of India Plus on X on April 12, 2018. Per the post, Saravanan Hari, a big MS Dhoni fan, was beaten up outside Chepauk Stadium in Chennai. Saravanan Hari, one of @msdhoni 's biggest fans was beaten up outside Chepauk on Tuesday. We also found other media reports about this incident. News Nation included portions of this video in its report about Cauvery protestors attacking Chennai Super King supporters. The people who assaulted me should know I am a Tamilian like them," Sarvana said responding to the incident at the time, as per The News Minute.

According to a News18 report , the BCCI shifted Chennai Super Kings' remaining home games to Pune after the state administration expressed inability to ensure security.Â

title: Fact Check: NOT Singapore flight in turbulence! This scary clip is from 2019
content:
This is an old video of a flight headed from Kosovo to Switzerland hit by turbulence in 2019.
One passenger died and 30 were reported injured after a Singapore Airlines flight from London encountered severe turbulence on May 21. The Singapore-bound Boeing 777-300ER reportedly dropped 6,000 feet  in a matter of minutes, following which, it made an emergency landing in Bangkok.
In its aftermath, a video  allegedly shot from inside the flight went viral on social media. In it, passengers could be seen screaming as they rose and fell together. Many social media users along with media outlets like Zee News  shared this clip, claiming that it showed the Singapore flight in turbulence.
One person shared the video  writing, "Shocking Video of the moment of turbulence on the Singapore Airlines Boeing 777-300, flying from London to Singapore, which resulted in the death of one person and injuries to 30 others." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this is an old video from 2019.
Reverse searching keyframes of the viral clip led us to a news report about this incident from 2019. According to it, this footage was shot on June 16, 2019, on a flight headed from Pristina in Kosovo, to Basel in Switzerland. Per reports, violent turbulence caused the ALK Airlines Boeing 737's flight attendant to hit the plane's ceiling.
The terrifying footage was reportedly shot by Mirjeta Basha , one of the passengers aboard. In it, people could be seen quickly putting on their clothing and bracing themselves seconds before a forceful jolt rocked the aircraft. The turbulence then slammed a flight attendant into the ceiling and spilt her craft full of drinks. The aircraft, however, continued for a normal landing and no emergency was declared.
According to an ABC news report , 10 of the 121 passengers on board were hospitalised for minor injuries after the plane touched down at the airport in Basel, Switzerland. Several media outlets shared the video in question  at the time, reporting the same.
While media outlets have shared some visuals from the Singapore flight that was hit by turbulence, it is more than clear that the video in question has no links to it. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: May 21, 2024 23:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Israeli UN ambassador holding 'Butcher of Iran' sign is doctored
content:
Viral video is doctored. In the original video, shot in September 2023, the Israeli ambassador to the UN was holding a poster that read, "Iranian Women Deserve Freedom Now."
Members of the United Nations Security Council observed a moment of silence on May 20  in remembrance of the Iranian President Seyyed Ebrahim Raisi, Foreign Minister Hossein Amir-Abdollahian, and other officials who recently died in a helicopter accident. Israel's envoy to the UN called the gesture a "disgrace" , criticising the forum's alleged inadequate response towards the captivity of over 100 Israeli hostages in the Gaza Strip.
In the midst of this, a video of Israeli ambassador to the UN , Gilad Erdan, began making the rounds on social media , in which he can be seen holding a poster that reads: "The Butcher of Iran will not be missed." Many shared the video , claiming that Erdan held this placard condemning the moment of silence held by the UN Security Council for the late Iranian President. One person shared the video on Facebook  writing, "'Butcher of Iran will not be missed' The sign displayed by the Israeli ambassador to the UN. The Iranian President who had signed 1000's death warrants for simply an act of protest, or distribution of flyers, including girls and boys as young as 13 or 14, was killed in a helicopter crash." The archive of such a post can be seen here India Today Fact Check found that this is a doctored video. In the original video, shot in September 2023, the Israeli ambassador to the UN was holding a poster that read, "Iranian Women Deserve Freedom Now." Our Probe In some social media posts , which shared a screenshot of the viral video, we noticed the Instagram watermark of the account "Diplo.act". With this clue, we found this video shared on an Instagram account by the same username . Its caption stated that the video was edited.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by DiploAct (@diplo.act)
India Today Fact Check found that this is a doctored video. In the original video, shot in September 2023, the Israeli ambassador to the UN was holding a poster that read, "Iranian Women Deserve Freedom Now." Our Probe
In some social media posts , which shared a screenshot of the viral video, we noticed the Instagram watermark of the account "Diplo.act". With this clue, we found this video shared on an Instagram account by the same username . Its caption stated that the video was edited.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by DiploAct (@diplo.act)
A post shared by DiploAct (@diplo.act)
A subsequent search using relevant keywords led us to multiple media reports  from 2023 about this video. According to them, Israel's Ambassador to the UN, Gilad Erdan, staged a protest as Iran's President Ebrahim Raisi spoke at the UN General Assembly on September 19, 2023.
Erdan held up a placard with a picture of Mahsa Amini, who died in police custody in 2022 after being arrested in Tehran reportedly for not wearing a hijab "properly". The message on it read: "Iranian women deserve freedom now."
Following this, Erdan was escorted out of the UN General Assembly hall by the security officers. Some reports said at the time that he was detained by UN security personnel. However, a UN spokesperson refuted this , adding that the Israeli official had merely spoken with security, and that at no time was he detained.
Gildad Erdan himself shared a longer version of the video on September 20, 2023, on X, in which the original poster can be seen clearly. New moral stain for the UN ‼️ When President Raisi of Iran, the "Butcher of Tehran," began his speech, I waved a picture of Mahsa Amini, the innocent Iranian woman who was brutally murdered by the regime one year ago for not wearing a hijab "properly."
