title: Fact Check: Yes, you can RTI the National Testing Agency. Viral claim is misleading
content:
The NTA, while an autonomous body, does fall under the RTI Act and has a designated CPIO to process RTI queries.
The National Testing Agency (NTA) has been in the eye of the storm amid alleged irregularities in the NEET, the undergraduate medical entrance exam, and the cancellation of the UGC-NET. As students and parents called for the agency's abolition, the Centre replaced the NTA's Director General Subodh Kumar Singh with Pradeep Singh Kharola.
Amid controversies and calls for reforms, a social media post claimed that the NTA is a private institution and does not fall under the Right to Information (RTI) Act. Senior journalist Pankaj Pachauri shared the NTA's certificate of incorporation under the Societies Registration Act on X, and wrote, "Shocking to know that the NTA is a private society deciding the future of the students to publicly funded government institutions. Not under RTI = no info. No public oversight = no accountability. That's why the govt and the ministry can wash their hands off the scam." Its archive can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that the NTA is an autonomous body under the Department of Higher Education of the Ministry of Education of India that comes under the RTI. Our Probe
Perusing the NTA website, we found its certificate of incorporation under the Registration and MoA tab. The registration certificate states that it was incorporated on May 15, 2018, under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
The NTA is an independent autonomous body created following Cabinet approval,  which also provided a one-time grant of Rs 25 crore. The agency is administered by its general body, and chaired by its chairperson (appointed by the Government of India). The Centre can also issue directions to the NTA regarding its policies, which it's bound to comply with.
It's worth noting that autonomous bodies can be either statutory (created by an Act of Parliament) or non-statutory. The former are governed by the provisions of the Act under which they are created. The latter are governed by the Act under which they were incorporated, such as the Societies Registration Act, and Trust Registration Act. However, in both cases, the government exercises control.
Can you send RTI queries to the NTA?
Organisations and bodies need to fulfil certain criteria to be under the purview of the Right to Information Act. According to the act , this includes bodies that are formed by approvals or notifications issued by the government and also substantially financed by it. The NTA fulfils these criteria, making it a public authority for the application of the RTI Act.Â
While there have been questions about the transparency and accountability of these autonomous bodies in contrast to statutory autonomous bodies, the RTI portal lists the National Testing Agency as one of the several public authorities to seek information under the Act.
The NTA website also hosts the details of the Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) and the First Appellate Authority. There are several news reports on the responses sought by citizens from the NTA under the RTI Act. Some of these reports can be seen here and here. The last available report of the number of RTI queries processed by the NTA can be accessed here  for Financial Year 2022-2023. Thus, it is clear that the NTA does fall under the purview of the RTI Act, and the viral post claiming otherwise is misleading. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jun 26, 2024 21:48 IST

title: Fact Check: Afghan players DIDN'T chant 'Vande Mataram', viral clip is edited
content:
This video of the Afghan cricketers' celebration is from 2023. It has been edited to add the "Vande Mataram" chants.
Afghanistan sealed its first-ever T20 World Cup semi-final spot  with a thrilling victory against Bangladesh on June 25. India also had a role to play in the making of this history, as its win over Australia on June 24 cleared the way for Afghanistan to punch its semi-final tickets .
Now, a video of the Afghanistan squad  seemingly chanting "Vande Mataram" is making the rounds on social media. A banner of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup can be seen behind the players.
Sharing this video on Instagram , one person wrote, "Afghanistan team is happy. Afganistan team proudly says Vande Mataram after India beating Australia in T20 world cup super 8." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video from 2023 has been edited to add the "Vande Mataram" chants.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a news report  containing its screenshot. This MSN report from October 24, 2023, stated that the Afghan team celebrated its victory in a one-day international against Pakistan in the ICC Cricket World Cup 2023.
We then found the original video  shared on October 23, 2023, by Mohammad Nabi, former captain of the Afghanistan cricket team. In the original clip, the players could be heard cheering together along with religious chants of "Allah-Hu-Akbar". This video was also shared by several social media users  along with MSN journalist Faizul Haque  at the time.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Mohammad Nabi (@mohammadnabi07) According to news reports , the Afghan team was celebrating its third-ever win at a Cricket World Cup. It was also Pakistan's first loss in a one-day international (ODI) against Afghanistan, which was on the ninth rank at the time. Videos of both, players and fans, celebrating emerged on social media  following this victory. It is thus, clear that an old video of Afghan players was edited to show them chanting "Vande Mataram" following the team's entry into the T20 World Cup semi-finals. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jun 26, 2024 22:57 IST

title: Fact Check: NEET paper leak accused were NOT arrested from Congress office in Deoghar
content:
The building in the video is not the Congress party's Deoghar office but the LNJP Hospital in Patna where the accused, arrested from Deoghar, were taken for medical examination. The accused men were arrested from a house in Deoghar, very far away from the local Congress office.
The Bihar Police's Economic Offences Unit arrested six people from Jharkhand's Deoghar  in the NEET paper leak case on June 21. In its aftermath, a video going viral on social media purports to show the accused being apprehended at the Congress office in Deoghar, where they were allegedly hiding.
An X user wrote while sharing the video : "6 NEET accused were arrested by Bihar Police from Congress office in Deoghar, Jharkhand in #NEETPaperleak case. And Congress was meeting and inciting NEET aspirants by their crocodile tears. Connect the dots". Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the building in the video is not the Congress party's Deoghar office but the LNJP Hospital in Patna where the accused, arrested from Deoghar, were taken for medical examination. The accused men were arrested from a house in Deoghar, very far away from the local Congress office. OUR PROBE
Upon searching, we found that the viral video was shared by news agency ANI on X on June 23. ANI's post stated that the video showed the accused arrested from Deoghar in the NEET case being taken from the LNJP hospital in Patna after their medical examination. #WATCH | Bihar: 6 accused arrested in connection with UG NEET case being taken from LNJP hospital, Patna after their medical examination. Bihar Police arrested the accused from Jharkhand's Deoghar on June 21. pic.twitter.com/sOmBKQUHtS — ANI (@ANI) June 23, 2024
#WATCH | Bihar: 6 accused arrested in connection with UG NEET case being taken from LNJP hospital, Patna after their medical examination. Bihar Police arrested the accused from Jharkhand's Deoghar on June 21. pic.twitter.com/sOmBKQUHtS — ANI (@ANI) June 23, 2024
The images of Patna's LNJP hospital available on Google Maps  also match the building seen in the viral video, thus confirming that the clip is from Patna, not Deoghar.Â
Where were the accused arrested in Deoghar?
Quoting Deoghar SDPO Hrithik Srivastava, The Times of India  reported that the suspects were hiding allegedly in the house of Jhunu Singh near AIIMS Deoghar in the city's Devipur locality. The Bihar police arrested the six accused from Jhunu Singh's house and brought them to Patna.Â
The FIR filed in this case mentioned that the accused were caught in Jhunni Singh's farmhouse, located near AIIMS Deoghar. Reports use both names, "Jhunnu" and "Jhunni".
India Today's Deoghar correspondent Shailendra Mishra tracked down Jhunni Singh and spoke to him. Singh denied any link with the arrest and said that his name was being falsely used in the media reports. He said he runs a small eatery near AIIMS Deoghar and the place from where the accused were arrested was near the eatery. Singh added that he had nothing to do with this case and that he doesn't belong to any political party.Â
As per Google Maps , AIIMS Deoghar is around 12.5 km from the Congress office in Deoghar, which is located at Bajrangi Chowk .   So, while we couldn't independently verify any political affiliations of Jhunni Singh, it is clear that the six accused were not arrested from the Congress office in Deoghar. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jun 27, 2024 18:10 IST

title: Fact Check: This Virat Kohli statue at Times Square, New York is NOT real, it's CGI
content:
This statue is not real but was created using CGI. A mattress company named Duroflex has made it.
Has a statue of Virat Kohli been erected at Times Square in New York City? Many on social media are sharing a video  alleging that a "life-sized" golden statue of the Indian cricketer was recently unveiled at Times Square.Â
Sharing the viral clip , a Facebook user wrote, "Just Unveiled: A  larger-than-life statue of Virat Kohli at the iconic Times Square. This King's Duty, we are going global and making history!" Its archive can be seen here ( https://perma.cc/M3E7-9YQV  ).Â
The same claims were shared by multiple news and entertainment channels like Hindustan Times  and ZoomTV .
India Today Fact Check found that Virat Kohli's statue in the viral clip was CGI — not real!
On reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we found that Duroflex, a mattress company, made it. On June 23, 2024, Duroflex uploaded this video on its official Instagram channel . We saw that the caption featured the hashtag #CGIanimation. Computer-generated imagery (CGI) is a technology that uses computer graphics to create images or videos.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Duroflex (@duroflexworld) We also found the video uploaded on Duroflex's YouTube channel, whose title also mentioned "CGI". Thus, it became clear that the statue is not real. Looking at the video, we saw a crossing blimp overlapping with a building, which is only possible if a video is created using computer technology. The image can be seen below. We then reached out to Duroflex. The company's customer support executive Kiran Kumar confirmed to India Today that the statue of Virat Kohli was not real but was created using CGI. As the T20 World Cup is going on in the USA & West Indies, the CGI-made Virat Kohli statue was a part of Duroflex's marketing campaign. Kohli was made Duroflex's brand ambassador  in May last year.  - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jun 27, 2024 21:33 IST

title: Fact Check: No, this photo DOESN'T show Eid clothes being left on a Palestinian child's grave
content:
The image is from April 2023 and was taken in Turkey. It shows a father had placed Eid clothes on the grave of his eight-year-old daughter, who was killed in an earthquake.
Since October 7, 2023, more than 37,000 Palestinians have been slaughtered in Israeli attacks in the Gaza Strip, and at least 86,000 others have been injured. Amid the ongoing carnage, a photo made the rounds on social media, showing a dress placed on a grave.Â
A Facebook user wrote while sharing the photo: "A Palestinian father leaves Eid clothes on his daughter's grave (8 years old)."  Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the image is from April 2023 and was taken in Turkey. The grave was of an earthquake victim. OUR PROBE
A reverse image search of the picture led us to a news report by Al-Khaleej, a news oragisation based in Sharjah, United Arab Emirates. Dated April 22, 2023, this report  featured the same photo and stated that a Turkish man purchased an Eid dress for his daughter, who died in the earthquake that occurred in Turkey and Syria in February 2023 and placed it on her grave.Â
Similar reports were also published by Gulf Today  and Akhbarelyom . We also found the viral image posted on Instagram  by Turkish Journalist Nevzat Cicek in April 2023. He wrote that the photo from 2023 showed clothes left by a Turkish father on his daughter's grave on Eid.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by NEVZAT ÇİÇEK (@nevzatcicekofficial) Several news reports  have highlighted the devastating earthquake that struck Turkey and Syria on February 6, 2023. Two destructive earthquakes hit southeastern Turkey and northern Syria, resulting in the loss of numerous lives  and extensive damage to residences and infrastructure in the area. Thus, it is evident that an old photo is being falsely linked to the ongoing Israeli onslaught in Gaza. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Jun 28, 2024 16:43 IST

title: Fact Check: Trinamool's Mahua Moitra, Sayani Ghosh DIDN'T doze off in Parliament
content:
The viral photo is misleading. In the actual footage of the Parliament, both leaders can be seen thumping their desks as they listened to Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Arvind Ganpat Sawant's address.
A photo featuring All India Trinamool Congress leaders Mahua Moitra and Sayani Ghosh seemingly asleep during a Parliament session is making the rounds on social media . The photo featured Midnapore MP June Malia watching the session while sitting between the two leaders who sat with their eyes closed.Â
Those sharing the photo took a swipe at the leaders , writing, "West Bengal's Krishna Nagar MP Mahua Moitra and Jadavpur MP Sayani Ghosh spent the whole night thinking about the development projects of respective regions. Hence, they decided to sleep in Parliament. Krishnanagar and Jadavpur people are really 'FORTUNATE' to get them". Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this photo is misleading. In the actual footage of the Parliament, both the leaders could be seen thumping their desks as they listened to Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Arvind Ganpat Sawant's address. OUR PROBE
We looked at the footage of recent Parliament sessions available on the YouTube channel of Sansad TV  and found a video from June 26 . Its thumbnail featured TMC MPs Mahua Moitra, June Malia, and Sayani Ghosh, sitting behind Mumbai South MP Arvind Ganpat Sawant. In it, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Arvind congratulated Om Birla on being re-elected as Lok Sabha Speaker while addressing the Parliament.
At the 1:57 mark, Arvind Sawant said. "What we need is harmony, not hatred." At that moment, MPs sitting behind Arvind, including Mahua Moitra and Sayani Ghosh, begin thumping their desks. During this, both the leaders lowered their eyes for a bit and a screenshot of this exact moment was shared with misleading claims.
The first session of the 18th Lok Sabha began on June 24  and the 264th session of Rajya Sabha started on June 27. During the first three days, newly elected MPs took oaths and elected the Speaker of the Lok Sabha . President Droupadi Murmu addressed a joint sitting of both houses on June 27, following which Lok Sabha was adjourned till July 1  as Opposition members stormed the well of the House demanding a discussion on the NEET issue.  - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jun 28, 2024 20:16 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Om Birla's daughter clear UPSC without appearing for exam? Nope, here are the facts
content:
Anjali Birla did appear for the UPSC exam in 2019. She was selected through the Consolidated Reserve List, which is part of the UPSC selection process.
Following Bharatiya Janata Party MP Om Birla's re-appointment as the Lok Sabha speaker, a rumour went viral on social media that his daughter Anjali Birla cleared the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) exam without even appearing for it.
An X user shared Anjali Birla's photo and wrote, "India is the only country where you can clear UPSC without sitting in the examination. But for that, you have to be born as a daughter of Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla. Anjali Birla D/o Om Birla cleared UPSC without giving any examination, she is a model by profession. Modi Govt is making a mockery of our Education System." Its archived version can be seen here .
Similar claims were made on Facebook  and Threads as well.
India Today Fact Check found that the viral claims are not true. Anjali Birla did appear in the UPSC exam in 2019 and was selected through the Consolidated Reserve List, which is part of the UPSC selection process. OUR PROBE
We found news reports  about how Anjali Birla cleared the UPSC exam in her first attempt. According to Mint's report, the results for the 2019 exams were declared on August 4, 2020–829 aspirants cleared it. Anjali's name was on the reserve list, which had 89 aspirants whose names were announced on January 4, 2021.
We found the reserve list notification from January 4, 2021, on UPSC's official website. It noted that according to rules 16(4) and 16(5), the commission makes a reserve list of qualified candidates. Eighty-nine such aspirants were selected for this list and Anjali Birla was one of them. Anjali's name and her roll number (0851876) can be seen in the picture below.
To reach the interview stage, a UPSC aspirant has to appear for prelims and mains exam. When we checked the results of the 2019 UPSC prelims, we found Anjali Birla's name in the list of qualified candidates.
We also found the 2019 UPSC mains exam's results which were declared on January 14, 2020. Anjali's name and roll number can be seen in this list as well.
The UPSC is responsible for the appointment of Grade A employees along with IAS officers. Every year, according to the Central government's demand, such aspirants are recommended. This list is called the Consolidated Reserve List.
The UPSC issued a clarification on the matter on January 7, 2021, according to which, the Union makes a Consolidated Reserve List in which aspirants from reserved and non-reserved categories are recommended.
A similar claim had gone viral previously as well. At the time, Aaj Tak had debunked this . The Quint had spoken to Anjali Birla, who had said, "UPSC had earlier notified that they have 927 vacancies for the 2019 batch. But when the final results came out, they had only filled 829 vacancies. So, in that August 2020 list, my name was not there because I missed the cut-off for the General category by 8 marks. Now, in the notification that was released in January 2021, you can see that UPSC mentions that the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) asked for more vacancies to be filled."
Anjali Birla, a graduate of Delhi's Ramjas College, was selected for Indian Railway Account Service .
Thus, it's clear that Anjali Birla did appear for the UPSC exam and that the viral claim is baseless. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jul 1, 2024 15:51 IST

title: Fact Check: Not Olympic torch lighting! Viral video shows Easter custom and metal concert spectacle
content:
A video of fireworks and pyrotechnics inside what appears to be a church is being shared on social media, with the claims that it shows the lighting of the Olympic torch in Paris.Â
A Facebook user sharing the viral video wrote , "#ParisOlympics. Lighting of the Olympic torch from a church in Paris. Spectacular. #OlympicTorch #Olympics2024."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video does not show the lighting of the Olympic torch in Paris. The video combines footage from a religious ceremony and a heavy metal concert.
Reverse image searching the keyframes of the viral video led us to a Huffington Post report in Spanish dated April 9, 2023, containing a screenshot of the video. The report identified it as part of the tradition of "The Explosion of the Car" and the "Flight of the Dove" celebrated in Florence, Italy, on Easter Sunday. In this tradition, a cable is lit at the altar of the Cathedral, igniting a rocket dove. The ignited rocket dove travels via a metal wire to light a chariot outside the cathedral and finally returns to its starting point. It's an age-old tradition in Florence, eagerly awaited every Easter Sunday. It takes place at the main altar of the Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore.
Several reports and YouTube videos attribute the viral video to this age-old tradition in Florence.
Thereafter, we conducted a reverse image search on the second part of the video, which showed fireworks with rockets shooting into the sky. This search led us to several YouTube videos from a 2023 concert by the German metal band Rammstein  in Slovakia.
We also noticed the band's logo, a cross formed by the letters "R" and "T." Rammstein is renowned for their spectacular live shows featuring extreme pyrotechnic displays.
The torch for the Paris 2024 Olympic Games was actually lit in ancient Olympia in a traditional ceremony on April 16. The torch relay will finally culminate with the lighting of the Olympic flame in Paris at the opening ceremony. The video of the ceremony can be seen here .Â
Thus, clips from a celebration in a Florence church and a pyrotechnic spectacle at a metal concert have been merged to falsely claim they show the lighting of the Olympic torch in Paris for the 2024 Olympics. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jul 3, 2024 18:30 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Hathras stampede! This old video is from a pre-Holi event in Mathura
content:
This video is from March 17, 2024, and shows overcrowding during a pre-Holi event in Mathura.
In Uttar Pradesh's Hathras, a stampede at an overcrowded satsang for self-styled godman Narayan Sakaar Hari, also known as Bhole Baba, has reportedly led to at least 121 deaths. Now, a video  allegedly showing the tragic incident is going viral on social media .Â
Sharing the clip on Instagram , one person wrote, "At least 116 people, mostly women, lost their lives in a stampede during a religious event in Hathras district, Uttar Pradesh." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found this old video which shows a pre-Holi event in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura. It has nothing to do with the Hathras stampede. OUR PROBE
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a post from March 17, 2024 . It stated that this video showed a stampede at a pre-Holi event at a Mathura temple.Â
Further searches led us to a longer and uncropped version of the viral video shared by NDTV on March 17 . According to NDTV's report , this video was from the Shreeji Temple in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura, where a stampede broke out during a pre-Holi event on March 17. Devotees Injured During Stampede At Mathura Temple's Pre-Holi Event https://t.co/83FpzDtSBx pic.twitter.com/wGfu8ztCwv — NDTV (@ndtv) March 17, 2024
Devotees Injured During Stampede At Mathura Temple's Pre-Holi Event https://t.co/83FpzDtSBx pic.twitter.com/wGfu8ztCwv — NDTV (@ndtv) March 17, 2024
According to police officials , a massive footfall was recorded at the temple on the occasion of Laddoo Maar Holi, resulting in a "stampede-like" situation. At least six people reportedly lost consciousness and got injured. Doctors stationed onsite gave the victims first aid who were then transferred to nearby hospitals. Further, a contingent of police was sent to the temple to restore order.
At the time, the same video was also shared by other media outlets  while the Press Trust of India shared a video of the injured devotees . VIDEO | Several people injured after a stampede broke out at Shri Ladli Ji Temple in Uttar Pradesh's Barsana earlier today, during Holi celebrations. pic.twitter.com/GZu9Emqdvs — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) March 17, 2024
VIDEO | Several people injured after a stampede broke out at Shri Ladli Ji Temple in Uttar Pradesh's Barsana earlier today, during Holi celebrations. pic.twitter.com/GZu9Emqdvs — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) March 17, 2024
It is noteworthy that Mathura SSP Shailesh Kumar Pandey admitted to overcrowding during the Laddoo Maar Holi celebrations, but denied rumours of a stampede . #Stampede In #MathuraTemple : Mathura SSP Defies Rumours Of Stampede During Barsana #Holi Celebrations #DNAVideos | #MathuraTempleStampede For more videos, click here https://t.co/6ddeGFqM3o pic.twitter.com/Y9XeP8YQiD — DNA (@dna) March 18, 2024
#Stampede In #MathuraTemple : Mathura SSP Defies Rumours Of Stampede During Barsana #Holi Celebrations #DNAVideos | #MathuraTempleStampede For more videos, click here https://t.co/6ddeGFqM3o pic.twitter.com/Y9XeP8YQiD — DNA (@dna) March 18, 2024
It is thus clear that an old video was falsely shared as the deadly Hathras stampede. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jul 3, 2024 18:48 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Ayodhya's Rampath caving in! This 2-year-old clip is from Brazil
content:
Though multiple cave-ins have recently been reported in Ayodhya's Rampath, this is a two-year-old video from Brazil.
A video allegedly showing Ayodhya's newly constructed Rampath caving in, causing a woman to fall into the resulting sinkhole has been widely shared on social media.
People claimed on Facebook and X , "This is the condition of the road Rampath built in Ayodhya after the first rain. Its length is 13 kilometres. The total cost is Rs 844 crore i.e. about Rs 65 crore have been spent in the construction of one kilometre. The company that built the road is from Gujarat. Its name is Bhuvan Infracom Private Limited. Check all the facts. You will believe it yourself. Rest Ram naam satya hai ."
The archive of one such viral post can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that while multiple cave-ins have been reported recently in Ayodhya's Rampath, the viral video is more than two-years-old and from Brazil.
A reverse image search led us to several Brazilian news reports from June 2022. As per O Povo, a Brazilian tabloid, a woman named Maria Rosilene  fell into a crater in the Brazilian city of Cascavel.
The woman was rescued by nearby people as seen in the viral video. She sustained minor injuries. The sidewalk that caved in was newly-built with a layer of cement, which collapsed when she walked over it. Mulher cai em cratera que se abriu no Centro de Cascavel. Confira o momento: https://t.co/7eGteNAmlb (Vídeo: Reprodução/Vídeo enviado via WhatsApp O POVO) pic.twitter.com/mjNdaZUEBe — O POVO (@opovo) June 2, 2022 Brazilian news outlet UOL also shared a video report about this incident on YouTube on June 3, 2022. The Ayodhya Police also took to X to clarify that the video was not from the district, calling such claims "misleading and false news", and adding that "legal action will be taken against the person who spread this misleading news". This makes it clear that the video is not from Ayodhya at all. WHAT HAPPENED IN AYODHYA? After the heavy rainfall in Ayodhya last week, the Rampath reportedly suffered several cave-ins and water logging in multiple spots. Following this, six PWD and Jal Nigam officials were suspended by the Uttar Pradesh government on Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's order. According to Times Now, a notice was issued to a Gujarat-based firm responsible for the civil work in the area. Business Standard reported that the firm was Ahmedabad-based Bhuvan Infracom Private Limited. - Ends Published By: Prateek Chakraborty Published On: Jul 4, 2024 14:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Kerala coaching centre ad viral with FALSE communal spin on NEET scam
content:
This is an advertisement published in Mathrubhumi Daily for an entrance coaching centre in Kerala. There is no link as of yet between these students and the NEET scandal.
Even as the Central Bureau of Investigation arrested  an alleged conspirator in the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET) paper leak case, many online are attempting to communalise the national scandal, claiming that the leak's beneficiaries were primarily Muslims.Â
A Facebook user shared a photo of a newspaper ad featuring an array of photos of students and their scores, and wrote: "The above photos are NEET ENTRANCE QUESTION PAPER LEAK BENEFICIARIES, JUST LOOK N GUESS WHO N WHICH RELIGION THER ARE? All Muslims only." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this photo was an advertisement for a coaching centre in Kottakkal, Kerala, several of whose students achieved high scores in NEET. There is, as of yet, no apparent link between these students and the NEET paper leak. Nor is there any evidence to suggest Muslim students in particular benefited from the leak. OUR PROBE
This viral image appears to be from a Malayalam daily newspaper. We conducted a keyword search on Google about the "Environment Day celebrations" news item, partially visible in the viral photo. We found a report  with a similar headline in the online edition of Mathrubhumi Daily.Â
We then checked Mathrubhumi's e-paper from the same date and found the full advertisement. The ad contained the headline "Kottakkal Universal Institute NEET Result 2024" and showcased photos of students who achieved high scores in exams. It's evident from the pictures that the group includes not just Muslim students but also students from other communities. We contacted the authorities at Universal Institute in Kottakkal for further clarification. They stated that the information circulating on social media was entirely false. "The viral picture is an advertisement for Universal Institute published in Mathrubhumi daily. The ad features students from our institution who achieved the highest scores this year. Among them are students from different communities. Kottakkal has a Muslim majority, so most of the students here are Muslims. The propaganda with communal undertones is unfortunate," Dr Hameed, the institute's principal, told India Today Fact Check. Universal Institute also shared pictures of students who scored high in the NEET exam on its Facebook page . Moreover, Kerala has not yet reported any cases of NEET irregularities. Bihar, Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra are among the states that have registered NEET paper leak cases . advertisement Thus, it is clear that an advertisement published in Mathrubhumi Daily for an entrance coaching centre in Kerala has been shared online to give a communal spin to the NEET paper leak scandal. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Jul 4, 2024 19:49 IST

title: Fact Check: 'Sorry!' Bieber did NOT groove to 'Kukkad Kamaal Da'; viral clip is edited
content:
This video is edited. The original video showed Justin Bieber dancing to his song "Where Are Ü Now" at a music festival in California back in 2015.
International pop sensation Justin Bieber performed his famous songs at the grand sangeet ceremony of Anant Ambani and Radhika Merchant on July 5. Videos from this event, attended by Bollywood, sports, and fashion celebrities at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai, have now taken over social media.
One such video that caught the attention of many featured Bieber dancing to the tune of Kukkad from the 2012 movie Student of the Year. Many shared the video  claiming that Bieber danced to a Hindi song during his performance at Anant-Radhika's sangeet ceremony, shocking several people. It was also reported by a few media outlets , including Mashable .
India Today Fact Check found that this video is edited. The original video showed the global pop icon dancing to his song "Where Are U Now" at a music festival in California back in 2015. OUR PROBE
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to its longer version uploaded on YouTube in 2015. The video featured Bieber performing with Jack U — a duo of music producers Skrillex and Diplo.
The clip going viral can be seen at the 1:32 mark of this video , in which Bieber danced to his song "Where Are U Now". Its description stated that the video showed Bieber performing at an event called Hard Summer on August 2, 2015.
We then found several media reports about this performance. According to them , Hard is an annual music festival celebrating the intersection of electronic and live music culture. It was inaugurated in 2007. Its 2015 edition was held in Pomona, California, where Bieber performed with Jack U  on August 2, 2015. Bieber also posted a photo from this event on his Instagram account at the time.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Justin Bieber (@justinbieber) We also found another video of the event uploaded on the official YouTube channel of Jack U  on August 14, 2015. The video contained glimpses from the music festival, as well as behind-the-scenes clips, featuring Bieber rehearsing the dance steps he performed at the event. It is thus clear that a 2015 video of Bieber's performance was edited to claim that he danced to a Hindi song at Anant-Radhika's sangeet ceremony. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jul 6, 2024 19:26 IST

title: Fact Check: 2011 tsunami video from Japan FALSELY viral as Haridwar floods
content:
The video is from the 2011 tsunami in Japan.
The end of June saw heavy rainfall submerging roads and flooding the Sukhi River in Uttarakhand's Haridwar. Now, a video making the rounds on social media purports to show the holy city being inundated with several cars and containers being washed away by the water's current.Â
An Instagram user shared this video on July 2 claiming it was shot in Haridwar the same day. Others on social media, however, claimed that the video was from Dubai.
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from the 2011 tsunami in Japan.
With the InVid reverse image search, we found a similar video on the YouTube channel of TBS NEWS DIG, a prominent news outlet in Japan. The video was uploaded on February 25, 2021, with the Japanese title noting it showed the deadly tsunami that hit the coast of Miyako in Japan on March 11, 2011.
The tsunami was triggered by Japan's strongest recorded earthquake of 9.0 magnitude. Tsunami waves swept away cars and containers along the coast of Miyako in the Tohoku region. The disaster killed about 20 thousand people in Japan and injured many.Â
The viral video was the laterally inverted version of this YouTube video. Similar visuals can also be seen in reports about the 2011 tsunami published by the Mirror and the Daily Press . Thus, it is clear that the video is not from either Haridwar or Dubai. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jul 8, 2024 16:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Rahul Gandhi snub Assamese Gamosa? Not really, here's what happened
content:
This clipped video does not show Gandhi refusing his party scarf as well. He was also later photographed at the Silchar airport wearing the Assamese Gamosa.
Congress MP and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi on July 8 met flood-affected people in Assam before heading to Manipur where he visited relief camps housing people affected by the ongoing ethnic violence in the state.Â
Following this, a video of Rahul Gandhi in the middle of a crowd was widely shared.Â
Those sharing this clip  claimed it showed the leader refusing to wear an "Assamese Gamosa" offered by a Congress worker to welcome him at Silchar airport. The archive of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check has found that the post not only suppresses the complete truth but also misleads.
As the caption of the viral post suggests that it is from the Silchar airport, we used related keywords and found an extended version of the video on the YouTube channel of News18 Assam North East.
In this video, after the viral part, another man can be seen trying to greet Rahul Gandhi with a tricolour scarf, presumably of the Congress party. But the leader refused this as well, holding it with one hand and pushing it downward. A collage of screenshots from both moments has been compared here, making it quite clear that he snubbed both. This part was clipped out of the video. Subsequently, we found a post by the Congress Party on July 8, where some frames from Rahul Gandhi's arrival at the Silchar airport were shared. Here, he can be seen wearing the Assamese Gamosa, and holding several others in his hand while being welcomed by the Congress leaders of Assam and Manipur. LoP Shri @RahulGandhi receives a heartfelt reception at Silchar Airport from leaders of Assam and Manipur. pic.twitter.com/eFEb0wbKKT — Congress (@INCIndia) July 8, 2024 The chief of Assam Pradesh Congress, Bhupen Kumar Borah, hit back at these viral social media posts with a photo of him offering Rahul Gandhi an Assamese Gamosa at the Silchar airport on July 8. Dear , @AtanuBhuyan , be it known that some people can never see goodness in others. Shri @RahulGandhi ji accepted dozens of Gamosa inside the airport. Thereafter he came out to see hundreds of people outside holding Gamosas in their hands. Please understand that he came to… https://t.co/OepLMchYUc pic.twitter.com/jMm5bkLxOp — Bhupen kumar Borah (@BhupenKBorah) July 8, 2024 It is also important to note that during the Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra, Rahul Gandhi was seen with the trademark Assamese Gamosa not once, but several times. One such video can be seen here.  Meanwhile, Atanu Bhuyan, who first shared this video with the particular claim, later clarified they "did not get the pictures" that Congress shared. Dear @BhupenKBorah , I didn't say to please any 'master' but said what I saw in the visuals. We didn't get the pictures that you shared. Secondly, could you please tell me the name of that ONE RELIEF CAMP that Rahul Gandhi visited to meet the FLOOD-AFFECTED people of Assam? https://t.co/maYLUgQ1Cb — atanu bhuyan (@atanubhuyan) July 8, 2024 It is, however, evident that a clipped video of Rahul Gandhi was shared falsely claiming that he refused to wear an Assamese Gamosa. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Jul 9, 2024 18:24 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of people raising 'Rahul Gandhi Go Back' slogans is NOT from Manipur
content:
This video shows people protesting against Rahul Gandhi on January 21 in Assam during his Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi visited relief camps in the Jibram and Churachandpur districts of Manipur on July 8 to interact with people displaced by the ongoing ethnic violence between the Meiteis and the Kuki-Zos. It was his first visit after becoming the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and his third since the violence broke out in the state in May 2023.
Now, a video making the rounds on social media purports to show Manipuris sloganeering against him. The video featuring the news agency ANI's logo was shared with claims that chants of "go back" were chanted during his recent visit to Manipur.Â
Sharing the clip, one person wrote , "Rahul Gandhi has been asked to go back in Manipur by residents, as his inflammatory speeches would trigger in to new clashes. This was Yesterday 8/7/24, so he had to return." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this is an old video from Assam during Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra. It has nothing to do with his recent visit to Manipur.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to an NDTV report from January 2024. According to it, this incident took place at a roadside eatery in Assam's Nagaon on January 21. At the time, the crowd raised slogans against Rahul Gandhi and displayed placards with slogans such as "Anyay Yatra" and "Rakibul go back", referring to Rakibul Hussain, the Congress MP from Assam's Dhubri constituency and former MLA from Nagaon's Samaguri seat.
We then found a longer version of the viral clip, shared by the news agency ANI , on January 21 that mentioned that this video was from a protest against Gandhi in the Ambagan area of Assam's Nagaon. #WATCH | Assam: A large number of people carrying posters of 'Rahul Gandhi go back' and 'Anyaya Yatra' held a protest against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in the Ambagan area of Nagaon this evening. pic.twitter.com/e4fFIwqFSa — ANI (@ANI) January 21, 2024
#WATCH | Assam: A large number of people carrying posters of 'Rahul Gandhi go back' and 'Anyaya Yatra' held a protest against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in the Ambagan area of Nagaon this evening. pic.twitter.com/e4fFIwqFSa — ANI (@ANI) January 21, 2024
Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra entered Assam on January 18. On January 21, he and other leaders stopped at a restaurant in Ambagan  on the way to their night halt in Rupohi. Here, he was mobbed by a crowd raising slogans against him. The leaders were escorted out of the eatery by the security personnel.Â
At the time, this video was widely reported by several media outlets, such as News18 , News 24 , ABP Live , and AajTak .
Gandhi's Nyay Yatra successfully wrapped up its seven-day journey in Assam on January 25, during which Assam police also lodged an FIR  against Rahul Gandhi and other functionaries for allegedly inciting people attending his Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra "to disobey lawful orders and putting life and property in danger".
It is thus, clear that an old video from Assam was falsely shared as people in Manipur protesting against Rahul Gandhi. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jul 9, 2024 20:59 IST

title: Fact Check: Neither PM Modi nor Xi Jinping was received by Putin, misleading claim viral
content:
Both Narendra Modi and Xi Jinping were received by Russia's Deputy Prime Ministers. Putin was not at the airport to receive either of them.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Russia on July 8 for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. During his visit, PM Modi met with President Putin and addressed members of the Indian diaspora there. However, following PM Modi's visit, several social media users , including BJP leader Subramanian Swamy, claimed that the Indian PM was not received by the Russian president at the airport, whereas Putin had received the Chinese President Xi Jinping at the airport.
Former member of Rajya Sabha and BJP leader Subramanian Swamy, while quoting a Times of India tweet, wrote, "Putin did not come to the airport to receive Modi? Putin had received Xi." This claim was echoed by several users on X  and Facebook. An archived version of the post can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that the viral claim is misleading. Both Narendra Modi and Xi Jinping were received by Russia's Deputy Prime Ministers. Putin didn't receive either of them on their arrival. Our Probe
Upon running a keyword search, we found several news reports about PM Modi's Russia visit published on July 8. According to these reports, PM Modi was in Russia after five years. The reports mentioned that PM Modi was accorded a guard of honour upon his arrival at the airport in Moscow and was received by the First Deputy Prime Minister of Russia, Denis Manturov.
We then looked into China's President Xi Jinping's visit to Russia. According to various news reports, Xi visited Russia in March 2023. A press release on China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs' website stated that Xi Jinping arrived in Moscow on a special plane to pay a state visit to Russia at the invitation of President Vladimir Putin. It also mentioned that Xi was greeted by Russian Deputy Prime Minister Dmitry Chernyshenko and other senior Russian officials by the ramp.
We also found The Guardian's video report of Xi's arrival at Moscow airport, which shows that he was received by Russia's Deputy Prime Minister.
A Hindustan Times report about Modi's recent visit also mentioned that Manturov, who received PM Modi, is senior to the Deputy Prime Minister who received Chinese President Xi Jinping during his visit to Russia.
Thus, the claim that Putin received Xi Jinping but not PM Modi is misleading. The Russian president did not receive either of them at the airport. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jul 10, 2024 21:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Mount K(AI)lash! This stunning video is AI-generated
content:
This video of Mount Kailash was made using Midjourney by Tibet-based artists.
A stunning video that's been widely shared purports to show Mount Kailash — the striking peak in the south-west corner of Tibet in the Himalayan Mountains  — covered by lenticular clouds . Some called it the " raw power of nature in action ", while others called it the fury of the Hindu god Shiva , who is believed to reside there.
One person shared the video on Instagram , writing, "Mount Kailash, the king of sacred mountains, who see it can make a wish. Feel the awe-inspiring majesty and serenity of Mount Kailash. Mount Kailash will offer a profound purification of the soul." Its archive can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that this video was made with Midjourney by Tibet-based artists, who have made several such videos of Mount Kailash using AI. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video shared by an Instagram account named "Pure Tibetan" on June 28. On this account, we found several other videos of Mount Kailash , similarly showing surreal lenticular clouds  all around it.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Puretibetan (@puretibetan)
A post shared by Puretibetan (@puretibetan)
We then found a website called "Kailash Energy" hyperlinked in the bio section of this Instagram account. According to it, this website was based in Ngari Prefecture of China's Tibet Autonomous Region. It sells Tibetan crystals, gemstones, souvenirs, and accessories such as necklaces, bracelets, rings, earrings, etc.
We then contacted the people running this Instagram account -- Sonam and Namgyal, a Tibet-based artist duo. They told us that they aimed to share the supernatural and majestic phenomena of Mount Kailash with the help of AI. They shot the photo of Mount Kailash and then edited it using Midjourney.
Lenticular clouds are rare lens-shaped or saucer-shaped clouds, which typically arise from powerful winds at high altitudes, often near mountain ranges . This cloud formation has reportedly been spotted before over mountains in Sichuan , Turkey and over Japan's Mount Fuji .
Thus, it is clear that the video of Mount Kailash, surrounded by lenticular clouds, was made using AI. - Ends Published By: Prateek Chakraborty Published On: Jul 11, 2024 14:41 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral video of flooded Mumbai streets is from 2020, not recent
content:
This is a video from August 2020, when low-lying Mumbai areas got flooded after record-breaking rainfall. At that time, Uddhav Thackeray was leading the coalition government.
Mumbai and several regions across Maharashtra  have been experiencing heavy rainfall. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has declared a "red alert" for Mumbai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, Panvel, and the rural areas of Ratnagiri-Sindhudurg, predicting heavy rainfall.
Now, a video of heavily flooded streets  with vehicles being swept away by the water has gone viral on social media. Those sharing the video claimed that it showed the current situation in Mumbai and questioned the ruling government.Â
A Facebook user, while sharing the viral video , wrote, "This is called Masterstroke of Amrit Kaal." Its archive can be seen here . This is called Masterstroke of Amrit Kaal. pic.twitter.com/8U6nE1DKtR — Kaleidoscope (@kaleidoscopeic) July 9, 2024
This is called Masterstroke of Amrit Kaal. pic.twitter.com/8U6nE1DKtR — Kaleidoscope (@kaleidoscopeic) July 9, 2024
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is actually from the 2020 Mumbai floods.
Upon reverse-searching the keyframes of the viral video, we came across several social media posts  from August 2020 containing the same video. One post noted that the viral video  was shot in the CP Tank area in Gulawadi Circle in Mumbai.
Further, we found a report by the International Business Times , dated August 6, 2020, which included a screenshot of the viral video. The report highlighted that after heavy rains and stormy weather, hundreds of vehicles were submerged in the flooded streets of the city. At that time, Uddhav Thackeray-led Maha Vikas Aghadi  was ruling the state.
Many parts of South Mumbai, including Churchgate, Colaba, Marine Lines, Marine Drive, Kalbadevi, Dongri, Mohammed Ali Road, Byculla, Mazagaon, Grant Road, and Charni Road, experienced floods at the time. The city also witnessed gusty winds of up to 70 kmph, resulting in the uprooting of over a hundred trees and blocking many roads in South Mumbai.
A report in Mint  from August 6, 2020, noted that the city experienced the heaviest one-day rain in August in 47 years at the time. The Colaba weather station recorded 29.4 centimetres of rainfall in 12 hours, the highest downpour for a single day in August since at least 1974.
We also geolocated the exact location  of the viral video and confirmed that it was shot on Cawasji Patel Tank Road in Mumbai.
Thus, it's clear that an old video of the 2020 Mumbai floods is being shared as recent. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Jul 11, 2024 15:24 IST

title: Fact Check: Aishwarya didn't pose with Salman at Ambani wedding, edited photo viral
content:
This photo is edited. The original picture featured Salman Khan posing with just his sister Arpita and not Aishwarya Rai Bachchan.
Bollywood actor Aishwarya Rai Bachchan turned heads at the grand Ambani wedding on July 12, when she entered the venue with her daughter Aaradhya. She got the eyeballs not just for her dazzling look, but for giving the Bachchan family photo a miss .Â
At the Gala event, Amitabh and Jaya Bachchan posed for a family portrait with son Abhishek, daughter Shweta, son-in-law Nikhil Nanda, and the grandchildren, while Aishwarya and Aaradhya reached the venue shortly after, stirring a controversy.
Now, a purported photo from the lavish wedding, featuring Aishwarya Rai Bachchan posing with Salman Khan  is going viral on social media. Salman's sister Arpita Khan is also seen in the viral, which fuelled speculation of a rift in the marriage of Abhishek and Aishwarya . Aishwarya and Salman dated briefly in the early 2000s.
Sharing the photo , one person wrote, "Aishwarya didn't arrive with the Bachchan family, and now she's having picture with Salman bhai. This is my multiverse of madness." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral photo was edited. The original one featured Salman Khan with just his sister Arpita and not Aishwarya.Â
Reverse searching the viral photo led us to photos of Salman Khan from the wedding of Anant Ambani and Radhika Merchant, shared by Zoom TV . In it, the actor could be seen posing with his sister Arpita Khan, in the same background and attire as seen in the viral photo.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Zoom TV (@zoomtv)
A post shared by Zoom TV (@zoomtv)
Further searches led us to photos of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, posing along with her daughter at the venue, shared by ANI . Her attire and pose in these pictures matched that seen in the viral photo. A collage of the original photos of the two actors seen together in the viral photo can be seen below.
We also looked for media footage from July 12, showing the entry of Bollywood actors at the Ambani wedding. Multiple videos shared by different media outlets showed Salman Khan arriving at the venue with sister Arpita Khan . Aishwarya Rai Bachchan, on the other hand, came and posed for photos with her daughter Aaradhya . It is clear from the footage that the actors did not share space together at any time during the entrance, which is where the viral photo was supposedly shot.
 It is thus, clear that the viral photo of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan and Salman Khan posing together at the Ambani wedding is edited. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Jul 14, 2024 13:45 IST

title: Fact Check: Donald Trump shot in the chest? No, photo DOESN'T show bullet hole
content:
Donald Trump has said that he was shot in the ear. The "hole" visible in Trump's jacket is actually a fold in the coat of an officer protecting him.
Former US President and Republican candidate Donald Trump was shot while speaking at a campaign rally in Pennsylvania on Saturday. In what is being called an assassination attempt, Trump's ear was injured, and he was immediately taken away by the security staff. Amid this, various social media users, while sharing a photo of the attack , are claiming that Trump was shot in the chest, but he survived because he was wearing a bulletproof jacket. A hole can be seen in the viral picture of Trump's coat.
An X user, while sharing the picture , wrote, "Trump just started wearing a bulletproof vest as advised by his security detail. It saved his life!! He took a shot to the chest." Its archive can be seen here .Â
Various social media users made the same claim on Facebook , and Instagram .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral picture is a zoomed-in version of the original picture. The "hole" visible in Trump's jacket is actually a fold in the coat of an officer protecting him. Trump has said that the bullet pierced his right ear.
By performing a reverse image search, we found the original photo on Associate Press' website . The viral picture is a zoomed-out version of this image.
The AP image was clicked by photojournalist Evan Vucci and was also shared by ABC News on Instagram .     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by ABC News (@abcnews) By looking at the original picture, we could see that the alleged bullet hole was in fact a fold or a wrinkle on a female security staffer's coat who was protecting Trump. Contrary to the viral claim, we did not find any news reports that mentioned a bullet wound in Trump's chest. According to various American and Indian news outlets, Donald Trump said that the bullet pierced the upper part of his right ear. The incident happened when Trump was speaking at an election rally in Butler, Pennsylvania. The FBI identified 20-year-old Thomas Matthew Crooks of Bethel Park, Pennsylvania, as the suspect. Crooks was captured and killed by the Secret Service. An attendee at the rally was also killed. It is thus clear that Trump was not shot in the chest but in the ear. - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Jul 14, 2024 21:41 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of clash between Polish forces and refugees FALSELY shared as recent
content:
The video is from November 2021 and is being falsely shared as a recent event.
On July 11, illegal migrants on the Belarusian side of the border with Poland allegedly hurled makeshift spears  at Polish border guards through the steel fence. A 21-year-old Polish border guard reportedly lost his life in the attack. The day before the attack, the Police Army Chief reportedly warned of an all-out conflict  as Poland increased the number of its troops on its borders with Russia and Belarus amid tense relations between the two nations following the Russia-Ukraine war.
Now, a video of water cannons being fired at a large gathering of people is circulating on social media. Those sharing the video claimed it showed Polish forces using tear gas and water cannons on refugees from the Middle East and Africa at the Belarus-Poland border.
An X user shared the video , and wrote, "Today's feel-good video. Illegal migrants from the Middle East and Africa arrive at the Belarus-Poland border. Attacking the fences & barbed wire, the water cannon literally blows them away."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from November 2021, when Polish forces fired tear gas and water cannons at migrants trying to cross the border from Belarus, escalating the ongoing dispute between the two nations. No such incident has occurred recently.
Reverse-searching the keyframes of the viral video, we found several reports  from November 2021 containing screenshots of the video. A report dated November 16, 2021 , noted that thousands of migrants attempted to storm the Polish border from the Belarusian side. Polish security forces used tear gas and water cannons against refugees from Syria and Iraq gathered on the Belarusian side of the border. The refugees responded by throwing sticks and stones, while Belarusian border guards did not intervene to control the situation.
Poland, the European Union, and the US had then accused Belarus of orchestrating the migrant crisis  by luring thousands of desperate people from Syria, Iraq, Afghanistan, and other nations marred by violence into Belarus with the promise of a relatively easy crossing into the Eurozone via Poland. However, Poland didn't welcome the gathered refugees at its border.
We found similar video reports , confirming that the viral video is from 2021  and not recent.Â
We also performed a keyword search to determine if a similar incident occurred recently but found no such reports.Â
Thus, it's clear that an old video of a clash between Polish forces and refugees is being falsely shared as a recent incident amid heightened tensions at the border. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Jul 16, 2024 13:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Rohingyas turning rowdies against Mathura police? No, this video is from Assam
content:
This video is not from Mathura but from Assam. According to the police, it's a 2023 video.
A video of a tense confrontation between several men and police officers is making rounds on social media. In it, an elderly Muslim man could be seen attacking the cops with a bamboo stick.
Those sharing this video claimed it showed Rohingya Muslims in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura district attacking the police check who tried to check their identity cards.
One such post on X read: "Rohingyas or Rowdies? UP Police went to check IDs of Rohingya Muslims living in Mathura, UP. Instead of cooperating these illegal intruders started fighting with the Police. Deport all the Rohingyas from India."
India Today Fact Check found that the video in question is not from Uttar Pradesh but from Assam. OUR PROBE
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to this clip shared by Assam Minister Pijush Hazarika on X on June 28. The Assamese post roughly translates to, "This incident occurred in Dhing a few days ago." Dhing is a village in the northwest of the Nagaon district in Assam. কেইদিনমানৰ পূৰ্বে সংঘটিত হোৱা এইটো ধিঙৰ ঘটনা। চাওকচোন, এটা বিশেষ সম্প্ৰদায়ৰ লোকসকল কেনেদৰে অসহিষ্ণু হৈ আক্ৰমণকাৰীৰ ৰূপত কৰ্তব্যৰত আৰক্ষীক আক্ৰমণ কৰিছে! pic.twitter.com/zkiJah1Bix — Pijush Hazarika (@Pijush_hazarika) June 28, 2024
কেইদিনমানৰ পূৰ্বে সংঘটিত হোৱা এইটো ধিঙৰ ঘটনা। চাওকচোন, এটা বিশেষ সম্প্ৰদায়ৰ লোকসকল কেনেদৰে অসহিষ্ণু হৈ আক্ৰমণকাৰীৰ ৰূপত কৰ্তব্যৰত আৰক্ষীক আক্ৰমণ কৰিছে! pic.twitter.com/zkiJah1Bix — Pijush Hazarika (@Pijush_hazarika) June 28, 2024
He added, "See how the people of a particular community are becoming intolerant and attacking personnel on duty." Following the minister, a YouTube channel named The Pulse NE also shared this video.
A subsequent keyword search led us to a report from India Today North East dated June 28 that cited Hazarika's post and highlighted that the video triggered a series of controversies amid allegations by Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma that a specific group of people was causing disturbances in the state following the Lok Sabha election results.
However, an Assam Tribune report from June 29 quoted the Assam DGP GP Singh cautioning those sharing the video. Singh claimed in an X post that the video was old and asked people to refrain from sharing it. Please refrain from circulating old videos. Would attract provisions of law.
