The Mathura Police also took to X  to inform that the video was not from the UP district. pic.twitter.com/hveD604dDO — MATHURA POLICE (@mathurapolice) July 14, 2024
pic.twitter.com/hveD604dDO — MATHURA POLICE (@mathurapolice) July 14, 2024
Although we could not independently pinpoint the date or location of the video, it is clear that it's not from UP. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Jul 16, 2024 21:41 IST

title: Fact Check: No 'India-India' chants at Republican National Convention, video is edited
content:
The video was edited to add the chants. No such chants were raised at the event at the time.
On July 15, at the Republican National Convention in Milwaukee, Donald Trump announced JD Vance as his vice-presidential candidate. Vance greeted the delegates  at the convention with his wife, Usha, who is of Indian origin.
Now, a video going viral on social media claims to show Vance greeting delegates amid alleged chants of "India-India." Social media users claimed these chants were raised as Vance brought his wife Usha Chilukuri into the convention. An X user shared the viral video and wrote, "'India India' chants as JD Vance brings soon-to-be second lady Usha Chilukuri into the RNC convention. The new Republican Party. It just keeps getting better." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video was edited to add the chants. OUR PROBE
Upon conducting keyword searches, we found several video reports of the convention on YouTube, shared on July 15. Forbes live-streamed the event on its YouTube Channel . Here, at the three-hour mark, the viral clip can be seen, when the country band Sixwire performed  as Vance's nomination is announced.
Similar video reports containing the video can be seen here  and here . Nowhere in these videos can the "India-India" chants be heard.
Thus, it's clear that the video was edited to add the "India-India" chants. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jul 16, 2024 21:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Donald Trump NOT caught napping! Viral clip shows him mid-prayer
content:
This video shows Donald Trump along with other attendees of the Republican National Convention 2024 praying with their eyes shut.
Former US President Donald Trump arrived with a bandaged ear at the Republican National Convention — a four-day event that began on July 15 in Milwaukee  — making his first public appearance since surviving an assassination attempt. He received a rapturous reception from the crowd that chanted "Fight"  during his dramatic entrance.
Now, a video going viral on social media shows Trump sitting with his eyes shut. Those sharing the clip claimed that he dozed off during the event .
One person shared the clip, writing , "Trump caught falling asleep at the RNC. People always crack on our great President Biden about his ageing tactics, but here's Trump doing the same thing." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video showed Trump praying along with others attending the convention. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes of the viral video led us to an Instagram post containing a carousel of photos from the Republican National Convention. In it, the first image featured Trump, sitting with his eyes shut with a bandaged ear, while the rest of the photos showed others attending the event also with their eyes shut. The caption of the post stated that these photos showed attendees praying on night one of the RNC.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Carol Thurstin (@thurstinca) Taking this clue, we found the live streaming of the first day of the Republican National Convention on the YouTube channel of CBN News . Three hours into the footage, Trump made his entrance at the event amid loud cheers . Following this, some speakers including model Amber Rose, talked about the challenges they faced under the Joe Biden administration. Then, pastor James Roemke was invited to the stage for benediction. The clip going viral can be seen at the three hours and forty-eight minutes mark when Trump sat with his eyes shut as the pastor began a prayer for justice, unity and protection of Trump from violence. Along with Trump, the video featured several other attendees with their eyes shut throughout the prayer. After this, Republican party leader Harmeet Kaur Dhillon offered "Ardas" during which people shut their eyes again. Per reports, Trump officially secured the GOP nomination for president on the Republican National Convention's day one, while Senator JD Vance from Ohio became his vice president pick . It is thus clear that the viral video does not show Trump sleeping. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Jul 16, 2024 22:03 IST

title: Fact Check: IPS officer Anu Beniwal is NOT the new Puja Khedkar, didn't misuse EWS quota
content:
Anu Beniwal's father is not an IPS officer. Sanjay Baniwal, whose name is visible in the photo, is a retired IPS officer who hails from Anu's village in Delhi's Pitampura.
As the controversy over Maharastra cadre trainee IAS officer Puja Khedkar's OBC and disability certificates rages on, social media has been flooded with allegations of fraudulent use of reservations by several bureaucrats across India. Threads on X have detailed how many Indian Administrative Service, Indian Revenue Service, and Indian Police Service officers allegedly benefitted from EWS or disability quotas despite not being eligible for them.Â
One such allegation was made against Anu Beniwal, an IPS officer from the Madhya Pradesh cadre. Many shared a screengrab of an Instagram post from Anu Beniwal's account and a list of people who cleared the 2021 UPSC civil services exam (CSE). Alongside, they claimed that despite being the child of an IPS officer, Anu took advantage of the economically weaker section (EWS) quota.
The Instagram screenshot showed Anu in the police uniform pointing to the name "Sanjay Baniwal" written on a plaque listing IPS officers of the 1989 batch from different cadres. Many social media posts claimed this was Anu Beniwal's father. The list of selected CSE candidates showed the EWS category against Anu Beniwal's name. Some also question how Anu Beniwal, who was a DANIPS officer before getting selected into IPS, was eligible for the EWS quota. DANIPS stands for Delhi, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Police Service.
Some also question how Anu Beniwal, who was a DANIPS officer before getting selected into IPS, was eligible for the EWS quota. DANIPS stands for Delhi, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Police Service.
So, is there any validity to these claims? Let's take a look: WHO IS ANU BENIWAL?
Hailing from Delhi, Anu Beniwal is a 2022 batch IPS officer from the Madhya Pradesh cadre, currently posted in the Gwalior district. She cracked the civil services exam of 2021. On July 14, 2024, Beniwal posted a picture with her parents on social media and wrote that while they couldn't even complete their "school education", they still pushed her to fulfil her dreams. I'm extremely proud of my mummy papa who couldn't even complete their school education but pushed me to fulfill my dream. I'm proud of their journey of battling the worst of the health challenges and still managing to smile for my happiness. 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/CM9dc0UzTN — Anu Beniwal (@AnuBeniwalIPS) July 14, 2024
I'm extremely proud of my mummy papa who couldn't even complete their school education but pushed me to fulfill my dream. I'm proud of their journey of battling the worst of the health challenges and still managing to smile for my happiness. 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/CM9dc0UzTN — Anu Beniwal (@AnuBeniwalIPS) July 14, 2024
This begs the question: How could her father be an IPS officer if he did not finish school? To verify this, India Today Fact Check spoke to Anu Beniwal, who dismissed the social media claims about her father as false and baseless. She said that while her father's name was Sanjay Beniwal, he was not an IPS officer. She explained that her father had been ill for many years and suffered from hearing and heart issues.Â
Beniwal said her father started a small button factory many years ago but her uncle had to manage it as her father's health prevented him from working. She added that her immediate family did not own any land or property and she was raised by her uncle.
We also found an online live interaction with UPSC aspirants from January 2022 where Beniwal said that her parents could not finish their education. SO, WHO IS 'SANJAY BANIWAL' WHOSE NAME IS SEEN IN PHOTO?
Anu told us that the "Sanjay Baniwal", whose name was on the plaque and who she referred to as "Tauji" or uncle in her Instagram post caption, is not her father. The post is not visible on Beniwal's Instagram ID as she archived it after the controversy.Â
She said Sanjay Baniwal hails from her village in Delhi's Pitampura, and added: "We are not biologically related. I call him 'Tauji' (uncle) as a term of endearment because he is from my village and inspired me a lot in my UPSC journey." She also stated that her father's surname was "Beniwal", not "Baniwal", which Sanjay uses.Â
Sanjay Baniwal is a retired IPS officer of the 1989 batch from the AGMUT or the  Arunachal Pradesh-Goa-Mizoram and Union Territory cadre. His last designation was Director General (prisons) in Tihar Jail. EWS QUOTA DESPITE DANIPS POST?
"It is simple maths," Anu Beniwal said. Anu scored an all-India rank of 638 in CSE 2020 and was allotted the DANIPS cadre. But Beniwal applied for CSE 2021 under the EWS quota before CSE 2020's results were announced. As per her, she did not hold a DANIPS post when she applied for the 2021 civil services exams.Â
India Today confirmed the same from the information available online. The result of CSE 2020 was announced on September 24, 2021, in which Beniwal was selected for DANIPS. However, six months before that, the UPSC notified about the application form for CSE 2021 (Preliminary) on March 4, 2021. The last date for application was March 24, 2021. Thus, she could not have known about her CSE 2020 results when she applied for CSE 2021 .
Anu Beniwal also told us that her DANIPS training began in May 2022. "I hadn't even received my DANIPS salary when I appeared for the CSE 2021 interview," she told India Today Fact Check.
So, while we haven't independently verified the validity of her EWS certificate, we could corroborate Anu Beniwal's statements with government documents available online. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Jul 16, 2024 22:15 IST

title: Fact Check: Ambanis DID NOT serve food in banana leaves, viral clip is from different wedding
content:
Viral video is not from the Ambani wedding, but from the reception ceremony of South Indian actors Deepak Parambol and Aparna Das held on April 24.
Following the grand event that was Anant Ambani and Radhika Merchant's wedding, a video of people in traditional outfits eating sadya  from banana leaves and paper cups began making the rounds on social media. Those sharing the clip claimed it showed a meal served at the grand wedding. Some even mocked the Ambani family for not serving food in proper cutlery at such a lavish event .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral clip is not from the Ambani wedding, but from a South Indian wedding reception that took place in April.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to similar videos  of the couple seen in the viral clip, eating from banana leaves at a ceremony .Â
One such video was shared on April 24, around three months before the Ambani-Merchant wedding. Its description in Malayalam, translated into English, read: "Aparna Das had a meal with her husband!"
Further searches led us to media reports about the wedding of Aparna Das, an Indian actress who has done several Malayalam and Tamil films. Aparna tied the knot with actor Deepak Parambol on April 24. The wedding took place at Kerala's Guruvayur temple abd was attended by close friends and family. Later in the day, they threw a grand reception which was attended by film stars and other guests at a hotel in Kerala.
The wedding photographer shared photos of Deepak and Aparna from the wedding ceremony and reception , which the couple reshared from their official Instagram handles. From the outfits seen in these pictures, it is clear that the viral video is from their reception.
Thus, an old video from the reception of South Indian actors was falsely claimed to be from the grand Ambani-Merchant wedding. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jul 19, 2024 16:41 IST

title: How fake IFS officer Jyoti Mishra conned her family, the police, and the media
content:
Anyone who actively uses social media in India is bound to have read the name "Jyoti Mishra" more than once in the last few weeks. Made in the wake of the Pooja Khedkar controversy , the accusation against Mishra  was fraudulently obtaining Scheduled Caste reservations despite being Brahmin to pass the Union Public Service Commission's Civil Service exam.
Those making the allegations on social media supported them with a video and a photo of a document titled "Civil Service Examination 2021 - Service Allocation". The video shows an award ceremony where a woman addressed the crowd and introduced herself as Jyoti Mishra. The document shows the category "SC" written against the name "Jyoti". Many on social media claimed this was the Jyoti Mishra in question.Â
Soon, an X account claiming to be Jyoti Mishra posted a clarification , stating it was a case of mistaken identity. According to the post, the Jyoti on the viral list was a different woman from Haryana, who is an IAS officer. The post further claimed that she, Jyoti Mishra, cleared the UPSC exam in the general category, appearing on a different result sheet indicating her selection for the IFS. This post has since been deleted.Â
Several social media users also came to her defence, alleging a conspiracy to defame a Brahmin woman. An X user named Mahendra Vikram shared a screenshot of an alleged UPSC result showing Jyoti Mishra listed under the general category, claiming her father Suresh Mishra provided him with the document. Vikram also issued another clarification on behalf of Jyoti Mishra , stating she was from Raebareli and is currently posted as third secretary in Madrid, Spain, on probation. ज्योति जी के पिताजी मेरे क्षेत्र में पोस्टेड रहें हैं, ब्राम्हण हैं और उनकी बेटी का चयन भी सामान्य वर्ग में हुआ है, इनका स्पष्टीकरण भी आया है की उनका नाम दूसरी लिस्ट में था pic.twitter.com/DrYsxO8USQ — Mahendra Vikram (@BjpMahendraup) July 15, 2024
ज्योति जी के पिताजी मेरे क्षेत्र में पोस्टेड रहें हैं, ब्राम्हण हैं और उनकी बेटी का चयन भी सामान्य वर्ग में हुआ है, इनका स्पष्टीकरण भी आया है की उनका नाम दूसरी लिस्ट में था pic.twitter.com/DrYsxO8USQ — Mahendra Vikram (@BjpMahendraup) July 15, 2024
This prompted several news organisations like the Times of India and Zee News to report this controversy.
The truth, however, is that while Jyoti Mishra appeared for it in 2022, she never cleared the Civil Service exam. She then lied to her family about her selection, leading to her name being discussed in several news reports that year as a success story.Â
UP POLICE FELL FOR HER DECEPTION IN 2022 Â
Jyoti Mishra is the daughter of Sub-Inspector Suresh Mishra , a police officer in the state of Uttar Pradesh. In 2022, several media reports highlighted her "success story", portraying her as the daughter of a common policeman who passed the country's most competitive exam despite several difficulties.
This narrative soon spread to all corners, so much so that even the Uttar Pradesh police took to social media  to congratulate her. She was also invited to programs honouring her supposed achievement. यूपी पुलिस परिवार की ओर से सिविल सेवा परीक्षा 2021 में ज्योति मिश्रा,(D/O सुरेश नारायण मिश्र,एस.आई. कमिश्नरेट लखनऊ) को 432 रैंक,आदित्य वर्मा,(S/O संजय कुमार, पुलिस अधीक्षक नगर मिर्ज़ापुर)को 200 रैंक एवं चित्रांशु गौतम पुलिस उपाधीक्षक को 630 रैंक हेतु हार्दिक बधाई एवं शुभकामनाएँ। pic.twitter.com/XgOXSH99Wr — UP POLICE (@Uppolice) May 31, 2022
यूपी पुलिस परिवार की ओर से सिविल सेवा परीक्षा 2021 में ज्योति मिश्रा,(D/O सुरेश नारायण मिश्र,एस.आई. कमिश्नरेट लखनऊ) को 432 रैंक,आदित्य वर्मा,(S/O संजय कुमार, पुलिस अधीक्षक नगर मिर्ज़ापुर)को 200 रैंक एवं चित्रांशु गौतम पुलिस उपाधीक्षक को 630 रैंक हेतु हार्दिक बधाई एवं शुभकामनाएँ। pic.twitter.com/XgOXSH99Wr — UP POLICE (@Uppolice) May 31, 2022
Reports from that year stated that the daughter of Suresh Mishra, posted at Kakori police station in Lucknow, became an officer at 23 by securing 432nd rank in the UPSC examination.
WAS JYOTI MISHRA'S NAME IN THE CSE 2021 RESULTS?
We checked the final CSE 2021 result on the UPSC website and found only two women named Jyoti in the final list: Jyoti Yadav (OBC) and Jyoti (SC). There was no Jyoti Mishra listed under the General category. We also perused the "Mains" exam results and the "Service Allotment List" for 2021 , which similarly only listed Jyoti Yadav and Jyoti. None of the seven allotment lists for the year mentioned Jyoti Mishra, a general candidate.
LIST NAMIN JYOTI MISHRA AS A GENERAL CATEGORY IS FABRICATED
The CSE result showing Jyoti Mishra as a general category candidate was shared on X in her defence was fake and edited. In this list, Jyoti's name had been altered to "Jyoti Mishra", and her category changed from SC to General, with IAS replaced by IFS.
India Today spoke exclusively to Jyoti Mishra, who admitted that in 2020 she informed her father about her intention to prepare for the civil services. Her father, with difficulty, provided the needed money from his savings intended for her marriage.
She attempted the CSE in 2020 and 2021 but did not clear it. The turning point came when her younger sister Aarti saw Jyoti's name on the results list and called her to confirm. Jyoti decided to seize the opportunity and replied in the affirmative. Excited, Aarti informed their father, who then shared the news with colleagues and relatives, leading to wide media coverage.Â
HOW JYOTI MISHRA KEPT HER DECEPTION ON
Jyoti Mishra admitted to India Today that she crafted her lies to avoid repeatedly disappointing her family every year. To evade detection, she claimed to be an IFS officer posted in Spain. To support her lie, she started pursuing a Spanish language course, thinking that the foreign language could also secure embassy jobs. Astoundingly, she never held a passport.
WHAT DOES JYOTI MISHRA REALLY DO?
Currently, Jyoti Mishra works at a semi-government company in Delhi, earning enough to cover her expenses without family support.
JYOTI MISHRA'S FATHER SPEAKS OUT
Suresh Mishra, her father, told India Today that Jyoti graduated with a bachelor of commerce degree from the Motilal Nehru College in Delhi University and joined "Vision IAS", a coaching centre, to prepare for the UPSC exam. In 2022, she lied to her family about clearing the Civil Service exam prelims, mains, and interviews. Trusting his daughter, Suresh never verified her results or asked for her roll number.
He recounted how Jyoti claimed to have been selected for the IFS. He was told that she went to the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy of Administration in Mussoorie for training. She later informed the family that she was assigned to Spain for language training. Despite never asking for money, Jyoti's fictitious success story went unquestioned by her family.Â
Suresh is now in shock after he realised the extent of his daughter's well-crafted cobweb of lies and fears the embarrassment it will bring to the family. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jul 19, 2024 17:51 IST

title: Fact Check: 2018 photo of Muslim man destroying statue of naked woman is from Algeria, NOT France
content:
The incident occurred in Setif, Algeria, in 2018, not France.
A post that has recently been widely shared online features two images — one of a man disfiguring a statue with a chisel and hammer, and the other of the mutilated statue of a naked woman. The statue's breasts and face appeared completely chiselled out. Allegedly, this act of vandalism took place in France and a Muslim man carried it out because he believed nudity to be a sin in Islam.
A Facebook user sharing the photo , "FRANCE. A man destroys the breasts and face of a female statue of a fountain, considering nudity as 'sin' (haram)." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the incident didn't take place in France but in Algeria, where a man vandalised this statue in 2018.
We ran a reverse image search and found several news reports from October 2018 containing the viral photo. A report by The New Arab, dated October 10, 2018, noted that the incident occurred in Algeria. It stated that a man with a hammer attacked and damaged a statue of a bare-breasted woman, an emblem of the eastern city of Setif.
Another report cited Setif communications director Mohamed Touiri, who stated that a Salafi, an ultraconservative Muslim, was responsible for disfiguring the face, breasts, and an arm of the statue.Â
Reports also stated that in 1997, during a period of peak extremist violence in Algeria, Islamists blew up the statue using dynamite. But it was later repaired in Italy.
Similar reports identifying the place of the incident as Setif in Syria can be seen here and here .Â
The Ain el-Fouara statue is located in the heart of Setif and serves as the centrepiece of a fountain, roughly 300 kilometres east of the capital Algiers. Created by French sculptor Francis Saint Vidal , the colonial-era statue dates back to 1889 and is a significant landmark in Algeria that draws thousands of visitors daily.
Thus, it is clear that this is an old incident that did not occur in France but in Algeria. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Jul 22, 2024 14:04 IST

title: Fact Check: Israeli swimmers DIDN'T call for release of hostages through human formation
content:
The viral picture is not from the Paris Olympics but from November 2023. The photo also has been digitally augmented, as evidenced by the same formations being repeated.
A photo of swimmers spelling out the slogan "BRING THEM HOME NOW" with their bodies has been widely shared as the 2024 Paris Olympics began. Allegedly, the photograph  showed Israeli swimmers at the Olympics demanding the release of hostages taken by Hamas on October 7, 2023.
A Facebook  user, while sharing the viral picture, wrote, "THE ISRAELI Olympic team was not allowed to wear their yellow 'Bring them home now' pins at the Olympics. SO the Israeli swimmers decided to show it this way for the whole world to see…" Its archive can be seen here .
The Free Press Journal, a news outlet, has also shared the photo with the same claim in a video report .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral picture is not from the Paris Olympics. It's also digitally augmented. OUR PROBE
A reverse image search led us to a post from November 19, 2023 by the Israel Ministry of Foreign Affairs  which contained the viral picture. The post said: "A beautiful tribute by Israel's national artistic swimming team in tribute to the 240 hostages being held by Hamas terrorists in Gaza. We will not stop until each and every one of them are brought home."
We also found a post  by Aviva Klompas, a former speechwriter for Israel's Mission at the United Nations. Klomaps shared the same photo on X on November 20, 2023, and attributed it to photographer Adam Spiegel. Israel's swim team pays tribute to the 240 hostages held by Hamas. #BringThemHome 📸 Adam Spiegel pic.twitter.com/UFm78zundu — Aviva Klompas (@AvivaKlompas) November 20, 2023 It is, thus, clear that the viral picture is not from the ongoing Paris Olympics. We also found an article in the Israeli news portal Ynet . The article mentioned that this photo featured Israel's artistic swimming team at the national pool at the Wingate Institute. The photograph featured athletes Eden Belcher, Shelly Bobritsky, Ariel Nashi, Nicole Nakhshonov, Kati Kunin, Maya Dorf, Neta Robichak, Shani Shraizin, Noi Gazela, and Aya Mazor. This article also cited Adam Spiegel as the photographer. We found Spiegel on Instagram , where his bio mentioned he is a fine art aerial photographer. His profile contained many similar aerial photos, and several of them featured swimmers. We also found that he shared the viral photo  on November 19, 2023, with the caption: "Home, now."     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Adam Spiegel (@im.adamico) We could not find any credible news report suggesting a ban on wearing "Bring Them Home" pins in the Paris Olympics, a slogan used to call for the return of the hostages abducted by Hamas following the attack on Israel on October 7, 2023. DISCREPANCIES WITH VIRAL PHOTO Looking closely at the viral image, we observed that the formations for the letters E, O, H, M, and N were repeated. We also observed that in the exclamation formation, the swimmers appeared to have been shrunk down. This suggests that the image was edited. A comparison can be seen below. advertisement It is thus clear that the picture is both old and edited. - Ends Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Jul 29, 2024 21:12 IST

title: Fact Check: Video from 2017 falsely shared as 2024 Venezuelan post-election protests
content:
The video is from 2017 when thousands of anti-Maduro protesters gathered for the "Mother of All Marches" along a highway in Caracas, Venezuela.
After Venezuela's President Nicolas Maduro secured a third term  on July 28 in a disputed election, many Venezuelans took to the streets, alleging electoral fraud.
Meanwhile, a video of a massive public gathering  with white smoke billowing in the background went viral on social media. Those sharing the video claimed it showed visuals of protestors overtaking the country following the election results.
A Facebook user shared the video and wrote, "Venezuela Riots. Protestors have completely taken over following the election result. Insane footage." Its archive can be found here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from 2017 when thousands of anti-Maduro protesters gathered for the "Mother of All Marches" along a highway in Caracas, Venezuela.
Reverse-searching the keyframes of the viral video, we came across several social media posts  containing it from April 2017. A Facebook user shared the video in April 2017 with a caption in Spanish that read , "People united shall always be victorious," while referring to Maduro as a dictator.
Similar posts from 2017 can be seen here  and here . This makes it clear that the video does not show recent protests in Venezuela.
A YouTube user also shared the video in April 2017, calling it the "Mother of All Marches" in Caracas. The description noted that tens of thousands of anti-Maduro protesters gathered in the capital on April 19, 2017. These protesters marched along a highway in Caracas , following a call from Opposition leaders to protest against President Maduro's policies.Â
The march, one of the largest in Venezuelan history, was named "Mother of All Marches." The demonstrators were met by riot police, which led to clashes and several casualties .
This protest came after the country's top court attempted to nullify the opposition-dominated Legislature . The court later restored power to the body after it drew anger from Venezuelans.Â
Thus, the viral video is an old clip from a 2017 protest and is being falsely shared as recent. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Jul 31, 2024 13:46 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Wayanad landslide. This video of a house getting drowned is from China
content:
This video is not from Wayanad, Kerala. It dates back to June this year and shows a flood in Meizhou, China.
Torrential rains triggered massive landslides in the hilly areas of the Wayanad district in Kerala killing more than 150 people . Dozens are still feared trapped. In its aftermath, a video of different stages of a house getting submerged by floodwaters was widely shared. Allegedly, this video was from Wayanad.Â
A Facebook user shared the clip with the caption , "Terrific footage in # wayanad , Kerala. #WayanadLandslide #WayanadDisaster." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video shows a flood in Meizhou, China, in June this year. OUR PROBE
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip  uploaded to a YouTube channel named "Disaster Update" on June 25, 2024. The caption reads, "16 June 2024 - Meizhou, Guangdong, China - Timelapse of severe flooding."
Per the description of this video, Meizhou, located in the Guangdong province of China, experienced subtropical monsoons with significant rainfall during the summer months. On June 16, 2024, Meizhou saw severe flooding due to heavy rains.Â
A subsequent search with keywords led us to Chinese news reports  featuring several screenshots from the viral video. These reports noted that water was released from the Huangtian Reservoir in the Meizhou area of Guangdong Province at noon on June 16. As a result, the village of Huangtian drowned in a flood within a few hours with water levels rising to two metres.
Another report  quoted Chinese government officials stating that at least 38 people died and two went missing due to the heavy rain and flood in the southern China area. Reuters in its report  dated June 21, also mentioned that 38 people lost their lives. It is, thus, clear that the video is not from Wayanad, Kerala, but from a village in Meizhou, China. - Ends Written By Surajuddin Mondal Published By: Ajmal Published On: Jul 31, 2024 17:40 IST

title: Fact Check: Samsung HAS NOT pulled its billion-dollar ad campaign from the Paris Olympics
content:
Samsung has not pulled its ad campaign from the ongoing Paris Olympics. An article from a satire website is being shared as fact.
Widespread criticism of the Paris Olympics' controversial opening ceremony has forced organisers to apologise. Now, social media users are claiming that the electronic giant Samsung has pulled back its billion-dollar campaign because the Olympics have allegedly gotten "too woke".
A Threads user wrote, sharing a still from the ceremony and another photo of the Samsung logo wrote: "Breaking: Samsung Drops Out of $1 Billion Advertising Campaign with Olympics, 'They've Gone Woke'." Its archive can be seen here.
An article published on July 29 by a website called "UK Discoverer" was also mentioned in the Threads post. The article reads, "In a surprising and highly publicised move, Samsung Electronics has announced its withdrawal from a $1 billion advertising campaign with the International Olympic Committee (IOC). The decision comes in response to what the company describes as the Olympics' increasingly 'woke' agenda, a stance that has stirred significant debate within both corporate and sporting worlds."
The opening ceremony that took place on July 26 caused massive outrage, with many claiming that it disrespected Christians.
India Today Fact Check found that claims regarding Samsung's withdrawal as the advertising partner are not true. The article was first published by a satire website.
A keyword search did not yield any credible reports about Samsung pulling out from the Olympics advertisement campaign. If something like this happened, it would surely be reported widely globally. We went through Samsung's official social media accounts and saw several Olympics posts with hashtags like #officialpartner and #Paris2024.
On the official website of the International Olympic Committee, we could not find any press releases about Samsung's withdrawal. The official website of the IOC mentions Samsung as a "global partner". It also says that the global partnership will continue through 2028.
Upon closely looking at the photo shared with the viral claim, we saw the logo "Rated Satire" in the top left corner. Searching further, we discovered that an article regarding Samsung and the Olympics was first published on July 28 on Epsotts, a satire website. Epsotts's "About Us" section says it specialises in satire and fake news.
In its fact-check article, Reuters spoke to the IOC regarding the viral claims. A spokesperson for the IOC said to Reuters that the claim is "incorrect," adding that the IOC has an agreement with Samsung through 2028.
The fact-checking website Snopes also noted in a different report that UKDiscoverer has a "track record" of posting false claims.Â
It is thus clear that Samsung has not pulled its ad campaign from the ongoing Paris Olympics. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Jul 31, 2024 21:31 IST

title: Fact Check: This ISN'T Ismail Haniyeh! Video of Gaza man viral as Hamas chief's last words
content:
The video is neither recent nor of Ismail Haniyeh. It showed a man injured in Israeli attacks in Gaza back in November 2023.
The assassination of Hamas chief Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran has caused a stir with Iran's Ayatollah Ali Khamenei ordering a direct attack on Israel in retaliation.
Now, a video , allegedly showing the last words of Haniyeh right before his death is making the rounds on social media. The clip features an injured man with bloodstains on his face and clothes, saying something with a finger pointed up. Those sharing it claimed that this is the last video of Haniyeh, where he appealed to Muslims to help the people of Gaza right before his death.
Sharing the clip on Facebook , one person wrote, "Last words of Ismail Haniya shaheed R.A. Plz help Gaza." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video is neither recent nor does it show Ismail Haniyeh. This video showed a man injured in Israeli attacks in Gaza back in November 2023.
Upon reverse searching the keyframes of the viral video, we found it in multiple posts from November 2023 , making it clear that it predates the death of Haniyeh.
The Arabic caption of one such post translates to: "Bleeding with blood. A Palestinian raises his index finger high and chants, We are all with the resistance. A steadfastness that you will only find in Gaza."Â
Further, we found a Telegram channel as well as an Arabic news report that shared this video at the time, stating it is from Gaza. According to them, the man seen in the viral video said, "We are all with resistance."
We noticed that the viral video had the name "Mohamed Obied" written in it. A Google search about this name led us to an Instagram account of a Palestinian journalist named Mohamed Obied .
Obied has shared several videos of Palestinian victims of Israeli airstrikes on this account. He shared the viral clip on November 6, 2023 . According to the post's caption, the children of this man died in the Beach Camp, also known as Al-Shati or Shati, a Palestinian refugee camp located in the northern Gaza Strip.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Mohamed obied |محمد عبيد (@mohamed_obied77)
A post shared by Mohamed obied |محمد عبيد (@mohamed_obied77)
We then contacted Mohamed Obied on Instagram, who confirmed that he shot this video on November 6, 2023, at the Al Shifa Hospital in Gaza. The man seen in the video was admitted in an injured condition while some of his family members died in an Israeli attack at the Beach camp.
It is, thus, clear that an old video of a man injured in an Israeli attack in Gaza is being shared as the last video of Hamas chief Ismail Haniyeh. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Aug 2, 2024 17:09 IST

title: Fact Check: This photo of 'new legend of Olympics' shooting backwards is edited!
content:
The viral photo is edited. It originally featured Turkish Olympian Yusuf Dikec, who was replaced with a Thai comedian shooting backwards.
A photo of a man holding a mirror in one hand and a gun in the other, aiming backwards, has left many amazed on social media. Those sharing the image hailed the man as the "new legend" of the Paris Olympics 2024, as the event's backdrop is visible in the picture .
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this impressive picture is edited. The original photo featured Turkish Olympian Yusuf Dikec, who was replaced with the image of a Thai comedian shooting backwards. OUR PROBE
A reverse search of this photo led us to a news report about Yusuf Dikec, featuring a similar photo . Turkish Olympic shooter Yusuf Dikec won a silver medal in the 10-meter Air Pistol Mixed Team event . The 51-year-old shooter became an internet sensation overnight for competing without any optical gadgets, eye cover, or ear protection. A comparison between the original photo of Dikec and the one going viral can be seen below. Further search led us to a tweet by "Thai Enquirer," a media outlet in Thailand. The tweet contained a collage of multiple Olympic shooters, including the viral photo. The caption read, "Another shooter has entered the scene: Thai comedian Pongsak 'Theng Therdtherng' Pongsuwan." Another shooter had entered the scene: Thai comedian Pongsak "Theng Therdtherng" Pongsuwan. #Thailand #Olympics #Olympics2024 #Paris2024 #OlympicGames #โอลิมปิก2024 #โอลิมปิก #โอลิมปิกเกมส์ pic.twitter.com/VArp0C405u — Thai Enquirer (@ThaiEnquirer) August 2, 2024
Further search led us to a tweet by "Thai Enquirer," a media outlet in Thailand. The tweet contained a collage of multiple Olympic shooters, including the viral photo. The caption read, "Another shooter has entered the scene: Thai comedian Pongsak 'Theng Therdtherng' Pongsuwan." Another shooter had entered the scene: Thai comedian Pongsak "Theng Therdtherng" Pongsuwan. #Thailand #Olympics #Olympics2024 #Paris2024 #OlympicGames #โอลิมปิก2024 #โอลิมปิก #โอลิมปิกเกมส์ pic.twitter.com/VArp0C405u — Thai Enquirer (@ThaiEnquirer) August 2, 2024
Another shooter had entered the scene: Thai comedian Pongsak "Theng Therdtherng" Pongsuwan. #Thailand #Olympics #Olympics2024 #Paris2024 #OlympicGames #โอลิมปิก2024 #โอลิมปิก #โอลิมปิกเกมส์ pic.twitter.com/VArp0C405u — Thai Enquirer (@ThaiEnquirer) August 2, 2024
With this clue, we found a media report  about Pongsuwan. According to the report, Pongsak Pongsuwan is a comedian known for his appearances on "Ching Roi Ching Larn," a comedy show by Thai TV production company Workpoint Entertainment.
Additional searches led us to a video of the comedy show  featuring Pongsuwan on the official YouTube channel of Workpoint Official. In the video, Pongsuwan can be seen using a mirror to aim backwards and shoot at a balloon behind his back. At the 3:10 mark, he can be seen in the same pose as in the viral photo.
It is thus clear that the photo of a man shooting backwards at the Olympics is edited. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Aug 3, 2024 19:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Old Karate contest photo shared as Palestine flag raised at Paris Olympics
content:
The photo is from a Karate International Championship held in Slovenia in 2022. Karate was not included in the Paris Olympics.
In light of the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict, a photo allegedly showing two Egyptian karate players holding a Palestinian flag on the winners' podium is going viral on social media . The claim states that the Egyptian black belts raised the Palestinian flag after defeating Israel at the Paris Olympics.
The photo shows the Egyptian players  standing in first and second place on the podium, with an Israeli competitor holding his flag in third place. A Facebook user sharing the viral photo , wrote, "Two Egyptian black belts raised the Palestinian flag after defeating an Israeli opponent at the Paris Olympics." An archived version of the viral post can be found here .
India Today Fact Check found that the photo is from a Karate International Championship held in Slovenia in 2022, and not the Paris Olympics. Moreover, karate was excluded from the Paris Olympics.
A reverse image search of the photo led us to several social media posts  from November 2022, where it was captioned as being from a karate international championship in Slovenia, with Egyptian players raising the Palestinian flag.Â
Using this clue, we found reports from " The Palestine Chronicle " and " Middle East Monitor "  dated November 21, 2022, which included the viral picture. According to these reports, Egypt's U-15 youth team showed solidarity with Palestine by holding the country's flag after taking first and second place at the World ITKF Traditional Karate Championship in Slovenia. The Israeli competitor finished third in the tournament.
Additionally, "Egypt Independent" also carried the viral photo  with the same information. The video of the incident can also be found on the YouTube channel of the International Traditional Karate Federation (ITKF).
 Thus, it is clear that the viral photo has no connection to the ongoing Paris Olympics. It's worth noting that karate debuted at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics but was not included in the Paris Games due to concerns about its entertainment value and youth appeal. - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Aug 5, 2024 15:44 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Muslim Awami League leader lynched in Bangladesh given false communal spin
content:
The victim's name is Shahidul Islam Hiran. He is a Muslim and local Awami League leader from Jhenaidah, Bangladesh.
Amid violent protests that led to the resignation of Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina , a disturbing video is doing rounds on social media. The video, which shows a hanging dead body, has been widely shared with the claim that it shows an elderly Hindu man being lynched and hanged on a statue in Bangladesh by extremists chanting religious slogans.Â
An X user shared the clip , and wrote, "Heartbreaking. An old Hindu man is lynched and hanged on a statue by terrorists of Jamaat-e-Islami in Bangladesh. Islamists were seen raising Allah-Hu-Akbar slogans around him… #SaveBangladeshiHindus." An archive of this post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the person in the video was not Hindu. He is Shahidul Islam Hiran, General Secretary of Awami League's Jhenaidah Sadar Upazila unit and Chairman of the local municipal body. He is a Muslim. OUR PROBE
We noticed several users replying under the viral post who identified the victim as Shahidul Islam Hiran. With this clue, we searched the internet and found a YouTube video  uploaded on August 5, 2024, titled "Awami League leader and Chairman Hiran was killed and hanged by the crowd in Jhenaidah."Â
Further search led us to a Bengali news report  featuring a screenshot from the viral clip alongside a photograph of Hiran. The report detailed that Shahidul Islam Hiran tragically lost his life when an angry mob attacked and set fire to his house in Stadium Para, Jhenaidah City. Afterwards, the mob carried his charred body and hanged it in the Piara area.
For corroboration and to confirm these details, we contacted Tanveer Islam, a fact checker associated with Rumor Scanner, an independent fact-checking organisation in Bangladesh. He confirmed that the deceased person seen in the viral video is indeed Shahidul Islam Hiran.
Thus, the viral video does not show an elderly Hindu man being lynched and hanged in Bangladesh. Instead, it shows Shahidul Islam Hiran, a Muslim Awami League leader from Jhenaidah, Bangladesh. - Ends (Written by Surajuddin Mondal.) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Aug 6, 2024 20:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of dead Muslim family from Bangladesh shared with communal spin amid unrest
content:
The July 28 video precedes Sheikh Hasina's exit from Bangladesh and shows a Muslim family from the country's Brahmanbaria district, found dead under mysterious circumstances.
Following former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's escape from Dhaka, there have been reports of Hindu temples being attacked in various districts of the country. Violent mobs also allegedly targeted Hindu families, the reports said. A horrific video now being shared on social media shows a man, a woman, and two young children hanged to death in a house.Â
An X user alleged while sharing the video: "An entire Hindu family was wiped out by Islamic jihadists in Bangladesh just because they were Hindus. Where are the eyes of the world? #SaveBangladeshiHindus." Several Facebook and Instagram users also posted the viral video with similar claims. An archive of the post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from July 28 and precedes Sheikh Hasina's exit. The video also shows four members of a Muslim family found dead in Brahmanbaria's Nabinagar in Bangladesh. Our Probe
On reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we found it was shared on Facebook on July 28 . The caption (originally in Bangla) said: "Four mysterious deaths of the same family in Nabinagar Brahmanbaria."Â
A subsequent keyword search led us to various news reports published in Bangladesh's English and Bangla news outlets. According to a report by The Daily Star , a family of four was found hanged to death in their house in the Nabinagar area of the Brahmanbaria district. The report mentioned that the dead were identified as Sohag Mia, 33, his wife Jannat Akhter, 25, and their two daughters aged four and two.
Reports noted that Sohag Miya was a cloth merchant in the Nabinagar market. According to Sirajul Islam , the assistant superintendent of Nabinagar Police Station, the bodies were recovered from the Bijoypara municipality area around 9 am on July 28.Â
According to another Bangladeshi news outlet , Sohag Miya had a loan of five lakh taka and his sister Yasmin said he was depressed. Police superintendent Mohammad Shakhawat Hossain told reporters that they suspect Sohag Miya killed his wife and two daughters and committed suicide over to a family dispute.
Tanveer, a Dhaka-based journalist, told India Today Fact Check that the family found dead was Muslim, adding that no one was arrested in this case as the police suspected it was a case of suicide. He also said there was no further update on the case because of the ongoing civil unrest in Bangladesh.
It is thus clear that the four people seen dead in the viral were not Hindus, but Muslims. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Aug 8, 2024 17:22 IST

title: Fact Check: Hindu women being tied up and sold by Muslims in Bangladesh? NOPE, here is the truth
content:
This video shows students in a Dhaka university tying up Chhatra League leaders amid the quota-reform protests. Chhatra League is the students' wing of the Awami League, Sheikh Hasina's party.
Amid violence and unrest in Bangladesh following the resignation of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, a video of burqa-clad women tying up other women by rope to a pillar went viral on social media . Those sharing it claimed that Muslim women in Bangladesh took Hindu women as hostages to be tortured and sold into sex slavery.
One person shared the video on Facebook writing, "Hinid(sic) women in Bangladesh are being taken hostage and sold by the Muslims that just came into power. Where is the outrage? Where are the protests?" Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video precedes Sheikh Hasina's exit and shows students in a university in Dhaka, tying up leaders of the Chhatra League, the student wing of the Bangladesh Awami League, amid the quota-reform protests.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to the same video shared by a Facebook user on July 18 . Its Bangla caption stated that the video was from Badrunnessa College. A Google search revealed that Begum Badrunnessa Government Girls' College is located in Dhaka. At the time, many shared the viral clip  stating that it is from the same college .
Further searches led us to several media reports  about this incident. Four leaders of the Bangladesh Chhatra League (the student wing of the Bangladesh Awami League) were reportedly made to hold their ears and do sit-ups by student protesters at the Begum Badrunnessa Government Girls' College . Additionally, student protesters tied two Bangladesh Chhatra League leaders to a pillar using ropes, a video of which went viral on social media.
As per reports , the incident took place on July 17 in the college dormitory. Students protesting against the quota reforms at the college tied up leaders of the Awami League students' wing after an altercation . However, when teachers intervened, they were able to leave the college campus.
Habiba Akhtar Simon, the general secretary of the Chhatra League at this college reportedly  left the campus before the incident occurred. Moreover, there were allegations against Simon and Selina Akhtar Shelly, the president of the Chatra League, of beating up college students in the past. This old grudge fueled anger among students who then punished the four student leaders present at the campus during the protest.
We also found videos of the four leaders doing sit-ups at the college campus along with other footage of this incident in Facebook posts from July 17.  Thus, it is clear that a video of students tying up student leaders of the Chhatra League was shared as from ongoing unrest in Bangladesh, with a false communal allegation. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Aug 8, 2024 18:39 IST

title: Click, bet, lose: How online swindlers lure, trap and exploit people in India
content:
For Sahil, a resident of suburban Hyderabad, the night intervening June 3 and 4 was an anxiety-riddled one. He tossed and turned, unable to sleep. As the 24-year-old IT professional doom-scrolled in the dark, he couldn't help but second-guess the Rs 3 lakh he had borrowed to place an insane bet: that the National Democratic Alliance would win nine or more seats from Andhra Pradesh in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.Â
But as counting began in the morning, Sahil felt silly about the previous night's disquiet. The NDA, an alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party, the Telugu Desam Party, and the Jana Sena Party, was leading comfortably in the state. By the afternoon, he was already daydreaming about the car he wanted to buy with the Rs 6 lakh he thought he would win. Â
The final tally practically made him jump with joy. The NDA won 21 of the state's 25 Lok Sabha seats, far higher than he could have imagined. He was on top of the world.Â
On June 5, the day after the election results, Sahil logged into Cricbet99.win, the website where he placed the bet, to rake in his rewards, only to be rudely made aware that he had lost.
Panicking, he contacted the website's customer support. There, he was given the baffling explanation that according to the website's rules, in Andhra Pradesh, the NDA comprised only the BJP and the YSRCP (Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party). The two parties had won just seven seats, so he technically lost the bet. This was the first time Sahil learned this rather strange "definition" of the NDA.
Sahil kept typing into the customer care chatbox. But soon, the responses he received began to appear automated. And then, there was silence. They hung him out to dry. Â
Sahil isn't alone. Many others bet large sums of money on election results and were cheated out of their winnings on similar flimsy grounds by platforms like Cricbet99.win, Winbuzz, Reddy Book, and Jannat Book. Â
Prabhakaran, another victim, told India Today: "My friends and I pleaded with them. Some even said that this left them with no option but to end their lives." Â
Akshay, another Andhra Pradesh resident who lost Rs 1.5 lakh, felt that reaching out to such unresponsive helplines was not enough. He started looking for other victims like him on social media and found close to a hundred. They banded together and threatened to take the matter to the police. This had some impact. Within the next few days, a number of these platforms settled smaller bets of less than Rs 1 lakh. This was the first hint that these betting platforms could be interconnected. On further investigation, India Today Fact Check found more evidence to support this premise. We found that their social media accounts promote each other. At least some of them can be linked to the infamous 2023 Mahadev betting app case . And all of them use similar tactics to lure victims. BABAS, BOLLYWOOD, DEEPFAKES "It started with a link shared by a friend over email. Initially, I used to bet only on major cricket matches. But gradually, I got addicted. I started betting on stuff as trivial as pre-match tosses. These websites are designed to get people addicted," Sumit S from Tamil Nadu, who has been gambling online for a decade, told India Today. "Many of my acquaintances also signed in on these platforms because they saw some celebrity promoting them on social media." advertisement While certain celebrities have indeed endorsed online betting platforms, deepfakes of actors , sportsmen, industrialists, and even spiritual leaders are often used to lure people. A video viral on Facebook shows Aniruddhacharya Maharaj, the self-styled godman  who famously defined a biscuit as "vish ki kit" (a kit of poison), endorsing a "betting expert"  called Cricket Pandith. This is, of course, a manipulated video. In another deepfake video, actor Hrithik Roshan seems to be promoting Rocky Bha i, another alleged "expert". India Today Fact Check found at least 24 such deepfake videos  featuring celebs like Akshay Kumar , Rajkumar Rao , MS Dhoni  and more. Digvijay Singh, the co-founder of Contrails AI , a Bengaluru-based startup developing a deepfake detection tool said that most of these were created by first generating an AI-cloned celebrity voice and then lip-syncing it with publicly-available footage. 'EXPERTS' THAT DON'T EXIST The deepfakes promoting so-called betting "experts" like Rocky Bhai, Hitler Fixer, and Tiger Dubai are all fake — personas created using stolen photos of actors and influencers to make people believe that these "betting experts" live lavish lives. advertisement For instance, US-based trader Umar Ashraf's  Instagram photos  were used  to create  the profile of the fictitious Rocky Bhai. Similarly, actor Nameer Nawaz Khan's photo  was used by "betting expert" Kabir Diwan , another fictitious person. LAYERS OF DECEPTION We found that for the uninitiated, even reaching the betting app was a rather multi-stepped complicated process. When you click on these ads, you're led to websites like Toptipperonline.xyz , Best-onlinetipper.xyz , and Therealprediction.online . From here, you're directed to the Telegram channels of "experts", and finally to the actual betting website or app, where you place your bets. Some of the betting websites promoted through such Telegram channels are Cricplus.pro , Reddybook.club , and Winbuzz.live . Why do these betting apps make the process this complicated? According to Arielle Garcia, the Director of Intelligence at Check My Ads, a non-profit advertising watchdog: "Driving users to a landing site which then directs them to Telegram would help evade landing page scans that Meta might perform during ad review."  advertisement WHERE DOES THE MONEY GO? To understand how people are scammed, we decided to put ourselves in the victims' shoes. We followed a deepfake ad which led us to the betting platform Cricplus.club. To create a new account, we followed a set of instructions given by the website representative through a WhatsApp chat. We were asked to pay a mandatory charge of Rs 100 to a provided bank account. We observed something strange here. The deepfake-powered online betting platform wanted us to make the payment to a "kirana" or grocery store. Clearly, something fishy. It was a Bank of Maharashtra account belonging to the "Shubham General and Kirana Stores". The Google Pay profile of the account also confirmed the same thing. Following the Indian Financial System Code or IFSC associated with this account, we located the home branch of that account. We contacted both, the central helpline of the Bank of Maharashtra as well as the concerned branch manager. The branch manager told us on the condition of anonymity that this account belonged to a nearby departmental store. While the manager refused to give us details of the account's transactions, he did confirm that the transactions' patterns were "unusual". He also told us that following our email to the Bank of Maharashtra head office in Pune, there was an official enquiry about the same account. "Currently, we are monitoring it, and as a precautionary measure, we have frozen withdrawal from the account," the manager said. He explained that he had come across cases in the past where people were not aware that their accounts were being used for fraud. They just agree to let someone use their bank accounts for a small sum without realising this is illegal. Several news reports  confirm what the manager said. Such accounts are called "mule" accounts. While we were working on this story, the Bank of Maharashtra head office informed India Today Fact Check that this case has been reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit under the Union Ministry of Finance's Department of Revenue for further investigation. THRIVING IN A GREY ZONE Online betting in India exists in a legal grey zone because of somewhat vague definitions. When betting is a game of skill, it is considered legal; but it becomes illegal  when it's a game of chance. A lack of a centralised law leaves the betting industry largely unregulated. This makes it difficult for victims to find recourse. Shivam, a betting app scam victim, told India Today that he did not approach the police because he was unsure if betting on elections was legal. He was afraid that filing a police complaint might just land him in more trouble. There is also an element of shame. Betting is considered an addiction and is looked down upon. Several victims we spoke to expressed guilt and embarrassment about their losses and decided to let the matter go rather than report it to the police. But there is another more pressing reason why these websites and apps escape legal action. They operate from across borders, making prosecution difficult. When we looked into the Facebook pages sharing the deepfake ads for betting websites, we noticed that the location mentioned in their  "intro" sections  shows names of Indian cities. However, a look at their "Page transparency" section reveals that this is misleading. Many of them are managed from countries like Bangladesh, Ghana, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Venezuela, and the US. Though it is possible to manipulate the location mentioned in the page transparency section, according to experts, it is uncommon. HOW THEY TARGET YOU The scam betting platforms are careful about flying under the radar to avoid detection. They precisely target people who are likely to fall prey, at times using a tactic called "dark posts" . As the name suggests, dark posts are not visible to everyone. Unlike regular posts, these sponsored posts promoting the betting platforms do not appear in the timeline of the Facebook pages sharing them. Targeted advertisement is not a new phenomenon. In 2016, during Donald Trump's presidential campaign, such ads  were used to target black voters. The scammers keep scouring data about the people who give out even the smallest of signals that they might be interested in online betting. They do this through ad trackers and malware. Your every click on such websites and ads sends them a signal that you could be a potential target.  REINCARNATION OF MAHADEV SCAM? Mahadev Book , a betting platform, was accused of laundering money through a "Benami" bank account network. Former Chief Minister of Chhattisgarh, Bhupesh Baghel, among others, was accused of accepting bribes from the app's promoters. The Centre banned many betting websites that were part of Mahadev's syndicate at the time. However, there are reports of these websites resurfacing with new avatars .  Two platforms we looked into, Winbuzz and Cricbet99, both promoted through deepfake video ads, were mentioned in an FIR filed by the Maharashtra police in the Mahadev app case. We also found that several social media accounts in the name of the Mahadev app promoted the betting websites Winbuzz  and Laser247 . We could not independently verify if these "Mahadev" social media accounts are connected to the original scam or if they are riding on its popularity. FOR VICTIMS, IT'S A LONG ROAD TO JUSTICE Even as many fraud cases go unreported, it is widely known that misleading ads are used to trap gullible people. The Annual Complaints Report 2023-24  released by the Advertising Standards Council of India (ASCI) highlighted that illegal offshore betting rank second in the list of all fraudulent ads. ASCI's CEO Manisha Kapoor said, "We report such cases to the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting for further action." However, that hardly helps victims like Sahil, who lost, even as the NDA won in Andhra Pradesh. The website that defrauded him also figures in an FIR about the Mahadev scam. But thousands of people like Sahil are waiting for the day when investigators join these dots and bring them to justice. (Victims' names changed at their request) - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Aug 9, 2024 20:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Video from Canada edited to cast Bangladeshi protesters as pro-Pakistan
content:
The viral clip is edited. It is not from Bangladesh, but from Canada during Pakistani Independence Day celebrations in 2023.
As the situation continues to unfold in Bangladesh following Sheikh Hasina's escape, a video  allegedly from the country is being shared on social media featuring people holding Pakistani flags. Purportedly, it shows Bangladeshi Muslims raising Pakistani flags and chanting pro-Pakistan slogans.Â
An X user while sharing the video wrote, "Bangladeshi Muslims with Pakistan flag are threatening 'Direct Action' on Hindus. We helped them get their country Bangladesh and they threatening us of Direct action day and want to merge with Pakistan … the same Pakistan which r@ped more than 5 lakh Bangladeshi women, k!lled millions …Bangladesh truly is a b@s***rd ch!ld which don't deserve  to exist." Several people also shared the video with similar claims on Facebook . Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral clip is not from Bangladesh. It shows a Pakistan Independence Day celebration in Toronto, Canada, in 2023. The video was also edited to replace its original audio with Bangla slogans.
Reverse-searching the keyframes of the viral clip, we found several Instagram videos from August 2023. These videos, shared by a disc jockey named "Djmian", had similar visuals. Upon comparing the two, we observed signages for shops like "Lahore Tikka House" and "Desi Burger" in both. A comparison can be seen below.
Interestingly, the Instagram videos did not have the Bangla slogans heard in the viral clip.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by DJ Mian (@djmian) We then searched the locations seen in the viral clip on Google Maps. We found Lahore Tikka House and Desi Burger located in Gerrard St E, Toronto, Canada. A video shared by Djmian on August 17 mentions that the videos were from the 2023 Pakistan Independence Day celebration in Canada. We also found various YouTube vlogs from the same location from August 16. In these vlogs as well, no Bangla slogans could be heard. Instead, celebratory songs in Punjabi are heard in the videos. What do the Bangla slogans say? In the viral video, the slogans that can be heard are, "Bhuru kaata Pamela, aar korish na jhamela. Aar korish na jhamela, Bhuru kaata Pamela. Pakistan-er Khaleda, Pakistan-e chole Jaa. Pakistan-e chole Jaa, Pakistan-er Khaleda." Bhuru  is eyebrows, Pamela  is a name that Awami league (Sheikh Hasina's party) supporters mockingly call former prime minister Khaleda Zia. The slogan translates to: "O eyebrowless Pamela, don't create a mess anymore, don't create a mess anymore, O eyebrowless Pamela. You are Pakistan's Khaleda, better go to Pakistan. Better go to Pakistan, Pakistan's Khaleda." This is a slogan that has long been used by Awami League supporters against Khaleda Zia. We also found a video report from May 31, 2018, where the same slogan can be heard. It is thus clear that the viral clip is edited. It is not from Bangladesh, but from Canada during the Pakistani Independence Day celebration in 2023. advertisement  - Ends With inputs from Riddhish Dutta Published By: Vivek Published On: Aug 9, 2024 21:47 IST

title: Fact Check: Zelenskyy did NOT respond to a question about Kursk with a smile, here is the truth
content:
Viral video is from the 2023 Nato Summit held in Lithuania, where Zelensky was responding to a question about the delivery of weapons from America.
Russia launched a "counter-terror operation" in three border areas as Ukraine's cross-border attack in the Kursk region entered its fifth day on August 10. This is Kyiv's biggest cross-border offensive since Moscow invaded Ukraine two-and-a-half years ago, leading to the imposition of a federal-level emergency in Kursk.
Now, a video making the rounds on social media showed Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, seemingly at a public event, smiling and allegedly responding to a question about the situation in Kursk with "I don't know".
One person shared the video on Facebook writing, "Journalist: 'Zelenskyi, what's going on in Kursk?' Zelemsky: 'I don't know'".
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from the 2023 Nato Summit held in Lithuania, where Zelenskyy was responding to a question about the delivery of weapons from America.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to its longer version shared on the YouTube channel of The Independent, on July 12, 2023. Its description stated that this video showed Zelenskyy speaking after the Nato Summit in Lithuania's Vilnius concluded with the declaration of support for Ukraine.
In it, the viral clip can be seen at the mark of 6:51, when a journalist asked Zelenskyy when Ukraine would receive long-range missiles from the United States. In response, Zelenskyy said "I don't know" while smiling. He added that it was a complicated decision that had not been made at the time and that Ukraine was having a conversation about it with the Biden administration.
The two-day Nato summit, held on 11-12 July 2023, in the Lithuanian capital Vilnius, was attended by Ukraine in the hopes of getting a Nato membership, but it could only get pledges of more arms and ammunition . Ukraine had long been asking the US for long-range ATACMS missiles, but the US remained reluctant, fearing escalation in the war . However, the US quietly delivered a small number of ATACMS missiles that were reportedly used by Ukraine for the first time on the battlefield on October 17, 2023.
As per reports, Zelenskyy has not made a direct reference to the situation in Kursk so far. On August 6 , Zelenskyy released a video stating that Ukraine is gaining an upper hand in the usage of drones, strategically impacting the war. In another video, released on August 8 , Zelenskyy said that Russia needed to "feel" the consequences of the war it brought to the land of Ukraine. He further praised the ability of the Ukrainian army "to surprise" and achieve results on the battlefield as he announced the launch of the "Army+", a new application for soldiers.
However, Mykhailo Podolyak, a senior adviser to the president's office, made the first acknowledgement of the incursion and said that the root cause of any escalation was unequivocal aggression of Moscow . Ukrainian officials have remained tight-lipped about the attack. On Wednesday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the Ukrainian army "know how to surprise and ... how to achieve results" without directly referencing the assault. https://t.co/2UJhDJWOjg pic.twitter.com/3WGV3a7sTs — DW News (@dwnews) August 8, 2024
Ukrainian officials have remained tight-lipped about the attack. On Wednesday, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the Ukrainian army "know how to surprise and ... how to achieve results" without directly referencing the assault. https://t.co/2UJhDJWOjg pic.twitter.com/3WGV3a7sTs — DW News (@dwnews) August 8, 2024
It is thus, clear that an old video from the NATO summit was falsely linked to Ukraine's cross-border offensive in Kursk. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Aug 10, 2024 19:12 IST

title: Fact Check: These Bangladeshi women forced to do sit-ups are NOT Hindus
content:
Both videos show Mulsim Chhatra League members being harassed. These clips do not show the persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh.

Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we came across a video of the same incident uploaded to YouTube on August 8. The caption suggested that the woman was a leader of the Chhatra League, the student wing of Sheikh Hasina's party Awami League.
Further searches led to another video of the same incident , showing the woman who had confronted the woman in black, displaying items recovered from her purse. Among the items was an identity card from the Upazila Parishad elections, where she served as a polling agent. This featured her name written in Bangla, Afsana Ibad.

title: Fact Check: No, this vandalised structure in Bangladesh is NOT a Hindu temple
content:
The structure in the viral clip is not a Hindu temple, but a Sufi shrine in the Jessore district. It was attacked on the night of August 5.
On August 10, Hindus in Bangladesh took to the streets to protest the violence against the community after Sheikh Hasina's exit from the country. Now, a video being widely shared on social media purports to show a Hindu temple being set on fire in Bangladesh by Muslims.Â
Sharing the viral clip on X , a user wrote, "Islamists torched a Hindu temple in Thakurgaon district of Bangladesh." The viral clip was also shared widely on Threads  and Facebook . The archive of one such post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the structure in the viral clip is not a Hindu temple, but a Sufi shrine in Bangladesh's Jessore district. It was attacked on the night of August 5. OUR PROBE
By reverse searching keyframes from the viral clip, we found a longer version of the video uploaded to Facebook  on August 7. The caption of the video shared by "Sunni TV" read: "Was the movement made to break the Shrine?" Looking at this video closely, we found that the video was recorded on the night of August 5. At the 03:03 minutes mark, a smartwatch was visible which displayed the day and date — Monday, August 5.
We found another Facebook post from August 7 which featured the same video. Its caption (originally in Bangla) suggested that the structure was a shrine called Hazrat Garib Shah Mazar Sharif.
We saw a clearer picture of the shrine in a Facebook post from August 8 . We translated text written on it using Google Lens. It read, "Hazrat Garib Shah Mazar Sharif." It was thus clear that the structure that was vandalised was not a temple, but a Sufi shrine.
We also found a YouTube video shared on August 7 , where spectators could be seen narrating how the shrine was attacked. We also found a news report which mentioned the attack on Hazrat Garib Shah Mazar . WHERE IS THE MAZAAR LOCATED?
We searched the location on Google Maps  and found that it is not located in Thakurgaon District as claimed in the viral posts. Instead, the shrine is located at Gorib Shah Road in the Jessore (also spelt as Jeshore) district of Bangladesh. The Google Maps screenshot can be seen below. Jessore is more than 400 kilometres away from Thakurgaon. We also spoke to Tanvir, a Dhaka-based fact-checker working with Rumor Scanner, who corroborated that the incident took place on the night of August 5. It is thus clear that a video of a Sufi shrine being attacked is being shared as that of a Hindu temple. It's noteworthy, however, that there are reports that mention how Hindu temples and Hindu homes were attacked in the violence that erupted after August 5. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Aug 12, 2024 21:09 IST
