India Today Fact Check found that the video shows a scuffle between the anti-quota protestors and Chhatra League students at Jahangirnagar University in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Our Probe
Reverse searching key frames of the viral video led to the original stream, posted by Syeda Ananya Faria, who identifies as a Jahangirnagar University student. The video was streamed at approximately 1:18 am on July 16.
Although this video did not carry a caption, the complete version helped us understand that there was no incident of rape or molestation. Instead, it depicted a group of students hiding in a place and trying to save their lives. The cries of "bachao" (save us) and "they will kill us" in Bangla are fairly audible here.
We went through other posts on Faria's Facebook profile and found that around 12:14 am on the same day, Faria shared a post of another Jahangirnagar University student, Ayasha Siddika Bristy, who shared some videos and wrote, "We are suffering from shelterlessness. While protesting in front of Vice-Chancellor Sir's residence, we got a tip with evidence that hundreds of armed outside goons were coming to beat us in pickup trucks. We have broken the gate and are staying at the residence of VC to be secure."
Faria shared another post  at 1:40 am, pleading for the administration's help. She wrote, "For God's sake send the police. They are attacking us with bricks, fire and glass. We are at VC's door. Will we be safe if they open the gate!"Â
None of the posts mentioned any kind of sexual assault taking place there.Â
To understand what happened at Jahangirnagar University on July 16 at midnight, we searched using relevant keywords and found several Bangladeshi reports. Per The Daily Star's report , a three-way conflict between anti-quota protestors, the Bangladesh Chhatra League, and the police resulted in midnight mayhem at Jahangirnagar University.
Another report published in the United News Of Bangladesh mentioned that more than 50 students were injured, and the protesting students had to take refuge inside the VC's residence.
Speaking to India Today Fact Check, Syeda Ananya Faria said that on July 16, Chhatra League cadres attacked some students brutally when they were holding a peaceful rally against the quota system. She said, "We went to the VC seeking justice, who neither came in front nor talked to us. While returning, the Chhatra League cadres again attacked us with weapons, when we took shelter in the courtyard of VC's residence. The police also didn't help. So, a few of us started doing Facebook Lives and sought help. Seeing this, a few hundred students came from campus and saved us."
Faria added, "I can't even imagine how some people can give this a communal spin."
Thus, it becomes clear that a month-old video of the clash between two groups of students was shared with a communal spin to it. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Aug 13, 2024 23:27 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show a BJP leader slapping a bank manager
content:
The man, Mayur Borde, is not a BJP leader, but a youth wing leader of the Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana. The incident occurred at the Warud branch of the Bank of Maharashtra in Maharashtra's Jalna district on August 13.
In a video that's been shared widely on social media shows a bunch of sitting in what appears to be a Bank of Maharashtra office when a verbal altercation escalates to violence. The assaulter, allegedly a Bharatiya Janata Party leader, could be seen slapping the man behind the desk multiple times.
Sharing the viral clip on X , a user wrote, "A BJP leader has the audacity to slap a Public Sector Bank Manager. The Arrogant BJP should soon be taught a lesson." An archived version of the post can be seen here . The viral clip was also shared by several Facebook users .
India Today Fact Check found that the man assaulting the bank manager was not a BJP leader but Mayur Borde, leader of the Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana. He assaulted a branch manager of the Bank of Maharashtra in Maharashtra's Jalna district. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching the keyframes of the viral clip, we found its screenshots published in various Marathi  and English  media reports. An Indian Express report  mentions that this incident took place in Maharashtra's Jalna district on August 13. The report further states that Mayur Borde, a leader of Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana's youth wing, slapped the manager of the Warud branch of the Bank of Maharashtra.
Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana is a farmers' union affiliated with the Swabhimani Paksha, a political party. According to a report by TV9 Marathi , farmers trying to withdraw money from their accounts were sent away multiple times by the bank manager Dhirendra Sonkar. The farmers reportedly complained to Borde about the same. Angry with the "harassment of farmers", Borde went to the bank with the farmers and the argument led to him slapping Sonkar.
The bank manager, Dhirendra Sonkar, filed a First Information Report against Borde at Jaffrabad police station. IS MAYUR BORDE A BJP LEADER?
Mayur Borde is the youth wing leader of Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana. Its political wing, Swabhimani Paksha, was formed by Raju Shetti in 2004. Shetti was a two-time Member of Parliament from Hatkanangale Lok Sabha constituency in Maharashtra's Kolhapur district from 2009 to 2019. Shetti joined the Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance in 2014 but left in 2017 after alleging that the party cheated farmers.
In 2024, Shetti fought the Lok Sabha polls independently and lost to Shiv Sena's Dhairyasheel Sambhajirao Mane.
Hence, it is clear that Mayur Borde is not a BJP leader. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Aug 14, 2024 16:57 IST

title: Fact Check: 2023 video of Trump talking about new variant of Covid-19 linked to monkeypox
content:
This video has nothing to do with the monkeypox crisis. It is from August 31, 2023, and shows Trump talking about the new variant of Covid-19 that was spreading in the US at the time.
The World Health Organization declared the increasing spread of monkeypox in Africa a global health emergency on August 14 after a new variant of the virus was identified. 1,100 people have reportedly died in the Democratic Republic of Congo since the current outbreak of monkeypox or mpox began in January 2023. The highly contagious disease has now spread outside the continent , with cases emerging in Sweden and Pakistan.
As countries prepare themselves to battle the spread of the disease, a video of Donald Trump allegedly warning of election fraud in the US amid the spread of mpox started making the rounds on social media . In the video , Trump accused the "left wing" of trying to bring back lockdowns and reviving the Covid-19 hysteria as the US heads into the 2024 presidential elections.
In one such Instagram post  the text inside the video read: "Trump warns of potential election fraud and lockdowns in connection with monkeypox." Its archive can be seen here . The Free Press Journal also carried this video  claiming that Trump warned of lockdowns and election fraud amid the mpox crisis. India Today Fact Check found that this video has nothing to do with monkeypox. It is from August 31, 2023, and shows Trump talking about a new variant of Covid-19 that was spreading in the US at the time. OUR PROBE A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video posted on a YouTube channel in September 2023, making it clear that this video predates the current monkeypox crisis. The description of the video stated that Trump attacked Democrats for efforts to bring back Covid-19 mandates ahead of the 2024 elections. Further searches led us to multiple news reports about this video, dated August 30, 2023. According to them, Trump released this video , asking people of the United States to stand firmly against the resurgence of mask mandates, vaccine mandates and lockdowns in the country. He alleged that the sudden resurgence of alarm over new variants of Covid-19 in the US was meant to manipulate the upcoming elections.
India Today Fact Check found that this video has nothing to do with monkeypox. It is from August 31, 2023, and shows Trump talking about a new variant of Covid-19 that was spreading in the US at the time.

Back in August 2023, several hospitals, colleges, and institutions reintroduced requirements for staff or visitors to wear masks to limit the spread of new coronavirus variants, EG.5 and BA.2.86. The admissions of patients suffering from COVID-19 in the US had been steadily rising since July 2023.

title: Fact Check: Video of Kohli condemning violence against women is OLD
content:

The rape and murder of a trainee doctor in Kolkata 's RG Kar Medical College and Hospital has led to major protests  taking place across the country. A video  now going viral shows Indian cricketer Virat Kohli condemning violence against women.Â

title: Ever got a video call from Flipkart Support? This is what happened to me on Raksha Bandhan
content:
While most Monday mornings fill me with dread, August 19 began on the most perfect of notes. The chatter of cousins and the intoxicating aromas of khoye ki barfi and dal kachori woke me up on that fateful sunny morning in Kanpur, my home town. It was Raksha Bandhan and I couldn't wait to see what my brother had got me this year.
As I tied the Rakhi around his wrist, my eyes wandered around, trying to see if my brother was hiding my gift behind his back. He wasn't. He teased me for a few minutes, claiming he had forgotten to buy me anything this year. I playfully indulged his excuses, till he finally admitted that my gift was on its way: A brand new smartphone!
It took me no time to bully him into giving me his phone so that I could track the package online. The Flipkart app showed that the phone would be delivered the same day. Great. But I was impatient. And I ended up calling the number listed for the delivery person, who politely mentioned he'd reach my place in a couple of hours.Â
But a couple of hours passed, and then some. I called him again. He said he was on his way to my home and would reach in an hour. When he didn't show up again, I called him once more. He apologised for the delay but assured me my phone would reach me the same day. And then, he went awol. Sometime around the afternoon, Flipkart informed us that the delivery was delayed and that I would receive my brand-new phone in four days.Â
Obviously, I was both heartbroken and furious. The customer service chatbot gave me automated responses, which only added to my fury. Finally, I did what most desparate customers do when they fail to get results. I took to X to complain to Flipkart.Â
Within minutes, I got a response from two different X accounts called Flipkart Support, which provided "customer service" phone numbers. Immediately, I found this fishy. For one, neither account replied to my post — rather, they quoted my complaint. And when I took a closer look at the account handles, I was in no doubt this was a scam. The X handles were "@flipkart2468" and "@BonmKumar54580", clearly indicating they weren't official accounts.Â
As a journalist who has investigated online scams and frauds for years, my "Spider-Sense" was tingling. I decided to see where these numbers would lead me. So, I gave one of them a call.Â
The person on the other end patiently listened to me and assured me that my phone would be delivered the next day. He added that he had escalated the matter to his senior manager who would call me soon. "Please do receive the call," he insisted before hanging up.
To my surprise, the call I received next was a WhatsApp video call. While the profile picture featured the Flipkart logo, the question anyone should ask at this point is: What official customer support helpline video calls you?Â
I picked up the call but immediately switched off my camera. The person on the other end kept insisting that I switch on my camera. "If you do not want to show your face, you can flip the camera. But it is necessary to keep the camera on during our call," he said. This, again, should be a red flag for anyone. Why would you need to keep your phone camera on during a customer service call?
And then came the show-stopper. The person on the other end asked me to click on the "three dots" in the bottom left corner of the call and select the first option. If I did this, I would end up sharing my phone screen with him, something you can do on a WhatsApp video call.Â
Obviously, I refused. And in case you experience this, so should you!
There is no good reason to share your screen with a stranger ever. And the person on the other end tried to justify this with vague reasons like "standard procedure". It's not.Â
After insisting for a couple of minutes, he gave up, and hung up the call before threatening, "Let's see how your problem gets resolved now!"
The scammers bit off more than they could chew by trying to defraud me. But here's how things would have gone had I not been vigilant:
Step 1: They would get you on a WhatsApp video call. Step 2: They would get you to share your screen with them. Step 3: They would then send you a request from a malicious app and note down the OTP (one-time password) when it pops up. Step 4: They would use that to drain your bank account. THE 'FLIPKART' SCAM
After this episode, I checked and found that multiple X accounts like these try to defraud people by responding to them with fake customer service numbers. In fact, Flipkart has shared a detailed post on how to spot fake accounts like these.
Reeta Yadav, the cyber crimes head at the Noida Sector 36 police station told me that scammers use such tactics to ensure they can see your screen and sensitive information like OTPs. Â
"These days, everybody is in a hurry and such scammers take advantage of this," said Mohan Krishnamurthy Madwachar, the country manager for Sattrix, a cyber-security firm. "To reach out to customer care executives, it is always safe to connect through the official website or App of the e-commerce platforms."
But this isn't the only approach. Most experts told me that another way scammers try to defraud is by getting you to install a screen-sharing app on your phone, which gives them complete control over your device. They use apps like TeamViewer, RemotePC, AnyDesk and more to take control of your device and subsequently rob you. A HAPPY ENDING
After this odd experience, I dug around and found the official customer service number for Flipkart. I called them and explained my problem, and they assured me that my phone would reach me the following day. This time, thankfully, the delivery person did as was promised. My Rakhi gift almost turned into a Rakhi grift. Make sure yours doesn't as well by being just a little cautious. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Aug 20, 2024 22:49 IST

title: Fact Check: Did a bird unfurl Tricolour in Kerala? Get the 'right' angle here
content:
Another video of this incident from Kerala revealed that the bird flew and sat on a tree behind the flag and had no role to play in the hoisting of the flag.
A video  that looks like it came straight out of a patriotic movie, features a bird unfurling the national flag. The viral video shows a group of people trying to hoist the national flag, which gets stuck at the top of the flagpole. Suddenly, a bird flies towards it and as it flies away, the flag unfurls .Â
Those sharing the video claimed that a bird helped unfurl the flag during Independence Day celebrations in Kerala .
A person shared this video on Instagram writing, "During a flag-hoisting ceremony in Kerala, the national flag got stuck at the top. To everyone's surprise, a bird appeared out of nowhere and managed to unfurl the flag. The incident, captured on video, amazed viewers and quickly went viral. The unique moment highlighted both the unexpected intervention and the patriotic spirit of the occasion. Many users on the internet say it's an unimaginable clip".
India Today Fact Check found another video of the incident shot from a different angle, which revealed that the bird flew and sat on a tree behind the flag and had no role to play in the hoisting.
As the incident was allegedly from Kerala, we conducted keyword searches in Malayalam and found a Facebook post dated August 17 containing the viral video. The caption stated that this incident took place at an Anganwadi centre in Malappuram's Mampad.Â
We then contacted Shihab, a member of ward 7 of the Mampad Panchayat, who hoisted the national flag on August 15. He sent us another video of the same incident, shot from another angle, that makes the whole story clear as day.
Shihab told India Today that this incident took place at an Anganwadi centre in the Maramangalam village of Kattumunda. Kattumunda is a ward in the Mampad Panchayat of Kerala's Malappuram district.Â
He said, "The viral video was recorded from where it looked like the bird came near the flag. But, if you watch the video carefully, you will realise that it was away from the flag and sat on a coconut tree. The video was also shared by Asianet News in a video report about the incident.
It is thus, clear that the video of a bird helping people unfurl a national flag was nothing but an optical illusion created due to camera angle.
(Translated by Sanjana Saxena) - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Aug 21, 2024 16:56 IST

title: Fact Check: This Bangladeshi woman forcefully made to resign by students is NOT Hindu
content:
The video shows Amena Begum, a Muslim woman who was the principal of a government college in Bangladesh, resigning from her post amid pressure from student protestors.
Amid global protests against attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh since the fall of the Sheikh Hasina-led government, a video of a woman forcefully made to tender her resignation is making the rounds on social media. According to those sharing the clip, Muslims in Bangladesh forced this Hindu woman to resign from her government job.
In the clip, a woman is seen writing something on a piece of paper in a crowded office. She throws her pen away in anger as a person puts a stamp on that paper and then shows it to the people surrounding her, who cheered loudly. The woman then leaves the premises of a building surrounded by a huge crowd.
Sharing the video on Instagram, one person wrote, "Mass forced resignation of Hindus from government offices in Bangladesh. Jago Hindu Jago."
India Today Fact Check found that the video showed Amena Begum, a Muslim woman who was the principal of a government college in Bangladesh, resigning from her post amid pressure from student agitators.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook post, dated August 11, containing the video. Its caption in Bangla stated that Amena Begum, the principal of Kabi Nazrul College, resigned and threw away her pen.
Further searches led us to multiple media reports about this incident. According to one report, the principal of Kabi Nazrul Government College, Amena Begum, quit on August 11, after protesting students demanded her resignation. Reportedly, student protesters began chanting slogans demanding her resignation from 11 that morning. As soon as Begum reached the campus, the agitating students surrounded her in the office.
Giving in to the pressure, Begum resigned from her post writing "I resigned" on a white paper and signing it. Per reports , the protesting students accused Begum of not inquiring into the death of four students and the hundreds of students who got injured during the anti-quota protests. The students also alleged that she supported Sheikh Hasina's party, the Awami League, and accused her of corruption and various irregularities.
Following this incident, students also demanded the dissolution of the teachers' council of the college, accusing the members of being pro-Awami League. Following this, the vice principal of the college, Saleh Ahmed Fakir dissolved the teachers' council as well.
We also found the Facebook page of Kabi Nazrul Government College, where a post made on August 7 this year featured the photo of Amena Begum. It stated that she was a member of Awami League's Education and Human Resources Subcommittee (2022-2025).
It is thus, clear that a video of a Muslim principal of a government college in Bangladesh being forced by students to resign was passed off as atrocities on Hindus in the strife-hit country. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Aug 22, 2024 19:52 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of police beating up Bharat Bandh protesters in Meerut is 6 years old
content:
The viral video is from 2018 when police beat up protestors from a different Bharat Bandh.
Many Dalit and Adivasi organisations protested the recent Supreme Court verdict on Scheduled Caste reservations and observed a Bharat Bandh on August 21 . Amid this, a video  allegedly from Uttar Pradesh's Meerut is being shared on social media with claims that the UP police had beaten up the protesters. In the viral clip, a few men can be seen running outside a building that looks like a police station.Â
Sharing the viral clip on X , one person wrote, "Some glimpses of today's Bharat Bandh in Meerut, UP. Don't mess with UP Police and @myogiadityanath ji."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is old. It is from 2018 when police beat up protestors from a different Bharat Bandh.
Reverse searching the keyframes of the viral clip, we found several news reports from 2018 , where screenshots from the viral video were used .Â
According to an April 4, 2018 report in News18, the video was shot at Meerut's Kanker Khera police station. The report stated that the people running out of the station were miscreants who allegedly caused violence  during a Bharat Bandh on April 2, 2018. It is, thus, clear here that the viral video has nothing to do with the strike on August 21, 2024.
According to various media reports  from 2018, Dalit organisations observed a Bharat Bandh in the country against changes to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.Â
The strike turned violent in Meerut. We found various news reports  that mentioned arson, vandalism, and ruckus by the protestors in the Uttar Pradesh city. Some reports  also claimed that people had died during the 2018 strike.
We then contacted AajTak's Meerut correspondent Usman Chaudhary, who was in Meerut during the said incident in 2018. Chaudhary corroborated that the viral clip was from 2018 and showed Meerut's Kanker Khera police station.Â
Chaudhary said that during the Bharat Bandh in 2018, some miscreants vandalised a Shobhapur police check post on the Delhi-Dehradun Highway. The Shobhapur check post falls under the Kanker Khera police station. Following the ruckus, the police detained many protestors and brought them to the station, where they were beaten up.
However, there are also reports of the police beating up protestors during the Bharat Bandh on August 21 in Bihar's Patna. However, nothing of that sort had been reported for Meerut at the time of writing this. - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Aug 22, 2024 21:33 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of water gushing out of floodgates is from Andhra Pradesh, not Tripura
content:
This video is not from Tripura, but of Andhra Pradesh's Srisailam Dam discharging water from its gates.
As Bangladesh recovers from weeks of political turmoil and loss of lives due to violence, floodwaters inundated the country's eastern region, affecting some 4.5 million people . Simultaneously, heavy rain triggered landslides and floods in India's northeastern state of Tripura, forcing 65,000 people out of their homes.
While floods affected both countries, the disaster also stirred a political controversy as Bangladesh accused India of causing sudden floods by opening a river dam in Tripura.
Now, a video is going viral on social media in which a huge amount of water is gushing out of a dam, as people look from a distance. Many shared the clip , claiming it showed Tripura's Dumbur dam on the Gumti River.
One person shared the clip  on Facebook and wrote, "Status of Dambu Hydroelectric Power Project or Dambu Gate in Tripura, India. May Allah protect us from this terrible situation."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video is not from Tripura. It showed Andhra Pradesh's Srisailam Dam discharging water from its floodgates. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to similar videos  of the dam gushing out water, uploaded by multiple YouTube channels  in August this year . According to their description, this was Srisailam Dam.
The Srisailam Dam  is constructed across the Krishna River on the border of Mahabubnagar District of Telangana and Kurnool district of Andhra Pradesh. We then went on Google Maps and looked for photos of the Srisailam Dam . A comparison between them and the dam seen in the viral video confirmed that they are the same. Further searches led us to multiple media reports  about the opening of the gates of Srisailam dam. According to the reports, 10 out of the total 12 gates of the Srisailam Dam were opened on July 30 this year, attracting tourists in large numbers. 25 personnel were deployed on both sides of the ghat road to regulate the traffic. 3.59 lakh cusecs of water was reportedly released downstream, into the Nagarjuna Sagar. Per reports, the gates of the Srisailam dam were closed on August 12  as the rains stopped in Maharashtra and Karnataka and the inflows into the dam receded . A video of tourists capturing selfies as the Srisailam dam gushed out water from its gates was shared by a Telugu media outlet on July 31 . Notably, the Ministry of External Affairs issued a press release on August 22 , clarifying that the floods in Bangladesh were not triggered by release of water from the Dumbur dam in Tripura. Instead, the catchment areas of the Gumti River, which flow through Bangladesh as well as India, witnessed the heaviest rains of this year, primarily causing floods. advertisement Further, Tripura Power Minister Ratan Lal Nath tweeted  that no floodgates had been opened. However, excess water from the Gumti reservoir escaped through a spillway as it crossed the 94-m full capacity mark. Flood situation in Bangladesh not due to release of waters from Indian dam on Gumti River, Tripura: https://t.co/8hcnRkoBF1 pic.twitter.com/p5zY0LII7D — Randhir Jaiswal (@MEAIndia) August 22, 2024 It is thus, clear that a video of Andhra Pradesh's Srisailam Dam was falsely shared as from Tripura, implicating India of causing floods in Bangladesh. - Ends Published By: Pathikrit Sanyal Published On: Aug 24, 2024 20:31 IST

title: Fact Check: 2018 video of Congress leader's remarks shared in connection with upcoming J&K polls
content:
Congress leader Haji Sagheer Saeed Khan did make these remarks but in 2018. The party distanced itself from the controversial statement at the time.
For the first time after the abrogation of Article 370 in 2019, Jammu and Kashmir will see Assembly elections  in September and October. This will also be the first Assembly elections in a decade there. The Indian National Congress announced it will contest in alliance with Farooq Abdullah's Jammu and Kashmir National Conference.Â
A video now making the rounds shows a man, allegedly a Congress leader, speaking on terrorists and terrorism in the valley. The man can be heard saying, "If Congress comes to power, we will end the violence caused by the BJP. The people who are jailed for terrorism would be released. Those who are killed in the name of terrorism, their families would be compensated with Rs 1 crore." He further says that those BJP leaders who ordered the Indian Army to encounter people would be hanged under the Congress rule.
An X user, while sharing the viral clip , wrote, "Congress promises to J&K people that if they win: They'll release all the terrorists locked in jail They'll give 1 crore compensation to the families of those who were killed. They'll hang all the BJP leaders who spoke against terrorism."
The viral clip was shared by several users on Facebook  as well. Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral clip is from 2018. At the time, the Congress had distanced itself from Sagheer Saeed Khan's controversial remarks. OUR PROBE
Several X users claimed that the Congress leader in the video was Sagheer Ahmed . We also observed the logo of "JK Media" in the viral clip. Using these clues, we ran a keyword search and found the viral clip uploaded to the YouTube channel JK Media on December 26, 2018.Â
This made it clear that the viral clip is not related to the upcoming elections in Jammu and Kashmir . According to this clip, Congress leader Sagheer Saeed Khan made these remarks in Jammu.
We also found several media reports  regarding Sagheer Saeed Khan's statement. According to a report by News18 , the controversial statement was made by Haji Sagheer Saeed Khan, who was a minority cell observer in the All India Congress Committee.
In June 2018, the Bharatiya Janata Party withdrew its support to the Jammu and Kashmir People's Democratic Party-led government and the Governor's Rule was subsequently imposed in Jammu and Kashmir. Later on December 20, 2018, the President's Rule was imposed by the then-Governor Satya Pal Malik. These controversial statements by Haji Sagheer Saeed Khan had landed the party in a soup.
According to an India Today report , the Congress at the time distanced itself from the leader and his remarks. "The Congress disowns and rejects Sagheer Saeed Khan's statement. He is not a spokesperson of the party. He has no mandate to speak on such issues. We will recommend our national leadership to take action against him. We stand with our security forces in the fight against terrorism," Ravinder Sharma, then-chief spokesperson of the Jammu and Kashmir Congress said.
Furthermore, we found a video statement by Ravinder Sharma on the Jammu and Kashmir Congress' official Facebook page as well.
It is thus clear that the controversial statement by the Congress leader is not recent. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Aug 27, 2024 23:12 IST

title: Fact Check: Call 7837018555 to get free drop home? No, this service is ONLY for Ludhiana women
content:
1091 is a helpline service for women in any kind of trouble and operates in many states. 7837018555 provides a pick-and-drop facility to women at night but only in Ludhiana.
A message making rounds online claims that if women get stuck without any kind of transport at night, they can call a police helpline number and receive a drop home free of cost.
The viral message reads, "The police have launched a free travel scheme where any woman who is alone and cannot find a vehicle to go home between 10 pm and 6 am can contact the police helpline numbers (1091 and 7837018555) and request a vehicle. They will work 24x7 hours. The control room vehicle or the nearest PCR vehicle/SHO vehicle will take her safely to her destination. This will be done free of cost. Spread this message to everyone you know. Send the number to your wife, daughters, sisters, mothers, friends, and all the women you know. Ask them to save it. All men please share with all the women you know." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral helpline number 7837018555 is only available in Ludhiana. On the other hand, 1091 is a Central Social Welfare Board number under the National Commission for Women. It's a helpline number for women in distress.
We found a December 1, 2019 report in the Hindustan Times, according to which, this helpline was started in Ludhiana after the gang rape and murder of a doctor in Hyderabad. Reportedly, the Ludhiana police introduced a free night pick-up and drop service for women and there were two helpline numbers, 1091 and 7837018555, available from 10 pm to 6 am for women in need of assistance. Both numbers stated in the news report were the same as the viral claim.
We sent the viral message to a police officer who handles this helpline, who told us that the number 7837018555 was started by Ludhiana Police in 2019 and is still active. The officer added this was not a national helpline number but only for the women in Ludhiana. However, when we called this number, no one answered.
It is a nationwide helpline for women by the Central Social Welfare Board under the National Commission for Women. Any woman in distress can seek help by dialling this number. We called this number, and a woman police officer from Delhi picked up the phone.Â
She told us that if any woman is unable to find a vehicle at night and feels unsafe, she can seek help through this number. India Today Fact Check could not independently confirm if this number provides the service in every Indian state.Â
BLANK MESSAGES AND MISSED CALLS WON'T WORK Â
According to the viral message, in an emergency, women can get help by just sending a blank message or giving a missed call to 1091 and 7837018555. However, the police officers handling these numbers told India Today Fact Check that this is untrue. Women will have to make a call to get help.
Several states have helplines for women travelling at night, for example, women in Uttar Pradesh can call 112 in such a situation. A similar helpline was started by the Nagpur police in 2019, through which women could reach their homes safely at night. Aaj Tak Nagpur correspondent Yogesh Pande told us this facility is still available. रात्रि 10 से सुबह 6 के बीच अकेली महिलाएं क्या करें? 🚨112 पर कॉल करके एस्कोर्ट करने के लिए अनुरोध करें ! 🚨अपनी लोकेशन, निकटतम पहचान चिन्ह यदि ज्ञात हो तो उसे शेयर करें ! 🚨 PRV (पुलिस प्रतिक्रिया वाहन) आप तक पहुंचकर, आपको घर तक सुरक्षित एस्कोर्ट करेगी । pic.twitter.com/ysFI6KxDf3 — Call 112 (@112UttarPradesh) August 23, 2024
रात्रि 10 से सुबह 6 के बीच अकेली महिलाएं क्या करें? 🚨112 पर कॉल करके एस्कोर्ट करने के लिए अनुरोध करें ! 🚨अपनी लोकेशन, निकटतम पहचान चिन्ह यदि ज्ञात हो तो उसे शेयर करें ! 🚨 PRV (पुलिस प्रतिक्रिया वाहन) आप तक पहुंचकर, आपको घर तक सुरक्षित एस्कोर्ट करेगी । pic.twitter.com/ysFI6KxDf3 — Call 112 (@112UttarPradesh) August 23, 2024
In many states, women can ask for help at night by dialling the 112 helpline. According to a News18 report , since the start of this helpline, 1,781 women from 11 districts of Chhattisgarh have benefited from it.Â
While many states have the facility to drop women home at night, some state police departments called the viral message misleading. For example, the Karnataka Police called this message fake and wrote that in an emergency, one should dial 112.
Similarly, the Hyderabad Police termed the message fake and Kolkata police also refuted this message in 2019.
It is thus clear that the 7837018555 number helps women to reach home at night but it is available only in Ludhiana. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Aug 30, 2024 20:20 IST

title: Fact Check: Kohli DID NOT demand death penalty for Kolkata rape-murder accused
content:
This video is edited. In the original video, a 2022 interview, Kohli spoke about his IPL performance.
Following the Kolkata rape-murder case that spawned protests across India, the West Bengal government called a special session of the state Assembly to pass a new anti-rape bill on September 2.
Now, a video of the former captain of the Indian cricket team, Virat Kohli, talking about the RG Kar murder and rape case is making the rounds on social media . In it, Kohli can be heard condemning what happened to the victim, adding that all the rapists should be hanged to death.
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video was edited. In the original video, Kohli was talking about his IPL performance in this 2022 interview.
Reverse searching keyframes of the viral video led us to a similar video of Kohli in a post dated April 7 . In it, Kohli could be seen discussing how many Indian Premier League teams had the opportunity but did not back him until he became successful. He also spoke about his 2018 England tour.
With the help of this clue, we found the original video shared on the official YouTube channel of Royal Challengers Bengaluru on February 26, 2022. In the video, Kohli talked about how the IPL changed his life, what the Royal Challengers Bangalore team meant to him, how he handled the highs and lows in his life, and more.
In this video, the portion going viral on social media can be seen at the 6:52 timestamp. In it, Kohli said how in the first three years of the IPL, he could not play up to his potential because he was not playing at number three in the IPL.Â
As opposed to the viral clip, Kohli can be heard saying, "I felt like the composition of that team, where they were amazing players, and rightly so in the right positions, I was not able to play in the position that was my strength." The movement of Kohli's lips and face in this portion matches the viral clip.
It is noteworthy, that Kohli has not issued any statement about the Kolkata rape-murder case at the time of writing this report.Â
Recently, another video of Virat Kohli , seemingly criticising top-order batter Shubman Gill went viral on social media. It was later found out that the video was taken from his 2019 interview with American journalist Graham Bensinger and an AI-generated audio of Kohli was added to it. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Aug 30, 2024 21:41 IST

title: Fact Check: Cleric removing taweez from Muslim child's neck in Bangladesh given communal spin
content:
The child seen in the video is not Hindu but Muslim. His name is Sohail Haque and the cleric removed a taweez or amulet from around his neck.
Approximately 50 lakh people in 11 districts of Bangladesh have been severely affected by flooding. According to the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief in Bangladesh, the floods have killed at least 67 people.Â
A video now viral on social media purports to show a Muslim cleric removing a sacred thread from around a Hindu child's neck as the child stands in water. An Instagram user shared the clip, and wrote, "A Maulvi gave relief material to a Hindu child in Bangladesh and cut off his 'mala' in return while saying Subhan Allah, Allah Hu Akbar. When the child asked for 'Mala' , they told him to take the relief material and leave and not worry about Mala ."
India Today Fact Check found that the boy in the video is not Hindu but Muslim. His name is Sohail Haque, and his father is Abdul Haque. They reside in the Char Algi village in the Noakhali district of Bangladesh. No Hindu deity's picture or mala was removed from around his neck. Instead, the man removed a Muslim amulet or "taweez". Our Probe
The video contained Bangla text, which translates to: "Relief materials handed over to the son in Noakhali and removed his shirk."
A subsequent search with related keywords led us to a Facebook page named Tawheed Academy and Islamic Center, where we found the same clip. The post in Bangla translates to: "Alhamdulillah, Tawheed Academy and Islamic Center distributed relief materials to 200+ families among the flood victims of Noakhali." We then contacted the Tawheed Academy and Islamic Center to get to the bottom of the matter. Malek Miyazi, the assistant principal of the Jami'a Darut Tawheed Madrasa, which is run by Tawheed Academy and Islamic Center, told India Today Fact Check that he was the individual who removed the taweez from a child's neck. "The child seen in the video is not a Hindu. He is Muslim and his name is Sohail Haque. His father's name is Abdul Haque. They reside in Char Algi village, Noakhali district, Bangladesh. And no Hindu deity's picture or mala was torn from his neck. Instead, a Muslim's taweez was removed," he explained.Â
We then contacted the Tawheed Academy and Islamic Center to get to the bottom of the matter. Malek Miyazi, the assistant principal of the Jami'a Darut Tawheed Madrasa, which is run by Tawheed Academy and Islamic Center, told India Today Fact Check that he was the individual who removed the taweez from a child's neck. "The child seen in the video is not a Hindu. He is Muslim and his name is Sohail Haque. His father's name is Abdul Haque. They reside in Char Algi village, Noakhali district, Bangladesh. And no Hindu deity's picture or mala was torn from his neck. Instead, a Muslim's taweez was removed," he explained.Â
Miyazi said: "A taweez is an amulet, often containing verses from the Quran or other religious inscriptions, that is worn by some Muslims for protection or healing. However, according to Islam, relying on a taweez for protection might imply a lack of trust in Allah, which is called Shirk. So during the distribution of relief, we remove any taweez we see on someone's body to free Muslims from Shirk. When this child came to us for relief, we noticed a taweez around his neck. I removed it with my teeth. This is not an issue of Hindu-Muslim relations, as there is no Hindu community in that area; it is entirely inhabited by Muslims."
Miyazi also provided an introduction video of a child as evidence of his religious identity. In the video, the child states his name and identity and reads from the Quran. He says, "My name is Sohail. My father's name is Abdul Haque. My home is in Char Algi village, Noakhali district, Bangladesh. I am a third-grade student at a local madrasa."
Thus, it's clear that the viral video doesn't show a Muslim cleric removing a sacred Hindu thread from around a Hindu child's neck; instead, it shows the cleric removing an Islamic amulet from a Muslim child. - Ends (Written By Surajuddin Mondal) Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Sep 3, 2024 19:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Flogged for converting to Christianity? No, this old clip is related to an affair
content:
This video is over two years old and from Sangareddy, Telangana. It shows a brawl between two families over an alleged extramarital affair.
A disturbing video of a youth getting beaten by a mob with sticks is making rounds on social media. Allegedly, this video showed how a Hindu man was assaulted because he converted to Christianity. Â
One such post  was captioned: "Is leaving Hinduism and converting into other religion crime in this country? This man was brutally beaten by mobs just because he left Hindusim and converted himself into Christian." Another post read: "HINDUS ATTACK A MAN FOR CONVERTING TO CHRISTIANITY."
India Today Fact Check has found that this incident is more than two years old and is unrelated to conversion. OUR PROBE
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we came across the same clip shared on X  in July 2022. The post identified the victim as Begari Naresh, a Scheduled Caste man who was thrashed in Sangareddy, Telangana. This post did not mention anything about a religious conversion.
Subsequent searches with the help of related keywords took us to a report in the online news website The Moonayak , that featured screenshots of the same incident. Per the report, the victim B Naresh (26) was a Dalit youth who was allegedly romantically involved with a woman from the same village and was beaten by her relatives.
Telangana Today , in a report dated July 4, 2022, noted that the incident took place in the Chelemamidi village of Jharasangam Mandal. According to the report, B Naresh was already married and was having an extramarital affair with a woman. But, they were reportedly caught by the woman's family members in a compromising position.
On July 5, 2022, The New Indian Express reported that the victim was also beaten up by the woman's husband and his relatives. Naresh's parents and grandmother who came to his rescue, were also beaten up and they all were admitted to the hospital. Later, a case was registered against the woman's husband and his relatives at Jharasangam police station.
Thus, it is more than evident that a two-year-old incident was falsely peddled as a case of religious conversion in India. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Sep 3, 2024 21:59 IST

title: Upload, undress, blackmail: AI 'nudify' apps emerge as new weapons of extortion
content:
More than anything else, desperation drove Rishabh towards apps that promised quick loans: easy money only a few clicks away. He was stone broke. He was also under the burden of high-interest loans he had taken earlier. And his credit score made him an ineligible customer at most banks. This vicious cycle pushed him into the murky waters of instant personal loan apps -- waters full of loan sharks -- for a measly sum of Rs 30,000.
When Rishabh defaulted on two EMIs, terse warnings on phone calls soon turned into menacing threats. "You can't even imagine what we'll do if you don't cough up the money by tomorrow," the lender's henchman warned him over the phone. Tomorrow arrived and he was none-the-richer. Obviously, he couldn't pay.Â
The real nightmare began after that.
The next afternoon, as Rishabh called a friend to figure out his options, his wife Shefali burst into the room, tears streaming across her face, fear and distress flashing in her eyes. Someone had sent her a nude photo of her.
She had never taken such a photo, but it looked impossibly real, down to the earrings and necklace she was still wearing. Before they could even process what happened, they got four more calls from friends and family. Everyone had received the same nude photo of Shefali.
Loan sharks can go to any extent to get their pound of flesh, explained Delhi-based cyber security expert Prabesh Choudhary. "Rishabh was too nervous and ashamed to go to the police. So, his friend advised him to come to me for help," Choudhary said.
Choudhary, who has had experience with several such cases, told India Today, "What people don't realise is the moment you download these loan apps, they get access to your phone gallery. Through this, the companies get hold of photos on your device. After that, with just a few clicks, they can undress any woman in your family to blackmail you."
Creating non-consensual fake nudes is not a new phenomenon. But artificial intelligence (AI) has made it infinitely easier. So much so that even school-going teens are now doing it. A recent survey in the US  conducted by the anti-child sexual abuse non-profit organisation Thorn found that one in every 10 minors knows peers who created deepfake nudes.
India is hardly immune to this. In May this year, a Bengaluru teen shared AI-generated nudes of his ninth-grade classmate on Instagram . Later, he and two others -- another minor and one adult -- were arrested .
"It was a rather difficult phase for my daughter. One of the boys had a crush on her and he was probably the one who shared fake nudes of my daughter in a boys' Instagram group, hoping another boy in her class would be implicated," the victim's mother told India Today. TELEGRAM: OPEN WEB'S DARKNET
Big tech's efforts to curb these apps and tools haven't been very successful. TikTok and Meta blocked the keyword "undress" last year to reduce access to such services. Google, too, removed certain ads for similar tools.
But in the badlands of Telegram, known to be a notoriously lenient app  rife with disinformation, radicalism, narcotics trade and even child pornography, "nudify" apps thrive in various forms.
According to Telemetrio , a Telegram search engine and analytics platform, the keyword "undress" was used more than 2,800 times between August 30 and September 5 in India alone.
Hundreds of channels on Telegram offer "undressing" services that even let you alter the size and shape of women's breasts and rear. We are deliberately withholding the names of these channels and apps to avoid their further promotion.
Some even allow you to dress people in suggestive clothing like wet t-shirts, bikinis and lingerie. All you need to do is upload a woman's photograph and follow some basic instructions. Some Telegram channels lead to websites with ready-made templates. Upload any person's photo and their face will be superimposed on short porn clips.
Telegram channels like these often offer suggestions about how people can use their tools. One disturbing ad for such a tool encouraged people to photograph unsuspecting victims on the metro, and then "nudify" them. Another tool prompted the question, "Why waste time trying to impress a girl when you can easily undress her using our services?"
These channels also post images of popular actresses, encouraging you to "undress" them. Famously, 'Animal' actor Rashmika Mandanna was a victim of something similar. Global pop icon Taylor Swift's AI-generated nudes also created a massive controversy earlier this year.
Many channels offer these services on a freemium model: free credits followed by charges. Others allow you to pay using your credit card, with "undressing" packages ranging between Rs 199 and Rs 19,999.
According to Sam Gregory, executive director of Witness, an organisation that promotes the ethical use of generative AI, "undressing" is a misleading term for what these apps and tools actually do. He explained that these tools use generative AI models trained on extensive data of female-identified bodies, both clothed and nude.
When you upload a photo, the algorithm identifies the areas covered with clothes and erases them. After that, it replaces those areas with pixels that match the skin tone, lighting and shadows, and contours of the original photo using a generative AI technique called inpainting .
These tools are designed to pander to the male fantasy. So, even if you upload a male-identified person's image, the undressed version will contain feminine features. Some of these tools even warn people not to upload pictures of men or animals.
We decided to test this and uploaded an AI-generated photo of a man. Unsurprisingly, it added breasts to the body. When we fed it an AI-generated image of a man with the head of a rabbit, the result was a naked woman with a human face that somehow retained the rabbit's whiskers. advertisement WHAT CAN VICTIMS DO? Google recently made it somewhat easier to remove non-consensual nude images or videos from its search results. Victims can request Google to remove it by filling out an online form. Experts advise that victims should try to document every instance of AI image-based abuse via screenshots or save image and video files. These files can later be used in takedown requests and legal action. According to Sam Gregory, some tech platforms and search engines match known non-consensual sexual images reported to them and remove duplicates. This, however, only applies to particular platforms and won't prevent circulation on private messaging apps. "Practically speaking, it is very hard to remove all fake nudes. And typically, the harm is already done by the time they are removed, if at all," he said. (Names of victims have been changed) - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Sep 6, 2024 19:58 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of candlelight march in Bangladesh falsely linked to Kolkata rape-murder case
content:
While people in Kolkata indeed took out a candlelight protest for the rape-murder victim, this video has nothing to do with it. It is from Bangladesh.
Many parts of Kolkata went dark on the evening of September 5 after the city's residents turned off their lights  and hit the streets with candles as a mark of protest against the rape-murder of the trainee doctor at RG Kar Medical College.Â
A drone footage is now making the rounds on social media, claiming to show the same protest, a large gathering of people holding candles.Â
An X user shared the video and wrote: "History has been created! The people of entire Kolkata took to the streets today. It is impossible to stop this movement until Tilottama gets justice. #RGKarProtest". The Bharatiya Janata Party's Amit Malviya also tweeted the same video and claimed that it showed the protest against the rape-murder of trainee doctor in West Bengal. He deleted the post later.Â
India Today found that the video has nothing to do with Kolkata's rape-murder case. It's a video from Bangladesh.Â
With the help of reverse image search, we found the viral video on a YouTube channel named "ANICUR ROHOMAN M" . It was uploaded to the on August 11, 2024, much before Kolkata's recent candlelight march.Â
The Bangla title of the YouTube video suggests that it is from Bangladesh's Uttara where people gathered in the memory of martyrs of 2024. The location mentioned in the description is also Bangladesh. Â
A Bangladeshi Facebook user Nondontott also shared the video  claiming it was shot on August 9 in Uttara in tribute to martyrs. Â
Tamzid Islam Zihan, a Bangladeshi Instagram user, posted a higher-quality version of the same video on August 9 with the cation: "Candlelight vigil Uttara". India Today reached out to Zihan who confirmed to us that he shot this video with his drone in Uttara, Bangladesh.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Tamzid Islam Zihan (@__tamziddd__)
A post shared by Tamzid Islam Zihan (@__tamziddd__)
We also found Bangladeshi news reports  from August 9 and 10 regarding this candlelight march on YouTube. Citizens of Bangladesh joined this protest in memory of those people who were killed during students' unrest in the country.Â
Also, the background music in the viral video is not original but taken from a concert video of Bangladeshi musician Rahul Ananda.
Thus, it's clear that the viral video had nothing to do with protests in Kolkata. - Ends (Translated by Arjun Deodia.) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Sep 9, 2024 16:38 IST

title: Fact Check: Does this clip show huge protests in Manipur? No, its AI-generated
content:
The viral clip is AI-generated and has nothing to do with the ongoing clashes in Manipur.
As the violence in Manipur continues, a video making the rounds online shows a huge crowd protesting. An X user shared the clip and wrote, "The situation in Manipur has significantly worsened, with no coverage from Indỉạn🇮🇳 media. Frustration is mounting, as thousands of people have taken to the streets demanding freedom from India." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral clip is AI-generated and has nothing to do with the ongoing violence in Manipur. Our Probe
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we came across the same clip shared by an Instagram user named Manab Jyoti Gogoi  on February 1, 2024. The video was shared with a caption, "Manipur wants peace, All images are AI-generated." title: Fact Check: No 'Rail Jihad', no vandalism. Video of Vande Bharat repair work VIRAL with false claims
content:
This man is a contract worker with Indian Railways in Ahmedabad. He is breaking the Vande Bharat's window glass to replace it. He is also not Muslim.
Anyone even remotely active on social media must have seen the video of a man smashing a Vande Bharat Express window with a hammer. The video has caused massive outrage among social media users, with some putting a communal spin on this alleged act of vandalism, claiming that the man was Muslim.
A Facebook user shared the viral video and wrote, "India's path to development and growth is obstructed by the actions of certain individuals, such as the person who damaged the Vande Bharat express train with a hammer, highlighting the need for a change in behavior." Many termed the video "Train Jihad". A few such posts can be seen here , here .
India Today Fact Check found that this was not vandalism. The man is a contract worker with Indian Railways in Ahmedabad, who was breaking the train's window to replace it. He is also not Muslim. Our Probe
Multiple responses  to the viral posts pointed out how the man was breaking the glass to replace it. A crack at the bottom of the glass of the window is visible.Â
"Trains of India", an X user shared another video showing how windows are replaced in Vande Bharat trains. We also found various YouTube videos  of window replacements in Vande Bharat trains. All of them involved breaking the glass with a hammer. This is how #VandeBharatTrain glass is replaced, this protocol is followed at maintenance pits as: • Quick & easy • Glass glued tightly • Less TAT for train at pit lines Meanwhile proper procedure is followed at workshop where train goes for schedule maintenance every 2yrs. https://t.co/UHx2OWcT9C pic.twitter.com/POkBVeevow — Trains of India (@trainwalebhaiya) September 10, 2024 Who is the man in the viral video? Reverse-searching the keyframes of the viral video led us to the Instagram account @singare_mahi_manish (  https://ghostarchive.org/archive/NcUT3 ) which contained videos of a man whose appearance and shirt matched the man in the viral video. We also saw various videos featuring Vande Bharat trains on this account. This pointed to the Instagram account being related to the viral video. In several Reels shared by this account , we noticed Gujarati signages and posters, indicating the user may be from Gujarat. We reached out to the Instagram user Manish and others he follows for more information. One such person we contacted confirmed to India Today Fact Check that Manish is an employee of a private maintenance company that works with Indian Railways. They said that Manish, who hails from Bihar's Ara, lives in Ahmedabad, where he repairs Vande Bharat train windows. Even though the face of the man in the viral video was not visible, the friend said that they could identify Manish. Railway's response When we first contacted Railway officials, they denied having any information about the viral video. After gathering all the information about Manish, we contacted the Railway officials again. A senior railway official then confirmed to us that the video was from the Indian Railways' Integrated Coaching Depot in Kankariya, Ahmedabad. He also told us that the video was recorded 5-6 days ago, during an inspection of the Ahmedabad-Mumbai Vande Bharat Express. advertisement The Railway official also corroborated the fact that the window was being smashed only to be replaced. They also confirmed that the man seen in the video was Manish Kumar Gupta, who works with a contract-based company with Indian Railways. What did Manish say When India Today Fact Check finally managed to contact Manish Gupta, he confirmed that the man in the viral was him. However, he also said that his seniors asked him to not say anything in this matter. In fact, Manish had originally shared the video himself on his Instagram account. He later deleted it when it went viral. It is thus clear that the video shows neither vandalism nor the conspiracy theory called "Rail Jihad". - Ends (With Inputs from Shubham Singh, The Lallantop) Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Sep 13, 2024 12:44 IST

title: Fact Check: FAKE Adani press release threatening Kenyan officials goes viral
content:
This press release is fake. The Adani Group confirmed in a statement that it never issued this fabricated letter.
A press release, allegedly issued by Adani Energy Solutions, part of the Adani Group, has gone viral on social media . In it, the company allegedly threatens Kenyan protestors demonstrating against the proposed handover of Nairobi's Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) to the Adani Group.Â
The viral letter cautions those planning to participate in these demonstrations that "such actions could have serious consequences. If these threats persist, we will have no choice but to reveal the names of government shareholders who have benefited from our investments. Additionally, we will also publish the names of individuals who have received substantial bribes from our company".
This so-called press release, dated September 10, 2024, featured the signature of Krishna Dutt Tiwari, the Adani Energy Solutions Limited country manager in Kenya.
Those sharing the alleged press release on social media commented that if the Adani Group could bribe government officials in Kenya, it could do the same in India as well.Â
India Today Fact Check found the press release was fake and was never issued by the Adani Group. The conglomerate clarified this through a statement on September 16. ADANI'S KENYA CONNECTION
The Kenyan government proposed leasing the Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) to the Adani Group for 30 years , in exchange for $1.85 billion of investment by Adani into the airport's expansion. Subsequently, hundreds of workers at Nairobi's JKIA went on strik e on September 11 against this takeover.Â
Workers feared job cuts among other things and the protests led to flight delays and passengers stranded at Kenya's biggest airport. The strike ended when protestors were assured that the contract wouldn't be finalised without the airport union's approval.Â
It's noteworthy that the Kenyan government also recently awarded the Adani Group a public-private partnership to build power transmission lines . This project was also mentioned in the fake press release. THE FACTS
First and foremost, no official press note from any global corporation would use language like this, which also admits to bribing government officials.Â
In the Adani Group's official website's media centre , we did not find any press release threatening Kenyan officials issued either on September 10 or any other date. Rather, we found the Adani Group's refutation of the viral press release, issued on September 16.Â
As per the statement, the Adani Group, its companies and subsidiaries, never issued any press release related to Kenya. It also says that the company will take legal action against anyone spreading this false narrative. Know more: https://t.co/P8Ybq6c8YI pic.twitter.com/aIcBvh6CSf — Adani Group (@AdaniOnline) September 16, 2024
Know more: https://t.co/P8Ybq6c8YI pic.twitter.com/aIcBvh6CSf — Adani Group (@AdaniOnline) September 16, 2024
There are also telltale signs in the viral letter, pointing to it being forged. There is a discrepancy in the date format. There are also inconsistent paragraph breaks throughout the statement.
Thus, it is clear that the viral post is a fake Adani Group press release. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Sep 16, 2024 16:58 IST

title: Fact Check: Water jets spray out of Guatemalan road, NOT Indian

title: Fact Check: This is NOT Netanyahu's reaction to the pager blasts in Lebanon
content:
This video has nothing to do with the September 17 pager blasts in Lebanon. It dates back to 2021.
At least 12 people were killed and around 2,800 were injured after pagers exploded across Lebanon on September 17. These explosions purportedly targeted members of Hezbollah. Both the Lebanese government and Hezbollah have blamed Israel for this.Â
Now, a video of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is being widely shared on social media where he is whistling a tune playfully. Allegedly, this video was shot in the aftermath of the Lebanon explosions.Â
A Facebook user shared the video and wrote: "11 people were killed, 4000 were injured, 400 out of them are serious injuries in the Israeli cyberattack on Lebanese citizens, and Netanyahu appeared in a video whistling and celebrating this terroristic attacks. Such a cold-blooded war criminal."
An Instagram user wrote: "Prime Minister Netanyahu has made his first official statement about the massive beeper attack in Lebanon." Their archives can be seen here and here .
India Today found that this video is three years old and unrelated to the serial pager explosions in Lebanon.  Â
Many social media users reacting to the viral video pointed out that it dates back to 2021. Â
A subsequent search led us to a Facebook user who shared it in March 2021. This proved it has nothing to do with the serial explosions in Lebanon.Â
We scanned Netanyahu's social media accounts and found he shared the video in question on TikTok on March 11, 2021. Its caption in Hebrew says, "Do you recognise the song?"Â
His Facebook page shared many similar live videos of Netanyahu sitting in his car in March 2021. In these videos, he interacts with people during live sessions. One such clip can be seen below.
This video was also included in a March 2021 report  in the Israeli news outlet Kikar. Per the report, Netanyahu was travelling across the country ahead of the elections. According to the report, in the viral video, Netanyahu was whistling the anthem of his party, Likud.
Thus, it's clear that an old video of Benjamin Netanyahu was falsely shared in connection with pager blasts in Lebanon. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Sep 18, 2024 22:41 IST

title: Fact Check: Muslim cop in UP arrested for supplying money and weapons? Nope, this was a bribery case
content:
The man in the viral video, head constable Shahnawaz, was arrested for demanding a bribe of Rs 15,000.
Was a Kanpur deputy superintendent of police arrested for supplying crores of rupees and weapons to his friends? This is what's being alleged alongside a video of a man in police uniform being taken into custody.Â
A Facebook user shared the viral clip and wrote: "Traitor in Police -: Latest News. Shahnawaz Khan, who worked as DSP in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh, was caught by anti-corruption team with illegal weapons and ,Crores of Rs. He was caught red handed as he was handing out guns, pistols etc. to his friends… It is true that a Muslim can never be a patriot... even if he is in a government job, he is ready for anything to spread terror... Now Yogi Baba will take this case well."
India Today Fact Check found that Shahnawaz, a head constable and not a DSP, was arrested for demanding a bribe of Rs 15,000 — not for supplying money and weapons to his friends.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to several media reports featuring screenshots of the video. According to a September 10 report in the Navbharat Times , a constable was arrested by the UP Police's Vigilance team in Kanpur for demanding a bribe of Rs 15,000 for filing a chargesheet in a case.Â
Several media reports also mention that the person seen in the video in police uniform was head constable Shahnawaz. We did not find any mention of crores of rupees orf weapons, as claimed in the viral posts. कानपुर: 15 हजार रुपये की रिश्‍वत लेते हुए हेड कॉन्‍स्‍टेबल गिरफ्तार @NavbharatTimes pic.twitter.com/yyXt1NGHva — NBT Uttar Pradesh (@UPNBT) September 10, 2024 What happened? According to Amar Ujala , head constable Shahnawaz was a peshkar (person who does documentation) in the ACP's office in Babupurva, Kanpur. There, to file a case filed under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, the head constables Shahnawaz and Yogesh Kumar demanded a Rs 20,000 bribe, which was later renegotiated to Rs 15,000. Following this, the victim filed a complaint with the Vigilance department. The Vigilance department then entraped Shahnawaz when the victim arrived at the police station to bribe him. This arrest was captured in the viral video. No weapons or money charge India Today Fact Check contacted the UP Police's Vigilance team for further verification. Rajesh Singh, a peshkar in the department, refuted the viral claims and said, "Shahnawaz was arrested only for taking a bribe of Rs 15,000. There were no weapons of crores of cash with him." It is thus clear that the viral claims are false. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Sep 19, 2024 15:33 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of Israeli airstrikes on Lebanon is OLD
content:
This video dates back to February 19 and shows an alleged airstrike by Israeli forces on Hezbollah weapons warehouses in Sidon city.
In the aftermath of the series of explosions of communication devices across Lebanon, for which Hezbollah has blamed Israel, a video of a massive roadside explosion recorded from a moving vehicle began making the rounds on social media. Allegedly, Israeli fighter jets launched airstrikes on Hezbollah outposts in Lebanon. BREAKING : Air Strikes Now !!! Watch Out !! Israeli fighter jets launch a wave of airstrikes hitting Hezbollah targets in Lebanon. Others claimed that the video showed an explosion in solar energy systems installed in several areas of Beirut, Lebanon's capital.
India Today Fact Check found that the video in question dates back to February this year, and is thus unrelated to the blasts on September 17 and 18, 2024.Â
At the time of writing this report, there were no reports of Israeli aerial strikes on Lebanon. Reverse searching screengrabs from the viral video led us to a news report from February 19 that noted this clip was from Sidon, a coastal city in Lebanon, where the Israeli Air Force launched a strike on Hezbollah weapons warehouses.
A search with subsequent keywords led us to a 20-minute-long clip uploaded to the YouTube channel of Al Jadeed News, a Lebanese television news channel on February 19. This compilation of videos depicting air strikes and bombarding featured the viral clip around the three-minute mark.
The title and description of the YouTube video noted that these alleged Israeli attacks took place on the outskirts of Sidon city towards Ghazieh. title: Fact Check: Netanyahu compared to 007 post-Lebanon blasts? Nope, 2021 clip goes viral
content:
This video is from October 2021, when a reporter compared Netanyahu to the fictional British spy after a photo of him in black glasses went viral.
A video of an interaction between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and a reporter is making the rounds on social media. Those sharing it claimed that after the Lebanon blast, a reporter showed footage of an explosion and then compared Netanyahu with the fictional British spy James Bond. To this, Netanyahu replied that he is "Netanyahu. Benjamin Netanyahu."
Sharing the video on Facebook, one person wrote, "Although Israel and the IDF are not commenting on whether Israel is behind the pager explosions, the memes and jokes are non-stop. Even Bibi was able to joke around as he prepares for imminent war with Lebanon. Man with phone: 'Netanyahu, did you know that they're now comparing you to James Bond?' Netanyahu: 'Nonsense. It's Netanyahu; Benjamin Netanyahu'."
One such post featured footage of the pagers exploding in Beirut along with the viral clip, while others posted it with hashtags such as "pagers" and "Mossad", Israel's spy agency that's believed to be behind the attacks .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from October 2021, and therefore unrelated to the Lebanon blasts.Â
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to a Facebook post dated October 25, 2021. Its caption in Hebrew read: "Why James Bond? Opposition leader Netanyahu surprises with a new TikTok video Benjamin Netanyahu - Benjamin Netanyahu." The video also featured the TikTok logo and the username "@bnetanyahu". This made it clear that this video predates the Lebanon attack by almost three years.
We then checked Benjamin Netanyahu's TikTok account and found he shared the viral video himself on October 24, 2021, writing "Netanyahu. Benjamin Netanyahu" in Hebrew.
We also found a news report about this interaction from the same time. According to it, Netanyahu, an Opposition leader at the time, was compared to James Bond after a photo of him in black glasses went viral. The photograph was reportedly from his meeting a week ago in the Knesset with MK Nir Barkat, the Likud leader currently serving as Minister of Economy in Israel.Â
Responding to the comparison made by a reporter, Netanyahu got into the character and replied, "Not James Bond. Netanyahu, Benjamin Netanyahu."Â
It is noteworthy that " No Time to Die ", the twenty-fifth spy film in the James Bond series, was released on September 30, 2021, possibly leading to the comparison.
It is thus, clear that a 2021 video of Netanyahu responding to his comparison with James Bond was falsely shared as recent. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Sep 19, 2024 22:29 IST

title: Fact Check: Tamil Nadu man beaten up for mocking Hindus after Tirupati row? Here is the truth
content:
This video is from August 2019 and shows activist Piyush Manush being beaten up by the BJP cadre for barging into their Salem office.
Controversy over alleged traces of beef tallow, fish oil, and lard (pig fat) in the ghee used to make laddus at the Sri Venkateswara temple in Tirupati reached the apex court on September 20 after a lawyer filed a plea alleging that the act violated fundamental Hindu religious customs.
Amid this, a video began making the rounds on social media  featuring crowd hitting a man, allegedly for mocking Hindus over the Tirupati row. Those sharing the clip  identified the victim as Piyush Manush, adding that he released a video titled, "Beef laddu for all Hindus delivered by Perumal himself" following which people in Tamil Nadu's Salem beat him up.
One person shared the video on Facebook writing , "Piyush Manush, the guy who mocked Hindus with a video titled 'Beef Laddoo for all Hindus delivered by Perumal himself' has got a better treatment at Salem, Tamil Nadu. Good resistance."Â
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video is from August 2019, and shows a pro-congress Tamil Nadu activist being beaten up by the Bharatiya Janata Party cadre for barging into the party's Salem office.
With the help of a keyword search, we found an extended version of the video in question, shared on a YouTube channel named "NewsGlitz Tamil" on August 28, 2019. The channel logo and watermark were present in the viral clip. Its description stated that Piyush Manush was assaulted at the BJP office.  We then found multiple media reports about this incident. A Tamil Nadu activist Piyush Manush was reportedly attacked at the BJP office in Salem on August 28, 2019. He suffered minor injuries and was admitted to the Salem Government Hospital. Manush, an environmental activist, was reportedly vocal against many government schemes and corporate initiatives across Tamil Nadu. Per reports, Manush went to the Salem BJP office to seek views of the leaders on the economy, Kashmir crisis, and confront them about threats that he allegedly received from the BJP . BJP leaders, in turn, accused Manush of evading taxes and spreading hatred against Hindus. The heated argument ended with BJP workers garlanding Manush with slippers and beating him up. Police reportedly received complaints about this incident from both sides. The issue also triggered outrage on social media , with Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam President (and now Tamil Nadu Chief Minister) MK Stalin condemning the attack on Manush , and the BJP demanding Manush's arrest for entering party office without permission. பாஜக அரசின் அவலங்களை ஆதாரத்துடன் முன்வைத்து விவாதித்த சமூக செயற்பாட்டாளர் @piyushmanush அவர்கள், சேலம் பாஜக அலுவலகத்தில் 50க்கும் மேற்பட்டவர்களால் கொடூரமாக தாக்கப்பட்டிருப்பது வன்மையாக கண்டிக்கத்தக்கது.
— M.K.Stalin (@mkstalin) August 28, 2019 The criminal trespasser into BJP office in Salam piyush manush should be arrested immediately
— H Raja (@HRajaBJP) August 28, 2019 In a Facebook post, dated August 28, 2019 , Manush stated that he would visit the BJP office in the evening. Later, he live-streamed his visit , capturing the heated argument with the BJP workers. On September 21, 2024, he also debunked the viral clip in circulation, stating it is from 2019. It is noteworthy, that Piyush Manush has indeed made a video about "Beef laddoo" at Tirupati  on September 19, 2024. However, the viral clip has nothing to do with the Tirupati row. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Sep 22, 2024 13:32 IST

title: Fact Check: This drone attack is from Russia, unrelated to Israel-Lebanon war
content:
This video dates back to July 22, 2024, and shows a drone attack by Ukraine on an oil refinery in Tuapse, Russia.
Amid Israeli airstrikes on Lebanon that have reportedly killed at least 492 people and left more than 1,600 injured, a video of a "Hezbollah drone" allegedly reaching "oil refineries in northern occupied Palestine" and exploding was widely shared. Â
One such post read: "BREAKING NEWS. 'Israeli' media: Hezbollah drone reaches oil refineries in the north of occupied Palestine. Alahed English." 🔴 BREAKING NEWS 🔵 "Israeli" media: 🇱🇧 Hezbollah drone reaches oil refineries in the north of 🇵🇸 occupied Palestine. Alahed English... pic.twitter.com/tvp0jlLONz — Suat KılıçtaÅŸ (@Suatklcts) September 23, 2024

India Today Fact Check has found that the video is nearly two months old and from Russia.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an X post featuring the clip from July 22 this year. This made it evident that the video could not be related to the recent escalation between Israel and Lebanon. Detailed footage of a Ukrainian Lyutiy drone hitting an oil refinery in Tuapse this morning. pic.twitter.com/L3wl72WmDu — NOELREPORTS 🇪🇺 🇺🇦 (@NOELreports) July 22, 2024

title: Fact Check: 2021 clip of Lebanese villagers detaining Hezbollah members FALSELY shared as recent
content:
This clip is from August 2021, when villagers in Lebanon's Chouaya detained Hezbollah members for firing rockets from their area, fearing Israeli retaliation.
Lebanon saw its deadliest day in nearly two decades on September 23, after Israeli airstrikes killed nearly 500 people across the country. Amid this, a video allegedly showing Lebanese Druze people stopping Hezbollah members from attacking Israel was widely shared. The Druze are an ethnoreligious group in the region.Â
The clip shows a huge crowd of people in skull caps surrounding a vehicle and shouting at a man sitting inside, while others can be seen dragging another man at a distance. Sharing it on Facebook , one person wrote, "Breaking: Lebanese Druze have set up checkpoints in their town to ensure no Hezbollah terrorists try to hide amongst them. When people cheer on Hezbollah in the West, they should know that Hezbollah is also the enemy of the Lebanese people."
India Today Fact Check found that this video has nothing to do with the ongoing conflict. It is from 2021.Â
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook post , dated August 6, 2021, containing its screenshot. The caption in Arabic stated that people blocked the roads for this man in Lebanon who came to attack with missiles.Â
Further searches led us to several media reports about this incident. According to a Times of Israel report dated August 6, 2021, Druze residents in the Chouaya village of Lebanon's Hasbaya District detained Hezbollah forces driving through the village with rockets in a truck. The villagers accused Hezbollah of firing rockets from between their homes, putting the residents in danger. The Lebanese Army reportedly arrested four suspects and confiscated the rocket launchers mounted on the vehicle.
We also found the viral clip , along with other videos of the incident shared by multiple journalists at the time. La vidéo fait le tour de la toile au #Liban . Des villageois druzes arrêtent, frappent et insultent des hommes du #Hezbollah venus récupérer la camionnette qui a servi aux tirs de roquettes. @alishoeib1970 vas-y toi aussi stp, on va voir comment tu es si héroïque ! pic.twitter.com/YudufqGErK — Matthias Inbar (@MatthiasInbar) August 6, 2021
