Nineteen rockets were reportedly fired at northern Israel from Lebanon on the morning of August 6, 2021. According to a Reuters report, Hezbollah later issued a statement clarifying that its fighters fired the rockets from remote areas, and villagers stopped them in Hasbaya while they were returning. However, two residents of the village told the New York Times that the villagers heard a launch nearby and went to stop the crew, worrying about Israeli retaliation on their village.Â
It is noteworthy that Lebanese Druze leader and former Member of the Parliament Walid Jumblatt recently said that instead of blaming Hezbollah's policies or position in Syria, Lebanon should come together and find a solution against the Israeli threat.

title: Fact Check: Did Hezbollah chief Hassan Nasrallah cry after Israeli strikes on Lebanon? This clip is OLD
content:
The viral video has nothing to do with Israel's recent strikes on Lebonan. Nasrallah's video is more than two years old.
After the pager and walkie-talkie blasts, Lebanon was hit by Israeli air strikes on September 23, killing over 500 people so far. The attacks reportedly killed Ibrahim Muhammad Qabisi , a top commander of the paramilitary group and political party Hezbollah.
Now, a video of Hezbollah secretary-general Hassan Nasrallah sobbing is making the rounds on social media. Allegedly, he cried after losing his commanders in these Israeli attacks.Â
An X user captioned the video : "Hezbollah terrorist commander Nasrallah was laughing on 7th October when innocent Israelis were been murdered by Hamas Terrorist. Today, he is crying after losing 100s of his commanders to pager blasts. Even his own life is in danger". Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video has nothing to do with Israel's recent strikes on Lebanon. The Nasrallah video is more than two years old.Â
A reverse image search of keyframes from the video led us to a Facebook post from August 12, 2022, containing the same video. This proves the video has nothing to do with the ongoing escalation between Israel and Lebanon.Â
A longer version of the video was also shared by several YouTube Channels on August 12, 2022. Their Arabic titles suggested Nasrallah cried while commemorating the death of Imam Hussein, the grandson of Prophet Muhammad. The first frame of the YouTube video also features words like "Ashura" and "Hussein". Also, in the video, "Muharram" and "Hussein" can be seen written behind Nasrallah.Â
There are reports from August 9, 2022, saying that Nasrallah addressed mourners commemorating Ashura in a televised speech. Ashura marks the martyrdom of Imam Hussein.
There are also reports from 2009 and 2018 about how Nasrallah cried while delivering speeches during annual Ashura ceremonies.
Hence, it's clear that an old video of the Hezbollah chief was falsely linked to recent attacks on Lebanon. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Sep 25, 2024 17:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Spectacular new bridge in J&K? No this video is from China
content:
This video is not from Jammu and Kashmir. It shows the Aizhai Bridge in central China.
Jammu and Kashmir is undergoing rapid transformation with new road and rail infrastructure underway. National Highway 44 is a major project poised to revolutionise the region's transport sector, with completion expected by 2026.Â
A video now going viral, however, purports to show National Highway 44 open for business.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video actually shows the Aizhai Bridge in China.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to a YouTube video  from September 20, 2024, titled "Aizhai Bridge — Hunan, China Road". While not the same video, this clip appears to feature the same bridge. In this video, Chinese text can also be seen written on the tower.Â
Using a keyword search, we found a detailed report in The Guardian published in 2012, according to which, this is the world's highest and longest tunnel-to-tunnel bridge, located in central China.Â
The Aizhai suspension bridge spans 1,176 metres, linking two tunnels and carrying traffic 355 metres above the Dehang Canyon. Construction began in October 2007, with the main sections completed by the end of 2011. The Guardian report includes many pictures.Â
The Aizhai Bridge is situated in Jishou City, within the Xiangxi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, and was built as part of the express way linking Chongqing Municipality in south-west China to Changsha, the capital of Hunan.Â
There are many aerial videos of the Aizhai Suspension Bridge available on YouTube. You can watch one such video below:
We also checked for information on NH44, which is a multi-state highway connecting 11 states from Srinagar to Kanniyakumari. It links major cities such as Agra, Delhi, Hyderabad, and Bangalore. There are many tunnels and bridges along NH44 in Jammu and Kashmir. You can read the detailed report from the PWD about road development in Jammu and Kashmir here .
It is thus clear that a video of the Aizhai Bridge in China was falsely shared as a bridge in Jammu and Kashmir.
(Written by Deenadayal M) - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Sep 25, 2024 20:16 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of Russian attack on Kyiv FALSELY shared as Yemeni strike in Israel
content:
This video shows a Russian airstrike from 2023 in Kyiv, Ukraine.
Amid its ongoing strikes on Lebanon, the Israeli military reportedly intercepted a surface-to-surface ballistic missile launched from Yemen on September 27 morning. A video now going viral shows a blast.Â
Sharing it on Facebook , one person wrote, "The moment Yemeni missiles reached occupied Tel Aviv and hit their targets." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video shows a 2023 Russian airstrike in Kyiv, Ukraine.Â
Many people responded to the viral post claiming the video was old and from Ukraine. Reverse searching keyframes from the video led us to a video report by ABC News that included the viral clip, uploaded to its official YouTube channel on August 30, 2023.Â
As per the report, on August 30, a barrage of Russian missiles and drone strikes rained down on Kyiv, Ukraine, killing at least two people. Debris from targets intercepted by the city's air defences fell on several buildings.
As per a Reuters report from August 2023, this airstrike by Russia on the capital was its most powerful in months. The attack was carried out near a supermarket in Kyiv. Two people died and three were wounded in the overnight strike. A DW report from the same time also said the viral clip was from Kyiv, Ukraine.Â
Thus, it's clear an old video of a Russian airstrike on Ukraine is being falsely shared as a Yemeni attack on Israel. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Sep 27, 2024 19:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of furniture store fire VIRAL as Hezbollah attack on Haifa
content:

title: Fact Check: IDF soldiers dancing after killing Hezbollah chief? No, this clip is from 2023
content:
This video is from 2023 when an Israeli pop star performed to boost IDF soldiers' morale.
Hezbollah on September 27 confirmed that its leader Hassan Nasrallah had been killed in an Israeli air attack at their headquarters in south Beirut, Lebanon.Â
A video now going viral allegedly shows soldiers in the Israel Defence Forces uniform partying and dancing after returning from the attack. Sharing the video, an X user wrote , "The Israeli fighter jet pilot returns to base after successfully eliminating Nasrallah." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from 2023 when an Israeli pop star performed to boost IDF soldiers' morale.Â
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video in an X post dated November 10, 2023. As per the post, the man dancing with the soldiers was Avihu Pankhasov. This made it clear that the video is old and therefore unrelated to Nasrallah's killing. כמה שאני אוהב אותם שמחים אביהו פנחסוב קורע מצחוק. pic.twitter.com/ZTZ2PAZbdL — אורן חסקי 🇮🇱haski oren (@haski_oren) November 10, 2023
כמה שאני אוהב אותם שמחים אביהו פנחסוב קורע מצחוק. pic.twitter.com/ZTZ2PAZbdL — אורן חסקי 🇮🇱haski oren (@haski_oren) November 10, 2023
A search with subsequent keywords led us to several media reports that contained the viral clip. As per The Jewish Chronicle , an Israeli army officer invited famous pop star Avihu Pinhasov to perform for his unit stationed in northern Israel to boost morale.
In a breach of military rules, several soldiers were seen holding their assault weapons in the video. After it went viral, the soldiers were reportedly disciplined by the IDF, and those who played with weapons were temporarily suspended from operational activity.
We also found a video report in The Telegraph  that included the viral clip. Uploaded to its official YouTube channel on November 17, 2023, the report noted that several IDF reservists were suspended over raucous behaviour during Avihu Pinhasov's visit.
Thus, it's clear an old video of an IDF morale-boosting party is being falsely linked to Nasrallah's death.

title: Fact Check: This video DOESN'T show Lebanese people celebrating Nasrallah's death
content:
This video is from a protest in Lebanon in 2020. It has nothing to do with Hassan Nasrallah's death in an Israeli strike.
Did Lebanese citizens celebrate the killing of Hezbollah chief Hassan Nasrallah? That's what a video now going viral allegedly shows. In it, two women can be seen singing in Arabic with a crowd of people holding flags.Â
An X user wrote alongside the video : "Lebanese citizens are also celebrating the kotletification [sic] of the tyrant Nasrallah. Well deserved! Party all night." Its archive can be seen here .Â
Nasrallah was killed in Israeli air strikes on September 27 in Beirut, Lebanon.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from a protest in Lebanon in 2020. It has nothing to do with the ongoing war between Israel and Lebanon.Â
With the help of reverse search and keywords, we found the video shared on TikTok by user "k.reem" on January 20, 2020. This means the video can not have anything to do with Nasrallah's death. The TikTok user captioned the video with words and hashtags like "revolution", "Lebanon", and "anger".Â
While scanning the profile, we found several other videos of the same woman seen in the video. On September 29, the woman clarified in a TikTok post that her video was being circulated with the misleading claim that she celebrated the Hezbollah chief's death in Lebanon. She further added that the video was from 2020 and showed the Lebanese revolution. She also wrote that she no longer lives in Lebanon.Â
The Lebanese Revolution began on 17 October 2019 and lasted for months. It was a series of anti-government protests in response to corruption and economic crises in the country.Â
Notably, there are reports that people in some parts of Syria celebrated the death of Nasrallah on the streets. However, it's clear this four-year-old video of a protest in Lebanon does not show that. - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Sep 30, 2024 18:51 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Palestine president call PM Modi a 'Zionist slave'? No, it's fake
content:
This quote is fake. No news reports mention Mahmoud Abbas making such a comment.
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas recently addressed the United Nations General Assembly in New York, calling Israel's war "one of the most heinous crimes of our era". In his speech, Abbas called for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza and an end to military aggressions in the West Bank and East Jerusalem.Â
Now, a post  going viral on the internet claims that Abbas called Prime Minister Narendra Modi a "Zionist slave".Â
The post featured Abbas's photo and the text: "Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas calls Indian PM Modi a 'Zionist slave'." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral claim is fake. There are no news reports about Mahmoud Abbas making such a comment.Â
A keyword search related to this alleged comment on PM Narendra Modi yielded no credible news report. Both leaders are quite popular. If Mahmoud Abbas made such a statement, there would have been news reports about it, both in India and international news outlets.Â
We could not find any official social media account of the Palestinian President. However, on his official account, PM Modi shared photos with President Mahmoud Abbas on September 23, 2024.Â
Sharing the photos, Modi wrote : "Met President Mahmoud Abbas in New York. Reiterated India's support for early restoration of peace and stability in the region. Exchanged views of further strengthening long-standing friendship with the people of Palestine." Met President Mahmoud Abbas in New York. Reiterated India's support for early restoration of peace and stability in the region. Exchanged views of further strengthening long standing friendship with the people of Palestine. pic.twitter.com/LnmAm7dDax — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) September 23, 2024 We found several media reports covering this meeting published on September 23. Per the reports, PM Modi assured Mahmoud Abbas of more assistance to Gaza and reiterated India's support for peace and stability in the region. As per The Economic Times , Modi recalled how India was one of the first countries to recognise Palestine, and conveyed India's continued support for Palestinian membership of the UN. Major media outlets like The Hindu , the Hindustan Times , The New Indian Express , and others followed the developments after this meeting. But none of them mentioned the comment from the viral post. Thus, it is more than clear that the claim of Mahmoud's comment calling PM Modi a "Zionist slave" is fake. (Written by Ashish Kumar) - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Oct 1, 2024 21:17 IST

title: Fact Check: Israeli man hides in a tunnel amid Iran missile attack? Let's 'dig' deeper
content:
The video has been reversed in motion. It shows a man escaping an illegally made secret tunnel in New York in January 2024.
Iran reportedly launched more than 180 ballistic missiles at Israel on October 1. Iran claimed that the attack was limited to Israeli security and military targets, and was in response to the killing of Hezbollah chief Hassan Nasrallah and Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh.Â
As millions of people rushed to shelters as the night sky above Tel Aviv and Jerusalem lit up with explosions, a video allegedly showing this was widely shared on social media.Â
It showed a man stepping into a roadside tunnel. Those sharing it claimed that this man was trying to take cover during the Iranian missile attack in Tel Aviv. Sharing it on Facebook , one person wrote, "Heartbreaking images out of Tel Aviv today as a young man is forced to hide from the Iranian bombardment."Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video, reversed in motion, actually shows a man escaping an illegally made secret tunnel in New York.Â
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a news report containing screenshots of the video in question, dated January 9, 2024. It is thus clear that the video does not show the recent attack on Israel.
The report stated that a scuffle unfolded outside a synagogue on January 8, 2024, as authorities attempted to close a secret underground tunnel, constructed illegally in the Crown Heights neighbourhood of Brooklyn, New York. The tunnel reportedly provided access to the building next door and also had a secret entrance and exit from the street.Â
Members of the Orthodox Jewish community attempted to obstruct labourers and the police who came to seal the underground tunnel with concrete and shut it down. At least nine people from the New York Hasidic Jewish community were reportedly arrested in the incident. An emergency structural inspection was also carried out later in the area. There were concerns that the illegal excavation work underneath the buildings could have caused damage to the neighbouring structures.
Some reports stated that the tunnel was dug in secrecy around six months before the incident to expand the iconic synagogue associated with the Chabad movement. Others reported that a group of people had created a transit route for themselves in the form of a tunnel without seeking necessary permits when synagogues and roads were closed during the Covid-19 pandemic.
It is thus, clear that an old video of a man escaping from an illegal underground tunnel in New York was falsely linked to the ongoing Israel-Iran conflict. Â - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Oct 2, 2024 16:57 IST

title: Fact Check: Netanyahu running to bunker after Iran attack? No, this video is years old
content:
This video dates back to December 2021 and shows Netanyahu running from his Knesset office to vote on time.
Hours after Iran's missile attacks on Tel Aviv, Israel, a video of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sprinting down a building corridor began making the rounds on social media. While sharing this, many claimed that it showed Netanyahu fleeing to a bunker in response to the Iranian attacks.
One such post  read, "Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu is running to save his life… How many days he will hide in bunker."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is nearly three years old and unrelated to Iran's recent attack.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the original one shared by the official X account of Benjamin Netanyahu  on December 14, 2021. The caption in Hebrew roughly translated to, "I am always proud to run for you. It was taken half an hour ago in the Knesset."
A round of searches with keywords also led us to a Hebrew news report  dated December 13, 202i, which noted that Netanyahu, the head of the Opposition at the time, ran from his Knesset office to arrive in time for the voting in the Plenum.
The Knesset is the unicameral legislature of Israel that passes all laws, elects the president and prime minister, and approves the cabinet. The Knesset Plenum is the supreme authoritative body of the Knesset. Knesset resolutions are adopted through voting in the Plenum.
This makes it evident that the video is completely unrelated to the Iranian attack on Israel. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Oct 2, 2024 17:56 IST

title: Fact Check: 2023 video from Russia VIRAL as Iran blowing up buildings in Tel Aviv
content:
This 2023 video shows a Ukrainian aerial attack in Russia's Moscow.
Israeli officials have not reported any serious injuries as a result of the October 1 air attack, when Iran fired about 180 missiles, many of which were reportedly intercepted by Israel's defence system.
Amid this, a video of an explosion in a tall building in the middle of a street went viral on social media . In it, a woman can be heard screaming in the background as the building is attacked , and air raid sirens blaze in the area. Those sharing the clip , claimed that it was shot during Iran's missile attack in Tel Aviv .Â
Sharing the clip on Facebook , one person wrote, "Hypersonic missiles are landing at the heart of Tel Aviv. The Iron Dome has failed."
India Today Fact Check found this 2023 video shows a Ukrainian aerial attack in Russia's Moscow.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a post on the Russian social media platform VK . This post from July 2023 claimed the video in question showed drones landing in one of Moscow's buildings.Â
Further searches led us to a BBC news report about this video, dated July 30, 2023. According to it, Russia's Defence Ministry stated that three Ukrainian drones were downed on July 30, 2023, while two drones crashed into office buildings. Moscow accused Kyiv of conducting the drone attack, which damaged the facades of two office buildings. The Vnukovo Airport was also briefly shut in the wake of the aerial attack. No injuries were reported.
Following the drone attack, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, in a video address, said that the attack on Russian territory was "inevitable, natural, and absolutely fair", adding that the war was returning to Russia. The report also carried a photo of a skyscraper that was damaged in this attack.
Per reports , one explosion occurred in the 50-storey IQ-Quarter building, while another explosion took place in the OKO tower complex in Moscow International Business Centre on July 30, 2023.
It is thus, more than clear that a 2023 video of Ukraine's attack on Russia was falsely shared as recent footage from Tel Aviv. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Oct 2, 2024 19:00 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Hezbollah destroying Israeli tank. This 2023 video is from Ukraine
content:
While Hezbollah claims to have destroyed Israeli tanks on October 2, this video is from 2023 and shows Ukrainian forces destroying a Russian T-90M tank.
Eight Israeli soldiers were killed in Lebanon on October 2 as its troops carried out cross-border raids in southern Lebanon. The Lebanese political and paramilitary group Hezbollah also said it destroyed Israeli tanks during the battle.
A video now going viral allegedly shows Israeli tanks being destroyed by Hezbollah. Sharing the video, an X user wrote , "Hezbollah destroyed an Israeli Tank which recently entered Lebanon." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from 2023 and shows Ukrainian forces destroying a Russian tank.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an X post  dated October 8, 2023. Per the post, this video is from around Kreminna in the Luhansk region of Ukraine. The post further claimed that Ukraine's 66th Mechanised Brigade destroyed 25 Russian tanks in four days. This means the video is old and unrelated to the ongoing Israel-Lebanon conflict.Â
The official account of the Ukrainian Ministry of Defence also shared the video the same day, identifying the tank in the video as a T-90M. russian «no-analogue» T-90M. Oops. pic.twitter.com/BoEhklE93J — Defense of Ukraine (@DefenceU) October 8, 2023
russian «no-analogue» T-90M. Oops. pic.twitter.com/BoEhklE93J — Defense of Ukraine (@DefenceU) October 8, 2023
A search with related keywords led us to a longer version of the video uploaded to YouTube in October 2023, describing this incident to be from the Russia-Ukraine war.
We also found several media reports from October 2023 that contained the viral clip. As per the Czech news channel CNN Prima News , the incident occurred not far from Makjivka in the Luhansk region. The report also noted that the Ukrainian 66th Brigade destroyed a Russian T-90M tank on the battlefield. The T90s are one of Russia's most powerful armoured vehicles and have been deployed by Russia in its invasion of Ukraine.
A detailed report about this incident in the Kyiv Post notes the Russian tank appeared to launch grenades in the direction of Ukrainian lines as a possible defensive tactic before being destroyed by an anti-tank missile launched by Ukrainian forces. The Russian military at the time confirmed the loss of 45 T-90 tanks and 2,362 tanks of all types since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022.Â
Thus, it's clear that an old video from the Russia-Ukraine war was falsely shared as Hezbollah forces destroying an Israeli tank.

title: Fact Check: 2017 video from Syria shared as Hezbollah missile attack on Israeli troops
content:
The viral video is from 2017 and shows the Syrian rebel group, Army of Glory, targeting Bashar al-Assad's forces in northern Syria.
Amid Israeli ground incursions into Lebanon, a video allegedly showing a Hezbollah fighter firing an anti-tank guided missile (ATGM) at Israeli troops has gone viral on social media. Chants of "Allahu Akbar" could be heard in the background as missiles hit the target, causing explosions.
Sharing the clip on Facebook , one person wrote, "Hezbollah showed how it cheerfully shoots an ATGM at a column of occupiers infantry who are marching in tight formation along the road."
India Today Fact Check found that this is a 2017 video from Syria.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip in a post dated October 3. According to its caption in Hebrew, the viral video shows a Syrian rebel group attacking the Syrian army years ago.
Further searches led us to media reports from 2017, containing screenshots of the video in question. According to them, this video is from April 25, 2017, and was released by a Syrian rebel group named the Army of Glory.
The Army of Glory or Jaysh al-Izza is a Sunni Islamist Syrian rebel group active in northwestern Syria, mainly in the northern city of Hama and its surroundings.
Per reports , violent clashes took place in Syria's Hama between rebels and Syrian President Bashar al-Assad's forces backed by Iranian militias. Reportedly, this was after the latter attempted to regain control over areas controlled by the rebel group.Â
The video showed an Army of Glory fighter attacking three groups of Assad's forces with missiles during their advance on the Zlin checkpoint, south of Latamneh city.Â
At the time, several Syrian journalists shared this video  on X noting at least 25 people were killed in this attack in Syria's Hama.

News reports note Hezbollah, the Lebanese paramilitary group, has used anti-tank guided missiles against Israel and has released videos showing off its anti-tank arsenal .Â

title: Fact Check: Viral video of boat accident is from Congo, NOT Goa
content:
This video is not from Goa. This accident took place in the Congo.
A video of an overcrowded motorboat capsizing has been widely shared online as a tragic accident in Goa. An Instagram user wrote , "Goa accident today 23 bodies recovered, 40 people rescued and 64 missing. The greed of the boat owner in overloading, the overconfidence of travellers too. It's very sad, tragic."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from the Democratic Republic of the Congo.Â
Reverse searching keyframes from the video led us to an Al Jazeera English report that included the viral clip, uploaded to its official YouTube channel on October 3. As per the report, a boat carrying scores of passengers capsized on Lake Kivu in eastern Congo.Â
Further searches led us to multiple news reports published on October 4 containing the viral video. As per the Associated Press , at least 78 people died in this incident in the Democratic Republic of Congo.Â
The Guardian reported that in the early hours of October 3, a boat believed to be carrying 278 passengers capsized near the shores of Lake Kivu. A BBC report from the same day stated the boat was going from Minova in South Kivu to the Goma area. It noted that accidents due to overloading were common in the Congo.
We found several news reports about similar boat accidents in the Congo. In June this year, 80 people were killed when a boat capsized in Kinshasa, the capital of Congo. In October 2023, 40 people were killed in a similar incident.
We also checked if such an incident happened in Goa recently. According to a local news report , a fishing boat capsized in Goa's Chapora River on September 26. All four onboard were successfully rescued.
Thus, it is clear that a boat capsizing in Congo was falsely linked to Goa.Â
(Written by Arjun Deodia and Ashish Kumar) - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Oct 7, 2024 20:55 IST

title: Fact Check: 99% discounts on Flipkart? No, this is a fraud website
content:
This website impersonating Flipkart is a data harvesting operation. It is in no way affiliated with the e-commerce brand.
We've all seen ridiculous offers during the sale season. But a more than 99 per cent discount is too good to be true. Under the guise of Flipkart's Big Billion Days Sale, this is exactly what's being offered: a Rs 80,000 Apple Watch for less than Rs 500; expensive Canon DSLRs, LG washing machines, and Samsung smartphones for about the same; and much more. Â
While the website linked in posts promising these literally unbelievable discounts looks like Flipkart — it also features the Big Billion Days Sale stamp — you already know we wouldn't be talking about it here if it was legitimate.Â
So, yes. Of course, it's not the real Flipkart website. A spokesperson for the company confirmed this to India Today Fact Check. But there's more to it.Â
First things first. While the website looks like Flipkart, its URL reads exclisivese.live, and not flipkart.com. You'd think this is an easy red flag to spot. But take a moment and consider how often you look at the URL when you launch a link in the in-app browser of whatever social media platform you found it on.
Of course, there are many other discrepancies even if you miss the URL. Elements such as the shopping cart, categories like "offer zone", "fashion", and "electronics" etc. are not clickable. You can only click on the deals mentioned on the homepage. Additionally, while all products list 99 per cent discounts, the numbers don't add up when you calculate the percentages of the sale prices to the retail prices.Â
All of this should be enough to tip you off about potential fraud. Suppose, however, you're curious about the deals regardless. What happens then?
When you select a product and click on "Buy Now", you're redirected to a new web page and asked to fill in personal details, like your name, address, and phone number.Â
As a rule, you should always be careful about what details you provide on any website. But for websites that scream fraud, it's always a no-no! Websites like these either harvest your data to sell to others or use your details to commit financial fraud.Â
We entered false details to see where this would lead us. This redirected us to the "order summary" page and then the "payments" page.Â
Unlike the real Flipkart website or app, this payments page only features three options: PayTM, PhonePe and BHIM UPI. It doesn't allow payments through debit or credit cards, net banking, or cash on delivery. You select only one of the three options and click "Buy Now", which doesn't work.Â
This makes it clear that the sole purpose of this website is simply data harvesting.Â
Using DomainTools, we found that "exclisivese.live" has been reported for phishing, malware, and spam.Â
The Flipkart Big Billion Days Sale began on September 27 and ended on October 6. So, if you see posts like this pop up now, you know it's fraud. Priyanka Serrao, the associate director for corporate affairs and external communications at Flipkart, also told India Today Fact Check that this website was not affiliated to the e-commerce brand in any way.Â
She explained that Flipkart has processes to report and take down such fraudulent sites and shared a recent blog post by the company highlighting precautions people can take to avoid getting scammed.Â
The lesson: 99 per cent discounts sound too good to be true — because they are. - Ends Published By: Radha Basnet Published On: Oct 8, 2024 18:09 IST

title: Fact Check: 'Hand of God' against Iran? No, this video of missile making self-goal is from Ukraine
content:

title: Fact Check: Barking up the wrong tree! This video doesn't show Israeli military dog training
content:
The first part of the video shows a demonstration by the Belgian Federal Police. The second part features social media influencer and former German soldier Michael Rogosin training his dogs.
A video allegedly showing how Israel trains military dogs has been widely shared online. The video montage shows dogs in protective gear being air-dropped and airlifted along with other military personnel. It shows the dog being trained to attack people as well.Â
But is this video really from Israel? India Today Fact Check found that the first part of the video shows a Belgian federal police dog demonstration and the second part features former German soldier Michael Rogosin training dogs. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story OUR PROBE Upon looking closely, we noticed that the helicopter seen at the beginning had the word "politie" written on it. This is Dutch for "police". Additionally, we noticed a logo on the helicopter. A keyword search based on these clues revealed that the logo belongs to the Belgian Federal Police.Â
Upon looking closely, we noticed that the helicopter seen at the beginning had the word "politie" written on it. This is Dutch for "police". Additionally, we noticed a logo on the helicopter. A keyword search based on these clues revealed that the logo belongs to the Belgian Federal Police.Â
A keyword search in the Dutch language led us to the video of the dog jumping from the helicopter on the YouTube channel of the Dutch media outlet NOS Jeugdjournaal, shared on August 28, 2022. The video was titled in Dutch: "Police dog dropped from helicopter stops fake criminal".Â
We also checked the official social media pages of the Belgian Federal Police, where a similar video was shared on Facebook on September 22, 2022.
We also found a Dutch news report related to the video. According to it, the video was shot on a beach in Koksijde, Belgium, where 130 dogs belonging to the police, the fire brigade, and customs demonstrated various skills at an event. The special units' dogs showcased how to jump from a helicopter to eliminate terrorist threats. A translation of the report can be seen below.
The viral video's second part consists of two scenes of a man training a dog. The watermark 'Tactical K9 Family' can be seen as a mirror image in both scenes. This led us to an Instagram page of the same name. The video uses two reels from the Instagram page. In the first video , a man wearing a hat and military vest can be seen training a dog. The second video was also shared on a YouTube channel of the same name.
Another account listed in the bio of the Instagram page revealed that the person in the video is Michael Rogosin , a social media influencer and former German soldier. His content primarily focusses on training dogs.Â
Thus, it is clear that this video does not show Israeli military dogs being trained.Â

title: Fact Check: Jumbo save? No, this video of an elephant rescue is AI-generated
content:
This video is not real. It's AI-generated.
Imagine an elephant stuck on a narrow cliff, being rescued by a gigantic crane. What a magnificent sight that would be, right? You don't have to really imagine it — this scene has been widely shared in a video on social media. One Facebook user who shared this fantastic video wrote, "US police rescued an elephant stuck in a rocky mountain".
India Today Fact Check found that the video is not real. It's AI-generated. OUR PROBEÂ
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to the same video uploaded to a YouTube channel named AThing Inside on October 2. It was titled "US police rescued an elephant stuck in a rocky mountain". As we write this article, the video has been viewed over a million times. The video's description noted that it was "altered or synthetic content", meaning its sound or visuals were "significantly edited or digitally generated".Â
After checking carefully, we found many other animal-related AI-made videos uploaded to the AThing Inside channel. In several videos, these animals were shown in unrealistic situations, such as a lion standing on top of a crocodile , or a panda eating a giant python . All these videos carried the same "altered or synthetic content" disclaimer. The channel's bio says: "I will turn dry videos into new funny videos".Â
Other factors also point to the video being AI-generated. The elephant's skin looks very smooth and shiny. At one point, it appeared to have more than one tail. The cliff's terrain changes from scene to scene. And the people in the background move in a manner that's often observed in AI-generated videos.Â
We searched online to find out if such an incident had happened in the US, but we found no credible media report that could confirm it. Thus, it is clear that this video of an elephant stuck on a rocky mountain is fake.
(Written by Ashish Kumar) - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Oct 8, 2024 23:26 IST

title: Fact Check: Deepender Hooda breaks down after defeat in Haryana? No, this video is old
content:
Viral video is from June 4, 2024, when Hooda got emotional after he won the Rohtak Lok Sabha seat.
The ruling BJP defied anti-incumbency in Haryana and secured a historic third term by winning 48 out of the total 90 Assembly seats , while the Congress lost yet another chance to come to the power. It could get only 37 seats.
Amid the party's morale-crushing defeat, a video of Rohtak MP Deepender Singh Hooda, who is the son of former Haryana CM Bhupinder Singh Hooda, wiping off his tears went viral on social media. Those sharing it claimed that Hooda broke down after the party's dismal show in Haryana.
Sharing this video an X , a user wrote, "This man did padayatra across Haryana, addressed 100+ rallies, remained active on the ground. Feeling sad for Deepender Hooda, his efforts deserved a better ending. We are with you." Its archive can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from 4 June 2024, when Hooda cried out of joy after winning the Rohtak Loksabha seat. Our Probe
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to its longer version ( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dj_Kq76DxL8 ) shared by a YouTube channel back in June 2024. The video description noted that Hooda got emotional after winning the Rohtak Lok Sabha seat by three lakh votes.Â
Further searches led us to a media report about this video dated June 5, 2024. According to it, Deepender Singh Hooda won the Rohtak Lok Sabha seat by more than three lakh votes. Following the victory, a huge crowd of party workers gathered at his house for celebration, making the Congress leader emotional.Â
On June 4, 2024, news agency ANI also shared a video on X , featuring Hooda thanking the party workers and celebrating his victory at his home, while supporters chanted in his support. #WATCH हरियाणा: रोहतक लोकसभा सीट से कांग्रेस उम्मीदवार दीपेंद्र सिंह हुड्डा के घर पर जीत का जश्न मनाया जा रहा है। pic.twitter.com/2dANokoLyy — ANI_HindiNews (@AHindinews) June 4, 2024

Deepender Hooda contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Rohtak and defeated BJP's Arvind Kumar Sharma by more than three lakh votes. In the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, Hooda had contested from the same seat, but lost by a slim margin of seven thousand votes.Â
Thus, an old video of Hooda getting emotional after his Lok Sabha victory was falsely linked to the party's defeat in the Haryana Assembly elections. Â - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Oct 9, 2024 18:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Actresses share peck? No, this video of Kareena and Kiara was made with AI tech
content:
This video is not real. It's AI-generated.
A series of videos allegedly showing prominent Indian actresses kissing each other have gone viral on social media platforms. The most talked-about clip amongst these shows Kiara Advani and Kareena Kapoor Khan  sharing a kiss.Â
Similarly, another clip shows actresses Janhvi Kapoor and Nora Fatehi . Yet another features Kajal Aggarwal and Tamannaah Bhatia . Archives of two such posts can be seen here and here .
India Today Fact Check found that these videos are AI-generated. They were created by modifying still images of these actresses using an AI tool called Vidu.Â
To begin with, had there been real publicly available videos of these fairly popular actresses kissing each other, it would have been all over the news. However, we didn't find any such reports.Â
Secondly, multiple elements in these videos hint at them being AI-generated. For example, in the video featuring Janhvi Kapoor and Nora Fatehi, their hand movements look extremely weird. Similarly, in the other video, Kajal Aggarwal seems to be kissing Tamannaah Bhatia below her nose and above her lips. HOW WERE THESE VIDEOS CREATED?
Upon carefully looking at them, we observed the watermark of Vidu , an AI tool that can create realistic videos using still images. Vidu is one of the many tools  being used to create short video clips of people hugging or kissing each other.   Â
Using Vidu, we generated a video of AI-generated creatures with human bodies and animal heads kissing each other within seconds. This was very similar to the viral videos. REAL IMAGES, FAKE VIDEOS
Using reverse search, we found that the viral video featuring Kareena Kapoor Khan and Kiara Advani was created using a still from a commercial for the beauty brand Tira . In the original image, actress Suhana Khan also posed with them. However, she was cropped from the image while creating the viral video.   Â
Similarly, Janhvi Kapoor and Nora Fatehi's video was created using two separate images. While the former's photo was taken from an episode of the celebrity talk show Koffee with Karan , the latter's was taken from a food supplement commercial .   Â
We compared the viral video with the original images and found that some stills were altered to increase the actresses' bust sizes. In some cases, the images were even laterally inverted or mirrored to show them facing each other in the video.Â
Thus, it's clear that none of these videos are real. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Oct 14, 2024 20:31 IST

title: Fact Check: Goa is not gone! Ratan Tata's beloved dog is alive and well
content:
Goa is alive and well. Ratan Tata's close aide Shantanu Naidu debunked the news of Goa's death.
Just days after the death of industrialist Ratan Tata, many on social media claimed that his pet dog, Goa, died soon after his passing. Alongside this claim, many shared a video of the dog sitting beside Tata's tricolour-draped casket.Â
One such post read, "Sad news. Ratan Tata's pet dog Goa dies after 3 days of his death. That's why they say that dogs are more faithful to their masters, than human beings!"
India Today Fact Check found that the viral posts about Goa's death are fake. Ratan Tata's close aide Shantanu Naidu to a police officer confirmed the dog is alive.
With the help of a keyword search, we found an Instagram post by Sudhir Kudalkar, a senior police inspector at the MHB Colony police station in Borivali West, Mumbai. The post noted that Ratan Tata's pet dog was alive and well. It added that this was confirmed by Tata's close aide Shantanu Naidu. In the caption, Kudalkar urged people not to share posts containing such rumours.
The post also contained a screenshot of Kudalkar's WhatsApp chat with Shantanu Naidu, where he debunked the news of Goa's death. The clarification was also picked up by many news outlets soon after.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Sudhir Kudalkar (@sudhirkudalkar) It is noteworthy that Sudhir Kudalkar himself is widely known for his love for animals. He feeds several stray dogs every day on the premises of the police station and also shares videos of his furry friends now and then. He has also reportedly been felicitated by organisations such as PETA (People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals), the AWB (Animal Welfare Board), and the Government of Maharashtra for working for the welfare of stray animals.  THE STORY OF GOA Years ago, during a trip to Goa , a stray dog began following Ratan Tata. The industrialist took a liking to the animal and decided to adopt him. He brought him to Mumbai and named him after the place he came from — Goa. Mumbai's Taj Mahal Hotel and the headquarters of the Tata Group, Bombay House, also keep their doors open for stray animals. Earlier, another video of a dog trying to climb atop a coffin went viral on social media. Many shared it alleging that this was Goa, paying his last tribute to Ratan Tata. We fact-checked this as well. You can read the report here . Thus, it's clear that the posts about the death of Ratan Tata's dog are untrue. - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Oct 15, 2024 22:36 IST

title: Fact Check: IDF soldiers crying after Hezbollah drone attack? No, this photo is 20 years old
content:
While the photo shows Israeli soldiers, it's from 2004 and has nothing to do with the ongoing Israel-Lebanon conflict.
On October 13, Hezbollah attacked Israel's army base with drone strikes, killing four IDF soldiers and injuring many. As per the IDF , the base targeted was located 33 kilometres south of Haifa.Â
Now a photo making the rounds on social media allegedly shows Israeli soldiers sitting on a floor with their heads down. Those sharing the photo claimed it showed IDF soldiers crying after Hezbollah's latest drone strike.
One such post said, "BREAKING: ISRAELI soldiers are reportedly 'crying, a lot,' as predicted by Hezbollah's Hassan Nasrallah before his martyrdom". Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found that while the photo shows Israeli soldiers, it's from 2004 and has nothing to do with the ongoing Israel-Lebanon conflict. OUR PROBE
With the help of a reverse image search, we found the photo on the stock image website Alamy . As per the information on Alamy, the picture was taken on April 3, 2004, when the Israeli army found a tunnel in a house during an operation at the Rafah refugee camp, adjacent to the Palestinian town of Rafah.Â
The soldiers in the photo were reportedly waiting as specialists inspected the tunnel. It was shot by Associated Press photographer Oded Balilty.Â
There are other images from the same search operation available on Alamy .
An NBC News report  published on April 7, 2004, noted that Israeli troops found several tunnels at the time on the border between Egypt and the Gaza Strip, where the Rafah refugee camp is located.Â
Hence, it is clear that this photo, which is more than two decades old, has nothing to do with the ongoing Israel-Lebanon conflict. - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Oct 15, 2024 23:12 IST

title: Fact Check: Leer-biceps! This video DOESN'T show shirtless Muslim man harassing Hindu woman
content:
This was not a real incident. It's a staged video.
Picture this: a man and a woman walking on the street are suddenly accosted by another man who takes off his shirt and flexes his muscles. What makes this already strange encounter stranger is that the woman starts slapping the shirtless man, almost chasing him away. This is a video  that's been widely shared  online and those sharing it claimed the shirtless man was Muslim and the woman was Hindu.
An X user wrote alongside the video that "Abdul" removed his shirt to show his body to a "Hindu woman and is well treated by the brave Hindu woman. Resist the unrighteous. This is the right path. Salute." The name Abdul is often used online as code for Muslims to avoid infringing community guidelines. The viral post's archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found this was a staged video. It doesn't show a real incident.
Responding to one of the viral posts, many claimed that this was a scripted video, taken from an Instagram account called "tamannakohli786787". We checked the Instagram account and found the viral video shared there on September 19 with hashtags like "reels" and "entertainment".Â
The profile suggests that the woman in the video is Tamanna Kohli, a video creator with more than eight thousand Instagram followers. On the account, we found several similar videos that show different men flexing their muscles and then getting thrashed by Kohli.Â
Apart from this, the two men in the viral video can also be seen acting in other videos shared by the account.Â
To verify if the video was staged, India Today Fact Check spoke to Tamanna Kohli. She confirmed the video was completely scripted and that she created it for "public awareness". There was no Hindu-Muslim angle to it, she added.Â
Thus, we ascertained that this video did not show a Muslim man harassing a Hindu woman on the street. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Oct 17, 2024 16:59 IST

title: Fact Check: This video doesn't show 'reality' of Bahraich violence, it's from Maharajganj
content:
This October 11 video is from Mishraulia village in UP's Maharajganj, more than 200 km from Bahraich. It took place two days before the violence in Bahraich.
In the aftermath of communal violence in Bahraich, Uttar Pradesh, during which a Hindu man, Ram Gopal Mishra, was killed, a video allegedly showing the incident was widely shared online. Those sharing the video claimed: "This video reveals the truth about how the violence in Bahraich actually started."
In the video, people can be seen dancing to loud music while marching through a street with saffron flags featuring the iconic " Angry Hanuman " image. Suddenly, one of the people standing outside a house pulls away the flag and throws it, after which a clash starts.
Sharing the video  on X, one person wrote in Hindi: "Make the truth of Bahraich go viral, Hindus. Look carefully, first the Jihadis snatched the saffron flag and tore it, then threw stones at the Durga procession. After this, the situation in Bahraich worsened. Show the world who the real rioter is." Other similar posts can be seen here and here .
India Today Fact Check found that this incident took place in Mishraulia village in the Maharajganj district in Uttar Pradesh, more than 200 kilometres away from Bahraich. OUR PROBE
We observed that some people responded to the viral posts claiming the video was not from Bahraich but from Maharajganj. With the help of a keyword search, we found several news reports about this incident.
According to an ETV Bharat report , this incident took place during the Durga Puja Dola procession in Uttar Pradesh's Mishraulia village, which falls under the Nichlaul police station, on October 11. The report stated that following the incident, police were heavily deployed in the area. At the same time, the police registered a case against 12 named persons and five unidentified people.
Reports in Live Hindustan  and India TV also mention that this incident took place in Mishraulia village of Maharajganj in Uttar Pradesh. It's worth noting that Mahrajganj is more than 200 kilometres away from Bahraich.
The Nichlaul police also confirmed that the incident took place in their area and that some arrests had been made in this case.
Thus, it is clear that this video does not show the violence that took place on October 13 in Bahraich, Uttar Pradesh.Â
(Written by Abhishek Pathak) - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Oct 17, 2024 19:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Students swimming amid Chennai floods? Yes, but this video is from 2023
content:

Heavy rains brought Chennai and other parts of Tamil Nadu to a standstill on October 15 and 16 , resulting in schools and colleges shutting down, frequent power outages, train and flight cancellations , and traffic congestion on waterlogged streets.Â
Amid this, a video of youngsters wading through waist-deep water on a street. They appeared to be carrying their bags on a mattress. Did the university campus flood recently as well?

title: Fact Check: Israel troops heading to Iran? Nope, this is GTA V
content:
This is footage from a modded version of the video game Grand Theft Auto V.
As the Israel-Lebanon conflict continues, a video now going viral purports to show Israel preparing to strike Iran. The video shows a convoy of military vehicles — armoured cars, trucks, and tanks — darting through meandering roads. Israeli flags are visible on the side of the road at one point. Text inside the video reads: "Israel getting ready for Iran."
India Today Fact Check found that this video was made in a modded or modified version of Grand Theft Auto V, a video game. It doesn't show a real military convoy. OUR PROBEÂ
A closer look at the viral video raised suspicions that the footage was animated. The watermark "Diar Gaming" can be seen in the video. Based on this clue, we found a Facebook account named Diar Gaming.Â
According to the information on the Facebook page, the page belongs to Omar Abdullah Mohiuddin , a gaming video creator from Ebril in Iraq. This viral video was shared on this account on September 9. However, this post contained no information about what video game it was from.Â
A keyword search based on the available clues led to the discovery of many gaming videos related to the Israeli army. On a YouTube channel called "Game Loverz", we found the laterally inverted or mirrored version of the viral video shared on August 2. The video was titled "Irani Fighter Jets, Tanks & Helicopter Attack on Israeli Army Tanks Convoy | Iran Israel War - GTA 5".
According to the information provided on the channel, this YouTube account belongs to Adnan Majeed , who lists their location as Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir. The account's bio states: "In this channel you can know all about GTA V. I am playing only GTA V and only share GTA V videos with you."
This channel featured several other similar GTA V videos, one of which was titled "Iran Attack on Israel Army Convoy | Israel Moving Tanks to Gaza - GTA 5".Â
Grand Theft Auto V is a 2013 open-world action-adventure game. The game has been modded or modified or customised by various gamers over the years. Mod services like FiveM  and 5MODS  are often used by players.Â
It's noteworthy that video game videos have been falsely shared as war footage in the past as well. You can read our fact-checks of those here , here , and here .Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral video does not show a real Israeli military convoy.Â
(Written by Deenadayal M) - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Oct 17, 2024 22:54 IST

content:

title: Fact Check: Saudi Arabia celebrating Yahya Sinwar's killing? No, this video is old
content:
This video is more than one year old and shows Saudi Arabia's National Day celebrations. It is unrelated to Yahya Sinwar's killing.
Following the death of Hamas chief Yahya Sinwar , killed by Israeli troops on October 16 in Rafah, a video of a magnificent show of fireworks began making the rounds on social media. Allegedly, it showed people in Saudi Arabia celebrating Sinwar's killing. Â
An X user shared the clip and wrote: "Celebrations erupt in Saudi Arabia following the death of Sinwar".Â
India Today found that the video is more than one year old and shows the celebration of Saudi Arabia's National Day. It has no relation to the ongoing Israel-Palestine conflict.
We observed many comments responding to the viral posts, saying the video showed celebrations of the Saudi National Day. With the help of relevant keywords, we found several similar videos of fireworks shows on YouTube , said to be from Saudi National Day events.
Saudi Arabia's national day is celebrated on September 23 every year, with massive fireworks displays  organised across the country.Â
Upon searching further, we found that the viral video was uploaded to the YouTube channel "Moamen Ahmed" on September 24, 2023. The Arabic caption suggests the video was from Saudi Arabia's 93rd National Day.Â
The channel also shared a similar video of fireworks in September 2022. It is to be noted that this video is also from the same location as seen in the viral video. The location of the video is mentioned in the description as "Thaghr Plaza".Â
We searched for this location on Google Street View and found this was indeed the location where the viral video was shot in Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh. A comparison of the Street View and the viral video can be seen below.
Thus, it's clear the video doesn't show Yahya Sinwar's death being celebrated.Â
What's Saudi Arabia's stance on the Israel-Palestine conflict?
In May this year, Saudi Arabia officially condemned the Israeli forces' attacks on Palestine, calling them genocidal massacres. The Kingdom also stressed the need for the international community to assume its responsibilities to stop the "massacres against the Palestinians."
However, The Atlantic reported last month that Saudi Arabia's Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman told US Secretary of State Antony Blinken that he does not personally care about the "Palestinian issue". The Middle East Eye conversely quoted a Saudi official who described this account as "incorrect". - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Oct 21, 2024 20:26 IST

title: Fact Check: Not Sharia! 2018 video from UP's Bulandshahr given FALSE communal twist
content:
This video from March 2018 shows a Hindu woman in UP's Bulandshahr being flogged by her husband Shaudan Singh for allegedly eloping with her neighbour.
A video of a man flogging a bound woman with a large crowd surrounding them has been widely shared on social media. Allegedly, the man was administering punishment under Sharia , or Islamic religious laws.Â
An X user wrote while sharing the video: "Under Sharia law, if a woman is raped, it's considered sex outside of marriage, and she is to be punished. In most Sharia countries, women are stoned do death if they report they were raped. So the one in the video got 'lucky' for only being flogged."
India Today Fact Check found that the viral claims are misleading. This video from March 2018 shows a Hindu woman in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr being beaten up by her husband on the village panchayat's orders.
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we found multiple reports from March 2018 featuring screenshots of the clip. According to a Hindustan Times report published on March 22, 2018, this incident took place in the Launga village of Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district. A woman was tied to a tree and beaten mercilessly by multiple men for seven hours. Reportedly, she was flogged for allegedly eloping.Â
Reports mentioned that the incident occurred on March 10, 2018, and the video went viral ten days later. The man in the green shirt seen beating the woman was her husband, Shaudan Singh. According to reports, Shaudan Singh was arrested by the police along with the village's former pradhan Sher Singh and his son Shravan. This makes it clear that the accused are not Muslims. The accused had also molested the woman after beating her.
According to these reports, the police said the panchayat came up with the punishment of flogging because they wanted to "teach the woman a lesson". Then Bulandshahr Superintendent of Police Praveen Ranjan Singh told the Hindustan Times that Sher Singh and his supporters convened a kangaroo court and ordered her public flogging.
In her complaint to the police, the woman said that she ran away with her neighbour, Dharmendra Lodhi, on March 5, 2018.
AajTak's Bulandshahr correspondent Mukul Sharma confirmed that the public flogging occurred on March 10, 2018, in Bulandshahr's Launga village, which falls under the Sayana police station. He added that both the victim and the accused were Hindus.
A report in Jansatta noted that police had filed an FIR against seven named and 12 unidentified persons.
It is thus clear that this video does not show a rape victim being punished under Sharia. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Oct 22, 2024 20:43 IST

title: Fact Check: This homeless dog lover didn't die in Israeli attacks in Gaza, photo is from 2020
content:
The photo is of a homeless Yemeni man who died in 2020. It has nothing to do with the Israel-Hamas conflict.
A heartbreaking image of a dead man surrounded by several dogs, some of them cozying up to him, has gone viral on social media. Allegedly, this man was killed in Israeli airstrikes in the Gaza Strip.Â
The caption with the photo reads, "Dogs bid farewell to their owner after he was killed by the Israeli occupation forces in the ongoing massacres against displaced Palestinians in the Gaza Strip...21 October 2024".Â
Believing the claim to be true, netizens are expressing sorrow by commenting broken heart emojis on the viral photo . Archived version of the viral photo can be seen here.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the photo is of a homeless Yemeni man who died in 2020. It has nothing to do with the Israel-Hamas conflict.
A reverse image search led us to an Arabic report of Al Jazeera, published on October 20, 2020. The report carries the viral picture which established that it is old and not from the Israel-Hamas war.Â
The report says that the man seen in the photo was a Yemeni citizen Ismail Hadi who died on the street in Ibb governorate in 2020. Hadi was known for his generosity towards stray dogs as he used to feed them despite being homeless.Â
After his sudden death in October 2020, stray dogs were photographed gathering around him in affection. Reportedly, the strays were not allowing the people to touch the body of the man.Â
As per the report of a web portal 'Alwatan Voice", the man died of a sudden heart attack. The news piece further says that Hadi would collect the leftover food from restaurants and feed it to the stray dogs every day.Â
Many Yemeni journalists and activists shared the viral photo on social media at that time and mourned the death of dog-lover Hadi. Some also shared the video of the incident.Â
Hence the claim with the viral photo is untrue. The photo is not from Gaza but Yemen and the man seen in it didn't die in Israeli airstrikes. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Oct 22, 2024 23:04 IST

title: Fact Check: Fire on water video is NOT from Bengaluru's flooded streets
content:
The video is neither from Bengaluru nor from India at all. It's from Vietnam's Can Tho.
Over the past few days, heavy rainfall in Bengaluru, Karnataka, has caused waterlogging and flooding in various parts of the city. Rescue boats have reportedly been deployed in the Silicon Valley of India to provide essential supplies.Â
Amid this, a video allegedly from Bengaluru is making rounds online. It shows a live electrical wire bursting into flames on a flooded road. An X user wrote , "Miracle in Bangalore. Water is on fire!" Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from Vietnam.Â
Many responded to the viral post claiming the video was not from Bengaluru but from Vietnam. A reverse search on the viral video's keyframes led us to a post dated October 15, 2024. It read: "This is what happened when lightning struck a powerline causing it to fall into floodwater. Can Tho in Vietnam." This is what happened when lightning struck a powerline causing it to fall into floodwater ⚡️👀 📍 Cần ThÆ¡, Vietnam (today I believe) pic.twitter.com/fSqAu5xboh — Volcaholic 🌋 (@volcaholic1) October 15, 2024
This is what happened when lightning struck a powerline causing it to fall into floodwater ⚡️👀 📍 Cần ThÆ¡, Vietnam (today I believe) pic.twitter.com/fSqAu5xboh — Volcaholic 🌋 (@volcaholic1) October 15, 2024
Further searches led us to several news reports about this video from October 16. As per CafeF , a Vietnam-based news channel, the video is from October 14, when heavy rain lasting nearly two hours caused deep flooding in the streets of the central area of Can Tho City, causing power disruptions in many households.
During this time, a high-voltage electrical wire broke and fell onto a waterlogged road. Fearing danger from the sparking flames, many passers-by turned their vehicles away while many drove through nearby despite it getting bigger. A VietnamPlus report published on October 16 claimed the incident took place in the southern Vietnamese city of Can Tho.
We found several news reports saying there were heavy rains in Can Tho on October 14, after which streets were flooded, causing heavy traffic jams in the area.Â
Notably, several parts of Bengaluru are facing waterlogging due to heavy rains. We, however, could not find any news report detailing an incident like the one seen in the viral video.
