title: Jio Mere Lal: Meet the secret superstar who outsmarted Reliance and secured JioHotstar.com
content:
The JioCinema and Hotstar merger has been in the works for quite some time now. As the months progressed and things started falling into place for this mega-merger that could change the future of OTT in India, one tiny but important element stuck out like a sore thumb. The Ambanis realised that the most obvious choice for the website — JioHotstar.com — was not available to them.Â
Before they could figure out who secured this, a dramatic letter appeared on this website. It said Reliance would have to shell out a little more than Rs 1 crore to get this domain, which currently belongs to an anonymous app developer based in Delhi. Interestingly, this secret superstar claims he wants this money (£93,345 or Rs 1,01,72,598) to pursue an executive MBA course at Cambridge University in the UK.Â
India Today reached out to this much sought-after man, who outsmarted Reliance and asked him how he is planning his moves in a battle that's anything but even. The conversation has been edited for brevity.Â
Before we come to the JioHotstar issue, tell us about yourself
For reasons you can understand, I don't want to disclose my complete identity. What I can tell you is that I am a 28-year-old middle-class guy from Delhi. I was born and brought up here. My father is a government servant and my mother is a homemaker. I have a startup that deals with film recommendation algorithms. I am a regular EMI-paying guy who hopes to make it big someday.
We found an Instagram account for JioHotstar. The name there says Vivek Kumar. Is that you?
No, that is not me. There are other smart guys out there too (laughs).
You said in the letter posted on JioHotstar.com that you want to pursue an executive MBA course at Cambridge University, UK and hope Reliance arranges for the fee. Are you a computer engineer?Â
I am an aspiring entrepreneur who is also into technology. I did my bachelor's in IT from a college in the Delhi-NCR and then did my master's in psychology.Â
Information technology with psychology? That's an unusual combination.
Yes, it is. But it helped me do what I always wanted to do. I combined both skills to develop an algorithm to recommend movies based on your personality. The app I made did not go very far due to financial constraints, but it helped me get selected for a short program at Cambridge University in 2021.Â
So, you've already been to Cambridge University.
Yes and no. The course I was selected for, the Cambridge Startup Accelerator Program, was offline. But then the pandemic happened and it became an online course. Later, after the course was over, I visited the Cambridge campus just to get the "feel" of it.
(He shared his photo from Cambridge with us. We are withholding it so as not to reveal his identity)
How hopeful are you that Reliance will pay you Rs 1 crore and let you return to Cambridge for an executive MBA programme?
See, I am well aware that I am but a small fry in front of the corporate giant that is Reliance. They will probably snatch the domain I registered in 2023 without paying me a penny. I know they have the clout and legal might. But I hope they don't do that. I have not done anything wrong or illegal. Jio is a brand, Hotstar is a brand, but "JioHotsar" is not a legal entity as of today — let alone in 2023, when I registered this domain.
You registered this domain in September 2023, before the merger was announced. How did you anticipate this? Do you closely follow business news?
Yes, I follow the news very closely, including business news. Registering the domain was a combination of luck and some foresight. I discussed it with a few friends when I read about the buzz around a JioCinema and Hotstar merger. They scoffed at the idea. But I went ahead and registered it because it did not cost a lot. Less than Rs 5,000. Since then, I have waited for this domain to turn into my ticket to Cambridge.
Why didn't you approach Reliance privately instead of publishing the letter on the website?Â
Oh, I contacted Reliance multiple times. I emailed many senior people. I never got a reply. In March, when the Reliance Group registered the domain JioHotstar.in, I thought they must be interested in securing JioHotstar.com because the "dot com" domain is much more popular. But when no one got back, I decided to go public.Â
And now people from the Reliance Group have spoken to you? What did they offer?Â
Yes, I spoke to a Reliance representative on a Zoom call, but he did not offer me anything apart from the few thousand rupees I spent registering the domain. They were curt and hung up abruptly when I refused to disclose my identity and declined their "offer". They also warned me of legal consequences, which is sad. The amount I asked for my studies is half of what Aakash Ambani gifted as expensive watches during his wedding. For such a big company, this is peanuts.
What if someone just hacked your website, and you lose control of it?
I am already being targeted. Some people figured out my email address and have been trying to reset the password to take over the domain. I'm constantly being bombarded with password reset notifications. Thankfully, so far they haven't succeeded. But it's a lot of stress to deal with this.Â
How are you coping with this stress? Have you taken your family into confidence?Â
I am more worried about my parents than myself. They are very worried because they think I am trying to take on Reliance and the Ambanis — which is definitely not the case.Â
It's also kind of funny. Some people have figured out I am the guy who has the domain and are blackmailing me for money to not disclose my identity. I don't know what to do (laughs). I haven't got any money from Reliance yet, and other people already want some part of that.Â
You asked for legal help in your letter. Has anyone volunteered?
Oh, yes! Many have. I was moved by their kindness. Lawyers, some of them from the Supreme Court — one of them is even from Cambridge — have written to me saying they will fight my case pro bono. But I don't want to enter a legal battle against Ambanis. I know my limits. At the end of the day, I am a common man, a film buff, and ironically, a JioCinema subscriber.
(With Pathikrit Sanyal) - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Oct 24, 2024 19:41 IST

title: Fact Check: What an explosive photo of the Lebanon sky! Pity it's AI-generated
content:
This photo is not real. It was generated using AI.
Middle East Airlines is the only commercial airline still operating in conflict-ridden Beirut as Israeli air strikes continue in southern Lebanon. The airline reportedly conducts daily assessments to ensure the safety of operations amid the risk of air raids.
Now, a photo allegedly showing an MEA flight landing with a huge explosion in the backdrop has gone viral. Many shared the photo with captions like, "A photo for the history books. MEA airline landing in Beirut International Airport as Israeli rains fire on the airport."Â
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this photo is AI-generated.Â
Reverse searching the photo led us to an Instagram post dated October 21. Along with the viral photo, the post contained another similar picture of a flight landing amid an explosion. The caption of the post stated that these photos were generated using AI, crediting another Instagram account named "@south.to.north".Â
While we could not find the viral photo on this account, we have reached out to them for more information.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Lebanon 🇱🇧 (@south.to.north)
A post shared by Lebanon 🇱🇧 (@south.to.north)
We also compared the flight seen in the viral photo with photos of MEA flights. We noticed several discrepancies in the aeroplane, such as the design of the tail and the blurred-out portion of the plane's body. A comparison between the two can be seen below.
We used the AI detection tool Hive Moderation , which stated there was a 91.7 per cent chance of it being generated using AI. Another such tool called TrueMedia stated there was substantial evidence of generative AI being used to create the photo.
Notably, as per news reports, Captain Mohammed Aziz, an adviser to the MEA chairman, recently stated that some of the most dramatic photos of jets landing in fiery hellscapes were generated using AI, adding that they will only operate as long as the threat assessment marks it safe.
It is thus, clear that the viral photo of an aeroplane landing amid explosions was AI-generated. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Oct 24, 2024 21:24 IST

title: Fact Check: Chinese troops chant 'Jai Shri Ram' amid disengagement at Ladakh? No, this video is old
content:
This video predates the India-China disengagement by several months. It has been present on social media since as early as January 2024.
After agreeing to de-escalate border tensions and end the standoff along the Line of Actual Control, India and China began disengagement in eastern Ladakh on October 25. Indian soldiers are reportedly retreating to the west of the Charding Nala and China's People's Liberation Army is heading back east, both forces dismantling tents and other structures on either side. Patrolling is expected to resume in the Depsang and Demchok regions soon.
Now a video making the rounds on social media allegedly shows troops of both nations chanting "Jai Shri Ram". In it, Indian troops could be seen teaching Chinese soldiers how to pronounce "Jai Shri Ram" and then chanting it together.
One person shared the video on Facebook  writing, "Brics summit outcomes: India & China begin troop disengagement in eastern Ladakh. Troop withdrawal has commenced at key friction points in Demchok and the Depsang Plains. Indian forces are withdrawing equipment in accordance with the agreement reached on Monday to end the border standoff."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video has been on social media since as early as January 2024, and thus unrelated to the recent disengagement decision.Â
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same video shared in a Facebook post , dated January 22, 2024, making it clear that it predates the India-China disengagement by several months. The post, however, contained no information about the video.Â
Further searches led us to news reports about this video, published in January this year. According to India TV , the video went viral on social media during the consecration ceremony of Ayodhya's Ram Mandir on January 22. Per reports, the video emerged from the Line of Actual Control at a time when China and India were locked in a border standoff.Â
The presence of tables of snacks and beverages between the troops indicates that it was shot during a meeting between the two sides. Quoting sources, several news outlets reported the video was not shot at the time of the Pran Pratishtha ceremony, but during a routine meeting between the troops three months before, around Diwali in 2023. There was, however, no official confirmation from the army regarding the clip.
We also found an X post dated January 22 that geolocated the video, stating it was from the Chepzi-Chumar border areas of southern Ladakh. The features and the mountains in the background as seen on Google Earth match the video's terrain. Geolocated @Kyangs_Thang . Chepzi-Chumar border areas, southern ladakh. Coordinates: 32.600858°, 78.513753. https://t.co/EknXIzff3o pic.twitter.com/DLctxZsxL4 — Nature Desai (@NatureDesai) January 22, 2024
Geolocated @Kyangs_Thang . Chepzi-Chumar border areas, southern ladakh. Coordinates: 32.600858°, 78.513753. https://t.co/EknXIzff3o pic.twitter.com/DLctxZsxL4 — Nature Desai (@NatureDesai) January 22, 2024
Incidentally, news reports about the video from January also mention that this video was likely from Ladakh's Chepzi-Chumar area. Thus, it's clear this video is not related to the recent disengagement process between India and China. - Ends Published By: Manisha Pandey Published On: Oct 25, 2024 16:48 IST

title: Fact Check: Modi wasn't snubbed for this BRICS group photo. He'd already left for India
content:
The viral video is from an October 24 event. But PM Modi left Russia on October 23.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Russia from October 22 to 23 to attend the 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan, Russia, where he held bilateral talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin and several world leaders. In its aftermath, a video from the event began making the rounds online that showed world leaders gathered for the photograph. PM Modi, however, was nowhere to be seen.Â
Sharing this video, many claimed that Putin  did not invite the Indian Pm for this photo-op, calling it an "international insult". One such post's archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video, while from the BRICS Summit, was shot on October 24. Modi had left for India the day before.Â
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an October 24 post on the news agency ANI's official X account. It read: "Russia: EAM Dr S Jaishankar with Heads of delegations at Kazan Expo International Exhibition Center, at the 16th BRICS Summit in BRICS plus format." #WATCH | Russia: EAM Dr S Jaishankar with Heads of delegations at Kazan Expo International Exhibition Center, at the 16th BRICS Summit in BRICS plus format. (Video: Host broadcaster via Reuters) pic.twitter.com/FvMG1d6Hxt — ANI (@ANI) October 24, 2024 The plenary session of the 16th BRICS Summit in the BRICS-plus format was attended by leaders from the Commonwealth of Independent States, as well as delegations from Asia, Africa, the Middle East, Latin America, and international organisations. Subsequent keyword searches led us to multiple news reports that said External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar represented Modi at the BRICS Plus event in Kazan on October 24. The event was attended by Putin, China's Xi Jinping, and Turkish President Recep Tayyip ErdoÄŸan. Jaishankar led the Indian delegation at this event as Modi had returned to India on October 23 after the main sessions of the Summit. We also found a video on ANI's X account from October 23 where PM Modi can be seen boarding an aeroplane. The post said: "Prime Minister Narendra Modi emplanes for Delhi after attending the 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan, Russia." This made it clear that when the BRICS Plus event took place on October 24, Modi was not in Russia at that time. #WATCH | Prime Minister Narendra Modi emplanes for Delhi after attending the 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan, Russia. (Source: DD News) pic.twitter.com/gF6bE4ZId2 — ANI (@ANI) October 23, 2024 For more information, we checked the PM's social media accounts and found that he last posted about the Summit on October 23, when he shared a video showing the event's highlights. We did not find any posts related to the Summit from October 24 or 25. advertisement The PM in fact shared photos of his meeting with German Chancellor Olaf Scholz on October 25 at his residence in New Delhi. Welcomed my friend, Chancellor Scholz, to my residence in New Delhi. Glad to be meeting him and discussing a diverse range of issues that will add momentum to the India-Germany friendship. Our nations have a strong track record of developmental cooperation and we look forward to… pic.twitter.com/c6spNi4VDk — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) October 25, 2024 Thus, it is clear that by the time the photo-op seen in the viral video took place at the BRICS Summit on October 24, Modi had already arrived in India. (Written by Ashish Kumar) - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Oct 25, 2024 19:03 IST

title: Fact Check: Israeli attack on Beirut, Lebanon, FALSELY viral as IDF's retaliation against Iran
content:
This video dates back to October 23 and shows Israeli attacks on Al-Laylaki, a suburb of Beirut, Lebanon.
In response to a missile attack by Iran on October 1, Israel launched a heavy assault on Tehran's military sites  in the early hours of October 26. While the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) claimed significant damage, Iran reported only two soldiers lost and minimal destruction .
Meanwhile, a video showing an explosion between buildings in an urban area has gone viral, with people claiming it captures Israel's recent attack on Iran.
These posts  were shared with captions that read, "#BreakingNews. Israel has launched its retaliation on the Islamic Regime. The whole world is watching you, Israel. **** the Islamic Regime of Iran."
Others shared this video on Facebook  and captioned it, "Tehran right now. Israel penetrates Iranian airspace easily and is now bombing the IRGC. May it be the end of this rotten regime".
However, the India Today Fact Check found that the video is not from Tehran or even Iran. It is from the suburbs of Lebanon's capital Beirut. OUR PROBE
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, the results led us to the same clip with a better resolution posted to X by a user on October 24, two days before the Israeli attack against Iran. ⚡️BREAKING: Israel is currently bombing Al-Laylaki area in the suburb Beirut, Lebanon. More than 6 airstrikes reported so far on the suburbs Beirut and Al-Mayadeen's office was also targeted. Israel continues to act with impunity. pic.twitter.com/PecSjmVQKS — Suppressed News. (@SuppressedNws) October 23, 2024 The caption of this post mentioned that the video shows an Israeli attack on the suburb of Beirut in Lebanon. The caption stated, "BREAKING: Israel is currently bombing Al-Laylaki region in the suburb Beirut, Lebanon. More than 6 airstrikes reported so far on the suburbs Beirut and Al-Mayadeen's office was also targeted. Israel continues to act with impunity." As the logo of Al Jadeed TV was visible in this video, subsequent searches took us to the original and extended version , posted by the Lebanese outlet in the early hours of October 24, 2024. The caption roughly translated to, "Al-Jadeed lens captures the moment of the violent raid on the Al-Laylaki area." عدسة الجديد ترصد لحظة الغارة العنيفة على منطقة الليلكي pic.twitter.com/Bc29gasmyI — Al Jadeed News (@ALJADEEDNEWS) October 23, 2024 Searches with the help of these clues took us to a France24 report featuring an aerial shot from this location. This report, dated October 23, mentioned that Israel carried out a wave of air strikes on Hezbollah's southern Beirut stronghold on Wednesday night, destroying a residential complex, as stated by the Lebanese state media. Therefore, it is safe to conclude that a video of an Israeli attack on Beirut, Lebanon, was falsely portrayed as a fresh attack on Iran by the IDF. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Oct 26, 2024 19:31 IST

title: Fact Check: Egyptian air drill FALSELY shared as Israeli jets returning from Iran
content:
This video doesn't show Israeli fighter jets returning from Iran. rIt shows a drill conducted by the Egyptian Air Force.
In response to a missile attack by Iran on October 1, Israel conducted a series of airstrikes on military bases in Iran  early last Saturday. While the IDF claimed significant damage, the Iranian army reported only four soldiers had died with limited damage to equipment.
In a video now going viral on social media, several fighter jets can be flying in the sky. Allegedly, these were Israeli fighter jets returning home from an attack on Iran.
People shared the clip  with captions that read, "Israel fighter jet squadrons all returning home from Iran after destroying its air defense systems and several military installations."
India Today Fact Check found that the video does not show Israeli fighter jets; rather, it shows a drill conducted by the Egyptian Air Force.Â
A reverse image search of the keyframe from the viral video led us to the same clip uploaded by an Instagram user on October 23, three days before the Israeli attack on Iran. Many commenters on the post suggested that the viral clip originated from Egypt or was related to the Egyptian Air Force. Based on the above information, a subsequent search with keywords led us to the same clip shared by an Egyptian TikTok user on October 3. The caption in Arabic said: "Egyptian Army." Further searches in Arabic led us to a report on the official YouTube channel of the Egyptian news outlet ElMehwar TV Channel, posted on October 3. The Arabic caption roughly translates to, "The Egyptian Air Force is participating in an air drill during the graduation ceremony for a new group of students from the Egyptian Military Academy." Another Egyptian news outlet, TeN TV, reported the same information in its coverage. Thus, it's clear that the viral video doesn't show Israeli fighter jets returning from Iran. - Ends (Written By Surajuddin Mondal) Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Oct 27, 2024 19:42 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Zelenskyy refuse to shake hands with UN Secretary-General?
content:
The photo was taken just before Zelenskyy and Guterres shook each other's hands on September 19, 2023, at the UN Headquarters.
The Russia-Ukraine war entered its 977th day on October 28. Throughout the conflict, Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has consistently opposed Russia on various international platforms, including the United Nations. He has also held multiple meetings  with UN Secretary-General António Guterres to discuss issues related to the war.
A picture now going viral on social media shows Guterres extending his hand to Zelenskyy, who, instead of shaking it, stares at the former's face. A Facebook user shared this picture and wrote on it, "Zelenskyy refuses to shake hands with the UN secretary-general."
India Today Fact Check found that on September 19, 2023, Zelenskyy met Guterres at UN Headquarters, where they shook hands. But the viral picture was taken just before the two leaders shook hands.
A reverse image search of the viral picture led us to an article published by the Associated Press on September 21, 2023. The eighth image in the report shows Zelenskyy shaking hands with António Guterres. The caption notes that Zelenskyy met Guterres on Tuesday, September 19, 2023, at the United Nations headquarters. We found similarities between this image and the viral picture, particularly in the backgrounds and clothing of both leaders.Â
Based on the above information, a subsequent search led us to another article  published by the official website of the President of Ukraine on September 20, 2023. It mentioned that "during the 78th session of the UN General Assembly in New York, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with UN Secretary-General António Guterres as part of the General Debate." Â
We also found a video  of Zelenskyy's meeting with Secretary-General António Guterres. This video, shot from a different angle, was shared on September 20, 2023, by the Ukrainian head on his official X account. The 18th second of this clip matches exactly with the viral image. After that, both leaders were seen shaking hands. I met with @AntonioGuterres to thank the UN for its efforts to mitigate the consequences of Russian aggression. We count on further active UN support in providing humanitarian relief to our people. We also discussed the prospects of reviving the Black Sea Grain Initiative. pic.twitter.com/kEqV5IvIjW — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) September 19, 2023
I met with @AntonioGuterres to thank the UN for its efforts to mitigate the consequences of Russian aggression. We count on further active UN support in providing humanitarian relief to our people. We also discussed the prospects of reviving the Black Sea Grain Initiative. pic.twitter.com/kEqV5IvIjW — Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa) September 19, 2023
Thus, it is evident that the claim about Zelenskyy's refusal to shake hands with the UN Secretary-General is false. - Ends (Written By Surajuddin Mondal) Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Oct 28, 2024 16:03 IST

title: Fact Check: 2017 truck ramming video FALSELY shared as recent Tel Aviv incident
content:
This video is from 2017. A Palestinian driver rammed his truck into Israeli soldiers in Jerusalem.
A truck rammed into a bus stop in Ramat Hasharon, a city northeast of Tel Aviv on October 27, killing one person and injuring a dozen others. The suspected terror attack occurred close to Israel's Glilot military base.
Now a video going viral on social media shows a truck crashing into several people and others running for their lives. Many claimed the video showed the recent truck ramming incident in Tel Aviv.Â
An X user wrote, "Confirmed reports from the occ territories, 17+ killed & 50+ injured (mostly critical) Zionist soldiers from the 8200 spy unit in Tel Aviv. Many stayed stuck under the truck for a long time. The hero went down and finished them off with a knife. See the cowards fleeing the stage." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from 2017 when a Palestinian driver rammed his truck into Israeli soldiers in Jerusalem.
A reverse image search led us to a Washington Post report containing the viral video's screengrab, published on January 8, 2017. As per the report , the incident took place just blocks from the US Consulate in Jerusalem when a Palestinian driver rammed his truck into a group of Israeli soldiers that day. Israeli police officials called this incident a terrorist attack.Â
According to a January 2017 report in The Mirror , the attacker, Fadi Ahmad Hamdan Qunbor, was an ISIS supporter. Four soldiers were killed in this attack, three of whom were women. Reportedly, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited the scene and discussed Israel's response.Â
We also found a video report by CBS New York  dated January 9, 2017, that described the attacker as a 28-year-old ISIS supporter.Â
Thus, it is more than clear that a 7-year-old video of a truck ramming into Israeli soldiers in Jerusalem is falsely shared as recent.Â
(Written by Ashish Kumar) - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Oct 28, 2024 18:53 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show Palestinian child trapped under rubble
content:
The child is from Syria, and not Palestine. The video also does not show her trapped under rubble but peeking from a hole in a wall.
As Israel's invasion of Gaza continues, a video allegedly showing a young Palestinian girl trapped under rubble has been widely shared online. An X user wrote alongside the video: "A Palestinian child trapped under the rubble awaits help. What a heartbreaking scene."
Similar posts can be seen here  and here . The viral post's archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that neither was the child trapped under rubble, nor is she from Palestine — she's from Syria.Â
Amongst the responses to the viral video, we found another clip  of the same child. In it, the child could be seen sitting in front of a wall, looking into a hole in it. The video then transitions to the viral clip, implying that this was the same child and that she wasn't trapped under rubble at all. This doesn't showcase a Palestinian child trapped under rubble. More videos, uploaded by the same person showcase the girl was not under rubble but looking through a hole in the wall. Additionally, nothing on the account indicates the origin of the mother and child. Example: https://t.co/UoWrlNBLG6 pic.twitter.com/K8AuzH2MkA — Tal Hagin (@talhagin) October 28, 2024
This doesn't showcase a Palestinian child trapped under rubble. More videos, uploaded by the same person showcase the girl was not under rubble but looking through a hole in the wall. Additionally, nothing on the account indicates the origin of the mother and child. Example: https://t.co/UoWrlNBLG6 pic.twitter.com/K8AuzH2MkA — Tal Hagin (@talhagin) October 28, 2024
We also found a video which featured the watermark from a TikTok account "userftdvvrl92i". We checked the account and found the viral video was uploaded to it on October 26, 2024.Â
We also found several other videos of the same child which showed her looking through the hole in the wall. One video also showed the child on the other side of the wall, where she could be seen playing. Screenshots of various TikTok posts can be seen below.
We found that the TikTok account addressed the video going viral as a Palestinian child trapped under rubble. They assured people of the wellbeing of the child in the caption of another video, similar to the viral one. The caption in Arabic also mentioned that the child is not from Gaza, but from Syria. The TikTok user also requested people not to repost videos of the child.
It is thus clear that a video of a Syrian child playing is being shared as a Palestinian child trapped under rubble. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Oct 28, 2024 21:10 IST

title: Fact Check: Was the German foreign minister not formally welcomed at Delhi Airport?
content:
This video shows Baerbock's visit to Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in January 2024.
German Chancellor Olaf Scholz visited India from October 24 to 26. He was accompanied by Germany's Minister for Foreign Affairs, Annalena Baerbock, along with several officials. During this visit, Scholz and Prime Minister Narendra Modi engaged in extensive discussions about strengthening strategic ties across various key areas.
A video now going viral on social media shows Annalena Baerbock disembarking from a plane. After stepping off the plane, she is heard saying something to the security guards. Some Facebook users shared this video and wrote "German Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock appeared surprised when she arrived in India to find no formal welcome on the tarmac." Others, however, claimed this video was from China.
India Today Fact Check found that this video is not of Annalena Baerbock's visit to India or China. It was shot at Kuala Lumpur Airport in Malaysia on January 12.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video directed us to the same clip shared by an X account on October 28. It mentioned that the clip was from China. However, Community Notes on the post stated that the video was actually filmed in Malaysia in January of this year.
Based on the above information, a subsequent search led us to a video shared by the German Foreign Ministry's official X account for Southeast Asia on January 19. The post said: "A visit to partners – enjoy the video recap of Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock's visit to Southeast Asia." A visit to partners – enjoy the video recap of Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock's visit to #SoutheastAsia . 🤔 What were the topics & who did she meet? ▶️ Watch to find out. pic.twitter.com/0zcTeEJ0uJ — GIC Southeast Asia (@GermanyInSEAsia) January 19, 2024 A detailed analysis of the first five seconds of the video reveals a direct match with the viral clip. Baerbock's clothing and the backdrop are identical in both videos, making it clear both were filmed in the same location and at the same time but from different angles. We also found a Deutsche Welle report  from January 16 that featured a photo of Annalena Baerbock, which matches the viral video. According to the report, on January 12, Baerbock arrived at the airport in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. In another report published by the Russian state-owned news agency RIA Novosti dated October 28, Sebastian Fischer, an official from the German Foreign Ministry, clarified that "a video circulating on social media, which claimed to show Annalena Baerbock's visit to India or China, is misleading. In reality, the video was filmed in Malaysia in January of this year, when the plane was incorrectly parked due to a misunderstanding." It should be noted that when Baerbock visited India from October 24 to 26, Nityanand Rai, India's Minister of State for Home Affairs, welcomed the German delegation at New Delhi Airport. And according to a report published by Deutsche Welle on October 11, a trip to Beijing was in the books for Baerbock. However, we found no further reports about the details of this trip. advertisement Thus, it is evident that the viral video is not from Annalena Baerbock's visit to India or China but from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. (Written By Surajuddin Mondal) - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Oct 29, 2024 18:13 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video of Hezbollah fighters brandishing weapons VIRAL as recent
content:
This video is from a military exercise held by Hezbollah fighters in Lebanon on May 21, 2023.
On October 27, five Israeli soldiers were killed and 14 were wounded in a battle in southern Lebanon. Israel and the Lebanese paramilitary group Hezbollah have been exchanging fire since October 2023, but it was only in October this year that Israeli troops entered Lebanon's territory.Â
A video now going viral allegedly shows armed Hezbollah fighters cheerfully posing with weapons. Those sharing it claimed the video was recent. Sharing it on Facebook, one person wrote : "Hezbollah mood right now. Are u ok Israel."
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from a military exercise in Lebanon back in May 2023.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to Reddit and X posts from 2023 containing the viral clip. This made it clear that the video was at least a year old and not recent. These posts stated the video showed a military exercise by Hezbollah. The report, carrying a screenshot of the viral video, stated that Hezbollah conducted a military drill in South Lebanon on May 21, 2023. During this session, the group showed different equipment and weapons used by its fighters.
We then found several other news reports about this drill. According to them, Hezbollah conducted a military exercise in a camp at the southern Lebanese village of Aaramta on May 21, 2023, only 12 miles north of the Israeli border. Nearly 400 people attended the drill, including Hezbollah supporters and journalists. 🎥 Des centaines de journalistes ont assisté dimanche à Aaramta, petit village au #Liban -Sud, à une simulation d'attaque par les miliciens du #Hezbollah . According to an Associated Press report the exercise came ahead of "Liberation Day", the annual celebration of the withdrawal of Israeli forces from south Lebanon on May 25, 2000. The manoeuvre included a simulation of the fighters' incursion into Israel by blowing up the separation wall. Â
Al Jazeera's report noted that about 200 Hezbollah fighters took part in this exercise, and carried out simulated raids using snipers, drones, anti-aircraft weapons, rocket launchers, rocket-propelled grenades, and other heavy and light arms.Â

title: Fact Check: Don't fall for Diwali offers selling iPhones for Rs 99! It's a scam
content:
This is a scam. These websites are just collecting your personal data.
Diwali offers keep getting wilder and wilder every year. But if you see an iPhone 13 or Samsung S23 being sold for just Rs 99, or an Oppo smartphone being sold for just Rs 9, you need to pause and tell yourself, "This cannot be real!"
And you would be right to do that. Because this is the tale of a scam that offers just that.Â
According to these posts going viral, all you need to do to avail these offers is share the Instagram Reel with your friends and enter your personal details on a website named "digital712.com". Most people would recognise this as obvious fraud. But many, as evident from a number of people sharing their phone numbers in the comments of these posts, still seem to be falling for it.
India Today Fact Check looked into the websites being promoted through these reels and found that the people running them could have a Rajasthan connection. Let's look at how we got there.Â
In the Reels going viral, an AI-generated voice prompts you to visit the website digital712.com. This is also linked to the bios of the Instagram accounts sharing them.Â
On the website, you'll be asked to click on a link to get a free smartphone. You'll then be asked to choose from options like the iPhone 13, the Samsung S23, or the Vivo V27. Next, you'll be asked for whom you want to make this purchase.Â
The website also advertises free phone recharge offers. If you try to avail them, you're asked for personal details like your phone number. This is a common modus operandi for data harvesting scams.Â
If you try to buy a smartphone or avail the recharge offers through digital712.com , you'll gradually be redirected to two different portals: earnwithfaith.in  and go.sapost.co.in . The actual websites are not linked here, only their archives. All three have a similar look and feel and feature articles focussing on money-making tricks, government schemes, and offers.Â
It's worth noting that after you enter your personal details in an attempt to buy these heavily discounted smartphones, the page simply refreshes. There is no actual way to buy the phones advertised there. This is just a data harvesting scam.Â
In the " About us " section of digital712.com, we found an email address. Saving this address to Outlook led us to the LinkedIn account connected to it. This person's LinkedIn bio claimed he was a teacher in Bikaner, Rajasthan.Â
We looked up the school listed on LinkedIn and contacted its owner. They confirmed to India Today Fact Check that the name given on the LinkedIn account was indeed a member of the faculty there. Through the school's owner, we reached the teacher in question.Â
He denied any link with these websites, the email listed in the "About us" section, or the LinkedIn account linked to this email. We asked him to send us the link to his original LinkedIn account. While he initially agreed to do so, he later said that he deleted the account — allegedly because it wasn't helping him find work. Interestingly, when we checked after speaking to him, the LinkedIn account we had discovered had been deleted.Â
In the " About us " section of the website earnwithfaith.in, we found another email. When we searched for this email on Google, we found Facebook, Instagram, and Snapchat accounts linked to it.  As per the information given on these accounts, the person operating them appeared to be a musician. Looking at his photographs, we felt that he could also be a minor. Hence, we are not revealing any information about him.Â
We also went through the pictures he shared on Snapchat and found that one of the images of a dolphin statue is from the Surpura Safari Park in Jodhpur.Â
Similarly, in another image, a Starbucks QR Code was visible. On scanning this code, we were led to the menu page of the Starbucks outlet at Jodhpur Park Plaza.Â
We noticed that one of the viral posts contained a phone number. When we searched for this phone number on Truecaller, it revealed the location as Rajasthan.Â
There is a whole network of Instagram pages promoting these scam websites. Some of these accounts are mobilemela_offers , paisa__kamao7 , and divya.tech . They even collaborate amongst themselves to promote such posts.
To sum up, a network of scam websites are trying to sell non-existent cheap smartphone deals to people to essentially harvest their data. - Ends Published By: Prateek Chakraborty Published On: Oct 29, 2024 21:46 IST

title: Fact Check: Diwali celebrations in Saudi Arabia? Here's what you need to know about this fireworks clip
content:
This video predates Diwali and likely shows a 2023 display in Riyadh.
As hundreds and thousands of spectacular fireworks videos flooded social media on Diwali, one purported to show how the festival of lights is celebrated in Saudi Arabia. In it, fireworks can be seen lighting up the sky behind several highrises. Men and burqa-clad women could be seen watching the display.Â
Sharing the video, an X user wrote , "Diwali celebration in Saudi Arabia. The Arab world is moving towards light from darkness." A Facebook user wrote : "Saudi Arabia witnesses Diwali celebrations, whereas liberal governments in India tend to curtail our festive traditions."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is old and does not show Diwali celebrations in Saudi Arabia in 2024.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to various Facebook pages and Instagram accounts featuring the same video. A Facebook page called Pak Qatar Community shared the clip on September 23 this year and wrote: "Saudi Arabia's 94th National Day." This made it evident that the video predates Diwali, which was celebrated on October 31 and November 1 this year.
Several other Instagram accounts and YouTube channels also shared the same video, claiming it to be from Saudi Arabia's National Day celebrations.
What is Saudi Arabia's National Day?
National Day in Saudi Arabia is celebrated on September 23 to commemorate the day in 1932 when King Abdulaziz Al Saud unified the different tribal areas into one country, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. This event was important for creating a shared national identity and government. It is a national holiday in the country.
Interestingly, during the course of our investigation, we found that the video is not from this year's National Day celebrations in Saudi Arabia. The same video was shared on another Instagram account on August 27 with the caption, "Welcome to Dubai." This means it could not have been from National Day celebrations in 2024.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by duba.i448 (@duba.i448)
A post shared by duba.i448 (@duba.i448)
We tried to find out whether any fireworks displays took place in Saudi Arabia on or before August of this year. We discovered that a similar celebration was held in Riyadh, the capital of Saudi Arabia, after the country had won hosting rights to Expo 2030 in November 2023.
Using Arabic keywords, we found a video of fireworks and drone display that was live on November 29, 2023, on the official YouTube channel of the Royal Commission in Riyadh.
This video featured a large multi-storey building covered with green lights, which matched the viral video. Visuals similar to the viral video can be seen around the three-minute mark. This indicates that the viral video likely dates back to November 2023.
While we can not confirm the exact date of the video, it is clear that it is unrelated to this year's Diwali Celebrations in Saudi Arabia.
(Translated by Abhishek Pathak) - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Nov 1, 2024 21:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Hindus celebrating Diwali in Nagaland? This video of fireworks is from Argentina
content:
This video is not from Nagaland. It is from the Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires, Argentina.
Videos of firecrackers and fireworks on social media are ubiquitous around Diwali. One such video now being shared purports to show how the Hindu festival was celebrated in Nagaland, a majority Christian state. The video  shows thousands of people setting off firecrackers from their seats. It was shared with captions like: "Hindus of Nagaland celebrating Diwali".
Another such post  claimed this video was from Nagaland's Dimapur Stadium. #HappyDeepavali With love ❤️ from 📍Nagaland,Dimapur stadium 🏟️ #Deepavali2024 celebration pic.twitter.com/24xukoqBOD — Xplore_Nagaland (@Nagaland_India) October 31, 2024

India Today Fact Check, however, found that the video is not even from India. It is from Estadio Mâs Monumental or Monumental Stadium in Buenos Aires, Argentina. OUR PROBE
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip uploaded to a football-related YouTube channel named V-Red Baller  on October 30, a day before Diwali was celebrated in India this year.
The video was titled: "River Plate fans go CRAZY vs Atlético MG at El Monumental for the Copa Libertadores!" Club Atlético River Plate, commonly known as River Plate, is an Argentine football club based in the capital Buenos Aires.
A search with related keywords led us to an X post by an Argentine football news account, which featured a similar video from this stadium. It was captioned: "The Estadio Monumental, in Buenos Aires, was filled with fireworks ahead of the 2024 Copa Libertadores semi-final.  Brazil's Atletico Mineiro drew 0-0 with River Plate to reach the final for just the second time." HOW DID NAGALAND CELEBRATE DIWALI? Though not on a large scale as portrayed, reports from India Today  and Nagaland Post  suggested that the skies were lit with fireworks on the evening of October 31, amidst a ban issued by the administration against the crackers. Governor La Ganesan also celebrated from Kohima Raj Bhavan and Chief Minister Neiphiu Rio wished people Diwali. Warm Diwali greetings to all who are celebrating. title: Fact Check: 2021 earthquake video shared as recent and linked to Iran's alleged nuke tests
content:
The viral video of the earthquake is old and has been online since November 2021.
A 4.8-magnitude earthquake struck Iran's Semnan province on November 3 as Israel braces for another Iranian attack. Amid this, a video going viral shows trucks parked on the road shaking during an earthquake in a deserted area.Â
Those sharing the video linked it to Iran's alleged nuclear tests. An X user wrote , "Just in: Earthquakes in Iran as trucks shake on the side of the road and dust rises from the mountains. Nuke tests?" Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is old and has been online since November 2021.
A reverse image search led us to a November 2021 CNN report containing the viral video's screengrab. As per the report , an earthquake of magnitude 6.3 shook Iran on November 14, 2021. This proves that the viral video is not recent.
We also found a TRT WorldNow video report dated November 14, 2021, that shows the moment when a powerful earthquake struck southern Iran, near the port of Bandar Abbas. The quake, measuring a magnitude of 6.5, prompted residents to flee their homes.
At least 27 people were injured and one died in this earthquake. Then-Iranian president Ebrahim Raisi reportedly ordered local authorities to focus on rescue and relief operations.Â
On November 1, news organisations quoted Kamal Kharrazi , an adviser to Iran's supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, saying that Iran can produce nuclear weapons and is prepared to change its policies on using them. Back in October, several media reports noted there were speculations about Iran conducting covert nuclear tests after a moderate earthquake  struck both Iran and Israel on the evening of October 5.Â
Thus, it is clear that a 2021 earthquake video is being linked to recent tremors in Iran.
(Written by Ashish Kumar) - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Nov 5, 2024 15:39 IST

title: Fact Check: Illegal voting in US elections? No, this video is from 2022!
content:
This video from October 2022 shows a routine electoral process in Arizona's Maricopa County.
Republicans have clinched control of the Senate and trends project Donald Trump leading in the Presidential race , as counting is underway after a full day of voting on November 5.Â
A video  allegedly showing people rigging voting machines in Pennsylvania is going viral on social media. It is noteworthy that voting hours were extended in Pennsylvania's Cambria County after a software malfunction impacted the voting machines.
Sharing the clip, one person wrote : "Breaking: Five Trump-leaning counties in Pennsylvania are experiencing Maricopa County. Widespread machine failures. This time ES&S and MicroVote partnering up with Dominion Rigging Systems."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video has no links to the US Presidential elections. It is from 2022 and shows a routine electoral process in Arizona's Maricopa County.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to the same video shared in an X post in 2023. The caption stated the video showed evidence of Maricopa officials tampering with the memory cards of voting machines. Maricopa is a county in the American state of Arizona. The date stamp, clearly visible in the bottom-right corner of this video, reads October 14, 2022.
Further searches led us to multiple news reports about this video. According to these reports , the viral video showed election workers in Maricopa installing new memory cards in the machines. The reports further stated that the clip was shot days before the US Midterm elections held on November 8, 2022, and showed a routine procedure, which happens every election.
Maricopa County also shared a screenshot of the viral clip on its official X account on May 31, 2023. It stated the video showed workers installing new memory cards containing the certified Election Program in the tabulators, adding that this routine process was live-streamed by the County's Ballot Tabulation Centre itself. Have you seen this viral video? The people sharing it are lying to you. So here we go, defusing a new election 'bombshell' that's a lot like the old 'bombshells.'🧵 pic.twitter.com/7Lv8XuKBMA — Maricopa County (@maricopacounty) May 30, 2023
Have you seen this viral video? The people sharing it are lying to you. So here we go, defusing a new election 'bombshell' that's a lot like the old 'bombshells.'🧵 pic.twitter.com/7Lv8XuKBMA — Maricopa County (@maricopacounty) May 30, 2023
Back in 2022, Republican gubernatorial candidate Kari Lake sued Arizona elections officials after she lost to Governor-Elect Katie Hobbs. The viral video was part of this lawsuit as well. Courts subsequently dismissed Lake's claims of election fraud by Maricopa County officials . Claim: "Maricopa County did secret testing of tabulation equipment. Just look at this video!" Facts: If it was a secret, why did we livestream it? That's the opposite of secret. People interested in the facts can find those in our May 10 court filing. Excerpt below: pic.twitter.com/Kwo35exdEk — Maricopa County (@maricopacounty) May 30, 2023
Claim: "Maricopa County did secret testing of tabulation equipment. Just look at this video!" Facts: If it was a secret, why did we livestream it? That's the opposite of secret. People interested in the facts can find those in our May 10 court filing. Excerpt below: pic.twitter.com/Kwo35exdEk — Maricopa County (@maricopacounty) May 30, 2023
It's noteworthy that amid the ongoing Presidential polls in the US, Donald Trump also alleged voter fraud was happening in Pennsylvania. However, election officials rejected this claim of illegal voters  and massive cheating .Â
It is thus clear a 2022 video was falsely shared to allege illegal voting in the 2024 US Presidential elections. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Nov 6, 2024 18:12 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of pro-Hindu sloganeering in residential society is NOT from Maharashtra
content:
This video has nothing to do with Maharashtra. It's from Uttar Pradesh's Kanpur and dates back to February 2022.
Ahead of the Maharashtra Assembly elections slated for November 20, a video showing a group of men at a residential society holding saffron flags and sloganeering in support of Lord Ram and Hindus was widely shared on social media. Residents standing on the balconies of their flats could also be seen supporting the men standing below.Â
Allegedly, this was from Maharashtra. One post featuring the clip said, "Finally, Hindus are awakening. Visuals from Maharashtra". Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the video had nothing to do with the Maharashtra elections. It's from Uttar Pradesh's Kanpur and dates back to February 2022.Â
We reverse-searched keyframes from the video and found that it was first shared on social media in February 2022. Posts from that time equated it to elections.
Using relevant keywords, we found a Facebook post that claimed this clip showed a "Prabhat Pheri" or a morning religious procession carried out by Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh workers in multiple residential societies in Uttar Pradesh's Kanpur. The names of the societies were also listed in another post.Â
We checked the photos of these societies available on Google Maps . While comparing them with the viral video, we found that it was a society named Diviniti Homes, located in the Kalyanpur locality of Kanpur.Â
India Today reached out to the secretary of Diviniti Homes. He confirmed that the video was from his society and was shot when some RSS workers arrived there before the Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh that spanned from February 10 to March 7, 2022, in seven phases. Polls in Kanpur took place on February 20, 2022.Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral clip has nothing to do with the upcoming Assembly elections in Maharashtra. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Nov 6, 2024 20:46 IST

title: Is this a Melania Trump body double? Conspiracy theory resurfaces amid US elections
content:
Donald Trump's stunning victory in the 2024 US presidential elections has had at least one unforeseen consequence. The resurgence of an old — and wild — conspiracy theory: the Melania Trump we see accompanying the president-elect is allegedly a body double! Yes, you did not read that wrong.Â
A photo of Donald and his wife Melania, sporting a pair of dark sunglasses, voting at the Morton and Barbara Mandel Recreation Center in Palm Beach, Florida, on November 5, was widely shared with this ludicrous claim. Similar photos and videos from the polling booth have been published by many American news agencies. One such photo shot by photojournalist Chip Somodevilla can be seen on the website of Getty Images as well.Â
Some went so far as to even compare the sunglassed Melania seen in these photos with photos of the "real" Melania. The so-called real Melania Trump's photos were from Donald Trump's closing rally at Madison Square Garden in New York. Photos and videos from the event make that clear. That is fake Melania. Pictured is Melania at MSG compared to today. Bone structure is not even close. pic.twitter.com/jiip1wp6Mt — Silvano (@Silvano29360) November 5, 2024
That is fake Melania. Pictured is Melania at MSG compared to today. Bone structure is not even close. pic.twitter.com/jiip1wp6Mt — Silvano (@Silvano29360) November 5, 2024
It doesn't bear mentioning, but let's do it anyway: there is no Melania Trump body double hanging out with the president-elect. A Snopes report notes that "in-person voters in Florida bring identification, or sign an affidavit of identity, or vote on a provisional ballot if they don't have identification. Anyone pretending to be Melania at the polling station would be in violation of election rules."Â
So, why are some people claiming otherwise? To get to the bottom of this, one has to look at where the conspiracy theory emerged from.
One of the earliest mentions of this outlandish claim was in a BBC report from October 19, 2017, titled, "Is Donald Trump using a fake Melania? Conspiracy theories flood social media." This report detailed how footage of Melania Trump in sunglasses next to her husband has got many wondering if a body double was being used. This was exacerbated by Trump, who said while speaking on the White House lawn, "My wife Melania, who happens to be right here."
According to a Vox explainer about the conspiracy theory from around the time, a man named Joe Vargas posted that the "Melania Trump" who appeared at the event was not the real first lady, but an impostor lookalike. This post was reportedly retweeted over 60,000 times.Â
Why did this theory get popular?
Why does any conspiracy theory get popular? The US has been a hotbed for ridiculous conspiracy theories for some time now. Even a decade ago, researchers found that about half of all Americans believed in some conspiracy or other.Â
According to a paper in the European Journal of Social Psychology , "a small part in motivating the endorsement of such seemingly irrational beliefs is the desire to stick out from the crowd, the need for uniqueness." Basically, people like to be seen in possession of obscure knowledge. According to another University of Nottingham paper, "People are attracted to conspiracy theories in an attempt to satisfy three psychological needs. They want more certainty, to feel in control, and maintain a positive image of their self and group."
Add these to a general mistrust in what is somewhat derogatorily called "the mainstream media" and an existing conspiracy/wish-fulfilment theory from the era — that Melania Trump actually hates Donald Trump — and you get a compelling narrative. That Melania does not want to accompany her husband to events and, therefore, the establishment had to create a body double to maintain the "illusion" of a happy marriage. Just look no further than this old HuffPost report that screams: "Melania Trump has a really hard time holding her husband's hand. Don't believe it? Here's the proof."
As Vox notes, "It's a theory that may say more about what we're willing to project on Melania Trump than anything she's ever done."
So there's no Melania body double?
No. Or at least, no one can really say so with any authority other than the Trumps, the White House, and maybe some national security personnel in the US.  - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Nov 6, 2024 21:43 IST

title: Fact Check: No 'Modi-Modi' chants during Trump's victory speech
content:
The crowd was chanting 'Bobby-Bobby' about Trump's ally Robert F Kennedy Junior. There were no 'Modi' chants.
Following Donald Trump's landslide victory in the US presidential elections, a video went viral on social media allegedly showing the crowd chanting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's name as Trump delivered his victory speech. Â
The video begins with Trump saying, "Make America healthy again," following which the crowd can be heard chanting someone's name. Responding to these cheers, Trump says, "I know he's a great guy and he really means it. He wants to do some things and we're gonna let him go do it." Allegedly this was about Modi.
India Today Fact Check found that the crowd was cheering for Trump's ally, Robert F Kennedy Junior. There were no "Modi" chants. Â
The full video of Donald Trump's victory speech was shared by all major American news channels. In the Fox News YouTube video of the speech, the viral clip can be seen at the 19-minute-37-second mark.Â
Looking at the whole video, it becomes clear that Trump was talking about Robert F Kennedy Junior, popularly known as RFK Jr. The crowd was actually chanting his nickname "Bobby", which can sound like "Modi".Â
In the video, Trump said, "There are fantastic people and we can add a few names like Robert F Kennedy Junior, he came in. And he's going to help make America healthy again." Right after that, the crowd chanted "Bobby-Bobby".Â
After that, Trump added, "I know he's a great guy and he really means it. He wants to do some things and we're gonna let him go do it. I just said but Bobby, leave the oil to me. We have more liquid gold, oil and gas. We have more liquid gold than any country in the world. More than Saudi Arabia, we have more than Russia. Bobby, stay away from the liquid gold. Other than that, go, have a good time, Bobby."  Â
During the speech, not even once did the crowd chant Prime Minister Narendra Modi's name. Trump, too, didn't mention Modi.Â
There are several news reports mentioning Trump's shoutout to Robert F. Kennedy Junior during his victory speech. Â
India Today's Washington DC correspondent Rohit Sharma also confirmed that there were no "Modi-Modi" chants during Trump's victory speech.Â
RFK Jr. initially contested as an independent candidate in the presidential elections. However, he later dropped out of the race and endorsed Donald Trump.Â
As per reports , Trump has hinted that he might make Kennedy in-charge of the US public health agencies. This has been a point of controversy as Kennedy is known to be an anti-vaccine activist and a conspiracy theorist.Â
It is thus clear that the viral video does not show PM Modi's name being chanted by the audience during Donald Trump's victory speech. - Ends Published By: Rishabh Sharma Published On: Nov 6, 2024 23:00 IST

title: Fact Check: This video of Trump promising to get Imran Khan out of jail is a DEEPFAKE
content:
This video is a deepfake, made using a 2017 video interview of Trump with NBC News.
Following his presidential victory, Donald Trump delivered a speech in Florida, thanking people for a powerful mandate and assuring his supporters he would fulfil his poll promises. But did these promises include getting the former Prime Minister of Pakistan, Imran Khan, out of jail and back to power? A video of Trump's alleged promise to Khan's supporters is currently viral on social media.Â
In the clip , Trump can be heard saying, "Hello my Pakistani American friends, I promise if I win I will try my best to get Imran Khan out of jail as soon as possible. He is my friend. I love him. I will support him to take over the government again and rock and we will work together to make our ties stronger."Â
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video is a deepfake. It was made using a 2017 video interview of Trump with NBC News anchor Lester Holt.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to an NBC News video report , dated March 12, 2017. In it, NBC News anchor Lester Holt interviewed Donald Trump about his decision to fire former FBI director James Comey.Â
According to the Trump administration, Comey was fired over his handling of the investigation into Hillary Clinton's emails. The Democratic Party, however, alleged that the former FBI director was fired because the agency was investigating alleged links between the Trump campaign and Russia.
In the NBC interview, the movement of Trump's eyelids and lips match the viral clip around the 12-minute-30-second mark. In the original video, Trump was then speaking about his meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov, one day after firing Comey. A comparison between the two clips can be seen below.
While reverse-searching keyframes from the video, we found multiple clips of Trump, in the same attire and background, shared before the US Presidential elections. In one such video , Trump made sensational confessions about the January 6, 2021, United States Capitol attack and his assassination attempt. Its caption mentioned that the video was made using AI.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Imran Khan (@dustyloads)
A post shared by Imran Khan (@dustyloads)
Another such video was uploaded to YouTube in March 2024. In this clip as well, Trump's suit and the background match the viral clip, but this time he could be seen promoting a YouTube channel.Â
It is noteworthy that both videos contained a logo of Parrot AI, an AI Voice Generator that can generate deepfake videos of several celebrities and politicians.Â
We also used this tool to create a deepfake of Trump. The resulting clip showed Trump in the same attire and background, speaking the lines we fed into the tool. The video can be seen below.Â
It is thus, clear that a 2017 video of Trump's interview with NBC was used to create this deepfake video of Trump talking about Imran Khan. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 6, 2024 23:04 IST

title: Fact Check: Old Nancy Pelosi video about Roe v Wade VIRAL as her reaction to Trump victory
content:
This video is from June 24, 2022, unrelated to Donald Trump's victory.
Defying pollsters' predictions, Donald Trump is all set to return to the White House after defeating Kamala Harris in the US Presidential elections.
In its aftermath, a video of former House Speaker and Democratic Party leader Nancy Pelosi was widely shared on social media, in which she can be heard saying, "There is no point in saying good morning because it certainly isn't." Allegedly, this was Pelosi's reaction to the Trump victory.
An X user wrote , "Communist Congresswoman Nancy Pelosi this morning after Donald Trump's victory: 'There's no point in saying good morning because it certainly isn't.' Pelosi seemed to have swollen eyes from crying so much over Donald Trump's victory." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from June 24, 2022, and therefore unrelated to Donald Trump's victory.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to the same video shared on X on June 24, 2022. This proves that the video is old and is not from the 2024 elections' aftermath. NANCY PELOSI: "No point in saying 'good morning,' because it certainly is not one." #LifeWins pic.twitter.com/ljlHEeNM0i — RNC Research (@RNCResearch) June 24, 2022
NANCY PELOSI: "No point in saying 'good morning,' because it certainly is not one." #LifeWins pic.twitter.com/ljlHEeNM0i — RNC Research (@RNCResearch) June 24, 2022
A further keyword search led us to an ABC News video report that contained this video. As per the report, Nancy Pelosi said this in a press conference in the wake of the Supreme Court's ruling overturning Roe versus Wade in June 2022, holding that there was no longer a federal constitutional right to an abortion.Â
In a minute-long video, Pelosi said that the Supreme Court was eviscerating Americans' rights and endangering their health and safety, assuring that Congress would continue to act to overcome this extremism and protect the American people. She said: "Today the Republican-controlled Supreme Court has achieved its dark, extreme goal of ripping away a woman's right to make their own reproductive health decisions."
We found several news reports published in June 2022 stating how Pelosi attacked the Supreme Court's ruling overturning Roe versus Wade, a landmark 1973 US Supreme Court decision that ruled the Constitution of the United States protected the right to have an abortion.
Thus, it's clear that an old video of Nancy Pelosi was falsely shared as recent linking it to Trump's victory.
