title: Fact Check: Are Waqf Board properties in India LARGER than the whole of Pakistan?
content:
The total area of Waqf Board properties in India is not 9.40 lakh sqkm. Rather, it is 9.4 lakh acres, which is 231 times smaller than the total area of Pakistan.
Ahead of the upcoming round of Joint Parliamentary Committee meetings regarding the Waqf Amendment Bill scheduled to begin on November 9, a post about the total assets of the Waqf Board in India has gone viral on social media.
It claims that the property of the Waqf Board is significantly larger than the area of Pakistan. Some Facebook users shared a postcard  stating, "The area of Pakistan is 8.81 lakh square kilometres. The area of the Waqf Board is 9.40 lakh square kilometres. One Pakistan was created outside, and one was created inside. Keep sleeping. This is the amazing work of Congress."
India Today Fact Check found that the total area of Waqf Board properties in India is not 9.40 lakh square kilometres. It's actually 9.4 lakh acres, which is approximately 3,804 square kilometres. In contrast, Pakistan's total area is 8,81,913 square kilometres, making it over 231 times larger than the area controlled by Waqf Boards in India.Â
A keyword search led us to the same postcard shared by an X account on November 5. In response to the post, another person claimed, "Size of Pakistan is 8.8 Lakh Square Km. While Size of Waqf board is 8.8 Lakh Acre (not km)." Size of Pakistan is 8.8 Lakh Square Km While Size of Waqf board is 8.8 Lakh Acre(not km) Waqf land is 60-70 times smaller than Pakistan. That too those lands where donated by rich muslims as a trust. Waqf didn't took any land from Hindu religion
— Youth Against Hate (@YouthAgnstHate) November 5, 2024 A further investigation led to a report published by The Economic Times on August 8 that stated the Waqf Board is allegedly the third-largest landholder in India, after the Railways and the Defence Department. It oversees 8,70,000 properties covering an area of 9,40,000 acres across the country, with an estimated total value of Rs 1.2 lakh crore. We came across a report titled " Explainer on Waqf Amendment Bill 2024 " published on the official website of the Press Information Bureau on September 13. Point 6 of the report, issued by the Ministry of Minority Affairs, states, "Wakf Boards currently control 8.7 lakh properties spanning 9.4 lakh acres across India with an estimated value of 1.2 lakh crores. India has the largest waqf holding in the World. Further, Waqf Board is the largest landowner in India after the Armed Forces and the Indian Railways." The 9.4 lakh acre property is approximately 3,804 square kilometres. In comparison, Pakistan's total area ( https://pakconsulatela.org/about-pakistan/ ) is 8,81,913 square kilometres, which means it is over 231 times larger than the total area managed by Waqf Boards in India. India Today also reached out to Mohd. Ali Khan , the former chairman of the Development Committee of the Central Waqf Council and a former Rajya Sabha MP. He stated that the claim suggesting the total assets of the Waqf Board in India exceed the total area of Pakistan is completely unfounded. advertisement He added that the total assets of the Waqf Board in India have already been published by the Ministry of Minority Affairs and that information is accurate. Zufar Ahmad Faruqi , the chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Sunni Central Waqf Board, corroborated this. Thus, it is evident that the area of Waqf Board properties in India is not 9.40 lakh square kilometres; rather, it is 9.4 lakh acres, which is 231 times smaller than Pakistan's total area. (Written by Surajuddin Mondal) - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Nov 8, 2024 15:23 IST

title: Fact Check: Did this Maharashtra MLA call Yogi Adityanath a 'rakshas'? Here are the facts
content:
Not Yogi Adityanath, her jibe was aimed at the BJP candidate for the Mira-Bhayandar constituency, Narendra Mehta.
Ahead of Assembly polls in Maharashtra, a video of MLA Geeta Jain, an independent candidate from the Mira-Bhayandar seat, allegedly criticising Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has gone viral. In this video, she can be heard calling someone a "rakshas" or demon.
"A monster. You see this city's atmosphere today, it's full of fear of returning to the five years after 2014. He has spread this fear of "batoge, katoge" (get divided, get slain). A demon has spread its dark magic, and I am here to break it," Jain said in the video.
Many linked this criticism to Yogi Adityanath, who had recently coined the phrase " batoge to katoge " during the Bangladesh unrest a few months ago and is now campaigning in Maharashtra.
Posts featuring the video claimed, "Meet Geeta Jain, MLA from Thane, Maharashtra. She is famous for her Anti-Muslim statements & Fear mongering. She wanted ticket from BJP but got rejected at last moment. Now she is calling Yogi Adityanath as Rakshas & condemning his statements which she used to appreciate before." Meet Geeta Jain, MLA from Thane, Maharashtra She is famous for her Anti Muslim statements & Fear mongering. She wanted ticket from BJP but got rejected at last moment Now she is calling Yogi Adityanath as Rakshas & condemning his statements which she used to appreciate before… pic.twitter.com/0qldg9BT35 — Veena Jain (@DrJain21) November 6, 2024 India Today Fact Check found that Geeta Jain did not refer to Yogi Adityanath as a 'Rakshas.' Instead, her remark was about a former MLA and the Bharatiya Janata Party candidate from the constituency, Narendra Mehta.
Meet Geeta Jain, MLA from Thane, Maharashtra She is famous for her Anti Muslim statements & Fear mongering. She wanted ticket from BJP but got rejected at last moment Now she is calling Yogi Adityanath as Rakshas & condemning his statements which she used to appreciate before… pic.twitter.com/0qldg9BT35 — Veena Jain (@DrJain21) November 6, 2024
India Today Fact Check found that Geeta Jain did not refer to Yogi Adityanath as a 'Rakshas.' Instead, her remark was about a former MLA and the Bharatiya Janata Party candidate from the constituency, Narendra Mehta.
Reverse-searching keyframes of the viral video led to an extended version of the statement and a detailed video report uploaded by a Facebook page called YSR News . In this video, Geeta Jain did not mention Yogi Adityanath. The caption and the voice-over explained that her remarks were directed at Narendra Mehta.
Responding to the "rakshas" jibe, Mehta later said that Geeta Jain was "out of her mind".
Narendra Mehta, the BJP candidate from the Mira-Bhayandar constituency, won this seat in 2014. But in the 2019 Assembly polls, Geeta Jain defeated him as an independent candidate.Â
Reportedly, she was aligned with the BJP and was all set to join the saffron camp. However, after her expectations were not met, she joined the Shiv Sena under Eknath Shinde's leadership.
In June 2022, amid Maharashtra's political turmoil, Jain switched sides and joined the BJP. However, after being denied a ticket  for the Mira-Bhayandar seat, she decided to contest independently once again. She launched her campaign on November 6, targeting her political opponent, Narendra Mehta.
When India Today Fact Check reached out to Jain, she said, "I have never uttered a word against Yogi Adityanath. I did not even mention Uttar Pradesh. I consider Yogi Adityanath to be an ideal man, and I try to follow his path. Narendra Mehta, accused of heinous crimes, has been using Yogi Ji's words to spread fear in the area. That is why I called him a rakshas."
Thus, it's clear that Geeta Jain was not attacking Yogi Adityanath and calling him a "rakshas". Her jibe was directed towards the BJP's Narendra Mehta. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Nov 8, 2024 16:57 IST

title: Fact Check: UP Police thrashed man for teasing cow? This is a mocktail of three different stories
content:
The video and photo of the police action is from old incidents from 2022 and 2023. They have no links to the viral video of a man mocking a cow.
Did a Muslim man in Uttar Pradesh get beaten up by the police for mocking a cow? A video making the rounds on social media shows a man sitting inside a car, telling a cow on the road: "Eid hai, bach ke. Eid hai, Eid. As-salamu alaykum (Be safe, it's Eid)."Â
The video then shows a photo of a man sitting in front of a police officer. It simultaneously shows a clip of a man being held by police, having trouble walking. The latter could be seen saying, "Gai humari mata hai (Cow is our mother)," repeatedly in pain.
A person shared the clip on Facebook writing, "Abdul Bhai forgot that he is in Uttar Pradesh." Some people, replying to one such post, condemned such action by police merely for making a joke.
India Today Fact Check found that the photo and video of the police action are unrelated to the viral clip of the man mocking the cow. In fact, even the photo and the video are from two separate cases.Â
In one such viral post on Instagram , we noticed people commenting  that the young man in the viral video was not Muslim, but Hindu. They added that he later deleted this video and apologised for this act of mocking a cow. Others added that his name was Nakul .
Further searches led us to an Instagram post from September 19 this year. The caption of the video asked users to share the clip, seeking police action.Â
This video contained a screenshot of an Instagram account that originally shared the cow mocking video in question. It belonged to a man named Nakul, and the username was "@n___nakul_". The account has been deleted now .
We did not find any news reports about the arrest of this man for mocking a cow. The police did not comment on the matter when we reached out.
Reverse searching the photo of the man and the cop led us to multiple news reports  about this incident dated July 1, 2023. According to them, police filed a case against nine people for throwing pieces of flesh near a Hanuman Temple on the Gurugram-Faridabad road.Â
The reports carried a photo of the two rag pickers, Obirul and Nadeem, arrested by the police in this case. The picture seen in the viral video of a man and a cop is a cropped version of the same.Â
Reverse searching keyframes from the video of the man saying "Gai humari mata hai" led us to news reports in AajTak and News18 . These reports from October 28, 2022, stated that Irshad alias Sonu was arrested by the Ghaziabad police for smuggling cows. During the arrest, police reportedly shot at him when he tried to flee. He was then filmed chanting "Gai humari mata hai" repeatedly after getting shot.
It is thus clear that police action in old cases from 2022 and 2023 was falsely linked to a video of a man mocking a cow and was shared with a communal spin. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Nov 8, 2024 19:10 IST

title: Fact Check: 2023 video FALSELY viral as recent attacks on Israeli soccer fans in Amsterdam
content:
This video is from 2023 and has nothing to do with the recent attack on Israeli football fans in Amsterdam.
Israeli soccer fans were attacked in Amsterdam, Netherlands, on November 7, after a Europa League football match between their team Maccabi Tel Aviv and Ajax. The latter won the match 5-0. Shocking video viral on social media shows Israeli fans being beaten up late at night. Reportedly, "Free Palestine" shouts were heard from the assailants.
Among the many videos allegedly documenting the violence, one that was widely shared shows a young man being repeatedly kicked by a mob at a train station. The young man trying to stagger away ultimately falls on the train's tracks.Â
Sharing this clip , an X user wrote, "Today they are attacking Jews in Amsterdam, tomorrow they will attack you inside your own country. Better unite and stand against radical Islamic terrorism." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from 2023 and has nothing to do with the recent attack on Israeli football fans in Amsterdam. OUR PROBE
Responding to the viral post, many people claimed that this incident was old . A reverse image search led us to several news reports containing the viral video's screengrabs published in May 2023.Â
As per Het Parool , an Amsterdam-based daily, a man was assaulted by a group of people after allegedly kissing an underage boy without his consent.Â
The assault took place on the evening of May 5, 2023, at Amsterdam's Bijlmer Arena station. The report said the police arrested seven minors suspected in this case. At least three suspects in a statement said a drunk white man kissed a minor boy without his consent, after which they attacked him.
According to another Dutch news report published on May 6, 2023, about 10 people were involved in the attack. We also found the same video shared on X in a post  dated May 6, 2023. WHAT HAPPENED IN AMSTERDAM ON NOVEMBER 7?
The New York Times reported that the police in Amsterdam said in a statement they had begun an investigation into multiple outbreaks of violence and 62 people had been arrested. Most of those arrested were later released. The clashes reportedly took place in several places where people had gathered, some in support of the Israeli team and others to protest its arrival. Five Israelis were hospitalised and later discharged, Amsterdam authorities said. Some others sustained light injuries.
The Times also reported that video footage from Amsterdam showed a group of men trying to take down a Palestinian flag from a building in central Amsterdam while shouting anti-Arab slogans. The Daily Mail reported the same.Â
Hendrikus Wilhelmus Maria Schoof, the Dutch prime minister, called the incidents "completely unacceptable" antisemitic attacks on Israelis in Amsterdam.Â
Thus, it's clear that a 2023 video is being falsely shared as footage of recent attacks on Israeli football fans in Amsterdam.
(Written by Ashish Kumar) - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Nov 8, 2024 21:19 IST

title: Fact check: Communal twist FALSELY added to video of villagers beating up cops in Bihar
content:
This is a recent video from Bihar's Motihari. But the cops were attacked by family and friends of the accused, who are Hindus, not Muslims.
A video  reportedly from Bihar's Motihari district showing a group of people beating a police squad with batons has gone viral. Those sharing the clip claimed Muslims attacked cops when they tried to arrest a person accused of kidnapping.Â
One such post reads: "Just let the numbers increase, then see brotherhood. In Motihari, Bihar, the group of peaceful Molla community attacked the police team that had gone to arrest the kidnapping accused. Two policemen suffered serious head injuries. They tried to snatch the pistol also."
India Today Fact Check found that while the video is from Bihar's Motihari, the people who attacked the police were Hindus, not Muslims.Â
Upon reverse-searching the keyframes of the video, we found several news reports about the incident. According to a Hindustan Times report from November 1, the Motihari police were investigating the alleged abduction of two cousins in an area under the district's Paharpur police station.Â
The police reportedly rescued one of the girls from Bettiah, and based on her input, visited Sareya Lipani village to rescue the second girl. There, the police team was attacked by the family members of the accused, along with several others. One of the arrested accused named in the report was Anita Devi.Â
A Dainik Bhaskar report said the police arrested one accused in the village. This angered his family members, who then launched an attack on the officials. Two policemen were seriously injured in the assault.Â
The Motihari police also released a statement about the incident on November 1, naming Anita Devi and Shambhu Prasad as the accused. पुलिस पर हमला करने वालों के विरुद्ध कड़ी कार्रवाई.... . . @bihar_police #HainTaiyaarHum #Bihar #champaran #motihari pic.twitter.com/xh3y9jZLrz — MOTIHARI POLICE (@motihari_police) November 1, 2024
पुलिस पर हमला करने वालों के विरुद्ध कड़ी कार्रवाई.... . . @bihar_police #HainTaiyaarHum #Bihar #champaran #motihari pic.twitter.com/xh3y9jZLrz — MOTIHARI POLICE (@motihari_police) November 1, 2024
India Today Fact Check reached out to DSP Ranjan Kumar of Motihari. The officer told us that the villagers who attacked the police were not Muslim but from the Mahto community. He clarified that they were Hindu. As per Ranjan Kumar, the police arrested five people in the case and were on the lookout for other suspects.Â
This proves that there is no communal angle in this case. - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Nov 11, 2024 20:01 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show an Indian immigrant being arrested in Greece
content:
This 2023 video is from the Greek island of Kos. A Bangladeshi immigrant was arrested for the rape and murder of a 27-year-old woman.
A video that's been widely shared online purports to show an Indian immigrant being arrested in Greece for sexually assaulting a minor. Sharing the viral clip on X, one person wrote , "An Indian immigrant was arrested in Greece for sexually abusing a 9-year-old minor Christian girl."Â
India Today Fact Check found this 2023 video from the Greek island of Kos shows a Bangladeshi immigrant being arrested for the rape and murder of a 27-year-old woman. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story OUR PROBE Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to a Greek City Times report published on June 22, 2023. Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to a Greek City Times report published on June 22, 2023. According to it, the man seen in the viral clip was arrested for raping and murdering a 27-year-old Polish woman who worked in a hotel on the Greek island of Kos.
A subsequent search led us to several other news reports about the case. We did not find any mention of an Indian immigrant being involved in the crime. However, according to several reports, the man was identified as a Bangladeshi immigrant, 32-year-old Salauddin S.

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show Bangladeshi immigrants harassing Hindu bikers
content:
This video does not have a communal angle. The bikers, who are Muslim, were stopped by locals for speeding in West Bengal's Malda district.
A video that's been widely shared on social media purports to show Hindu bikers being stopped by "Illegal Bangladeshi Muslims" in West Bengal. In the clip, a group of people can be seen having a heated argument with a number of bikers.Â
Sharing the viral clip , an X user wrote, "The terror of Bangladeshi Muslims in rural Bengal. Got this video from one of my Bengali Hindu friends who were forcibly stopped on a highway and extorted by these illegal Bangladeshi Muslims."
India Today Fact Check found that the video does not have a communal angle. The bikers, who were Muslim, were stopped by locals for speeding and allegedly endangering lives in West Bengal's Malda district.
A reverse image search of keyframes of the viral clip led us to a longer version of the video uploaded to a YouTube channel called Pradhan Rider 0.1 in July 2024. The account regularly posts vlogs related to biking. The viral clip can be seen at around the 10-minute mark in the longer video .
The full clip provided context to the argument. The man stopping the bikers was scolding them in Bangla for riding speedily on the highway and endangering the locals' lives.Â
We reached out to the owner of the YouTube channel, Pradhan Rider 0.1. The channel is run by 19-year-old Abdul Sohail, who told India Today Fact Check: "This video was recorded in June and I uploaded it on July 4, 2024. This incident happened in Hobinagar in the Malda district. We were stopped by locals, and they started scolding us because we were speeding." He also said the video was recorded by him.
Sohail explained this was a new highway where bikers often go to race and perform stunts. He said the locals did not like bikers speeding there, so they stopped Sohail and his friends. He also claimed that the day before the incident, the locals got into a heated argument with other bikers as well.Â
Talking about the viral claim, Sohail said, "What is being said is not true, I am a Muslim and my fellow bikers were also Muslims. Their names are Masoom and Samim. The neighbourhood is also dominated by Muslims. They did not try to extort any money from us. They were just worried about their safety."
Sohail lives in Chanchal in Malda. His house is roughly seven kilometres away from the place of the incident. Sohail added that they still cross that tea shop whose owner stopped them.
It is thus clear that the video of an argument between Muslim bikers and locals in West Bengal's Malda district is being shared with false communal claims. - Ends Published By: Poorva Joshi Published On: Nov 12, 2024 19:58 IST

title: Fact Check: This Bangladeshi woman with blood on her face is NOT Hindu
content:
This is Kohinoor Akter, a Muslim woman who belongs to Sheikh Hasina's party Awami League. She was beaten up during a proposed protest rally in Dhaka on November 10.
It's been three months since the formation of the new interim government in Bangladesh. Yet, political violence persists in the country. Now, a video of a woman with blood all over her face being rescued by the police forces from a mob is being widely shared. बांग्लादेश हिंदुओं पर अत्याचार जारी है। एक महिला पर ये कैसी क्रूरता ! pic.twitter.com/ITye8mjEu0 — हम लोग We The People 🇮🇳 (@ajaychauhan41) November 12, 2024
बांग्लादेश हिंदुओं पर अत्याचार जारी है। एक महिला पर ये कैसी क्रूरता ! pic.twitter.com/ITye8mjEu0 — हम लोग We The People 🇮🇳 (@ajaychauhan41) November 12, 2024
Allegedly, the woman in the video was a Hindu.Â
One claim on Facebook read: "Horrific video is from Bangladesh, watch it with wide eyes. This woman had a big business in Bangladesh. She had Muslim tenants in her house. Yesterday the same radical called some other 35 radicals and took over her house and raped her. They didn't ask the caste before doing this. So think before lending your home on rent to kut piece. Secular Hindu are you awake?"
India Today Fact Check has found that the woman in this video is Muslim, and belongs to the Awami League, the party of Sheikh Hasina. OUR PROBEÂ
Reverse-searching key frames from the viral video led us to several YouTube videos featuring this clip. Many of these videos mention the woman was Kohinoor Begum, a member of the Bangladesh Krishak League, which is affiliated to Sheikh Hasina's Awami League.
We also found a different video of the same incident, dated November 11, which said this woman suspected of being an Awami League member was thrashed by a mob in Dhaka's Bangabandhu Avenue.
A subsequent search with related keywords led us to several news articles from November 10, published by BBC Bangla , Bangla News24 and Channel I . According to these reports, Sheikh Hasina's party, the Awami League, called for a protest rally against the present regime on Noor Hossain Day, November 10, in Bangladesh.
However, Awami League workers and leaders couldn't gather as members of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, the Awami League's main opposition, had assembled on the ground, armed. Reportedly, two women suspected of being Awami League supporters were attacked and handed over to the police. However, these reports did not reveal any names.
Further searches led us to a Facebook post featuring two images. The first was of the woman in the viral video and the second was of another man. The post said: "Strongly condemn the attack and arrest of Kohinoor Apa and Rashed Bhai, Bangladesh Krishak League Central Committee Member, we want unconditional release."
India Today Fact Check reached out to a close associate of the Awami League, who confirmed under the condition of anonymity that the woman in this video was Kohinoor Akter, a member of the central committee of the Bangladesh Krishak League. They also said Akter is Muslim. At the time of writing this report, she remained in police custody.
Tanvir Mahatab Abir, a fact-checker from Bangladesh, also confirmed the same. He also shared with us her Facebook profile . There, we found several posts announcing she would take part in the protest rally.
We also found two photos of Akter shared by her on August 2. Both featured an ID that confirmed her name, designation, and association with the Awami League.
Thus, it is beyond any doubt that the woman seen in this video was Muslim and this was not communal violence. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Nov 13, 2024 16:01 IST

title: Fact Check: Trump already cracking down on immigrants? No, this photo is old
content:
This image dates back to September 2022, when immigrants were sent from Texas to Chicago by the state's Republican governor.
Donald Trump's victory in the 2024 elections has led to widespread concerns about a stricter immigration policy in the US, with many undocumented immigrants fearing their future in the country. Amidst this, an image allegedly showing immigrants stepping off a bus was widely shared. Those sharing it claimed Trump's crackdown on immigrants had already begun. REPORT: Buses are stopping at NYC shelters multiple times per day picking up migrants.... and driving them to Canada, in advance of the Trump migration crackdown. We are not prepared for whats coming. pic.twitter.com/etFC9LcKMZ — Tablesalt 🇨🇦🇺🇸 (@Tablesalt13) November 12, 2024
REPORT: Buses are stopping at NYC shelters multiple times per day picking up migrants.... and driving them to Canada, in advance of the Trump migration crackdown. We are not prepared for whats coming. pic.twitter.com/etFC9LcKMZ — Tablesalt 🇨🇦🇺🇸 (@Tablesalt13) November 12, 2024
One such post read, "REPORT: Buses are stopping at NYC shelters multiple times per day picking up migrants and driving them to Canada, in advance of the Trump migration crackdown. We are not prepared for what's coming."
India Today Fact Check found that the photograph is more than two years old and from Chicago. Also, no drastic crackdown on immigrants has been reported yet.
Although Trump is currently President-elect, he will officially assume office as President of the United States on January 20, 2025, the day he will be sworn in. He can only implement decisions or policies of the new administration once he takes office. Therefore, he can't crack down on immigration right now.
Reverse-searching the image led to an article in Block Club Chicago , dated December 7, 2022. The photograph, taken at Chicago Union Station on September 7, shows migrants boarding shuttles after disembarking from a bus sent from Texas.
According to the report, thousands of immigrants were sent to Chicago from Texas as part of a "political stunt" by Texas Republican Governor Greg Abbott. Chicago, under Democratic Governor JB Pritzker, had little choice but to accommodate the arriving migrants. ABBOTT'S STUNT
In 2022, Texas Governor Greg Abbott reportedly began sending migrants to Democrat-controlled cities like New York and Chicago. Over the next two years, Texas sent more than 100,000 migrants to other cities at a staggering cost of $148 million.
On the other hand, Trump has already made his intentions clear, with reports suggesting that Stephen Miller , an immigration hardliner and advisor to Trump, will be taking over policy planning for the deportation of immigrants and is expected to be the deputy chief of staff in the Trump administration.
Thus, it's clear that this photo is not related to Trump's election victory at all. - Ends Published By: Ajmal Published On: Nov 13, 2024 19:02 IST

title: Fact Check: This old video of tractor running over women protesters is from Punjab, not Haryana
content:
This video is old from Amritsar, Punjab. It's also from January 2021.
Hundreds of farmers have been camping at the Haryana-Punjab Shambhu border for more than nine months now, disrupting key highways and blocking the vital link between Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, and Jammu and Kashmir.Â
A video now going viral shows a water tanker running over several women sitting on the road. Sharing this video, many claimed that it was from Haryana. An X user wrote , "The state brutality against female farmers. Remember the symbol, Om. Bulldozer Justice in UP vs Tractor Justice in Haryana." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is more than three years old and from Amritsar in Punjab, not Haryana.
Responding to the viral post, many claimed that this incident was old and from Amritsar, Punjab. Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to the same video shared on X on January 28, 2021.Â
The post read, "2 Old Women were killed & 3 got injured when a tractor ran over them during the tractor parade." This proves that the viral video is not recent.
A further keyword search led us to an NDTV report published on January 26, 2021. As per the report, a water tanker hit a group of women who were going to join the sit-in being held in favour of the farmers' protests in Amritsar, Punjab.Â
The tanker hit five women, two of whom died. Three were seriously wounded. In its aftermath, people thrashed the tanker's driver and handed him over to authorities. The police later filed a case and took the driver into custody.
We found several news reports published in January 2021 stating how an uncontrolled tanker ran over the women walking in the rally in Amritsar. The tanker seen in the reports also resembles the one in the viral video.
As per Amar Ujala, as soon as the tanker's driver reached the protesting woman, he lost control of the tractor. The tractor kept moving for several metres, trampling the women. The women who died were Ninder Kaur and Simarjit Kaur, residents of Vallah, Amritsar.Â
It's noteworthy that the same video went viral during a farmers' Republic Day march in Delhi in 2021. At the time as well, India Today Fact Check debunked the misleading claims shared along with it.
Thus, It is clear that a 2021 video of a water tanker running over protesters in Amritsar was falsely shared as a recent incident in Haryana. - Ends (Written by Ashish Kumar) Published By: Vivek Published On: Nov 13, 2024 20:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Did a woman die trying to board moving train in Patna? The facts behind the viral video
content:
This accident took place in Kerala's Kannur. The woman survived with minor injuries.
A terrifying video making the rounds on social media shows a woman trying to board a moving train and falling, and reportedly losing her life in the process. The video shows her buying something from a kiosk when she suddenly realises the train behind her is departing. She panics, runs towards the moving train, and falls  while trying to board it.
Those sharing the clip claimed that this incident took place at Patna's Rajendra Nagar Station and that the woman died.Â
India Today Fact Check found that this incident took place in Kerala's Kannur and that the woman survived, though with some injuries.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to an Instagram post dated November 3 containing the viral clip. According to the caption in Malayalam, the incident took place at the Kannur railway station in Kerala. The woman fell on the tracks while trying to board the Puducherry Express. The railway police and passengers rescued the woman and took her to a hospital.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Vengara Live (@vengaralive)
A post shared by Vengara Live (@vengaralive)
We then found multiple news reports about this incident in Malayalam. According to them, the victim was a nursing student from Kiliyanthara, a village in the Iritty block of Kerala's Kannur district. She deboarded the train to buy chips when it halted at the Kannur railway station. As the train started leaving the platform, she tried to get on board and fell between the platform and the train.Â
According to a Mathrubhumi report , the 19-year-old was travelling from Thalassery to Mangaluru on the Puducherry-Mangaluru train. Unaware that the train only stopped for three minutes at Kannur, the woman stepped down to buy biscuits and other items. When she fell while trying to board the moving train, the passengers and railway police quickly informed the driver , who stopped the train.Â
The reports added that the woman only sustained minor injuries. The police immediately took her to the hospital for treatment. The woman reportedly even continued her journey to Mangaluru on a different train later.
A spokesperson from the Palakkad railway division told India Today Fact Check that the incident took place on November 3 and that the victim's name was Riya Rose. She was admitted to the Kannur General Hospital. Following first aid for a minor injury to her leg, Riya was discharged.
It is, thus, clear that a video of an accident in Kannur was shared with false, misleading claims. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Nov 13, 2024 21:17 IST

title: Fact Check: This is NOT a Houthi attack! This clip is from 2020
content:
This video from July 2020 shows a fire that broke out in a US aircraft carrier docked in San Diego.
Yemen's Houthi militants attacked two US missile destroyers on November 12 during their passage via the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait in the Arabian Sea. The attacks were not successful as US warships repelled them.
Now, a video  making the rounds online purports to show this attack. The video shows an aircraft carrier on fire. A Facebook user wrote, "Big blow on US, footage purportedly shows the aftermath of the Yemeni resistance attack on the American aircraft carrier Abraham Lincoln in the Arabian Sea, with multiple cruise missiles and drones." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from July 2020 when the US Navy warship USS Bonhomme Richard which was docked in San Diego for maintenance caught fire.
Responding to the viral post, several people claimed the video was old and showed a fire on a US Navy warship during routine maintenance at a San Diego base in 2020.Â
The 27-second-long viral video comprises three different clips. A reverse search revealed the clip used in the first 13 seconds was uploaded to the official YouTube channel of the US Nav y on July 14, 2020. It showed the air carrier USS Bonhomme Richard on fire at the San Diego Naval base during routine maintenance.
The second clip used in the video also shows the USS Bonhomme Richard warship. We found this clip in a CBS Evening News report published in October 2021, which said there was a fire in San Diego in July 2020.
As per the December 2020 FOX 5 San Diego video report, the third and last video was also from the same fire that broke out during maintenance on Bonhomme Richard on July 12, 2020, in San Diego. This proves that all the clips are of the same incident and from 2020.Â
Thus, it's clear this video does not show a Houthi attack. It's also noteworthy that this particular fire incident has previously been shared as Houthi attacks on more than one occasion. You can read India Today's fact-check stories on that here and here .Â
(Written by Ashish Kumar) ---------------------------------------- - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Nov 14, 2024 15:37 IST

title: Fact Check: This Sanjay Raut tattoo is photoshopped!
content:
This image is edited. The original image shows a man named Ramanna Jamadar who got Uddhav and Aditya Thackeray's faces tattooed on his back.
Some people take their adoration of politicians a little too far. One photo going viral right now, ahead of Assembly elections in Maharastra, purports to show just that.Â
The photo shows prominent Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) leaders Uddhav Thackeray, Aditya Thackeray, and Sanjay Raut tattooed on his back and buttocks! The archives of two such posts can be seen here and here .  Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral image was photoshopped. The original photo shows a man who only tattooed the likeness of Uddhav and Aditya Thackeray on his back. Sanjay Raut's tattoo was added digitally.Â
A quick reverse search of the viral image led us to a September 13, 2022 news report by Marathi news outlet Loksatta . This report has multiple other photos of the tattooed man, Ramanna Jamadar, a construction worker from ​​Solapur. In these photos, only the tattoos of Uddhav and Aditya Thackeray were on his back.Â
According to the report, Jamadar had tattooed the faces of Uddhav and Aditya Thackeray to express his loyalty towards the Shiv Sena and the Thackeray family. Â
A TV9 Marathi journalist spoke to Jamadar about his tattoo in August 2022. During this interview, he again revealed the two tattoos on his back.Â
Thus, it's clear that the viral photo was edited to add Sanjay Raut's likeness. - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Nov 14, 2024 15:46 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show Congress candidate's election rally in Maharashtra
content:
The video is neither recent, nor from Akola. It shows an Eid-e-Milad bike rally from September 2024 in Maharashtra's Latur.
As Maharashtra prepares to vote for assembly elections on November 20, a video has gone viral on social media that allegedly shows a rally by the Congress party. In the clip, a large group of people can be seen on bikes and cars. A few social media users are claiming that this is an election rally of Sajid Khan, the Congress candidate from Akola West constituency.
Sharing the viral clip, an X user wrote , "Look at their flags. Flags of Palestine, Iran, Iraq, ISIS, Hezbollah... No Indian flag. Guess this election rally is from which country? This is in the secular Maharashtra state Akola west. Congress party candidate Sajid Khan Mastan Khan election rally."
However, India Today Fact Check found that the video is of an Eid-e-Milad bike procession in Maharashtra's Latur; and not a Congress candidate's election rally. OUR PROBE
Upon reverse searching the keyframes of the viral video, we found it uploaded on a YouTube channel in October 2024. According to its title, the video is from the Eid-e-Milad bike rally in Maharashtra's Latur.
Taking a cue from this, we found several other videos from the Eid-e-Milad rally in Latur. In a video uploaded on September 19, 2024 by Latur News Official, visuals similar to the viral video can be seen. A comparison can be seen below.
We reached out to India Today's Latur correspondent Ravindra Dhanorkar, who confirmed to us that the viral video is indeed from the Eid-e-Milad procession that took place on September 19, 2024. He also told us that the location shown in the video is of the Old Bus Stand, Gandhi Chowk, Latur.
We also found the location on Google Maps. A comparison of the viral clip screengrabs and Google Maps street view can be seen below.
Some users had shared the viral clip a few months ago linking it to the Congress' rally in Haryana's Mewat. However, India Today Fact Check had debunked those claims as well.
Sajid Khan Pathan is the Congress candidate from the Akola West constituency. We saw videos of Pathan's election campaigns which do not have any resemblance to the viral clip.
We could not independently verify whether the flags seen in the rally are associated with Palestine, Iran, Iraq, ISIS, or Hezbollah. However, it is certain that the video of an Eid-e-Milad rally in Latur is being shared as a Congress candidate's election rally. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Nov 18, 2024 19:43 IST

title: Fact Check: 'Pushpa 2' trailer launch video passed off as MVA rally in Maharashtra
content:
The video is related to the trailer launch event of Allu Arjun's upcoming film "Pushpa 2: The Rule", held at Gandhi Maidan in Patna, Bihar.
A video allegedly showing a massive Maha Vikas Aghadi rally held at Mumbai's BKC ground has gone viral on social media . It shows a spectacular drone shot of a huge crowd. Some people can also be seen standing atop a tower-like structure.
Sharing this video, an X user wrote , "Crowd throng MVA rally at BKC in Mumbai | Overview of the meeting recorded by drone".
However, India Today Fact Check found that the video is of the huge crowd that had flocked Patna's Gandhi Maidan for the trailer launch event of actor Allu Arjun's upcoming film, 'Pushpa 2: The Rule'. OUR PROBE
We observed that several X users responded to the viral post , claiming that the video is related to the trailer launch event of "Pushpa 2: The Rule" movie.
A quick keyword search led us to several news reports  about this trailer launch event.
We came across a post on X featuring the viral video. As per the post, Gandhi Maidan was fully packed with fans who came to see Allu Arjun and Rashmika Mandanna. In the post, it is also mentioned that the video is related to the trailer launch event of the film "Pushpa 2: The Rule". बिहार वालों ने तो एकदम गर्दा उड़ा दिया, अल्लू अर्जुन और रश्मिका मंदाना को देखने के लिए गांधी मैदान हाउस फुल हो गया 😍❤️ @alluarjun @iamRashmika #Pushpa2 pic.twitter.com/tFQb8n7G4E — छपरा जिला 🇮🇳 (@ChapraZila) November 17, 2024 A subsequent search led us to an 86-minute-long video uploaded to the YouTube channel YouWe Media, an event management company that organised the trailer launch event of "Pushpa 2: The Rule". Several keyframes of this video match with the viral video. A close-up shot of the stage, similar to the viral video, appears around the 6:50 mark. Similarly, at the 9:15 mark, people can be seen perched atop the tower-like structure. A comparison between the viral video and the video posted to the YouTube channel of YouWe Media can be seen below. According to the news reports , a massive crowd gathered at Gandhi Maidan in Patna, Bihar on November 17 to see Allu Arjun and Rashmika Mandanna during the trailer launch event of Pushpa 2: The Rule. Reports  also mention some chaos at the event due to the overwhelming crowd. Therefore, it is clear that the viral video is not from any election rally but from the trailer launch event of "Pushpa 2: The Rule" held in Patna, Bihar. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 18, 2024 22:42 IST

title: Fact Check: Viral notice about change in retirement age of govt employees is FAKE
content:
The viral notice is fake. The Centre has not made any change in the age of retirement of central government employees.
Sharing the photo of what appears to be an official notification, many on social media claimed that the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Centre increased the retirement age of central government employees from 60 to 62 years. This alleged new rule will apply to employees who will retire after April 1, 2025. In this document that's being shared, an explanation for the reasons behind introducing this change and how it will benefit the employees was also given. Its archived version can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this notice is completely fake. The Centre has not made any change to the age of retirement for central government employees.
With the help of a keyword search, we found a post from the Press Information Bureau's fact-check unit dated November 19. The post stated that the viral notice was fake and that the government had taken no such decision. सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल हो रहे खबरों में दावा किया जा रहा है कि भारत सरकार ने केंद्रीय कर्मचारियों की रिटायरमेंट आयु में 2 साल की वृद्धि करने का निर्णय लिया है #PIBFactCheck ❌ यह दावा फर्जी है ✅ भारत सरकार ने ऐसा कोई निर्णय नहीं लिया है ⚠️ बिना सत्यता जांचे खबरें साझा न करें pic.twitter.com/KahXlVIrAF — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) November 19, 2024
सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल हो रहे खबरों में दावा किया जा रहा है कि भारत सरकार ने केंद्रीय कर्मचारियों की रिटायरमेंट आयु में 2 साल की वृद्धि करने का निर्णय लिया है #PIBFactCheck ❌ यह दावा फर्जी है ✅ भारत सरकार ने ऐसा कोई निर्णय नहीं लिया है ⚠️ बिना सत्यता जांचे खबरें साझा न करें pic.twitter.com/KahXlVIrAF — PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) November 19, 2024
Further searches led us to another post  containing photos of a three-page-long version of the viral document. The text on this document was copied from an article . Both the article and the viral document mentioned the source of their information as a website named NCCCC .Â
The website claims to be a "go-to source for the latest updates on government schemes, finance, trending topics, auto news, and more," with a mission "to offer timely, accurate, and thorough coverage of the issues that matter most to you."
This website featured a disclaimer that read: "The information provided on [the website] is for general informational purposes only. All content on the site is provided in good faith, but we make no representation or warranty of any kind, express or implied, regarding the accuracy, adequacy, validity, reliability, availability, or completeness of any information on the site." It further stated this website is not affiliated with any government institution, government department, or educational institution.
The website also had an article about the viral notice in question that talked about possibilities of change in the retirement age of government employees, while clearly mentioning at the end, that the government had not made any such announcement yet.Â
On August 9, 2023, Jitendra Singh, the Minister of State for the Department of Personnel and Training, responding to a question in the Lok Sabha, stated that no proposal for changing the retirement age of central government employees was under consideration by the government. A PDF of this Q&A session can be seen on the official website of the Parliament of India .
It is also noteworthy that in official Department of Personnel and Training notifications , a unique number, name of the department, date, and other details are provided. These were missing in the viral document.
According to the Department of Personnel and Training , every government employee shall retire from service after attaining the age of sixty years or on the expiry of any further extension granted by the central government in public interest. However, the age of retirement for doctors working in government ministries, departments, or other health services, can go from 62 to 65 years. Specialists in scientific fields can also be granted an extension of service up to the age of 64.Â
It is thus, clear that this notice about an extension of the retirement age for central government employees is fake. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Nov 20, 2024 13:53 IST

title: Supriya Sule, Nana Patole Bitcoin audios: What AI detection tools tell us
content:
On the eve of the Maharashtra Assembly elections, Ravindranath Patil, a former IPS officer from Pune, made startling allegations against Nationalist Congress Party (Sharad Pawar) leader Supriya Sule and Maharashtra Congress chief Nana Patole, accusing them of misappropriating Bitcoins from a 2019 cryptocurrency fraud case and using that to fund campaigning for the polls.Â
The former IPS officer alleged Amitabh Gupta, then commissioner of the Pune police and Bhagyashri Nautake, the former deputy commissioner of police who was handling the cybercrime investigations, were involved in the misappropriation of Bitcoins, which were used by the two political leaders.
The Bharatiya Janata Party later released several files as purported evidence of this . These audio files allegedly feature Supriya Sule, Nana Patole, Amitabh Gupta and Gaurav Mehta, an employee of an audit firm called Sarathi Associates. "Need cash in exchange of bitcoins...You need not to worry about inquiry… We will handle it when we come to power..." NCP (Sharad Pawar) leader Supriya Sule to Gaurav Mehta, the employee of audit firm Sarathi Associates. (3 voice notes) pic.twitter.com/Pulphd6Oki — BJP (@BJP4India) November 19, 2024
"Need cash in exchange of bitcoins...You need not to worry about inquiry… We will handle it when we come to power..." NCP (Sharad Pawar) leader Supriya Sule to Gaurav Mehta, the employee of audit firm Sarathi Associates. (3 voice notes) pic.twitter.com/Pulphd6Oki — BJP (@BJP4India) November 19, 2024
Online, many have called these audios AI-generated, even as Ajit Pawar of the rival NCP faction claimed one of the voices was his sister's and the other was "someone I have worked with extensively." Supriya Sule has denied this is her voice . As has Nana Patole. Meanwhile, the Enforcement Directorate has reportedly raided Gaurav Mehta's home in Raipur.Â
While speaking to India Today TV, the Baramati MP accused the BJP of conspiring to defame her. Supriya Sule said she has spoken against bitcoin in Parliament and has been an "honest and straightforward servant of the country". She further said that she sent a notice to the saffron party, while Nana Patole has filed a complaint against BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi for his accusations. ARE THESE AUDIOS AI-GENERATED?
India Today Fact Check used three publicly available AI detection tools to analyse the audio files.Â
The first is TrueMedia, founded by Oren Etzioni, a University of Washington professor. The second is the University of Buffalo's Deefake-O-Meter. The third is the Deepfake Voice Detector, created by Hiya, a company that screens calls for spam and fraud.Â
It's noteworthy that these tools' findings are not always accurate. Sometimes they also provide contradictory results.Â
Here is what each of these tools found:
TrueMedia uses three different detectors to determine the authenticity of an audio sample. As per the tool, there is "substantial evidence" of all four audio samples being AI-generated. However, one of the detectors was less confident about Nana Patole's alleged audio sample.
DeepFake-O-Meter has six different detectors. Four of these detectors were more than 80 per cent confident of Supriya Sule, Amitabh Gupta, and Gaurav Mehta's alleged audio samples being AI-generated.Â
DeepFake-O-Meter's confidence level was also comparatively lower for the alleged Nana Patole audio sample. But three of its six detectors said with more than 80 per cent confidence that it was AI-generated. HIYA DEEPFAKE VOICE DETECTOR:
As per scores provided by Hiya's Deepfake Voice Detector, Supriya Sule, Amitabh Gupta, and Gaurav Mehta's alleged samples were AI-generated. Whereas, the tool was uncertain about Nana Patole's alleged voice.Â
What is noteworthy is the alleged Nana Patole audio sample is only six seconds long. This short audio sample may not be adequate for tools to analyse. This may explain the low confidence score given by the tools. WHAT DO THE EXPERTS SAY
India Today is a part of the Misinformation Combat Alliance's Deepfakes Analysis Unit, which has a panel of tech and AI experts. Â
UC Berkeley professor Hany Farid, who specialises in the analysis of deepfakes, told India Today Fact Check that he analysed these audio samples with two of their models trained to distinguish real from AI-generated voices.
He said: "Collectively the models classify three of the audios as likely to be AI and one of the audios (the alleged Nana Patole audio) was too short for us to obtain reliable results. In addition, native speakers on our team hear telltale signs of AI generation in terms of cadence and intonation."
The DAU analysed all the audio samples and concluded that three of the viral audio clips were AI-generated, noting that for Nana Patole's sample, the confidence level of various tools was a tad lower. DAU's experts explained there could be two factors responsible for this. One, the audio clip is short, which may result in the tools not being able to trace any sign of manipulation. Two, the language being Marathi and tools not being trained on it long enough could also lead to low confidence on the part of the detectors.Â
Notably, Nana Patole dismissed the BJP's allegations and said, "Even (Prime Minister) Narendra Modi recognises my voice." He also told reporters that he is a farmer and does not understand Bitcoin at all.Â
Update: This story has been updated with the analysis from UC Berkeley professor Hany Farid, who responded to our queries after the story was published. - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Nov 20, 2024 18:12 IST

title: Fact Check: 'Shri Ram Jai Ram' sung at CPI(M) event? No, this video is edited
content:
The viral video has been edited. In the original video, the song "Neel Gagan Par Udte Badal" was being sung.
The Communist Party of India-Marxist's stance on religion has always been a hot topic. A video now circulating online purports to show a bhajan or devotional song starting with "Shri Ram Jai Ram" being sung at a CPI(M) event. The video shows people singing the song with musical instruments on a stage decorated with the party's flags and posters.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Hindus Of India (@hindusofindia)
A post shared by Hindus Of India (@hindusofindia)
One person shared the video on Instagram and wrote, "Communists singing Bhajan. Can't believe my eyes."
India Today Fact Check found that this video was edited. In the original video, they were singing an old Hindi film song that starts with "Neel Gagan Par Udte Bada" not "Shri Ram Jai Ram".Â
Looking closely at the viral video, one can see that the singer's lip movements do not match the lyrics and rhythm of the song.Â
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to the same video with different audio shared by the X account Divyendu Das on November 19.
The post quoted another Bangla post featuring the viral clip and said, "Employees of Trinamool Congress's IT cell‼ Meanwhile, they're spreading fake news against @CPIM_WESTBENGAL 24x7."
In the video shared by Das, the people on the stage could be heard singing an old Hindi film song called "Neel Gagan Par Udte Badal". It was originally sung by Mohammed Rafi and Asha Bhosle. Employees of Trinamool Congress's IT cell‼️ Meanwhile, they're spreading fake news against @CPIM_WESTBENGAL 24x7 . https://t.co/IV2IgkqkNM pic.twitter.com/02Lg6qpPV8 — Dibyendu Das (@dibyendux) November 19, 2024
Employees of Trinamool Congress's IT cell‼️ Meanwhile, they're spreading fake news against @CPIM_WESTBENGAL 24x7 . https://t.co/IV2IgkqkNM pic.twitter.com/02Lg6qpPV8 — Dibyendu Das (@dibyendux) November 19, 2024
We contacted Divyendu Das, who told us that this video is from the Tekhali Bazar area of Nandigram Block 1 in East Midnapore, West Bengal. He said this happened on Sunday, November 17.
With this information, we used some Bangla keywords and found the same video on a Facebook group called CPIM West Bengal. The post mentioned that the public meeting was organised to protest against the rampant violence against women in the country and the state, inflation, record unemployment etc.
We contacted local CPI(M) leader Paritosh Pattanayak, who is part of the political party's East Midnapore district committee. He told us that he was present at the public meeting that took place at the Tekhali Bazar in the Gokulnagar area. According to him, the video going viral was distorted and spread along with false claims by the Trinamool Congress.
He also shared the video of the public meeting on his Facebook page along with a picture of him speaking there. This clip, too, did not feature any devotional song.Â
It is thus clear that the audio in this viral video was manipulated.Â

title: Like Supriya Sule, you too could be a victim of audio deepfake. Here's what you can do
content:
For years, the word "deepfake" evoked the idea of manipulated images and videos. And with the advent of generative AI, both have become scarily easy to manufacture. But the kind of deepfake that continues to exist outside the public imagination is audio. And by far, this is a more insidious form simply because it's much harder to detect — at least compared to AI-generated images or videos.
On the eve of the Maharashtra Assembly polls, controversy erupted as four audio clips went viral. In the eye of the storm were Nationalist Congress Party (Sharad Pawar) leader Supriya Sule and Congress leader Nana Patole, who could allegedly be heard in these clips trying to misappropriate Bitcoin from an old cryptocurrency fraud case to fund their election campaigns.Â
Both Sule and Patole denied these were their voices and many online claimed they were deepfakes. India Today Fact Check tested them and both experts and detection tools pointed towards them being AI-generated.Â
Audio deepfakes are more ubiquitous than you'd think. And that's dangerous. Earlier this year, a man used a voice-changing app to pose as a female professor, lured seven school girls with scholarship offers, and raped them in Madhya Pradesh's Sidhi district. Scammers also hit the jackpot with audio deepfakes.Â
So, how can you, an ordinary person who may not be very tech-savvy, safeguard yourself from the threat of being duped through audio deepfakes? Here's a simple guide.Â
While there isn't a sure-shot formula to identify synthetic voices, there are red flags you can look out for. One such telltale sign is that AI-generated voices often sound flat, robotic, and lack natural modulation or emotion. Mispronunciations of names and complex words, especially in Indian languages, also indicate the use of AI. Â
Fraudsters often impersonate relatives or acquaintances and narrate fake scenarios to scare you. The idea is that in a moment of panic, you'll make hasty decisions which would benefit them.Â
So, you should always keep your cool. Verify their claims by directly contacting the person they're impersonating. Pay attention to background noises, and cross-check if they match the caller's claims — though fake ambient noises can also be simulated through online tools. And keep questioning them on details.Â
Delhi-based cybersecurity expert Anuraag Singh says scammers who attempt to deceive people try to make their story believable. "They do thorough research on their potential victims and then call them so that they can reveal personal details like vehicle number etc., to make people trust them."
Singh added that people should always record suspicious calls — it may be inadmissible in court but will likely help with the investigation. "If your device lacks this feature, put your phone on speaker and use an external device to record the conversation," he said. Â
And finally, there are plenty of free, easy-to-use AI detection tools that you can use to detect synthetic audio. One such tool is TrueMedia.org , founded by Oren Etzioni, a University of Washington professor.
Here you can simply upload the URL of the social media post bearing the audio file and click on the "Is it real" button. It will then analyse the sample and tell whether it is AI-generated. If you sign in to the TrueMedia website, you can also upload audio files.Â
Similarly, Hiya's Deepfake Voice Detector can also prove handy. Just install the Chrome extension and sign up for the free service. Whenever you want to check a suspicious voice sample, just play the audio and click on the extension. Next, click on the "Start Analysing" button. The tool will promptly declare if the sample is a deepfake. Incidentally, Hiya is a company that screens calls for spam and fraud.
It's noteworthy that these tools' findings are not always accurate. Sometimes they also provide contradictory results. And sometimes, they produce false positives.Â
So, while one solution may not be perfect, a combination of all three approaches mentioned above can mostly safeguard you against the menace of synthetic audio. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Nov 21, 2024 20:28 IST

title: Fact Check: Neck massage leaves customer paralysed? Viral video is scripted
content:
While cracking or twisting the neck can have serious consequences, the viral video is scripted.
A video making the rounds on social media purports to show how a "barber twists neck during head massage, leaves customer paralysed." In the video, a man can be giving a neck massage. After the barber twists the man's neck, he starts convulsing, and subsequently appears paralysed.Â
India Today Fact Check found that this was a scripted video, made to spread awareness. It does not show a real incident.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a longer version of this video uploaded to a YouTube channel named "3rd eye". This video contained a disclaimer at the end, stating it was made for entertainment and educational purposes.
The video description reads, "Disclaimer: Thank you for watching! Please be aware that this channel features scripted dramas and parodies of aware people in different situations. This channel brings social awareness videos. These short films are for entertainment purposes only!"
We also found another scripted video on this YouTube channel, shot in the same salon as the one seen in the viral video. This time, a barber ends up leaving his customer injured while shaving his beard. Interestingly, the barber in this video was also in the viral video, acting as a customer waiting for his turn in the salon.
It is noteworthy that a 30-year-old Karnataka man recently suffered a stroke  after his barber forcefully twisted his neck during a head massage. The victim was rushed to the hospital. It took him nearly two months to recover fully after the incident.Â
The New Indian Express article about this incident quoted Dr Sreekanta Swamy, Senior Consultant in Neurology at Aster RV Hospital, saying, "Rapid, unscientific neck twists — whether by barbers or individuals themselves can cause blood vessel tears, potentially leading to life-threatening strokes." The doctors also added that sudden, forceful movements around the neck can lead to strokes, paralysis, or even death if not properly diagnosed or treated.
It is thus, clear that while health experts warn that cracking or twisting of the neck can indeed have serious consequences , the viral video does not show a real incident. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Nov 22, 2024 14:14 IST

title: Fact Check: Adani Group DIDN'T get Rs 120 lakh crore loan from Indian banks. Data goof-up creates confusion
content:
This infographic actually shows the total amount lent by various banks as of September 2024.
Arrest warrants were issued in the United States on November 20 for industrialist Gautam Adani , his nephew, and six others for allegedly bribing Indian officials with $265 million (roughly Rs 2,238 crore) in exchange for solar power contracts. The Adani Group dismissed the allegations, calling them baseless.Â
Now, an infographic bearing the financial news website MoneyControl's logo is being widely shared. The graphic "Lenders exposure to Adani Group companies" shows the alleged amount Adani Group companies owe various public sector and private banks in India.Â
India Today Fact Check found that these figures are incorrect. Actually, what they show is the total amount these public and private banks lent as a whole as of September 2024. The loans to the Adani Group by these banks are a fraction of this amount.
Where did this infographic come from?
India Today Fact Check found that the infographic originated from a MoneyControl article published on November 21. Later, it was replaced with a new graphic containing the correct numbers. However, by the time the correction was made, several people online had picked up this infographic and shared it.
On MoneyControl's website, we found an article titled, "Banks' exposure to Adani Group: How big a worry is it really?" This article features an infographic that lists the State Bank of India's exposure to Adani Group companies as Rs 27,000 crore — much lower than the Rs 39.2 lakh crore shown in the viral image. Other banks' loans listed here are also significantly lower.Â
Taking a cue from this, we looked for an older version of the article to check if it was later modified by MoneyControl. It was.
On the Wayback Machine, we found an archive of the original article published on November 21. In this version, the infographic was the same as the viral photo.Â
This means MoneyControl first published the viral graphic with the wrong figures and later replaced it with a new graphic containing the correct numbers. The news article did not feature a disclaimer about this change. Additionally, the original graphic credited the figures to Nuvama Research, while the updated one credits it to bank disclosures.Â
Apart from the wrong infographic, the original version of the report also contained a factually incorrect paragraph:Â
"According to Nuvama Research estimates, SBI leads with Rs 39.2 lakh crore in total loans to the Adani Group as of September 2024. Bank of Baroda followed with Rs 11.4 lakh crore, while PNB and Canara Bank have exposures of Rs 10.6 lakh crore and Rs 10.12 lakh crore, respectively. Among private banks, ICICI Bank's loans to Adani Group stood at Rs 12.7 lakh crore, and Axis Bank reported Rs 10 lakh crore in exposure."Â
In the updated version of the report, this paragraph was revised to, "According to disclosure by banks, India's largest lender SBI's outstanding exposure to Adani Group companies stood at Rs 27,000 crore as of December 2022, while PNB's stood at Rs 3,300 crore, and Bank of Baroda's stood at Rs 5,300 crore."
India Today Fact Check reached out to MoneyControl for a statement. The story will be updated as and when we receive a response.Â
The loan amounts being shared in the viral infographic are incredibly huge. If this were true, it would mean that Adani Group companies owed Rs 120 lakh crore to the various Indian banks. This is almost 11 times more than the current market capitalisation  of Rs 11.60 lakh crore of the 10 public companies under the Adani Group. Also, Rs 120 lakh crore is more than a third of India's total GDP of around Rs 296.58 lakh crore for the current fiscal year.
How much money did banks lend Adani Group?Â
As per the Economic Times , the Adani Group's total debt is Rs 2.4 lakh crore, with a cash balance of Rs 59,791 crore. Domestic banks including SBI, PNB, and other institutions reportedly hold around Rs 88,100 crore or 36 per cent of the Adani Group's total debt. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 22, 2024 17:29 IST

title: Here's all we know about the viral video of the homeless child covered in silver paint
content:
A distressing video going viral right now shows a child covered in silver paint, dozing off at the side of a road. The video was originally shared on November 20 by an X user, who claimed it was from Kurnool in Andhra Pradesh and that the child was beaten up and had no food to eat. Andhra Pradesh minister Nara Lokesh also responded to this post , promising quick action. @naralokesh Good Morning Sir,it's a pleasure to write https://t.co/TPDAhiw3V1 is child I mentioned seen in kurnool City on roads brutally beaten up and not even given food.Please arrange your team and refuse https://t.co/xUUP5U7WYm dress circle shopping mall kurnool city. pic.twitter.com/Y3CENA2ne4 — Santhosh Kumar (@SanthoshKu34277) November 20, 2024
@naralokesh Good Morning Sir,it's a pleasure to write https://t.co/TPDAhiw3V1 is child I mentioned seen in kurnool City on roads brutally beaten up and not even given food.Please arrange your team and refuse https://t.co/xUUP5U7WYm dress circle shopping mall kurnool city. pic.twitter.com/Y3CENA2ne4 — Santhosh Kumar (@SanthoshKu34277) November 20, 2024
While many were disturbed seeing a child in this condition, this video triggered yet another debate on social media: was this a real child or AI-generated? AI OR REAL?
Aside from the child, the video featured a small bucket, an uneven cemented area, and a few vehicles. We noticed that all these objects had two shadows — one darker than the other.
This suggests the video was shot late in the evening or at night and the shadows were cast by two different light sources, likely streetlights. The streetlight closer to the child cast a darker and shorter shadow, while the other streetlight cast a lighter and bigger one.
As the objects moved, the shadows also moved in sync. Right now, even very sophisticated AI tools aren't capable of matching shadows and objects with such perfection. This rules out the possibility of the video being generated using AI.
In the video, we observed a bike with the number plate AP21 P7435. AP21 is the Regional Transport Office code of Andhra Pradesh's Kurnool district.
Moreover, the person, the person who shared the video originally, stated in another post the location of this video was Dress Circle Shopping Mall in Kurnool. We then checked the street view of this location on Google Maps . A beauty parlour named "Pratimas" can be seen right in front of the Dress Circle Shopping Mall. Using the contact number on the parlour's board, we contacted its owner, Pratima Ganesh.Â
Pratima confirmed to India Today Fact Check that the viral video was shot near the Dress Circle Shopping Mall, right in front of her parlour. She further told us that she often saw this child begging there in the evening. She further said that she had tried talking to the child about his parents and whereabouts, but he never responded and only asked for money.
Pratima also shared pictures of the spot where the viral video was shot, standing right on top of the uneven cemented area where the child could be seen sitting. It is thus, clear that the video was shot right in front of the parlour, next to the Dress Circle Shopping Mall in Andhra Pradesh's Kurnool.
On November 22, Kurnool police shared photos of two children covered in silver paint, stating they were forced to beg in Kurnool. In response to a tweet by Hon'ble Minister Sri Nara Lokesh about 2 children being coloured and forced to beg in Kurnool Town, District administration promptly responded and SP Kurnool instructed the police to take action (1/4) @naralokesh @APPOLICE100 @SanthoshKu34277 #APPolice pic.twitter.com/HiJAtDRpjR — Kurnool Police (@PoliceKurnool) November 22, 2024
In response to a tweet by Hon'ble Minister Sri Nara Lokesh about 2 children being coloured and forced to beg in Kurnool Town, District administration promptly responded and SP Kurnool instructed the police to take action (1/4) @naralokesh @APPOLICE100 @SanthoshKu34277 #APPolice pic.twitter.com/HiJAtDRpjR — Kurnool Police (@PoliceKurnool) November 22, 2024
A total of nine children, including the one seen in the viral video , who were forced to beg on the street were rescued by the police and their parents were counselled as well. - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Nov 22, 2024 21:45 IST

title: Fact Check: Fake covers! India Today magazine DID NOT publish these stories on Rahul Gandhi
content:
India Today has not published any such cover stories criticizing Rahul Gandhi. The magazine's November 25 and December 2 editions corroborate these facts.
The Maharashtra elections saw the Bharatiya Janata Party-Shiv Sena-Nationalist Congress Party combine, the Mahayuti, win 235 seats, leaving the Congress, the Shiv Sena (Uddhav Thackeray), and the Nationalist Congress Party (Sharad Pawar) with just 49. The Congress won only 16 seats.Â
Following this monumental defeat, two images allegedly featuring recent covers of the India Today magazine were shared widely on social media. These covers criticised Congress leader and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi.Â
Both covers featured Rahul Gandhi. The one allegedly published on November 23 reads, "89 Not Out". The other allegedly from December 2 showed Maharashtra's map and contained the texts: "Maha Raja of Mishap" and "Maharashtra slips away as Rahul Gandhi redefines leadership... again!" The archives of the viral post can be seen here .
India Today magazine did not publish any such cover stories criticising Rahul Gandhi. The magazine's November 25 and December 2 editions corroborate these facts.
The dates written on the viral covers are November 23 and December 2. On November 23, the magazine did not publish an edition. India Today is a weekly magazine. New editions are published every Monday. As November 23 was a Saturday, there cannot be a cover with that date. The nearest edition to that was published on November 25.Â
The cover story on November 25 was about stress at the workplace — nothing to do with Rahul Gandhi or the Maharashtra elections. This clarifies that the cover that referred to Gandhi as the "Maha Raja of Mishap" was doctored.
The December 2 edition of India Today magazine also does not feature a story about the Congress leader. Instead, the cover is about digital scammers and reads, "Beware of the new big con." Both actual India Today magazine covers can be seen below.
It is thus clear that these covers are fake. - Ends Published By: Devika Bhattacharya Published On: Nov 25, 2024 14:32 IST

title: Fact Check: Old video from anti-CAA protests FALSELY shared as Sambhal unrest
content:
The viral clip is neither from Sambhal nor recent. This December 2019 clip from Gorakhpur shows police lathi-charging anti-CAA-NRC protestors.
Protests against a mosque survey in Uttar Pradesh's Sambhal district turned violent on November 24. At least four people have reportedly been killed so far and dozens have been injured.Â
On the morning of November 24, a group of court-appointed advocates approached the Shahi Jama Masjid for a survey following a petition that claimed the Mughal-era mosque was constructed after demolishing a temple at the site. This led to local Muslim residents protesting, resulting in clashes with the police.Â
A video  now going viral allegedly shows the Sambhal police lathi-charging protestors.Â
In the viral clip, a large group of people can be seen being beaten up by policemen in a lane. Many can be seen wearing skull caps. Sharing the video , an X user wrote, "Yogi Ji's Police Back in Form This is the way to deal with these peacefools #SambhalJamaMasjid." An archive of the post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral clip is neither from Sambhal nor recent. The December 2019 video from Gorakhpur shows the police lathi-charging anti-CAA protestors. OUR PROBE
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral clip led us to the same video published by a YouTube channel in March 2020, making it clear that it is not from the recent clashes in Sambhal.
In the video, we observed several shops and their names written on the boards. We searched for these names on Google Maps  and found that the video is from Uttar Pradesh's Gorakhpur district, which is more than 650 kilometres from Sambhal. As can be seen in Google Maps, this area is Nakhas Chowk in Gorakhpur. A comparison of a shop seen in the viral clip and Google Maps Street View can be seen below.
Using this clue, we found several news reports that contained the viral clip and other videos of the same incident. According to a December 20, 2019 report in Live Hindustan , Muslims in Gorakhpur were protesting against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and the National Register for Citizens. Per the report, these protests turned violent in many districts of Uttar Pradesh including Gorakhpur, resulting in police lathi-charging people.Â
A video report in UPTak from December 2019 featured the same visuals as the viral clip. Live Hindustan reported this incident took place in the Nakhas Chowk of Gorakhpur, the same area we located on Google Maps.
In Sambhal, following the death of at least four people on November 24, the police denied firing live ammunition at protestors. It attributed the deaths to gunfire from country-made pistols allegedly used by protesters.Â
While many videos of clashes have emerged from Sambhal, it's clear that this video from 2019 does not show the violence there. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Nov 25, 2024 17:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Imran Khan supporters marching to Islamabad? No, this clip is not from Pakistan!
content:
This video is from Timor-Leste where a massive crowd gathered for the arrival of Pope Francis on September 10.
A massive protest launched by supporters of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan has now been called off by the Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, Khan's party, following a government crackdown. At least six people, including four paramilitary troopers, died in clashes between Khan's supporters and security forces.
A video now going viral allegedly shows a sea of Imran Khan supporters marching towards Islamabad against Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's government and the Pakistan army chief.Â
One such post reads, "BREAKING: Pakistan Army cancelled leave of all of its soldiers as lakhs of PTI supporters are marching towards Islamabad against Shehbaz Sharif Govt & Pakistan Army Chief General Asim Munir from different parts of Pakistan. You may witness another massacre by the Pakistan Army soon". Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from the Southeast Asian country of Timor-Leste, where a massive crowd gathered on September 10, 2024, to witness Pope Francis's arrival. OUR PROBE
With the help of a reverse image search, we found the viral video in a Facebook post from September 12, 2024, with the caption: "Pope Francis Welcome historic visit to Timoleste a Country with 100% Catholic root". This makes it clear that the video is two months old and unrelated to the recent protests in Pakistan.Â
A keyword search led to another video of Pope Francis's Timor-Leste visit on the Associated Press' YouTube channel. The video was uploaded on September 10. AP reported that an estimated six lakh people attended mass when Pope Francis arrived in the Catholic nation Timor-Leste on September 9.Â
Karlito Nunes, former representative of Timor-Leste to the United Nations, also posted photos of the event on September 11. One of the photos contains a similar visual of a crowd. The largest Holy Mass during the Pastoral Visit of Pope Francis in Asia-Oceania. My deepest gratitude to Hiss Holiness for making the visit to Timor-Leste 🇹🇱 and during 3 days with loved and joyful with our people. pic.twitter.com/g4qBJjFTTK — Karlito Nunes 🇹🇱🇺🇳 (@NunesKarlito) September 10, 2024
The largest Holy Mass during the Pastoral Visit of Pope Francis in Asia-Oceania. My deepest gratitude to Hiss Holiness for making the visit to Timor-Leste 🇹🇱 and during 3 days with loved and joyful with our people. pic.twitter.com/g4qBJjFTTK — Karlito Nunes 🇹🇱🇺🇳 (@NunesKarlito) September 10, 2024
A Facebook user named Anche Cabral also shared many similar videos on September 10 and 11, claiming they showed people gathered for Pope Francis' visit to Timor-Leste's capital Dili. One of the videos , which is much clearer than the viral video, shows posters of Pope Francis on a wall. Timor-Leste's national flag is also visible on these posters. The same can be seen in the viral video as well.Â
So, while thousands took to the streets to protest Shehbaz Sharif's government, the viral video is unrelated to that. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Nov 27, 2024 16:02 IST

title: Fact Check: This filmy chase sequence is AI-generated!
content:
This video was created using AI tools.
A video circulating on social media claims to show a man escaping police by blinding them with an incredibly bright torch. The clip features a speeding car on a highway when someone from inside the car flashes a blinding beam of white light. Within seconds, the said car vanishes in the darkness. Â
An Instagram user shared this video with the caption: "Bro used 100,000 lumens flashlight to escape from cops." Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that this video was created by an animator using AI tools. It does not show any actual chase. Â OUR PROBEÂ
Many social media users reacting to the viral video pointed out that it seemed AI-generated. Carefully looking at the video, one can also see a disclaimer stating the stunts in the video were created using AI tools. It also cautioned people not to attempt this as it could be dangerous.Â
