However, this disclaimer is barely readable for two reasons. First, the size of the text is too small, and second, it appears on the screen just for a few seconds.Â
In the video, we noticed a watermark "@ndm_electric".Â
A quick keyword search led us to an Instagram account called "@ndm_electric" whose bio stated the user's profession as an animator.Â
This Instagram account shared the video in question on November 25.     View this post on Instagram            Shared post on Time Instagram embed code generator
They also shared an Instagram story on November 26 clearly stating that the actions and stunts shown in the video were fake.Â
Thus, it's clear a video created using AI tools was shared as real. - Ends Published By: Admin Published On: Nov 27, 2024 17:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Muslim lawyer killed in Bangladesh was NOT defending Hindu priest Chinmoy Das
content:
The deceased lawyer identified as Saiful Islam Alif was an assistant public prosecutor in the Chittagong court. Subhashis Sharma is Chinmay Das's lawyer.
Bangladesh is once again on edge following the arrest of Hindu priest Chinmoy Krishna Das in a sedition case. Violence erupted on Tuesday at the Chittagong Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court premises after his bail plea was rejected, leaving one lawyer dead and several others injured.
Meanwhile, a post has gone viral on social media claiming the deceased lawyer was defending the priest, and he was Muslim. One such post read, "Muslim lawyer defending ISKON's Chinmoy Krishna Das killed in Dhaka."
Both Republic TV  and OpIndia published similar claims but later updated their stories. Reuters initially reported that the Muslim lawyer, Alif, was defending Das but later revised this information.Â
India Today Fact Check has found that the lawyer killed in the clash was not defending Chinmoy Das. He was a public prosecutor fighting for the state. OUR PROBE
A November 26 news report published in Prothom Alo , a leading Bangladeshi daily, featured an image of the deceased lawyer, Saiful Islam alias Alif, 35, and identified him as an assistant public prosecutor.
Several other news outlets, including the Business Standard , and the Dhaka Tribune also mentioned that Alif was a public prosecutor and the Bangladeshi interim government had ordered strict punishment for the culprits.Â
We also found the Facebook profile of Saiful Islam Alif , where he shared a video on November 25, which explained the grounds supporting Chinmoy Krishna Das's arrest.
According to a BBC Bangla report , the name of the lawyer representing Chinmoy Das is Subhashis Sharma.
Tanvir Mahtab Abir, a fact-checker from Bangladesh also shared with us the waqalatnama or the bail application plea of Chinmoy Das, which had the stamp of advocate Subhashis Sharma, a lawyer who practices in the Bangladesh Supreme Court and Chittagong Judges Court.
The press wing of the Chief Advisor of Bangladesh's interim government also debunked this rumour on Facebook and stated Subhashis Sharma is the Hindu priest's lawyer.Â
Therefore, it is more than evident that the Muslim lawyer killed on Tuesday in Chittagong was not defending Hindu priest Chinmoy Das. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Nov 27, 2024 19:34 IST

title: Fact Check: Hate crime in West Bank? This church attack video is old and unrelated to Christmas
content:
While the video shows a church attack in Bethlehem, it is from October 2022. Also, the incident had nothing to do with Christmas decorations.
A church was allegedly attacked in Beit Sahour, a town near the Palestinian city of Bethlehem, the biblical birthplace of Jesus Christ, in occupied West Bank. Those making this claim shared a video of an unruly crowd.Â
While many posts simply said "Palestinians" attacked a church in Beit Sahour because churchgoers had started decorating for Christmas, some laid the blame squarely on Palestinian Muslims . The archive of the viral video can be seen here .
India Today found that while the video shows an attack on a church in Bethlehem, it's from October 2022. The incident also had nothing to do with Christmas decorations.Â
We found the viral video in a news report  published by the Jerusalem Post on October 29, 2022. According to the report, dozens of Muslim men hurled stones at the Orthodox church of Beit Sahur, which injured many people.Â
The church authorities reportedly said that a quarrel between some young men prompted the attack on the church. Archbishop Atallah Hanna of the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Jerusalem strongly condemned the assault, saying it "distorts the image of our people and harms civil peace and the good relationship that binds us as the sons of the Palestinian people".
Another report related to the incident says that a quarrel took place between the church's people and outsiders during an annual event there. The dispute was settled for some time, but the outsiders returned and attacked the church.Â
We did not find the reason behind the quarrel reported by any credible news organisation. We also found no reports that said the church was attacked because of Christmas decorations.Â
The Jerusalem Post report mentioned that Wadie Abu Nassar, media spokesperson of the Assembly of Catholic Ordinaries of the Holy Land, condemned the attack in a Facebook post. We found the post. He said while the incident was unfortunate, what relieved him was that the city's residents from other religions defended them and condemned what had happened.Â
In his post, Nassar too did not mention if the attack was the outcome of Christmas decorations. India Today Fact Check reached out to Nassar, who clarified that the attack on the church had no connection with Christmas. He called it a local dispute. POPULATION DECLINE?
The viral claims about the church attack also said the Christian population of Bethlehem shrank from 80 per cent to under 10 per cent in just 20 years. While we couldn't find any credible report about a massive drop in Bethlehem's Christian population, some news reports say the Christian population in the city has dropped from 84 per cent to about 20 per cent in a century. According to a report in the Times of Israel , the Christian population in Bethlehem, as well as in nearby Beit Sahour and Beit Jala, was 86 per cent in 1950. This dropped to just 12 per cent by 2016. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 28, 2024 16:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of student clash in Bangladesh FALSELY shared with communal spin
content:
This video shows a clash between students from different colleges in Bangladesh.
The arrest of Chinmoy Krishna Das, a prominent Hindu priest in Bangladesh, has sparked a huge uproar. He was arrested on November 25 on sedition charges. A video  now going viral allegedly shows attacks on minority Hindus in Bangladesh by Muslims. The video  shows a large mob of mostly young people armed with sticks assaulting others.Â
Sharing this on X, a user wrote , "In Bangladesh Clear Video of Hindu Mob Lynchings while Azan is going on. Here in India, Hindu politicians stops their public speech when Azan starts in between speech as a mark of respect. Hindus must stop such policy, as they don't respect while lynching Hindus."
However, India Today Fact Check found that this video is related to a clash between students of different colleges in Bangladesh. It does not show the atrocities of Muslims against Bangladeshi Hindus.
The viral video featured the logo of BDNews24.com, a prominent Bangladeshi news portal. Based on this information, we found several videos on the portal's official YouTube channel , which featured clips from the viral video.Â
According to the title and description of one of these videos  from November 25, students of Dr Mahbubur Rahman Mollah College clashed with students of Government Shahid Suhrawardy College and Kabi Nazrul Government College in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
A subsequent keyword search led us to several news reports that stated this incident was related to a clash between students from different colleges in Bangladesh.
On November 16, Abhijeet Halder, a class 12 student suffering from dengue, was admitted to the Dhaka National Medical College Hospital, where he died on November 18. Fellow students alleged that medical negligence and wrong treatment by the hospital caused his death. After that, students in large numbers took to the streets and started demonstrations. However, the hospital denied all these allegations.
As per reports , on November 21, these protests turned violent. Protesters vandalised the Government Shahid Suhrawardy College and the Kabi Nazrul Government College and also looted the nearby shops. They also attacked the Dhaka National Medical College Hospital. Allegedly, this vandalism was carried out by the students of Dr Mahbubur Rahman Mollah College.
According to the Dhaka Tribune , following this, students of Shahid Suhrawardy and Kabi Nazrul colleges vandalised the Dr Mahbubur Rahman Mollah College and beat up students there to "avenge" the attacks on them.
More than 30 students were reportedly injured  in this clash between students of several colleges.
It is thus clear that the video of the clash between students in Bangladesh is being shared with a communal spin. - Ends (Written by Abhishek Pathak.) Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Nov 28, 2024 22:38 IST

title: Fact Check: Congress worker DID NOT celebrate Priyanka Gandhi's victory in Wayanad by shooting a cow
content:
This video is at least six months old and most likely from Manipur. It has nothing to do with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's victory in Kerala.
Beginning her journey as a Parliamentarian, Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was sworn in as a Lok Sabha member from Kerala's Wayanad constituency on November 28. Her massive electoral victory with a margin of over four lakh votes was celebrated by Congress workers and supporters after the by-poll results came out a few days back.Â
But, according to some on social media, one Congress worker went too far and allegedly shot a cow while celebrating Vadra's victory . They shared a video of this horrific act and identified the man as Mohammed Mujahid Islam, the media in-charge of Kerala Congress.Â
Sharing the video on Facebook , one person wrote, "This beast's name is Mohammed Mujahid Islam and he is the media in-charge of Kerala Congress. The height of hatred for Hindus is that he sacrificed a cow by shooting it for Priyanka Gandhi's victory. Share this video so much that it reaches the Home Ministry of India and he gets arrested. The character of the mothers of secular Hindu people must be bad, they must have been born only after being disgraced by some M, and they support." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video is at least six months old and likely from Manipur. It has nothing to do with Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's victory in Kerala. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to multiple news reports  about this incident from May 2024. According to them , the viral video showed a man shooting a cow in the head twice as an onlooker recorded the incident on a mobile camera in Manipur.
The Wayanad by-polls were held on November 13, while the counting was done on November 23. This means the viral video predates Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's victory by more than six months.Â
At the time, many on social media shared this video , claiming that the man was a Christian Kuki militant who shot the cow to mock Hindus. On May 7, the Indian branch of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals responded to one such post, stating PETA India's cruelty response team was working with Manipur Police's cybercrimes cell to get an FIR registered and take necessary actions against the man in the video. PETA India's Cruelty Response Team is working with Manipur Police's Cyber Crime Cell to confirm the details with respect to the location of the crime. Once it is ascertained we will work with the concerned district police to get an FIR registered and have necessary action taken.
— PETA India (@PetaIndia) May 7, 2024
PETA India's Cruelty Response Team is working with Manipur Police's Cyber Crime Cell to confirm the details with respect to the location of the crime. Once it is ascertained we will work with the concerned district police to get an FIR registered and have necessary action taken.
— PETA India (@PetaIndia) May 7, 2024
India Today Fact Check reached out to Deepthi Mary Varghese, General Secretary of Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee, who confirmed she is the media chief in the Kerala Congress, adding there was no one named Mohammed Mujahid Islam in her team.
It is thus, clear that the clip does not show a Congress worker killing a cow to celebrate Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's victory in Wayanad. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Nov 29, 2024 15:58 IST

title: AI image models are racing ahead so fast, they're unable to look back!
content:
George Cayley, arguably the father of aviation, conceived a prototype of the modern aeroplane in 1799. The first commercial flight  became reality on January 1, 1914, and flew from St. Petersburg to Tampa in Florida. It took one hundred fifteen years for this idea to take off.
Scientific innovations have always been relays and marathons, not sprints. Long painstaking journeys from pen-and-paper plans to tightening the final bolt. But generative AI is clearly the exception. The rapidity with which it has evolved is unlike any innovation in the history of mankind.Â
And this evolution has seemingly altered our brain chemistry. Case in point, at the fag end of October, Spain faced one of the deadliest floods in its history. It killed more than 200 people. It also gave the world one of the most talked about images showing the consequences of extreme weather events — floodwaters piling up dozens and dozens of cars on a street in Spain. But even as this very real photo  was widely shared, many believed it was AI-generated.Â
It's almost become second nature for many to count limbs and fingers when they see photos of people now, because even until very recently, generative AI had difficulty creating the right number of them — a quirk that will likely become a relic soon .Â
In the pursuit of separating what's real from what's not, we have armed ourselves with an arsenal of "detectors" — tools that use various metrics to deduce whether an image or video is real or AI-generated.Â
In contrast to today's hyperrealistic photos created using tools like Midjourney, most early AI-generated visuals were bizarre, surreal, and sometimes, unintentionally funny.Â
For instance, look at this 2017 AI-generated photo of a girl sitting at a restaurant with a pizza in front of her. One can barely make out what it's supposed to be. If one figuratively squints hard, they can probably identify what's supposed to be a pizza, and what's supposed to be a face.Â
Or this fruit stand — which can either be classified as a child's "art project" or a hitherto unseen expressionist masterpiece.
Were you scratching your head, wondering what this mess is? Don't worry, even our trusty detectors had trouble. Ranking detectors on old samples
We took three AI image samples, each created in 2017 , 2018 , and 2019  from online research repositories and tested them on five AI image detection tools. These tools are AI Or Not , Is It AI , Illuminarty.ai , Hive Moderation , and AI Image Detector .
All five tools correctly guessed the 2019 samples as AI-generated. But as we moved back in time, most of these tools had a hard time figuring things out.Â
Hive Moderation correctly — and confidently — declared all the samples as AI-generated. But AI Or Not and Illuminarty.ai were plagued with false results. More than half of the detectors failed to recognise the 2018 samples and even more fumbled the 2017 sample. The screenshots of all the detection test results can be seen here .
A spokesperson for Is It AI, one of the tools we tested, told India Today Fact Check: "Early AI-generated images lacked the sophisticated patterns and anomalies present in their recent counterparts. This could be one possible reason why the tools couldn't identify the older AI images." Â Notably, the 2017 and 2018 samples tested were of relatively lower resolution as compared to their counterparts from 2019. Gautham Koorma, a researcher at the UC Berkeley School of Information, told us that resolution plays an important role in detection accuracy. He explained, "Images smaller than 224x224 pixels may not match the expected input size for many modern neural networks." Detectors meet the strangers
Siwei Lyu, a professor of computer science and engineering at the University at Buffalo, told us that present AI detection tools have not been sufficiently trained on data for older image generation models that were replaced by better models very quickly.Â
Similarly, Dr Oren Etzioni, a researcher and the founder of TrueMedia, another AI detection tool, highlighted an important point: there are many types of AI-generated images from GAN  to diffusion , and detectors that haven't been trained on all the types cannot be expected to detect all types. A detector trained exclusively on GAN images may not perform well on diffusion-based images and vice versa.
Since generative adversarial networks or GAN images were introduced in 2014, AI-generated images have indeed come a long way . Within a decade, we went from images that looked like microscope slides  to images we fail to make out as synthetic.
In this cat-and-mouse game of generator versus detectors, it looks like the former will always get away by saying: "Catch me if you can!" - Ends Published By: Soumya Published On: Nov 29, 2024 17:31 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of 'hacker' claiming can tamper EVMs is from India Today sting
content:
The hacker Syed Shuja's claims regarding EVM hacking are false, seemingly intended to create mistrust in the Indian electoral process.
Following the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Mahayuti coalition's massive win in the Maharashtra Assembly, where it bagged 235 of the 288 seats, several Opposition leaders started raising questions about EVM tampering. Now, a video making the rounds online purports to show  a man claiming over a video call that he can hack EVMs.Â
Sharing the video, a Facebook user wrote , "This is how the EVM is hacked. A lot of details of how it's done and the cost involved in the latest election results in Maharashtra is revealed by the hacker."
In the video, the person claimed he could manipulate votes in 281 out of 288 Maharashtra Assembly seats. He explained that he could manipulate EVM signals using "frequency isolation" and specific applications on mobile phones and could pre-program EVMs to favour a particular party.Â
Mumbai Tak's watermark can be seen in the viral video. On Mumbai Tak's X account , we found this video shared on November 15. The post said the video was part of a sting operation. निवडणुकीआधी सर्वात मोठं स्टिंग ऑपरेशन,EVM हॅकिंगबाबत मोठा खुलासा #MaharashtraAssemblyElection #EVM #VidhanSabha pic.twitter.com/j8x9bP4PoC — Mumbai Tak (@mumbaitak) November 15, 2024
निवडणुकीआधी सर्वात मोठं स्टिंग ऑपरेशन,EVM हॅकिंगबाबत मोठा खुलासा #MaharashtraAssemblyElection #EVM #VidhanSabha pic.twitter.com/j8x9bP4PoC — Mumbai Tak (@mumbaitak) November 15, 2024
India Today journalists, posing as representatives of a political leader, contacted a hacker and recorded their interactions with him. The hacker explained his alleged methods of manipulating EVMs.
The man in the video call is Syed Shuja, a self-proclaimed cyber expert who claims to have worked with the Electronic Corporation of India Limited on EVM development from 2009 to 2014. The ECIL and Bharat Electronics Limited are public sector undertakings under the Ministry of Defence that manufacture EVMs and VVPATs for the Election Commission of India.
Shuja also claims to have a PhD minor in Mathematics from the Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University and a BTech degree in computer science from Shadan College, both in Hyderabad. No records of him reportedly exist at these institutions.Â
He claimed he was granted asylum in the US in 2018 after allegedly being attacked for discovering EVM tampering. However, we could not independently verify his claims of being attacked, his asylum status, or his current employment.
This is also not the first time that Shuja has claimed he can hack EVMs. On January 21, 2019, he held a press conference in London where he made several explosive claims.Â
Shuja in this sting failed to provide any concrete evidence to support his allegations. Hari Krishna Prasad Vemuru, a Hyderabad-based EVM expert who has previously been involved in EVM hacking debates, termed Shuja's arguments as "illogical".Â
Ajit Hatti, a cybersecurity expert, also debunked Shuja's claims about using Jio signals to manipulate EVMs, highlighting that Jio was not operational during the 2014 elections and that EVMs cannot communicate wirelessly. So, Shuja's explanations of "frequency isolation" for EVM manipulation appear to be false and without any technical foundation.Â
India Today's detailed video report on this viral video can be seen here .Â
The Election Commission of India termed Shuja's claims as baseless and lodged an FIR against him with the Delhi Police. The ECI has consistently maintained that EVMs are tamper-proof.Â
The ECIL was also quick to dismiss Shuja's allegations. His claims about working with the ECIL on EVM development were directly refuted by the company.Â
Thus, it's clear that Syed Shuja's claims regarding EVM hacking were false, seemingly intended to create mistrust in the Indian electoral process. - Ends Published By: Soumya Published On: Nov 29, 2024 19:04 IST

title: Fact Check: Arvind Kejriwal DID NOT snub Rahul Gandhi. Viral clip is edited
content:
This video is edited. The original video from the swearing-in ceremony of Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren showed Kejriwal greeting Gandhi before others.
Did Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal greet all INDIA bloc leaders except Rahul Gandhi at a recent public event? Many on social media claimed so, sharing a video , which has now gone viral on social media.Â
The video shows the former Delhi Chief Minister shaking hands with Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar, as Rahul Gandhi waits with his hand up on the stage. Rahul Gandhi then shakes hands with AAP's Raghav Chaddha. Meanwhile, Kejriwal goes ahead to greet Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge and West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee — seemingly skipping Rahul Gandhi altogether.Â
The viral clip ends with Kejriwal, Chaddha, and Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann waving their hands from the stage and going ahead to greet Samajwadi Party leader Akhilesh Yadav and Rashtriya Janata Dal leader Tejashwi Yadav, sitting further away from Rahul Gandhi.Â
Hinting at a crisis within the INDIA bloc, one person shared the video on Facebook, writing, "Kejriwal did not shake hands with Rahul Gandhi. It is clear that AAP is not in the mood to give Congress any importance in the Delhi elections." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video was edited. In the original video from the swearing-in ceremony of Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Kejriwal could be seen greeting Rahul Gandhi. OUR PROBEÂ
At the top right corner of the viral video, the news agency ANI's logo was visible. With the help of this clue, we found the video shared on the official X account of ANI on November 28. The post stated the video showed Kejriwal arriving at the swearing-in ceremony of Hemant Soren with his wife Sunita Kejriwal, MP Raghav Chaddha, and Bhagwant Mann. The clip was credited to Jharkhand government's Jhargov TV.Â
On the official YouTube channel of Jhargov TV, we found the full video of the oath-taking ceremony, streamed live on November 28. In it, at 2 hours 56 minutes, Kejriwal arrives with Raghav Chaddha and goes straight to Rahul Gandhi and shakes his hands. This part has been clipped out of the viral video.Â
Rahul Gandhi then tried to shake hands with Chaddha, but Kejriwal at the time was standing between them. It is thus, clear that Kejriwal not only shook hands with Gandhi but did so before greeting any other leader present on the stage.
Hemant Soren was sworn in as the 14th Chief Minister of Jharkhand at the Morabadi Ground in Ranchi on November 28, 2024.
Jharkhand governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar administered the oath of office and secrecy to Soren. Top leaders of the INDIA bloc were present at the swearing-in ceremony.Â
On November 21, the AAP released its first list of 11 candidates for the Delhi Assembly elections, scheduled to be held in February 2025. This list surprised many who were rooting for Congress and the AAP to fight the elections together.Â
Congress' Delhi unit chief Devender Yadav attacked the AAP multiple times, with his most recent statement being that the people of Delhi were fed up with the AAP government and had lost faith in the party.Â
However, Gandhi and Kejriwal haven't shown signs of falling out publicly — at least at the time of writing this report.
Thus, it's clear the viral video was edited and does not show Arvind Kejriwal snubbing Rahul Gandhi. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Nov 29, 2024 19:23 IST

title: Fact Check: No income tax for senior citizens 75 and above?
content:
The Centre has not given any tax relief to all senior citizens who are above 75 years of age.
A message being shared on social media claims that senior citizens above 75 years of age would not have to pay income tax any more.Â
A part of the viral post  reads, "The Modi government will not have to pay tax to the senior citizens of the country, because on the completion of 75 years of India's independence, senior citizens above 75 years of age will no longer have to pay tax on their income. According to the information given by the Central Board of Direct Taxes, the central government has changed the law to provide tax exemption to senior citizens, which includes important changes between Rule 31, Rule 31A, Form 16 and 24Q, and senior citizens above 75 years of age will have to submit a 12-BBA application to the bank to get tax exemption."
India Today Fact Check found the Centre has not given any tax relief to senior citizens above the age of 75.Â
Had there been any such announcement about tax relief for senior citizens, it would have been a big story. But, we could not find any credible news reports regarding the viral claim.
Instead, we found several reports on a statement about tax relief for senior citizens, which was recently made by Minister of State Finance Pankaj Choudhary in the Lower House of Parliament. According to a report  in Business Today, the Centre recently informed the House that currently no proposals are being considered by the government regarding tax relief for senior citizens.
We then found a post  made by the central government's Press Information Bureau. PIB Fact Check called the viral message fake. The post reads: "Senior citizens above 75 years, with only pension and interest income, are exempt from filing ITR (as per Section 194P). Taxes, if applicable, are deducted by the specified bank after computing the income and eligible deductions." ✔️Senior citizens above 75 years, with only pension and interest income, are exempt from filing ITR (as per Section 194P) ✔️Taxes, if applicable, are deducted by the specified bank after computing the income and eligible deductions
— PIB Fact Check (@PIBFactCheck) November 28, 2024 Do senior citizens get tax relief? Section 194P of the Income Tax Act, 1961 , provides conditions for exempting senior citizens from filing income tax returns aged 75 years and above. For senior citizens, the basic exemption limit is fixed at Rs 3 lakh income per annum. Super senior citizens, resident Indians who are 80 years and above, do not have to pay any tax or file returns up to Rs 5 lakh annual total income. Thus, it is clear that the viral message is misleading. - Ends Published By: Soumya Published On: Nov 29, 2024 22:53 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Andhra Pradesh DID NOT abolish Waqf Boards
content:
No, Andhra Pradesh did not abolish its Waqf Board. It only dissolved the existing board, which was inactive, to form a new committee.
As the Waqf Board debate continued in Parliament, the internet saw a flood of posts that claimed a National Democratic Alliance partner had abolished it in Andhra Pradesh. Several television channels reported the issue inaccurately, giving credence to these claims.
Reports from primetime news called this a "surgical strike" by Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu's administration. Many, including the Bharatiya Janata Party's Amit Malviya , shared posts praising this alleged move.Â
An X user wrote , "Chandra Babu & Pawan Kalyan does surgical strike on Waqf Board. Andhra Govt has abolished the Waqf in the state." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the Andhra Pradesh government has not abolished the Waqf Board's operations in the state; it has only dissolved the existing, defunct board.
A keyword search revealed several news reports in The News Minute , The Times of India , and The Economic Times . According to these reports, on November 30, the Andhra Pradesh government issued government order No. 75, which revoked government order No. 47, issued by the previous government on October 21, 2023. Order No. 47 elected three members and nominated seven others to the state's 11-member Waqf Board. The new order issued by the Andhra Pradesh Government can be viewed here .
A review of order No. 75 revealed reasons for the dissolution of the Waqf Board. The Andhra Pradesh High Court stayed the election of a board chairperson in November 2023. On November 29 this year, the CEO of the Andhra Pradesh Waqf Board raised concerns about the board's non-functioning and mentioned 13 writ petitions challenging its legality, fearing an administrative vacuum. Following this, the government decided to dissolve the current committee.
An India TV report contained a statement from Andhra Pradesh's Minority Welfare Minister, NMD Farooq, regarding the decision to dissolve the Waqf Board. Farooq stated that controversial appointments under order No. 47 led to legal challenges, with individuals approaching the state high court.Â
On November 1, 2023, the court temporarily halted the selection process for the Chairman of the Waqf Board, causing legal and administrative uncertainty. He emphasised, "The government will take the necessary steps to transparently manage Waqf properties. The welfare of minorities is a top priority for us."
An India Today report published on December 1 also said the Telugu Desam Party government led by N Chandrababu Naidu in Andhra Pradesh will withdraw the orders issued for the state Waqf Board during the previous YSR Congress regime and form a new board soon. The report also states that the earlier order was revoked, pointing out that the Waqf Board has remained inactive due to the lack of insufficient representation of Sunni and Shia scholars and former Parliamentarians, which led to the stalling of Waqf activities.
Additionally, the Andhra Pradesh Government's official fact-check unit issued a clarification on December 1. It noted the state government will take "appropriate measures to address these defects and constitute a new Waqf Board at the earliest." The Andhra Pradesh Waqf Board has remained non-functional since March 2023, leading to a period of administrative stagnation. The withdrawal of G.O. Ms. No. 47 became imperative due to several substantive concerns. These include 13 writ petitions challenging its validity, the… https://t.co/0yXCvIdK4q — FactCheck.AP.Gov.in (@FactCheckAPGov) December 1, 2024
The Andhra Pradesh Waqf Board has remained non-functional since March 2023, leading to a period of administrative stagnation. The withdrawal of G.O. Ms. No. 47 became imperative due to several substantive concerns. These include 13 writ petitions challenging its validity, the… https://t.co/0yXCvIdK4q — FactCheck.AP.Gov.in (@FactCheckAPGov) December 1, 2024
India Today Fact Check also spoke to L Abdul Khadir, the former CEO of the Andhra Pradesh Waqf Board. He said, "The previous board was dissolved due to several challenges, including the lack of a chairperson. It is understood that the government has begun the process of forming a new board, and we hope it will be established soon." Â
Thus, it is clear that the viral claims are misleading. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Dec 2, 2024 20:08 IST

title: Fact Check: Deepfake of India Today anchor, Elon Musk used to dupe people
content:
This is a deepfake video. The original Elon Musk video was about his meeting with PM Modi in 2023.
Get-rich-quick schemes on social media promoted through deepfakes are one of the most commonly used tactics by scammers. Case in point, here's a video of India Today news director Rahul Kanwal talking about an investment platform created by billionaire Elon Musk. It goes on to claim that even Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi allegedly uses it.Â
"Indians are in shock. Narendra Modi is secretly making millions of rupees per month using a financial programme created by Elon Musk for all residents of India," says the deepfake version of Rahul Kanwal, before the video switches to the owner of X, Tesla, and SpaceX.
Deepfake Musk says that he created this programme to liberate millions of Indians from "financial struggles and physical labour", adding that a Rs 21,000 investment yields about Rs 8 lakh per week — with some even earning Rs 30 lakh. How do you earn big bucks like this? Deepfake Musk claims you need to do nothing. All you have to do is register and wait for a "confirmation call" and then the programme allegedly does all the work for you. He also thanked PM Modi and Nandan Nilekani for helping him create the platform.Â
This ridiculously obvious deepfake has been viewed almost five lakh times. But in fairness to its viewers, many in the comments pointed out this was an obvious scam.Â
There are obvious clues that point out that this is a scam which has nothing to do with either Musk, Modi or Rahul Kanwal.
First and foremost, Rahul Kanwal's voice in this video sounds nothing like his actual voice.Â
Second, his deepfake was most likely made using footage from this India Today news report .Â
The show, "Operation Digital Arrest: India Today Exposes Digital Arrest Scam With Proof" was aired by India Today on television and various digital platforms on October 28. India Today's Special Investigation Team uncovered a digital fraud scheme involving fake couriers, fake cops, and fake government officials.Â
Third, the Elon Musk videos where he is talking to reporters and where he's seen interacting with PM Modi are from June 2023. The two met in New York during PM Modi's three-day visit to the United States. After the meeting, Musk expressed his desire to visit India and also called himself a "fan of Modi". You can see an India Today report featuring the original video of Elon Musk speaking and interacting with PM Modi below.
So, this is clearly a scam being advertised through deepfakes of Rahul Kanwal and Elon Musk. Surprisingly, when you click on the link accompanying the video, you're redirected to mosostats.com, a website that lists tech conferences in India in 2024-25.
Clicking on any of the listed events redirects you to principal.dev, a website that sells euro 999 "masterclasses".Â
These kinds of deepfake-powered schemes and scams are a dime a dozen. Here are a couple of stories featuring Mukesh Ambani's deepfakes . And this is also not the first time India Today reporters and anchors have been deepfaked. A deepfake of India Today anchor Rajdeep Sardesai  promoting a miraculous hypertension drug was once widely shared. On another occasion, Aaj Tak's Anjana Om Kashyap was similarly deepfaked . - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Dec 2, 2024 20:53 IST

title: Fact Check: Bengal village ritual FALSELY shared as Hindu temples' vandalism in Bangladesh
content:
This video is from a Kali Pooja which takes place every 12 years at the Sultanpur Kali temple in West Bengal's Purba Bardhman district.
Amid the coup in Bangladesh that led to the ouster of Sheikh Hasina, there were many allegations of persecution of Hindus in the country. Following the arrest of ISKCON priest Chinmoy Krishna Das on sedition charges, these allegations came to the forefront once again.
Now, a video allegedly showing a Kali temple being vandalised by Muslims in Bangladesh is making the rounds on social media. The clip shows two men trying to take an idol's head off as a crowd surrounds it. Another headless idol can be seen by its side.Â
Sharing the clip on X, one person wrote , "Yesterday in Bangladesh, Muslims attacked Kalibari i.e. Kali temple and destroyed the idols of Mother Kali and all the Hindu gods and goddesses. And the Hindu devotees present inside the temple were beaten. More than 20 Hindu devotees are badly injured. But the whole world is silent on the massacre of Hindus in Bangladesh." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is neither from Bangladesh nor does it show a temple being vandalised. This video is from a Kali Pooja that takes place every 12 years in the Sultanpur Kali temple in West Bengal's Purba Bardhman district.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook post  from November 29 which contained the same clip. According to this post, the video is from a "Sultanpur Kali Mata Niranjan". The location of the video said it's from Khandaghosh, a village in the Purba Bardhman district of West Bengal. An Instagram post  from November 30 also featured the viral clip and called it the 12-year tradition of "Kalimata Niranjan" in Sultanpur.      View this post on Instagram            A post shared by R@ghu nath Dey (@dey_raghu_) A subsequent keyword search led us to a Facebook post from November 26 on a page called the Sultanpur Kiranamayi Pathagraha , a library situated in Sultanpur in West Bengal's Purba Bardhman district. The caption in Bangla said these videos were from a Goddess Kali prayer which takes place once every 12 years. It also mentioned that this programme was organised by Sultanpur Kiranamayi Pathagraha. The Facebook post has several videos of prayers being offered in the same temple. A comparison can be seen below. We then contacted Devashish, a member of the Sultanpur library. He told India Today Fact Check that the video was from the same temple in Sultanpur. He also refuted the viral claims and mentioned that this was a religious ritual. Devashish explained: "On November 26, 2024, all goddess Kali devotees gathered in Sultanpur Kali temple for Kali Mata Niranjan. We performed prayer in front of the idol of Goddess Kali, which is 13 feet tall. The idol's height and weight prevent it from being taken for the visarjan (immersion). Hence, we immerse the idol in parts. The viral video shows the moment after the prayer when devotees take body parts of the goddess for immersion." Devashish also stated that there was no communal angle in the viral clip. advertisement We saw several Facebook videos , which showed devotees holding the head and various body parts of goddess Kali's idol and taking them for the immersion ritual. The crowd seen in these videos can be seen dancing and celebrating as well. We could also locate the temple on Google Maps. A comparison of the Sultanpur Kali Temple's images on Google Maps and videos from the prayer day can be seen below. It also corroborates the fact that the temple is not in Bangladesh but in West Bengal. We also reached out to Khandagosh police sub-inspector Rakesh Roushan, who said this is a years-old tradition that devotees perform while praying to Goddess Kali. He said, "The priest first takes the head of the idol and immerses it into the pond. Then the devotees take various body parts, carry out a procession in celebration, and immerse them." Roushan also refuted the viral claims about the video being from Bangladesh or any communal angle attached to it. On November 30, various news reports mentioned at least three attacks on Hindu temples in Bangladesh following the arrest of ISKCON priest Chinmoy Krishna Das. But the viral clip does not show any such attack. advertisement (With inputs from Surajuddin Mondal) - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Dec 2, 2024 23:12 IST

title: Fact Check: Muslim shrine demolished in Bangladesh now viral as Hindu temple
content:
This video shows the shrine of Muslim saint Hazrat Baba Ali Pagla being destroyed in Sirajganj, Bangladesh.
On November 30, various news outlets reported at least three attacks on Hindu temples in Bangladesh following the arrest of ISKCON priest Chinmoy Krishna Das on sedition charges. A video now going viral on social media allegedly shows Muslims destroying a Hindu temple in Bangladesh. The footage shows several people, many sporting skull caps, demolishing a building.Â
An X user shared the clip on December 2 and wrote "See how Hindu temples were vandalised, and Hindu devotees were beaten up in different cities of Bangladesh yesterday. But the whole world is silent on the massacre of Hindus in Bangladesh." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video from August 29 shows locals destroying the shrine of a Muslim saint Hazrat Baba Ali Pagla in Bangladesh's Sirajganj.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video directed us to the same clip  shared by a Facebook user on August 30. The post said the clip was from the shrine of Hazrat Baba Ali Pagla.
A subsequent search led us to a video on the official YouTube channel of Bangladeshi news outlet Metro TV on August 29. A detailed analysis of the video reveals a direct match with the viral clip. The headline of the video said this showed the shrine of Ali Pagla, located in Kazipur in Bangladesh's Sirajganj, being demolished.
On August 31, a report was published by the Bangladeshi news outlet Kal Bela, which featured a screenshot from the viral video. The report stated that on August 29, the shrine of the Muslim saint Hazrat Baba Ali Pagla was demolished in Shalgram, located in the Mansurnagar union of the Kazipur upazila in Bangladesh's Sirajganj district. The demolition was carried out under the direction of Golam Rabbani, a local imam. Following this, Rabbani was reportedly dismissed from his position.
A report in BDNews24 said Shalgram locals were angry with the imam, the primary accused in the demolition of the shrine. One local said, "How can Golam Rabbani, as a Muslim, destroy the shrine of another Muslim? Therefore, we have decided not to pray behind such an Imam and have dismissed him from his position."
Thus, it's clear the viral clip does not show a Hindu temple being demolished.
(Written By Surajuddin Mondal) - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Dec 3, 2024 17:46 IST

title: Fact Check: Old clip of Bangladesh brawl falsely shared as recent Hindu persecution
content:
Although both parties here belong to different religions, the incident dates back to June 2022 and shows a clash between two families over a land dispute.
Amid reports of anti-Hindu violence in Bangladesh, a video allegedly showing Muslim men attacking Hindu women in the country was widely shared. In the video , two men can be seen beating up a group of women with sticks and unleashing punches. This clip was shared with captions like, "Radical Muslims are openly trying to kill Hindu women!"
Such posts were also shared with hashtags like "Save Bangladeshi Hindus", "Hindu Genocide In Bangladesh", and "Free Chinmoy Krishna Das" — the last one referring to the Hindu priest who was recently charged with sedition in Bangladesh. Radical Muslims are openly trying to kill Hindu women!! #SaveBangladeshiHindus #HinduGenocideInBangladesh #FreeChinmayKrishnaDas #FreeChinmoyKrishnaPrabhu @tathagata2 pic.twitter.com/fvPnXs8MNf — Sayan Chakraborty (@sayan2024) December 3, 2024
Radical Muslims are openly trying to kill Hindu women!! #SaveBangladeshiHindus #HinduGenocideInBangladesh #FreeChinmayKrishnaDas #FreeChinmoyKrishnaPrabhu @tathagata2 pic.twitter.com/fvPnXs8MNf — Sayan Chakraborty (@sayan2024) December 3, 2024
India Today Fact Check has found that the video is more than two years old and unrelated to the present unrest.
Upon reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video, we found a YouTube video on the channel of Prothom Alo, a leading Bangladeshi news outlet. The video was dated June 3, 2022, making it evident that the incident predated even the ouster of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina.Â
According to the YouTube video, this incident took place in the Sitakund region of Chittagong. Reportedly, the two sides brawled over plucking jamun, also known as black plum or Indian blackberry. Reportedly, one of the women got injured during this and was later admitted to a hospital.
A Dhaka Tribune report noted this incident took place on June 2, 2022, and three women seen in the video were identified as Rani Das, Anjana Das, and Rima Das. The men were identified as Touhidul Islam and Alamgir.
Tapan Das, Rani's brother-in-law, told reporters that male members of their family live abroad. Hence, Touhidul's family tried to forge the documents to take over their land — adding that trouble between the two families had been going on for years. However, on June 2, 2022, when Rani and Rima saw Touhidul plucking berries from a tree, they went to stop them. Then, Touhidul attacked them. The local police said that Rani Das accused nine people in her complaint.
We also found another news report  from June 3, 2022, featuring a copy of a complaint filed by Touhidul against the Das family alleging they had threatened him over the disputed land for many years and that they had hit his son with an iron rod. Another report , however, quotes the local police official stating that the main accused, Touhidul was later arrested.
Thus, it is clear that although the video originally featured two groups from different religions, it is more than a couple of years old and related to a land dispute. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Dec 3, 2024 19:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of man floating away on waterlogged street is NOT from Chennai
content:
This is an old video from Pune, not Chennai. However, waterlogging has been reported in Chennai after heavy rains hit the region due to Cyclone Fengal.
Several districts of Tamil Nadu are in the grips of floods triggered by Cyclone Fengal. The cyclone has wreaked havoc across 14 districts of the southern state and affected 1.5 crore people, announced Chief Minister MK Stalin on December 2. Â
An unusual video now going viral purports to show a man floating along a waterlogged road in a crate in the Marina Beach area of Chennai.Â
An X user shared the video and wrote: "#CycloneFengal Vote for Freebies & Enjoy Boat ride on Road." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today found that this is an old video from Pune.Â
With the help of a reverse image search, we found that the video was shared  on June 8 on the Instagram account "dj_praful_official_". It was captioned: "Yerwada part 2." The account had shared another similar video on June 4 and captioned it: "Yerwada." This one featured a man floating away on a mattress on the same waterlogged road.Â
Yerwada is an area in the Pune district of Maharashtra. The Instagram user, Praful Sonawane, mentioned in his profile that he lives in Pune.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Praful Sonawane (@dj_praful_official_)
A post shared by Praful Sonawane (@dj_praful_official_)
The first video went viral on social media at the time when a torrential downpour waterlogged Pune's streets. Many news organisations published stories  about the video and said it was from Pune.Â
India Today also geolocated the street seen in the viral video. A board for the Deutsche Bank Group can be seen on a building behind the waterlogged street. Using this information, we found the building in Yerawada, Pune, on Google Street View. Â
The fact-checking unit of the Tamil Nadu government also debunked the claim that this video was from Chennai's Marina Beach. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Dec 4, 2024 20:45 IST

title: Fact Check: No, Pankaj Tripathi DID NOT campaign against the BJP in an ad. This video is edited
content:
The viral video is edited. In the original video, part of a UPI safety awareness campaign, Pankaj Tripathi only spoke about UPI fraud. He did not mention the BJP at all.
As political parties gear up for Assembly elections in Delhi scheduled for February 2025, the Aam Aadmi Party shared a video on December 5 featuring actor Pankaj Tripathi campaigning against the Bhartiya Janata Party. While this post has since been deleted, its archive can be seen here .
Starring as a peanut seller in the video, Tripathi says, "I sell peanuts, not my brain. Look at this message BJP has sent. It says, 'Vote for us, we will bring development.' Do you think I don't know anything? Here I will vote for them, and government money will disappear there. I am a peanut seller, not a fool. Remember, if the BJP tempts you, say, 'I am not a fool.'"Â
The official social media accounts of AAP Rajasthan and AAP Seelampur , along with several others , also shared this video.
India Today Fact Check found that the video was edited. The original video is a public service announcement and Pankaj Tripathi was talking about UPI frauds — not the BJP.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a Facebook post dated September 23. The video in this post appeared to be the same. But it had a few noticeable differences. In this version, Tripathi was talking about UPI fraud. He did not mention the BJP in the video.
Also, in this video, when Tripathi shows his phone screen, the photo on the device reads "Winner. Congrats! You have won a lottery of Rs 25,00,000! To claim your prize, click here," followed by a hyperlink. In the viral clip, this was replaced with the BJP's symbol and the text: "Vote for BJP". A comparison between the two can be seen here.
In November 2023 , the National Payments Corporation of India or the NPCI announced its collaboration with actor Pankaj Tripathi, appointing him as its "UPI Safety Ambassador". In September this year, the Indian instant payment system Unified Payments Interface or UPI rolled out an ad campaign called "Main Moorkh Nahi Hoon", featuring Tripathi as a peanut seller who received a fraudulent lottery message. It was made to raise awareness about scams related to digital payment services.
An NPCI press release dated November 6 noted the public sector company launched a UPI Safety Awareness Campaign. The campaign conceptualised by Ogilvy would feature Tripathi in a series of six ad films, highlighting common tactics used by scammers.Â
As of now, three such ads featuring Pankaj Tripathi as a peanut seller , a betel seller , and a business executive , have been released. India Today Fact Check also reached out to Pankaj Tripathi's PR team for a comment regarding the viral video. The story will be updated when we receive a response.
It is thus, clear that the video was edited to show Pankaj Tripathi campaigning against the BJP. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Dec 5, 2024 14:17 IST

title: Fact Check: This under-construction road is nowhere near Jammu and Kashmir!
content:
The viral video shows the construction of the G6911 Anlai Expressway in China, also known as the Ankang–Laifeng Expressway.
A video of an under-construction highway has been widely shared on social media. It shows a road being built with large bridges over a mountainside. Those sharing it claimed it was the National Highway 14 project underway in Jammu and Kashmir.
One Facebook post  containing the clip stated: "Massive project connecting Srinagar, Jammu and Ladakh will be completed soon. How much do you rate development under central rule?" Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video actually shows the construction of the G6911 Ankang-Laifeng Expressway in China. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral clip led us to a similar video shared on the Facebook page "Mike China Vlog" on August 22 . It was captioned: "The G6911 Anlai Expressway links Ankang in Shaanxi to Laifeng in Hubei, passing through stunning landscapes, including Chongqing. A scenic route connecting cultural treasures!"
A subsequent keyword search revealed another clear video of a similar road construction shared by the LinkedIn account "Civil Engineers World". The post states that this highway construction was taking place in Fengjie County, Chongqing, China. A similar video was also shared as a reel on the Instagram page "Living China".     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Sharing Travel (@livingchina) Another video of the construction of the Anlai Expressway in Fengjie County was shared on the YouTube page "Son Of China"  on June 12, 2024. The massive pillars seen in the viral video and the arch bridge across the river in the distance are clearly visible in this video. Another bridge can also be seen in the YouTube video. A search based on this clue revealed that these are the bridges across the Meixi River in Fengjie County. Google Maps  has photos of these two bridges and some construction work taking place nearby. The Ankang-Laifeng Expressway , known as the Anlai Expressway G6911, starts at the Huangyanghe Interchange of the Shitian Expressway in Hanbin District, Ankang City, Shaanxi Province, and ends at the Laifeng Interchange in Laifeng County, Enshi Prefecture, Hubei Province. It is 446.26 kilometres long. Meanwhile, the NH14 is not in Jammu and Kashmir at all. The highway starts at the NH-12 junction in Morgram, Murshidabad district, West Bengal, and connects Rampurhat, Siuri, Raniganj, Bankura, Garbeta, and Salbani before ending at the NH16 junction near Kharagpur . advertisement Incidentally, another video of a bridge from China was earlier shared as the still-in-construction NH44 in Jammu and Kashmir. You can read our fact-check about that here . Thus, it's clear a video from China was falsely shared as an Indian infra project. - Ends Published By: Sudeep Lavania Published On: Dec 6, 2024 12:50 IST

title: Fact Check: Video of Kurdish woman captured by Syrian rebel fighters is 5 years old, not recent
content:
This video is from 2019. However, the woman was indeed a Kurdish fighter who was captured by Turkey-backed forces in Syria.
After a week-long offensive in Syria, the rebel group Hayat Tahrir al-Sham claimed on Sunday, December 8, it gained control of the capital Damascus and overthrew President Bashar al-Assad's regime. As per a report in the Middle East Eye, tens of thousands of Syrian Kurds fled Aleppo, Syria' second-largest city, after its takeover by rebel groups including Hayat Tahrir al-Sham and the Turkey-backed Syrian National Army.Â
Now, a video of a masked man in combat fatigues carrying a woman in his arms is being widely shared on social media. Allegedly the man was a Hayat Tahrir al-Sham terrorist and the woman a Kurdistan Workers' Party worker.Â
A Facebook post containing the video read: "Breaking, One of Tahrir al-Sham's terrorists captures a Kurdish woman from the PKK and is taking her as booty. And another says Ah slaughter oh, slaughter. And these terrorists come out after reciting La Ilah is this Islam?". Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today found the video is not from the ongoing tension in Syria; it's from 2019. However, the woman was a Kurdish fighter who was captured by Turkey-backed forces in Syria.Â
Notably, the Syrian National Army and Kurdish forces have been fighting  against each other for a long time. Turkey considers Syrian Kurdish fighters terrorists. There are also reports of war crimes by Turkey-backed rebel forces on Syrian Kurds.
Reportedly, the Syrian National Army and the Hayat Tahrir al-Sham were working as a coalition to topple the Assad regime. Though Turkey has rejected claims of any involvement in the latest offensive, Kurdish force say that Turkey-backed fighters participated in it. OUR PROBEÂ
With the help of a reverse image search, we found the viral video in an X post shared by a news organization called Rudaw English. It claimed the Kurdish woman fighter was Cicek Kobane. She was captured alive by Turkey-backed militia. As per the video report dated October 26, 2019, Kobane was a member of the Kurdish Women's Protection Units. The group had called on the international community to intervene to save Kobane .
Turkish news outlet TRT World in an October 2019 video report about the incident noted the woman was captured in Ayn Issa in Syria. This report also contained a separate clip of Kobane in which, as per TRT World, she said that she was treated well by the forces.Â
Kobane was accused of organising terror attacks against civilians and Turkish security forces. In March 2021, she was sentenced to life imprisonment by a Turkish court on multiple charges including attempted murder, a Kurdish news outlet reported.Â
Thus, it's clear this incident is not recent but more than five years old. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Dec 9, 2024 09:31 IST

title: Fact Check: First photo of ousted Bashar al-Assad taking refuge in Moscow? Nope, this is from 2023
content:
The photo is from February 2023 when Assad and his wife visited a hospital in Aleppo, Syria, to meet earthquake victims.
A lightning offensive by Syrian rebels overthrew Bashar al-Assad's regime, reportedly forcing him to flee the country. As per reports, Assad and his family have been granted asylum in Russia's capital, Moscow. Kremlin sources reportedly told Russian news agencies TASS and RIA Novosti that Assad and his family were granted asylum on humanitarian grounds.Â
Now, a photo allegedly showing Assad after landing in Moscow is going viral. The photo was widely shared on Facebook  and X . Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral photo is from February 2023 when Assad and his wife visited a hospital in Aleppo to meet earthquake victims.
With the help of keywords, we found a video on the YouTube channel of the Syrian radio station Sham FM TV , uploaded on February 10, 2023. The video report detailed Bashar al-Assad's visit to Aleppo University Hospital to meet earthquake victims. The beginning of the video shows the same visuals as seen in the viral photo.Â
Syria Stream, a digital news platform, also uploaded a video on YouTube regarding Assad's hospital visit on February 10, 2023. This video also shows the same visuals of Assad with his wife and others after nine seconds.Â
Pictures of Assad's visit were also shared by the X account of the Syrian President at that time. The images show Assad and his wife in the same attire as seen in the viral photo. في أول محطة من زيارة الرئيس الأسد والسيدة أسماء الأسد إلى مدينة حلب توجها إلى مشفى حلب الجامعي للاطمئنان على حالة المصابين والمتضررين من الزلزال واستمعا منهم إلى أوضاعهم واحتياجاتهم. pic.twitter.com/CMfMthOZk2 — Syrian Presidency (@Presidency_Sy) February 10, 2023 The Turkey-Syria earthquake  of February 2023 killed more than fifty thousand people, of which over seven thousand died in Syria. At the time of publishing this on December 9, there were no publicly available photos of the deposed Bashar al-Assad from Moscow. Thus, it's clear the viral photo has nothing to do with Assad fleeing to Moscow. - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Dec 9, 2024 20:35 IST

title: Fact Check: This 500-year-old ancient Torah was NOT recovered from Assad's palace in Syria
content:
This video is not from Syria, but from Tunisia and dates back to March 2017.
Crowds roaming Bashar al-Assad's presidential palace found Louis Vuitton suitcases, luxury cars including Aston Martins and a Lamborghini, and much more — indications of how much wealth the deposed tyrant had accumulated as Syria suffered. Amongst the many videos of people looting Assad's palace, one clip claimed to show a rare Torah scroll, nearly 500 years old, that was found in the basement. A Torah scroll is a handwritten copy of the first five books of the Bible and is an essential part of the Jewish faith.
This video shows uniformed personnel unfolding a roll of a manuscript that appears ancient. In the latter part, the personnel are seen exchanging words with the journalists. This clip was shared across social media platforms with captions like: "This morning, an ancient 500-year-old Torah scroll was discovered in the basement of Bashar Al-Assad's palace in Damascus. Here is a short video of it. We are living through history almost every day!"
India Today Fact Check has found that the video is more than seven years old and from Tunisia, not Syria.
Responding to one such post, many Instagram users pointed out in comments that this clip is from 2017.
A reverse search of keyframes from the viral video led us to the original version shared by a Tunisian news outlet named Attessia TV Channel Nine  on March 14, 2017. This made it evident that the video can not be related to the toppled Assad regime in Syria.
The Arabic caption of this post suggested that the Torah manuscript discovered was more than 500 years old. Subsequent searches led us to an Al Jazeera report from March 17, 2017, that said this manuscript was seized by the Tunisian Ministry of Interior just as smugglers were trying to transport it to Europe.
This report mentioned that the manuscript was in Hebrew and the National Heritage Institute confirmed that it was from the 15th century and was a rare historical artefact of high value.
The Times of Israel in its report from March 12, 2017, mentioned that the scroll was made of ox skin and contained all five books of the Torah: Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, and Deuteronomy.
Thus, it is safe to conclude that a 2017 video from Tunisia, a nation in Africa, was falsely shared in connection to the Assad regime's fall in Syria. - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Dec 10, 2024 22:09 IST

title: Fact Check: Old, unrelated photos of Hindu idols FALSELY linked to Sambhal mosque survey
content:
The photos have no links to Sambhal. Three of the photos show idols recovered in Karnataka in February. The Sudarshan Chakra seen in the fourth photo is listed on an online shopping site.
Four photos of idols of Hindu Gods and a religious artefact are making the rounds on social media. Those sharing these photos claim these idols were found during the survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid in Uttar Pradesh's Sambhal.
A survey was initiated on November 19 following a petition filed by Supreme Court lawyer Vishnu Shankar Jain who claimed a temple existed earlier at the site of the mosque. On November 24, violence broke out in Sambhal, killing four when the Mughal-era mosque was surveyed for the second time.
Sharing the photos of the idols, one person wrote on Facebook , "1500 AD Vishnu Murti statue, Sudarshana Chakra, Hindu symbols found in Sambhal Masjid survey. Every Hindu share and save Hinduism." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the viral photos have no links to Sambhal. Three of the photos show idols recovered in Karnataka in February, while the Sudarshan Chakra, seen in the fourth photo, is listed on an online shopping site. Our Probe
Reverse searching the photos led us to an NDTV report  from February 7 that said a centuries-old Vishnu idol and a Shivling were found near the Telangana-Karnataka border from the Krishna riverbed.Â
These idols were recovered during the construction of a bridge in Raichur, Karnataka, in February. News reports added that these idols could date back a thousand years and were now in the possession of the Archaeological Survey of India. A TV9 Kannada report dated February 6 contained photos of these idols shot from different angles. All three photos of the idols featured in the viral collage are present in this report.
We then reverse-searched the circular artefact and found it on the Indiamart shopping website. This product, listed as Brass Sudarshanachakra Kalasham, is being sold online. The seller is Kolcharam Art Creations, a company based in Nagole, Telangana.
Anoop Sharma, India Today's correspondent from Sambhal, stated that the idols and artefacts had nothing to do with Sambhal, adding that the survey report has not yet been submitted to the court.Â
We also reached out to Mashhoor Ali Khan, secretary of the Sambhal mosque. He told India Today Fact Check that no such idols are present in the mosque, ruling out the question of them being found in the survey.Â
It is noteworthy that the Sambhal Advocates Commissioner who surveyed the Shahi Jama Masjid has requested a 15-day extension for submitting the survey report on the grounds of health issues. The court has, however, not passed any order and fixed January 8  as the next date of hearing, due to the Supreme Court's stay on the trial court proceedings in the Sambhal mosque case.
It is thus clear that at the time of writing this report, no Hindu idols had been found at the Sambhal mosque. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Dec 11, 2024 20:06 IST

title: Fact Check: This brawl DID NOT take place during the first meeting of Syria's new government
content:
This clip is from August 2024 and has nothing to do with Syria's newly appointed interim government. The clash took place during a meeting of lawyers in Afrin, Aleppo.
Following the toppling of the Bashar al-Assad government, Syrian rebels appointed Mohammed al-Bashir as the caretaker prime minister of the country. As per a report in Outlook magazine, the transitional government in Syria will remain until March 1, 2025. Following his appointment, Bashir chaired a meeting  in Damascus to discuss the transfer of portfolios and institutions.
Now a video of a fistfight between people in a public hall has gone viral on social media with the claim that the brawl broke out during the first official meeting held by the newly appointed Syrian government.Â
This video was widely circulated on X and Facebook . Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that the video is from August 2024 and has nothing to do with Syria's interim government. The clash took place during a meeting of lawyers in Aleppo.Â
A reverse image search of the video led us to a Facebook post  from August 10. The post featuring the viral video had the Arabic hashtag "Free Lawyers Association". This makes it clear that the video could not be from the recent meeting of the interim Syrian government.Â
We also found an Arabic report about the viral video published by the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights. The report published on August 10 said that a fistfight broke out inside a branch of Gaziantep University in Afrin, Aleppo governorate, between a delegation headed by the Minister of Justice in the "Syrian Interim Government" and lawyers of the "Free Lawyers Council".Â
The Free Lawyers Council had reportedly accused the minister of creating divisions within the Bar Association. A video report published by the Syrian news outlet Syrian TV said there were disagreements between the lawyers and the Syrian interim government that led to this brawl.Â
Thus, we can conclude that the video has nothing to do with the new Syrian government. - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Dec 11, 2024 20:30 IST

title: Fact Check: This is NOT Bengaluru techie Atul Shubhash's wife Nikita Singhania
content:
Atul Subhash's brother Bikas Modi has confirmed to India Today that this woman is not his brother's wife, Nikita Singhania.
Thirty-four-year-old techie Atul Subhash died by suicide on December 9, leaving behind a note and a video accusing his wife Nikita Singhania and her family of harassment, extortion, and false legal cases.Â
As the case took the nation by storm, a photo allegedly showing Nikita Singhania went viral on social media. The selfie showed a woman sporting sunglasses inside a car. Its archive can be seen here .
But is this the techie's estranged wife? Some people online pointed out that the photo did not show Nikita Singhania. India Today Fact Check spoke to Atul Subhash's brother Bikas Modi, who confirmed this was not her.Â
We found an Instagram and a Facebook  account featuring the profile photo. Both accounts were of a "Nikita Singhania" from Raipur. Both accounts were private. We contacted both accounts and will update the story as and when they respond.Â
As per news reports , Atul Subhash's wife Nikita Singhania works at Accenture and is based in New Delhi. Her family reportedly lives in Uttar Pradesh's Jaunpur. We did not find any reports pointing to a connection with Raipur, Chhattisgarh.
We then reached out to Atul Subhash's brother, Bikas Modi. He told India Today Fact Check that the viral photo was not of his sister-in-law. However, he confirmed that one of the photos used in various news reports did show her. Â AajTak's Samastipur correspondent Jahangir also shared with us a photo of Atul Subhash and Nikita Singhania. It is noteworthy that Atul's family lives in Bihar's Samastipur. A comparison of both photos makes it evident the woman in the viral photo is a different person altogether. Thus, it's clear the viral photo does not show the estranged wife of Bengaluru techie Atul Subhash. - Ends Published By: sharangee Published On: Dec 12, 2024 13:15 IST

title: Fact Check: A bridge from South Korea viral as 'Jammu National Highway'
content:
The image does not show the Jammu National Highway; it shows the Yeongdong Hongseong Bridge in Gangwon-do province, South Korea.
Jammu and Kashmir is undergoing rapid transformation. Earlier this year, in June, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated 84 major development projects valued at over Rs 1,500 crore and launched the Jammu and Kashmir Comprehensive Infrastructure Project worth Rs 1,800 crore.
Now, a picture of an overbridge has gone viral on social media, with many claiming it showed  the "Jammu national highway: Connecting the Kashmir Valley with the rest of India."
India Today Fact Check found that this is the Yeongdong Hongseong Bridge/Yeongdong Expressway in the Gangwon-do province of South Korea.
A reverse image search revealed that the photo has been widely circulated on the internet and social media and has been claimed to be from many countries over the years, often being described as one of their most beautiful tourist destinations. These claims include Nepal , Indonesia , and most recently, Pakistan .
To identify the source of the image, we conducted a thorough investigation using advanced tools. We discovered the photo was first posted on August 1, 2007, on Panoramio , a website dedicated to sharing images linked to Google Maps. This site was completely shut down  on November 4, 2016.Â
However, we were able to find an archive  of the site dated October 10, 2016, which included the viral image. The Panoramio user stated the photo was shot at a bridge in Daemiwon-ro, Ucheon-myeon, Hoengseong-gun, Gangwon-do, South Korea, and included the coordinates for the location on Google Maps .
In the Street View for these coordinates, we found the view from the bottom of the bridge matched  the bridge in the viral image. The bridge was marked as the "Yeongdong Expressway" on Google Maps.
Based on the above information, we conducted a search in Korean and discovered a commercial website that sells expressway cards (coupons). The card features the same bridge printed on it, and the text in Korean translates to "Yeongdong Hongseong Bridge".
We also discovered a drone video on the official YouTube channel of the Korean company Meritz, posted on June 1, 2021. The description indicates that Meritz was responsible for constructing the windbreak wall of the bridge. If we closely analyse the video, particularly the frame at 2 minutes 54 seconds, we can see an almost exact match with the viral picture.
Thus, it's clear that the viral image does not show a Jammu National highway; instead, it shows the Yeongdong Hongseong Bridge located in South Korea.
(Written By Surajuddin Mondal) - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Dec 12, 2024 15:35 IST

title: Fact Check: Protests already against new Syrian government? Nope, this video is from May
content:
This video is from May 2024 and shows people protesting against the HTS and its leader Abu Mohammed al-Jolani in Idlib following the custodial death of a man. It predates Bashar al-Assad's ouster by months.
The fall of the Bashar al-Assad regime in Syria has put global powers in a bit of a fix. Abu Mohammed al-Jolani's (also spelt as Julani and Golani in various reports) group Hayat Tahrir al-Sham, which seized control of Damascus, is recognised as a terrorist organisation by the United Nations, Turkey, the US and the European Union; though the United Nations  is reportedly considering revoking this status. And countries like Qatar, Egypt, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Jordan, Bahrain, Oman, and Italy are working towards opening diplomatic channels with the nation again.
But as many Syrians breathe free for the first time in years, some on social media claimed that a rebellion is already brewing against the HTS and Jolani. Many shared a video  alleging that a major protest had erupted in the Syrian city of Idlib. In the video , people in large numbers can be seen walking in the streets with placards and posters containing Arabic text. Sharing the clip on Facebook , one person wrote, "'Let Jolani fall'. 'Jolani, we don't want you'. A major protest erupts in Idlib — the stronghold of the Syrian opposition — against the new ruler of Damascus." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that this video is from May 2024 and shows people protesting against al-Jolani in Idlib, following the death of a man in police custody.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to its extended version shared on May 17 by the official YouTube channel of the Syrian media organisation Enab Baladi. The caption in Arabic stated that even after warnings from al-Jolani, protests demanding his resignation continued in Idlib. It is therefore clear that the video predates Assad's ouster by several months.
Further searches led us to news reports  about these protests against the head of the HTS. According to them, demonstrators in northwestern Syria demanded the resignation of Abu Muhammad al-Jolani, the release of detainees, and economic and policy reforms in the region.Â
An Associated Press report added that protests took place on May 17 in Jisr al-Shughour, Binnish, Sarmada, and Idlib, days after al-Jolani issued a warning against the protesters. On May 17, HTS forces cracked down on the protesters by firing bullets and beating them up in the Binnish town of Idlib. Before this protest, the HTS had also set up checkpoints and roadblocks to stop people from the neighbouring towns from reaching Idlib.Â
These protests started back in February, following the alleged torture and custodial death of a man in an HTS-run prison. The movement, per some reports , gradually declined afterwards as the HTS dealt with it through dialogue, promises of reform, and also suppression through its forces.
Thus, it's clear that the viral video does not show a current rebellion against the new HTS government in Syria.Â
The Rise of Abu Mohammed al-Jolani
Abu Mohammed al-Jolani was born Ahmad al-Sharaa in 1982 in Saudi Arabia . He grew up in the Mezzeh neighbourhood of Syria's Damascus.Â
In April 2013, al-Jolani established the Jabhat al-Nusra, the Syrian affiliate of the militant Islamist organisation al-Qaeda. Jolani, however, severed ties with al-Qaeda and rebranded the group as Hayat Tahrir al-Sham in 2017 to position it as a politically viable force in Syria. Under him, the HTS became the dominant force in Idlib and established a political and administrative arm called the Syrian Salvation Government in 2017.
According to the Associated Press , to rebrand the HTS, Jolani replaced his military garb with a shirt and trousers. He also began calling for religious tolerance, even appealing to the Druze community in Idlib. In 2021, he said in an interview: "Yes, we have criticised Western policies. But to wage a war against the United States or Europe from Syria, that's not true. We didn't say we wanted to fight." - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Dec 12, 2024 20:44 IST

title: Fact Check: 2016 car overturning video goes viral amid Chennai rains
content:
The viral video is not recent but from 2016. It shows a car overturning when Tropical Cyclone Vardah hit Chennai.
The India Meteorological Department predicts heavy rainfall across southern states and issued a yellow alert for heavy rains in Chennai, Kancheepuram, Tiruvallur, and Chengalpattu districts on December 11 and 12.
Now, a video of a car overturning amid a powerful storm is being widely shared with many claiming this was a recent incident in Chennai. Sharing this video , an X user wrote, "Heavy rains near the coast are intensifying, signaling the likelihood of more downpours in the coming hours. Please stay alert, stay safe, and remain indoors unless absolutely necessary. Take care! #ChennaiRainsUpdate  #chennairain" Its archive can be seen here.
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video is from 2016 and shows a car overturning when Tropical Cyclone Vardah hit Chennai.
Reverse searching the key frames of the viral video led us to CNN International post dated December 13, 2016. It read: "Car overturns as intense winds and heavy rain from Tropical Cyclone Vardah pound Chennai, India." This means that the video is not recent. Car overturns as intense winds and heavy rain from Tropical Cyclone #Vardah pound #Chennai , India https://t.co/SBVl4eG6Z1 pic.twitter.com/eCp8rcf1bc — CNN International (@cnni) December 13, 2016
Car overturns as intense winds and heavy rain from Tropical Cyclone #Vardah pound #Chennai , India https://t.co/SBVl4eG6Z1 pic.twitter.com/eCp8rcf1bc — CNN International (@cnni) December 13, 2016
In the post, we found CNN's detailed report about this video from DLF Garden City in Chennai. According to the National Disaster Management Authority, 10 people died during the cyclone.
We also found a Times of India report from December 12, 2016, that said the video was from Cyclone Vardah that led to heavy rains and storms in the coastal areas of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. At the time, many local Telugu news channels also covered this incident. A video report by TV5 News on this incident can be seen below. Thus, it is more than clear that a 2016 video from Cyclone Vardah in Chennai was shared as recent. - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Dec 12, 2024 23:36 IST

title: Fact Check: Giorgia Meloni DID propose an anti-Soros law. But she wasn't Italy's PM then
content:
This video is from June 2018. At the time, the Italian PM was Giuseppe Conte and Meloni was in the Opposition.
The winter session of Parliament has almost been a washout owing to frequent disruptions over the alleged affiliations of the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Congress party with billionaires Gautam Adani and George Soros respectively.
But has Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni also jumped into the ring now against George Soros? Many claimed so while sharing a video  of Meloni talking about Soros. "George Soros is worried about Italy? Right! The anti-Soros law is coming. Giorgia Meloni (PM of Italy)" read the text inside the video.
Sharing the clip , one person wrote in Hindi, "Here in India, the debate on George Soros is going on in Parliament for four days now.
