From Rahul Gandhi, Congress farmer movement, to INDI alliance, all funding is being done by George Soros. And in Italy, Giorgia Meloni is angry with George Soros and is saying that she is going to make a law, due to which George Soros and his NGO will not be allowed to enter Italy. And all the money deposited in the Italian bank accounts of George Soros and his NGO will be confiscated by the Italian government."
India Today Fact Check found that this Meloni clip is from June 2018 when Giuseppe Conte was Italy's prime minister, and Meloni was in the Opposition. Our Probe
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a post  stating that the viral video of Meloni talking about George Soros was six years old. Further searches led us to a post on Meloni's official X account dated June 4, 2018, containing the video in question. Its Italian caption read: "Soros is worried about Italy? Right! The anti-Soros law is coming." At the time, Meloni also shared the same video on her official Facebook and Instagram accounts. #Soros è preoccupato per l'Italia? Fa bene! In arrivo la legge anti-Soros... pic.twitter.com/hAaSq04WQx — Giorgia Meloni (@GiorgiaMeloni) June 4, 2018 We found a video report about this from June 5, 2018, on the official YouTube channel of an Italian news organisation, Vista Agenzia Televisiva Nazionale. Its description quoted Meloni saying that if the Italian government does its job well, a law proposed by the Fratelli d'Italia will come into effect and prevent people like George Soros from financing non-governmental organisations that allegedly weaken sovereign states. The Fratelli d'Italia or the Brothers of Italy is a right-wing populist political party led by Giorgia Meloni. Meloni's viral video was released a day after billionaire George Soros called for the European Union to compensate Italy for migrants landing there. This was in reaction to then-Interior Minister and far-right leader Matteo Salvini warning migrants to "pack their bags". We also found details about this video on the official website of Fratelli d'Italia in an article  dated June 4, 2018. It stated that the head of Fratelli d'Italia, Giorgia Meloni, declared that the party was working on an anti-George Soros bill to stop NGOs that promote illegal immigration after the same was done by Viktor Orbán's government in Hungary. It is noteworthy that Giuseppe Conte was sworn in as the Prime Minister of Italy as his party, the Five Star Movement, formed a coalition government with the far-right League party on June 1, 2018. Meloni, on the other hand, was sworn in as Italy's first female Prime Minister on October 22, 2022. Who is George Soros? advertisement Born in 1930 in Hungary, George Soros , a Jew, escaped the Nazi occupation and moved to the UK in 1947. Soros founded the philanthropic organisation Open Society Foundations , which supports democracy and human rights in more than 100 countries. In February 2023, while addressing the Munich Security Conference, Soros talked about the allegations against the Adani Group by the US short-seller Hindenburg Research and accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of being silent on the subject, stirring a controversy. Thus, it's clear that the video of Meloni talking about Soros is more than six years old! - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Dec 13, 2024 21:36 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT a drone in New Jersey! This video shows a plane crash in NY
content:
This video shows an airplane crash in New York, an accident that claimed the life of one person.
Amid reports of mysterious drones hovering in the sky, Governor of New Jersey Phil Murphy wrote a letter to President Joe Biden  on December 13, seeking answers about these alleged sightings. One such drone was reported to have crashed  into the backyard of a New Jersey resident, which later turned out to be a "hobby or toy type of drone", as per police officials. Frustrated residents have warned authorities to take matters into their own hands and shoot down  such drones themselves.
An alleged video of a drone crash is now going viral on social media  in which a huge white aircraft-like object can be seen in the middle of a street, surrounded by several cars with their sirens on.
A person shared the video on Facebook writing, "Mystery drone down, and now we can find out whose they are and why they are flying in our skies?"
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video does not show a drone, but a plane crash in New York, which claimed the life of one person. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a news report  about this incident dated December 13. According to it, a deadly plane crashed along Interstate-684 in Westchester County, New York, on the night of December 12. According to the New York State Police, two people were aboard the plane  when it crashed in a patchy area of the highway.
A man reportedly named Jacob Yankele Friedman  from New York, lost his life in the crash, while another person, identified as Kalmen Goldberger of Linden, New Jersey, got injured and was admitted to a New York hospital. Both the men present in the two-seat, single-engine airplane were reportedly licensed pilots .
According to the National Transportation Safety Board, the airplane was trying to land at the Westchester County Airport  after its engine failed. The highway remained closed for about seven hours for the investigation. The airplane that crashed was a "light sport" aircraft — a small plane that can be flown by people holding a sports pilot certificate.
It is thus, clear that a video of a plane crash on a New York highway was misidentified as a drone crash. - Ends Published By: Vadapalli Nithin Kumar Published On: Dec 14, 2024 19:18 IST

title: Fact Check: Hindu woman beaten for not wearing Hijab on Bangladesh? Here's the truth
content:
Police confirmed that the incident occurred on September 11, 2024, involving Aarohi Islam, a Muslim from the third-gender community, who was harassed by locals.
India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri recently visited Bangladesh to strengthen bilateral ties. Following his visit, Bangladesh's interim government announced that 88 cases had been registered , with over 70 individuals detained for violence against minorities, after initial denial of any persecution against the minorities.
Now, a shocking video of a group of men surrounding and hitting a woman with a stick and forcing her to do sit-ups while holding her ears has gone viral on social media. Those sharing this clip claimed that it showed radical Islamists beating a Hindu woman at Cox's Bazar sea beach for not wearing a hijab.
"Bangladesh: Radical Islamists beat up a Hindu tribal woman for not wearing a hijab on Cox's Bazar sea beach. Secularism is for those places where Hindus, Christians, or Buddhists are in the majority; otherwise, Sharia will be imposed. We need to act ASAP to save 18 million Bangladeshi Hindus," reads captions accompanying this video. Â
India Today Fact Check found that the incident dates back to September this year, and the victim here is not a Hindu but a Muslim. Also, the police identified them as third gender. OUR PROBE
A search of the keyframes from the viral video took us to a different video of the same incident, uploaded to the official YouTube channel of Channel i News on September 14, 2024. The video description mentioned a 23-year-old man named Mohammad Farukul Islam, who got arrested after the video went viral.
Subsequent keyword searches revealed several Bangladeshi news reports published in Prothom Alo , Dhaka Tribune , Dainik Bangla , Ajker Patrika , and BBC Bangla . As per these reports, Cox's Bazar Beach police arrested Farukul and confirmed that the original incident took place on September 11, involving a 20-year-old victim named Aarohi Islam, who is a Muslim.
The reports also cited police statements identifying Aarohi as belonging to the third gender. The incident occurred around 10 pm on the Sugandha Point of Cox's Bazar beach when Aarohi was roaming with a friend.
We also found a Facebook video on Channel i News's page featuring the statement of Aarohi Islam and the additional police super of Cox's Bazar, Jasim Uddin Chowdhury.
Here, Aarohi accused the attackers of labelling her with faulty charges of being associated with the Chattra League, the student wing of Sheikh Hasina's party, Awami League. On the other hand, Chowdhury was heard saying that the police responded promptly and held the main accused. He also confirmed that the victim was identified as Aarohi Islam, who belonged to the third gender.
Thus, it is more than evident that a three-month-old incident from Cox's Bazar Beach was falsely shared with a communal spin. - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Dec 14, 2024 19:55 IST

title: Fact Check: Not 'Love jihad'! This video of Hindu women rescued from Muslim man's house is SCRIPTED
content:
This video does not show a real incident. It is a scripted video created for entertainment and awareness.
A video of two people allegedly rescuing multiple Hindu women from a Muslim man's house has been widely shared on social media. The women could be seen covered in bruises.Â
Sharing the viral clip on X, one person wrote, "Muslim boys kidnap Hindu girls. Love jihad." Love Jihad is a far-right conspiracy theory that purports Muslim men target and seduce Hindu women to convert them.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the viral video does not show the rescue of abducted women at all. It is a scripted video made for entertainment and awareness.Â
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to its longer version uploaded to the YouTube channel "Naveen Jangra" on February 12, 2023. This featured a disclaimer at the 22-second mark that said the video "should be considered for entertainment purposes only."
The YouTube channel with more than 7.5 lakh subscribers features many scripted videos like the viral clip.Â
We contacted Naveen Jangra, who told India Today Fact Check that the video was created for entertainment and awareness, and did not show a real incident. Jangra, who is based in Delhi, said this video was shot in Delhi last year. Jangra has been creating such videos for five years. When asked about the people seen in the video, he told us that these were all paid actors that he hired to act in his videos. The same actors can be also seen in other videos  uploaded by Jangra.
It is thus clear that a scripted video is being shared with false communal claims. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Dec 16, 2024 21:25 IST

title: Fact Check: Drones in New Jersey? Nope, these three videos are old and unrelated!
content:
This video dates back to 2014 and was created for the promotion of the "Star Wars" franchise.
Mysterious drones have been spotted flying over New Jersey and other states across the northeastern US since mid-November. A group of federal agencies  have now said that these sightings are most probably a mix of legally flown aircraft, drones, and misidentified stars — and that they do not pose any risk to national security or public safety.
Meanwhile, old and unrelated videos have gone viral on social media in this context, with many sharing them with hashtags like "drone sightings" and "drones over NJ".
In this story, we'll look at three such videos. FIRST VIDEO
Claim: Dashcam footage  of an aircraft-like object lying on the corner of a road was widely shared as a drone that crashed in New Jersey recently. Its archive can be seen here .
Fact: This video dates back to 2014 . It was created to promote the "Star Wars" movie franchise. Many news outlets reported about it at the time . SECOND VIDEO
Claim: This video  shows a small object flying in the night sky. It was also shared as a recent drone sighting in New Jersey. Its archive can be seen here .
Fact: This video has been on the internet since as early as July 2008 . At the time, it was shared as a European black project aircraft. "Black project" is an informal term used to describe a secret military or defence project. Â
Claim: This video shows a man knocking down a drone flying in the sky with a stick. Those sharing it claimed that in New Jersey, a concerned citizen destroyed a drone. It was shared with captions like: "First New Jersey drone downed by a concerned citizen. It's a shame that he did what the US military couldn't do". Its archive can be seen here .
Fact: Using a reverse search, we found that many social media users shared  this video in August 2024. According to a September 2024 report published on a website named Dronewatch , this incident was from China. The man in the video, reportedly a farmer, was upset about chemicals reaching his crops from a spray drone in nearby fields. We, however, could not independently verify the exact date and location of this video.
Thus, it is clear that old videos are being shared in the context of the recent drone sightings in New Jersey, in the US. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Dec 17, 2024 22:45 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Indian men save Korean YouTuber only to rape her? No, this headline is doctored
content:
The article is doctored, and the headline has been edited.
A screenshot of an article in The Times of India has been widely shared on social media. The headline of the article read, "WATCH: South Korean YouTuber, harassed in Mumbai, meets two 'Indian heroes' who rescue her only to end up getting raped by them."Â
Those sharing this screenshot claimed that two young Indian men saved a Korean YouTuber from a molester only to later sexually assault her. An X user shared the screenshot and wrote : "Never trust anyone." Never trust anyone pic.twitter.com/es3Mqe8Lzg — The Wave (@TheWaveportal) December 19, 2024
Never trust anyone pic.twitter.com/es3Mqe8Lzg — The Wave (@TheWaveportal) December 19, 2024
India Today found the article doctored and the headline edited. Originally published by Times Now, not The Times of India, the article's headline was "[WATCH] South Korean YouTuber, harassed in Mumbai, meets two 'Indian heroes' who rescued her; shares video."Â
We searched for multiple keywords from the piece to see if any report matching this description was published by The Times of India. However, our search did not reveal any such report.Â
We also found another screenshot of a report featuring the same headline and lead shared on Facebook on October 22. But this report was not published by The Times of India; it was published by Mirror Now Digital. Additionally, this screenshot featured the name of its author, Sarmeeli Mallick.
Based on this, we conducted a follow-up search and found a report  on the official Times Now website dated December 2, 2022. This report shares similarities with the viral report we were investigating. It is authored by the same journalist, Sarmeeli Mallick, for Mirror Now Digital.
When we compared the viral article with the Times Now report, it became evident that the viral report was an edited version of the Times Now article. The headline of the Times Now article reads, "[WATCH] South Korean YouTuber, harassed in Mumbai, meets two 'Indian heroes' who rescued her; shares video." In the viral report, the phrase "shares video" was removed, and "only to end up getting raped by them" was included instead.
We also notice that a similar change has been made to the lead. The phrase "bid in Mumbai" was replaced with "ended up getting brutally raped by the two who are yet to be apprehended by the Mumbai police."Â
On November 29, 2022, a South Korean YouTuber was sexually harassed by two men, Mobeen Chand Mohammed Shaikh and Mohammed Naqeeb Sadrealam Ansari, in Khar, Mumbai. Two young men, Aditya and Atharva, witnessed the incident and stepped in to rescue her. On December 2, the YouTuber invited Aditya and Atharva to lunch as a gesture of gratitude.Â
The YouTuber shared the same pictures  used in the article and wrote : "Lunch with two Indian gentlemen who help me to post the video and save me on the street. Aditya & Atharva." However, she did not mention anything about Aditya and Atharva also harassing or assaulting her. We also could not find any reports suggesting the same. Lunch with two Indian gentlemen who help me to post the video and save me on the street👍 Aditya & Atharva pic.twitter.com/Cu9IYOjBMb — Mhyochi (@mhyochi) December 2, 2022
Lunch with two Indian gentlemen who help me to post the video and save me on the street👍 Aditya & Atharva pic.twitter.com/Cu9IYOjBMb — Mhyochi (@mhyochi) December 2, 2022
Thus, it's clear that the article was doctored, and the headline was edited.
(Written By Surajuddin Mondal) - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Dec 19, 2024 15:34 IST

title: Fact Check: This limping man is NOT a Gaza actor! The truth behind this viral video
content:
This video is not from Gaza but from Iraq's capital, Baghdad. The video was created for entertainment purposes.
The internet loves its slapstick comedy. But even by that standard, one video of a man with a bandaged leg accidentally limping on the wrong leg has an extraordinary number of views — at the time of filing of this story, the video  had over 62 million views on Instagram. The video shows a man with a bandaged leg getting out of a car with the help of two friends, and limping on the supposedly injured leg. He only course-corrects after his friend points out he's supposed to limp using the non-injured foot.Â
But why is this video this viral? Well, because those sharing it claimed the injured man was a Palestinian crisis actor caught fumbling on camera. People claimed that this Gazan actor was pretending to be a victim of Israel's war. A Facebook user captioned the video : "Actor in Gaza pretends to be a 'victim' but accidentally uses the wrong foot while limping with a supposed broken foot. Why would they need to act if there was an actual genocide?"Â
India Today found that the video is not from Gaza but from Iraq's capital, Baghdad. The video was created for entertainment purposes.Â
Upon reverse-searching the keyframes of the video, we found the clip on YouTube. It featured the watermark of an Instagram account: "x_hayder_r". We found the account on Instagram where the viral video  was shared on December 8 with laughter emojis. The account is managed by a man named Haider.       View this post on Instagram            A post shared by حيدر الاكرع (@x_hayder_r) A Baghdad address is also mentioned in the bio of the account. It appeared that the man wearing a cap in the viral video was the owner of the Instagram account. Many of his videos can be seen in the profile. Almost all videos show him selling some items. The account is followed by around five lakh people. It is thus clear that the account belongs to a content creator. We found that the Instagram user also shared a separate video  regarding the viral claim on December 14. The video shows him refuting the claim in Arabic. He said that the video was shot in Kadhimiya city in Baghdad, and it had nothing to do with Gaza. The video was made for fun, he said. Haider added that Israeli websites have been sharing his video with false claims. This makes it clear that the claim in the viral post is misleading. This is not the first time that such claims related to Israel's war on Gaza have gone viral on social media. Unrelated videos and images were shared claiming to show Gazans faking their injuries during the ongoing war. India Today Fact Check has debunked  such claims multiple times. - Ends Published By: Nakul Ahuja Published On: Dec 19, 2024 20:21 IST

title: Fact Check: Did Arvind Kejriwal insult Constitution and Ambedkar? This video is edited
content:
In this 2012 video, Arvind Kejriwal criticised the internal constitution of the Congress Party, not the Constitution of India.
As different parties in India compete for Dr BR Ambedkar's legacy , a nine-second-long video of Aam Aadmi Party supremo Arvind Kejriwal allegedly disrespecting the Constitution of India has gone viral on social media. In the viral clip, Arvind Kejriwal can be heard saying, "We were sitting… someone said whoever wrote the Constitution must have been drunk while doing it."
Sharing the video, an X user wrote , "BR Ambedkar was drunk while writing the Constitution: Arvind Kejriwal. He should be arrested. Share this maximum." Its archive can be seen here .
India Today fact check found that the video is clipped from a 2012 Arvind Kejriwal speech. In the original video, he was criticising the Congress party's internal constitution, not the Constitution of India.
Had Arvind Kejriwal made such controversial remarks, it would have attracted widespread news coverage. However, we found no credible news reports confirming this.
We observed that an X user, while responding to one of the viral posts, shared a 22-second-long video and claimed that the viral video was edited out of context. They claimed that Kejriwal made these remarks about the constitution of the Congress party. कांग्रेस के समर्थन में उतरे भाजपाई😱 ये है पूरा असली विडियो! बाबा साहब के भक्त अरविंद केजरीवाल जी ने कहा था "कांग्रेस का संविधान जिसने लिखा,उसने दारू पीकर लिखा होगा" भाजपा वाले उसे काटकर फर्जी वीडियो चला रहे है। @PunjabPoliceInd सबके खिलाफ कार्रवाई करेगी। झूठ नहीं,सच फैलाओ🔥 pic.twitter.com/0MB0tBuRLa — Devender Yadav (देव) (@DevenderYadav_) December 23, 2024 We then scanned Arvind Kejriwal's old speeches. This led us to the 17-minute-long original video uploaded to the official YouTube channel of the Aam Aadmi Party on December 3, 2012. According to the video's description, Kejriwal made this speech at Raj Ghat in New Delhi on November 25, 2012.  In this video, Kejriwal, while addressing a crowd, outlined the key points of the internal constitution of the Aam Aadmi Party and criticised the Congress party for not "following" its own party constitution. At the 4:35-minute mark, Kejriwal said, "I have read the constitution of all political parties. The constitution of the Congress Party says that no Congress worker will consume alcohol... We were sitting... Somebody said whoever wrote the constitution must have done it after drinking alcohol." This particular part was clipped from his speech and made viral as if he is disrespecting the Indian Constitution and its writers. The Aam Aadmi Party was officially founded on November 26, 2012. According to news reports , a day before the official launch of the party, Kejriwal addressed his supporters on November 25 at Raj Ghat. Thus, it is evident that Arvind Kejriwal did not make insulting remarks about the Indian Constitution or Dr BR Ambedkar in this video. advertisement (Written by Abhishek Pathak) - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Dec 23, 2024 18:33 IST

title: Fact Check: Biker harassing students in UP? This video shows incidents in Maharashtra, MP
content:
These videos show two separate incidents and neither is from Uttar Pradesh. The clip of the man on the bike is from Maharashtra. The clip showing a man being caught by the police is from Madhya Pradesh.
A video making the rounds online right now purports to show a Muslim man on a bike sexually harassing students in Uttar Pradesh. The video then cuts to several police officers apprehending and beating up a man, allegedly the same person who was on the bike.Â
The video was shared with captions like: "Abdul was molesting school girls every day. His activity captured in CCTV camera. Rest job done by UP police. Do you support this action of police?" Abdul is a euphemism often employed online to refer to Muslims.Â
India Today Fact Check found that the two clips show two different incidents, and neither is from Uttar Pradesh. The first video is from Maharashtra and the second video is from Madhya Pradesh.Â
Reverse-searching keyframes from the first half of the clip showing the man on the bike led us to a December 9 ABP Majha video report. According to the Marathi report, this video was from Maharashtra's Parbhani. The Marathi news outlet Sakal also reported the same in a video report.
We also found a Marathi news report from December 9. It said that on December 6 in Parbhani, a man called Aslam sexually harassed college students while on a bike. The act was caught on CCTV and quickly went viral online. A complaint was reportedly registered at the Nanalpeth Police Station in Parbhani and the accused was subsequently apprehended.
India Today Fact Check spoke to inspector Chitambar Kamthewad of the Nanalpeth Police Station. He said that the video was indeed from Parbhani. Per the officer, on December 6, the man was caught sexually harassing college students while riding a bike under the influence of alcohol. THE SECOND CLIP
We found this video shared on an Instagram account on December 9. As per the post's caption, on December 9 in Gadarwara in Madhya Pradesh's Narsinghpur district, a man was arrested in connection with a murder case. Using this information, we found news reports  about the incident that featured the viral clip.Â
As per reports , a man named Vikas Kuchbandiya was arrested for the murder of Madhur Chaurasia over a dispute of Rs 40,000. Some reports also mentioned that the accused had a previous criminal history and allegedly slit the victim's throat. This was corroborated by AajTak's Gadarwara correspondent.Â
Thus, it's clear that while the man on the bike in the first video is indeed Muslim, neither video has anything to do with each other or with Uttar Pradesh. - Ends Published By: Vivek Published On: Dec 23, 2024 19:17 IST

title: Fact Check: NOT Jaipur! This blazing tanker rolling across the street is from Russia
content:
This video is not from India at all. It shows a huge explosion at a gas station in the Chechen Republic of Russia.
At least 14 people died when a deadly collision  between an LPG tanker and a truck ignited a massive fire on the Jaipur-Ajmer highway on December 20. A video allegedly showing the accident  is now going viral on social media.
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video is not from India at all. It shows a huge explosion at a gas station in the Chechen Republic in Russia.Â
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to the same clip, shared in a Reddit post  dated October 12. According to it, this video shows an explosion at a gas station in the Chechen Republic.
Further searches led us to a post by the Russian state-controlled news outlet RT . Dated October 12, RT shared the video in question and said that Grozny locals captured the moment when a gas tank exploded and started hurling towards them following a huge blast at a gas station. Grozny is the capital city of the Chechen Republic. Grozny locals captured the moment that an exploded gas tank hurled towards them following a strong blast at a gas station pic.twitter.com/WoRVkMjq8A — RT (@RT_com) October 12, 2024
Grozny locals captured the moment that an exploded gas tank hurled towards them following a strong blast at a gas station pic.twitter.com/WoRVkMjq8A — RT (@RT_com) October 12, 2024
We then found several news reports about this incident. According to them, four people , including two children, died after a fuel tank exploded at a petrol station, causing a huge fireball in Russia's Chechen Republic.Â
The incident took place on October 12, following which, the head of the Chechen Republic, Ramzan Kadyrov, stated that he would personally take stock of the situation . He also made an Instagram post regarding the incident on October 13, offering condolences to the families of those who lost their lives.     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by К.А.Х. (@kadyrov95_)
A post shared by К.А.Х. (@kadyrov95_)
Quoting the Emergency Situations Ministry of the region, reports added that this explosion took place on Grozny's Mohammed Ali Avenue, close to the centre of the Chechen capital. The fire destroyed the gas station. A nearby apartment building and several cars were also damaged in the explosion that reportedly spread to an area of about 900 square metres.Â
The gas station where this incident happened had reportedly not been inspected for the last three years. At the time, multiple videos of this incident shot from different angles were shared by Al Jazeera as well.Â
It is thus clear that a two-month-old video from an explosion in the Chechen Republic of Russia was falsely shared as from the Jaipur blast. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Dec 24, 2024 18:45 IST

title: Fact Check: This is NOT a Muslim mechanic slicing seat covers to get more business
content:
The person seen tearing seat covers is Dheeraj Aggarwal, a coaching instructor from Dehradun. He is neither Muslim nor in the tyre repair business.
A video  allegedly showing a Muslim mechanic damaging bikes and scooters' seat covers and puncturing their tyres is now going viral on social media. In it, a person can be seen tearing the seat covers of two-wheelers parked by the roadside. In the second part, a man can be seen seemingly puncturing the tyres of a mini truck.  Â
An X user shared the video and wrote: "Mohammad Junaid was seen tearing the seats of vehicles parked on the roadside with a blender. When someone recorded the video & made it viral, it was found that Junaid had a puncture and seat cover shop on the same road. To expand his business, he punctures vehicles & tears seats."  Its archive can be seen here .Â
India Today Fact Check found that the person seen tearing seat covers is Dheeraj Aggarwal, a coaching instructor from Dehradun. He is neither Muslim nor in the tyre repair business.
Towards the beginning of the video, we observed two scooters with registration numbers starting with "UK", hinting at this video being from Uttarakhand. Â
We also came across a post  that claimed this video was from Dehradun's Nehrugram. Using this, we found the location on Google Maps . The grey shutter, three red staircases, and the orange-grey pillar seen in the viral video are also visible on Google Maps Street View.
Similarly, the boundary wall in front of the shop with the grey shutter is also visible in the Street View of this location.Â
At the time of writing this story, the Street View available on Google Maps for this location was from August 2022. Some of the shops in this location have changed now.
Raipur police station in-charge Pradeep Negi also confirmed to India Today Fact Check that this incident happened in Dehradun's Nehrugram. WHAT DID DHEERAJ TELL US?
We contacted Dheeraj Aggarwal to get more information about the video. He told India Today Fact Check that he runs a coaching centre in Dehradun and this incident happened on August 5, 2024.Â
He said, "There is a public parking area near my coaching centre in Dehradun's Nehrugram. Some random people used to park their vehicles in this parking area for the whole day and disappear. Owners of nearby shops asked them not to occupy the parking spot for the entire day, but they didn't listen to us. To teach them a lesson, we damaged the seat covers of some vehicles. However, somebody filmed us doing this and the video went viral. The police counselled me and even imposed a fine. However, the matter was ultimately closed. It is sad that now people are sharing it again in a misleading way."Â
Dheeraj also sent us a video message regarding this issue, which can be seen below.Â
The person allegedly seen puncturing tyres in the latter part of the video is not Dheeraj but someone else. We could not find any source for it. Dheeraj also told India Today Fact Check that it is not him in this video. Â Thus, it is clear that an old video of Dehradun-based teacher Dheeraj Aggarwal is being falsely shared as a Muslim mechanic tearing the seat covers of vehicles. - Ends Published By: Sahil Sinha Published On: Dec 24, 2024 20:02 IST

title: Fact Check: Brazil plane crash? No, the viral video is old and from the US
content:
This video dates back to August 13, 2023, and shows a MiG-23UB crashing during an airshow in Michigan, United States.
On December 22, a private plane crashed  into the city of Gramado in southern Brazil, killing 10 members of a business family. Now, a video purportedly showing the crash has gone viral on social media.Â
This video shows an aircraft flying over a lake eventually losing control before crashing. People sharing this video claimed this was the accident in Gramado. Such posts were shared with captions like, "10 People killed, 15 injured in Brazil plane crash" and "A tragic plane crash occurred in Gramado, a popular tourist city in southern Brazil, killing all 10 passengers on board. The Piper PA-42-1000 twin-engine plane was piloted by Brazilian businessman Luiz Claudio Galeazzi, who was travelling with his family."     View this post on Instagram            A post shared by Newsmelon. in (@news_melon_)
A post shared by Newsmelon. in (@news_melon_)
India Today Fact Check found that the video dates back to August 2023 and is from an airshow in Michigan, United States.
Reverse-searching keyframes from the viral video led us to a Sputnik Globe report  dated August 15, 2023. According to this report, the crash occurred in Belleville, Michigan, during the Yankee Air Museum's Thunder Over Michigan airshow. Reportedly, the aircraft was a Russian-made MiG-23UB fighter jet performing at the 25th Thunder Over Michigan Airshow, and an engine failure led to this catastrophe.
Subsequent keyword searches led us to a compilation of clips uploaded to the Daily Mail YouTube channel on August 14, 2023. Amongst these clips, the viral video was also featured. The YouTube video noted that the incident, which took place on August 13 that year, did not claim any lives.
A BBC report quoted the Wayne County Airport Authority stating that both pilots ejected safely before the crash and were safely rescued from Belleville Lake. According to officials, the jet crashed into unoccupied vehicles in the parking lot of the Waverly on the Lake Apartments in Van Buren Township.
Thus, it's clear that an old and unrelated video from an airshow was falsely shared as a recent plane crash in Brazil. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Dec 24, 2024 22:48 IST

title: Fact Check: Egypt uprising after Syria? No, these videos are old
content:
All three videos are from September 2019 when protests against President Abdel Farrah el-Sisi erupted in Egypt.
After Syria, is Egypt on the brink of an uprising? That's what's being claimed alongside a set of videos showing people tearing banners of Egypt's President Abdel Farrah el-Sisi and protesting on the streets.
Those sharing the videos  claimed, "PROTESTS ERUPT IN CAIRO AGAINST SISI. Egyptians hit the streets over Sisi's $45B capital project amid crushing poverty and inflation. Critics slam the move as lavish while citizens struggle to survive. Is Egypt on the brink of its next uprising?" The archive of such a post can be seen here .
India Today Fact Check found that all three videos are from September 2019 when protests against President Sisi erupted in Egypt. They are not recent at all. OUR PROBE
Using a reverse image search, we found the first video  in Facebook posts  from September 21, 2019. This itself makes it clear that the video is old, not recent.
We also found news reports  from the same day featuring similar videos of people tearing banners of Sisi. One such report  also features the screenshot of the second video. Per reports , these protests took place in multiple cities in Egypt including the capital Cairo.Â
The third video was also shared around the same time on Facebook.Â
At the time, massive protests erupted in the Egyptian cities of Cairo, Alexandria, and Suez. An Al Jazeera report  noted that thousands of pro-democracy protesters marched in cities across Egypt, demanding the resignation of President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi.Â
Protestors hit the streets after Egyptian self-exiled businessman and actor Mohamed Ali accused President el-Sisi of corruption and appealed people to take to the streets. El-Sisi dismissed the allegations.Â
Notably, we did not find any recent credible news report saying anti-government protests erupted in Egypt. Thus, it's clear that the viral claim is false. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Dec 24, 2024 23:01 IST

title: Fact Check: This video DOES NOT show a Houthi attack on an Israeli power plant
content:
This video is from Jeddah, Saudi Arabia and dates back to March 25, 2022. It shows Houthis bombing two oil tanks.
After the ceasefire agreement between Israel and the Lebanese militia group Hezbollah, Tel Aviv has shifted its focus to the Houthis, the Yemeni group blockading the Red Sea for about a year now.Â
A video  now going viral shows a massive fire engulfing a sizeable area, captured from a moving car. Those sharing this clip claimed the Houthis attacked the Rutenberg power station in Israel's Ashkelon.
"As I told you earlier, the HOUTHIS in Yemen. Yemen carried out a missile attack hitting the Israel Ashkelon power plant, so you can see the video now the power plant is still burning nonstop," one such post was captioned.
India Today Fact Check found that the video is originally from Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, and dates back to 2022. The attack, however, was carried out by the Houthis. Our Probe
A reverse search of the keyframes from the viral video led us to a post from March 25, 2022, featuring the same clip. As per the translation of the Arabic caption, these visuals were from Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, when the Houthis bombed two oil tanks in the Aramco facility. مشاهد من جدة بعد قصف خزانين نفطيين في منشاة تابعة لارامكو من قبل الحوثيين بحسب معلومات اولية. pic.twitter.com/IDXunyqmrG — ZaidBenjamin زيد بنيامين (@ZaidBenjamin5) March 25, 2022 The official Facebook Page of Qatar Day  also shared this clip on March 26, 2022, stating the same. This makes it clear that the video is not recent at all. According to Al Jazeera , Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said the group attacked Aramco's facilities with missiles and the Ras Tanura and Rabigh refineries with drones. He also said the Houthis targeted vital facilities in the Saudi capital Riyadh. A day after these deadly attacks, on March 26, 2022, Saudi Arabia retaliated in Sanaa, the Yemeni capital. Per reports , at least seven people were killed by the Saudi-led coalition in Sanaa and Hodeida during these retaliatory attacks. The military operations, however, halted on March 29, 2022, following a United Nations call for a truce during the Muslim holy month of Ramadan. It's also noteworthy that the Houthis claimed responsibility for a couple of drone attacks on the evening of December 25. According to a report in The Times of Israel , the drones were targeting a "vital and sensitive target" in Tel Aviv, and the other in Ashkelon's industrial zone. - Ends Published By: Anuja Jha Published On: Dec 26, 2024 18:45 IST

title: Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show the last moments of Azerbaijan plane crash
content:
This video has nothing to do with the Azerbaijan crash. It is from a different flight that was reported to have technical issues but landed safely in Algeria back in September 2024.
In a rare gesture, Russia's President Vladimir Putin apologised to Azerbaijan's President Ilham Aliyev on December 28, calling the crash of an Azerbaijani plane in Kazakhstan a "tragic incident" that killed 38 of the 67 people onboard.Â
On December 25, the plane is believed to have come under fire from Russian air defence systems targeting Ukrainian drones . After being hit, the plane was forced to divert towards the Caspian Sea but, soon after, crash-landed near Aktau airport in Kazakhstan. Now, a video allegedly showing the last moments just before the crash is going viral on social media.Â
The video in question features people sitting on their seats in a plane and chanting ' Allahu Akbar' in unison. Oxygen masks for the passengers could be seen hanging in the air. The text inside the video read : "Azerbaijan Airlines plane crashes. Allah Hu Akbar ."
India Today Fact Check, however, found that this video has nothing to do with the Azerbaijan crash. It was from a different flight that was reported to have technical issues but landed safely in Algeria.
Reverse searching keyframes from the viral video led us to several Facebook posts from September 2024 with the same video . Their caption in Arabic stated that an Air Algeria plane had to return to the airport due to a technical malfunction after takeoff. So, it is clear that this video predates the Azerbaijan crash by at least three months . Further searches led us to some news reports about this incident. According to them , the passengers on an Air Algerie plane sat in their seats, praying together after they were informed of a technical malfunction in the plane. On September 22, 2024, Flight AH3018 reportedly took off from Houari Boumediene International Airport, also known as Algiers International Airport . The plane was heading to Istanbul, Turkey, but it had to return an hour after takeoff, owing to a technical snag in the aircraft .
Further searches led us to some news reports about this incident. According to them , the passengers on an Air Algerie plane sat in their seats, praying together after they were informed of a technical malfunction in the plane. On September 22, 2024, Flight AH3018 reportedly took off from Houari Boumediene International Airport, also known as Algiers International Airport . The plane was heading to Istanbul, Turkey, but it had to return an hour after takeoff, owing to a technical snag in the aircraft .
The reports also carried the official statement of the Air Algerie airline , which stated that due to a technical malfunction, flight AH3018 had to return to the Algerian airport as a precautionary measure to ensure the safety of passengers and crew after it took off on the night of September 22 . The company provided accommodation to the passengers until a new flight was arranged for them on September 23. No casualties were reported in the incident.
We also found multiple videos of this incident, shot by different passengers , in X posts from the time of the incident . It is thus, clear that a three-month-old video of a different flight was falsely linked to the recent Azerbaijan crash. - Ends Published By: Akhilesh Nagari Published On: Dec 30, 2024 20:06 IST

title: Fact Check: This gruesome video of a dog attacking a young boy is NOT from India
content:
This gruesome dog attack took place in Brazil's Sao Paulo. The owner of the dogs was arrested by the police.
(Content Warning: Video contains disturbing visuals)
An eight-year-old boy suffered serious injuries after a stray dog attacked him  while he was playing football outside his house at Mira Road on December 16. According to reports, 18,705 people have been bitten by dogs  between January and October this year in Maharashtra's Kalyan-Dombivli city alone.
Now, a video allegedly showing a dog attacking a child in a residential society of Maharashtra's Kalyan city is going viral on social media. In the video, two dogs are running around in the play area of a building, while kids present there try to save themselves by climbing on top of a ride. Of the two dogs, one is seen biting the leg of a boy, who screams in pain. Seeing this, men and women rush to rescue the child by throwing sticks and stones at the dog, but it does not relent.
Sharing the video, one person wrote , "Kalyan Khadakpada Arihant Society. Stray dog attack on a child playing inside a society compound. Will AWBI, FIAPO, PFA, PETA take the responsibility and accountability of these stray dogs attacking, as children also have legally equal rights to live on Earth safely."
India Today Fact Check found that the video is not from India at all. It is from Brazil's Sao Paulo city. OUR PROBE
Reverse searching keyframes from the video led us to a news report from Brazil dated November 20, 2024. Two children, aged 11 and 12, got injured in this dog attack.
According to Brazilian news outlets, a Pitbull attacked children playing in a public playground in Vila Guilherme, a district in the Sao Paulo city of Brazil. The reports stated that on November 12, 2024, two dogs climbed over the wall of a gated property and attacked children . Out of the children present in the playground, an 11-year-old boy sustained serious injuries in his legs and was hospitalized at the Vereador José Storopolli Municipal Hospital. Marcos Sibioni, the owner of these Pitbulls, was indicted by the police for neglect of custody and serious bodily harm. He, however, denied negligence and claimed that the victims provoked the dogs, after which the dogs attacked them. Sao Paulo's Zoonosis Surveillance Division took the dogs into their custody . Some reports also added that the dogs were mistreated by the owner . Therefore, the viral video is from Brazil's Sao Paulo city and has no connection to Maharashtra. - Ends Published By: Ashutosh Acharya Published On: Dec 31, 2024 17:06 IST
